It is expressed in various secretory epithelia, the retina and sensory neurons, and mediates receptor-activated chloride currents in diverse physiological processes [[cite:PUB00069342]].

name: Protein of unknown function
description: This family represents a conserved region in a number of uncharacterised plant proteins.

name: zinc-finger of the FCS-type, C2-C2
description: zf-FLZ is a FCS-like zinc-finger domain found in higher plants. It is bryophitic in origin. It carries a zf-FCS-like C2-C2 zinc finger, consisting of a consensus cysteine-signature sequence with conserved phenyl alanine and serine residue associated with a third cysteine. It acts as a protein-protein interaction module [[cite:PUB00070912]].

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF592)
description: This region is found in some SIR2 family proteins ([pfam:PF02146]).

name: Surface lipoprotein assembly modifier
description: Surface lipoprotein assembly modifier (Slam) is a surface lipoprotein that may have a role in virulence [[cite:PUB00095100]]. In Neisseria, it is required for the surface display of lipidated virulence factors [[cite:PUB00095101]]. Proteins in this family contain an eight-stranded beta-barrel domain [[cite:PUB00095100]].

name: Zein-binding
description: This domain binds to zein proteins, [pfam:PF01559] [[cite:PUB00057496]]. Zein proteins are seed storage proteins.

name: Glycosyltransferase 61
description: This family represents the Glycosyltransferase Family 61. Members in this family are further processed into a mature form. It includes O-linked-mannose beta-1,4-N-acetylglucosaminyltransferase 2 (POMGnT2, also known as AGO61 or EOGLT) [[cite:PUB00083303]] and EGF domain-specific O-linked N-acetylglucosamine transferase (EOGT) [[cite:PUB00083304]]. This family also includes plant beta-1,2-xylosyltransferases [[cite:PUB00122264]].

name: Protein of unknown function, DUF596
description: This family contains several uncharacterised proteins.

name: Beta-trefoil domain of unknown function (DUF569)
description: This entry represents a domain of unknown function that has a beta trefoil fold. Some family members contain a two or three copies of the domain.

name: Immunity protein YezG-like
description: This protein family includes the immunity protein YezG from Bacillus subtilis and similar sequences predominantly found in Firmicutes. YezG is the antitoxin component of a LXG toxin-antitoxin (TA) module that promote kin selection, mediate competition in biofilms, and drive spatial segregation of different strains, probably helping to avoid warfare between strains in biofilms [[cite:PUB00101092]]. It shows an alpha/beta structure with an antiparallel beta-sheet.

name: PLATZ transcription factor
description: Plant AT-rich sequence and zinc-binding proteins (PLATZ) are zinc dependent DNA binding proteins. They bind to AT rich sequences and functions in transcriptional repression [[cite:PUB00045078]]. Included in this family is the protein RGF1 INDUCIBLE TRANSCRIPTION FACTOR 1 (RITF1), a transcription factor that plays a central role in mediating RGF1 hormone peptide signalling, leading to the production of reactive oxygen species (ROS) in roots to modulate meristem size and root growth, probably via oxidative post-translational modification of the transcription factor PLETHORA [[cite:PUB00096638]].

name: Rtf2 RING-finger
description: It is vital for effective cell-replication that replication is not stalled at any point by, for instance, damaged bases. Replication termination factor 2 (Rtf2) stabilizes the replication fork stalled at the site-specific replication barrier RTS1 by preventing replication restart until completion of DNA synthesis by a converging replication fork initiated at a flanking origin. The RTS1 element terminates replication forks that are moving in the cen2-distal direction while allowing forks moving in the cen2-proximal direction to pass through the region. Rtf2 contains a C2HC2 motif related to the C3HC4 RING-finger motif, and would appear to fold up, creating a RING finger-like structure but forming only one functional Zn2+ ion-binding site [[cite:PUB00066779]]. This domain is also found at the N-terminus of peptidyl-prolyl cis-trans isomerase 4, a divergent cyclophilin family [[cite:PUB00062056]].

name: Protein of unknown function, DUF601
description: This family represents a conserved region found in several uncharacterised plant proteins.

name: Protein of unknown function, DUF603
description: This family includes several uncharacterised proteins from Borrelia species.

name: Protein of unknown function, DUF604
description: This family includes a conserved region found in several uncharacterised plant proteins.

name: Vta1 like
description: Vta1 (VPS20-associated protein 1) is a positive regulator of Vps4. Vps4 is an ATPase that is required in the multivesicular body (MVB) sorting pathway to dissociate the endosomal sorting complex required for transport (ESCRT). Vta1 promotes correct assembly of Vps4 and stimulates its ATPase activity through its conserved Vta1/SBP1/LIP5 region [[cite:PUB00044969]].

name: Protein of unknown function, DUF599
description: This family includes several uncharacterised proteins.

name: Putative inner membrane exporter, YdcZ
description: DMT_YdcZ is a family of putative inner membrane exporters from both Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria.

name: PBDC1 protein
description: This entry includes PBDC1 protein from mammals and its homologues from fungi. PBDC1 homolog from S. cerevisiae also known as Ypl225w (Chp1, Chaperone 1 for eEF1A) functions as a co-translational chaperone by forming dual interactions with the eEF1A G domain nascent chain and the UBA domain of ribosome-bound nascent polypeptide-associated complex [[cite:PUB00160075]]. This protein primes the eEF1A nascent chains for binding to GTP as part of a folding mechanism which is tightly coupled to chaperone recycling [[cite:PUB00160075]].

name: S-adenosyl methyltransferase
description: This family contains a SAM (S-adenosyl methyltransferase) domain, with a central beta sheet with 3 alpha-helices on both sides. Crystal packing analysis of the structure PDB:3giw from [swissprot:Q82L35] suggests that a monomer is the solution state oligomeric form. An unidentified ligand (UNL, cyan) was found at the putative active site surrounded by the residues His57, His170, Phe171, Tyr216 and Met22 . The UNL is likely to be a phenylalanine or phenylalanine-like molecule. (details derived from TOPSAN).

name: Mitochondrial calcium uniporter
description: MCU functions with MICU1, an essential gatekeeper component of calcium-channel transport, to facilitate Ca2+ uptake into the mitochondrion [[cite:PUB00088836],[cite:PUB00109160],[cite:PUB00081393]].

name: Glycosyl-hydrolase family 116, catalytic region
description: This represents a family of archaeal, bacterial and eukaryotic glycosyl hydrolases, that belong to superfamily GH116. The primary catabolic pathway for glucosylceramide is catalysis by the lysosomal enzyme glucocerebrosidase. In higher eukaryotes, glucosylceramide is the precursor of glycosphingolipids, a complex group of ubiquitous membrane lipids [[cite:PUB00044658]]. Mutations in the human protein cause motor-neurone defects in hereditary spastic paraplegia [[cite:PUB00078737]]. The catalytic nucleophile, identified in UniProtKB:Q97YG8_SULSO, is a glutamine-335, with the likely acid/base at Asp-442 and the aspartates at Asp-406 and Asp-458 residues also playing a role in the catalysis of glucosides and xylosides that are beta-bound to hydrophobic groups. The family is defined as GH116, which presently includes enzymes with beta-glucosidase, [ec:3.2.1.21], beta-xylosidase, [ec:3.2.1.37], and glucocerebrosidase [ec:3.2.1.45] activity [[cite:PUB00044658],[cite:PUB00073615]].

name: PDDEXK-like family of unknown function
description: PDDEXK_6 is a family of plant proteins that are distant homologues of the PD-(D/E)XK nuclease superfamily. The core structure is retained, as alpha-beta-beta-beta-alpha-beta. It retains the characteristic PDDEXK motifs II and III in modified forms - xDxxx motif located in the second core beta-strand, where x is any hydrophobic residue, and a D/E)X(D/N/S/C/G) pattern. The missing positively charged residue in motif III is possibly replaced by a conserved arginine in motif IV located in the proceeding alpha-helix [[cite:PUB00044133]]. The family is not in general fused with any other domains, so its function cannot be predicted [[cite:PUB00075365]].

name: PNGase C-terminal domain, mannose-binding module PAW
description: The PAW domain is found at the C-terminus of PGNase, or peptide-N-glycanase, enzymes. It was named for 'domain present in PNGases and other worm proteins' [[cite:PUB00011448]]. PNGase catalyses the deglycosylation of several misfolded N-linked glycoproteins by cleaving off the bulky glycan chain before these proteins are degraded by the proteasome. PNGase specifically acts on the unfolded form of high-mannose type N-glycosylated proteins, and this domain appears to be the mannose-binding domain, which contributes to the oligosaccharide-binding specificity of PNGase [[cite:PUB00041628]].

name: ELMO/CED-12 family
description: This family represents a conserved domain which is found in a number of eukaryotic proteins including CED-12, ELMO I and ELMO II. ELMO1 is a component of signalling pathways that regulate phagocytosis and cell migration and is the mammalian orthologue of the C. elegans gene, ced-12. CED-12 is required for the engulfment of dying cells and cell migration. In mammalian cells, ELMO1 interacts with Dock180 as part of the CrkII/Dock180/Rac pathway responsible for phagocytosis and cell migration. ELMO1 is ubiquitously expressed, although its expression is highest in the spleen, an organ rich in immune cells [[cite:PUB00019508]]. ELMO1 has a PH domain and a polyproline sequence motif at its C terminus which are not present in this alignment.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF575)
description: Family of uncharacterised proteins. Contains several chlamydial members.

name: Protein of unknown function, DUF612
description: This family includes several uncharacterised proteins from Caenorhabditis elegans.

name: Divergent polysaccharide deacetylase
description: This family is divergently related to [pfam:PF01522] (personal obs:Yeats C).

name: PLAC8 family
description: This family includes [swissprot:Q9NZF1], the Placenta-specific gene 8 protein.

name: Dual-action ribosomal maturation protein DarP
description: The entry, previously known as DUF615, represents the Dual-action ribosomal maturation protein DarP (also known as YjgA) from Escherichia coli and related proteins. This protein binds pre-50S ribosomal subunits near the 23S rRNA L1 stalk, where it probably mediate correct positioning of the L1 stalk [[cite:PUB00104166]]. It plays a dual role in the late stages of assembly of the 50S ribosomal subunit where it promotes peptidyl transferase center maturation by modulating the docking of 23S rRNA helix H68, and maintains the stability of helix H89 with the help of uL16 (rplP), facilitating the final maturation of the peptidyl transferase center [[cite:PUB00155442]].

name: Protein of unknown function, DUF617
description: This family represents a conserved region in a number of uncharacterised plant proteins.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF562)
description: Family of uncharacterised proteins.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF613)
description: Family of chloroplast proteins of unknown function. Some members have two copies of the conserved region.

name: TOD1/MUCI70, glycosyltransferase-like domain
description: This entry represents a glycosyltransferase-like domain found in alkaline ceramidase TOD1 and the probable hexosyltransferase MUCI70 from Arabidopsis. MUCI70 is a predicted glycosyltransferase essential for the accumulation of seed mucilage, a gelatinous wall rich in unbranched rhamnogalacturonan I (RG I), and for shaping the surface morphology of seeds [[cite:PUB00095110],[cite:PUB00101913]]. TOD1 is an endoplasmic reticulum ceramidase that catalyses the hydrolysis of ceramides into sphingosine and free fatty acids at alkaline pH (e.g. pH 9.5) [[cite:PUB00101912],[cite:PUB00101914]].

name: NAT, N-acetyltransferase, of N-acetylglutamate synthase
description: This is the C-terminal NAT or N-acetyltransferase domain of bifunctional N-acetylglutamate synthase/kinases. It catalyzes the first two steps in arginine biosynthesis. This domain contains the putative NAGS - N-acetylglutamate synthase - active site. It is found at the C-terminus of Neurospora crassa acetylglutamate synthase - amino-acid acetyltransferase, EC: 2.3.1.1. It is also found C-terminal to the amino acid kinase region ([pfam:PF00696]) in some fungal acetylglutamate kinase enzymes [[cite:PUB00110296]]. it stabilises the yeast NAGK, N-acetyl-L-glutamate kinase, slows catalysis and modulates feed-back inhibition by arginine [[cite:PUB00059379]]. This domain is found to be the N-acetyltransferase (NAT) domain, and it has a typical GCN5-related NAT fold and a site that catalyzes NAG synthesis which is located >25 Angstrom away from the L-arginine binding site in the N-terminal domain [pfam:PF00696] [[cite:PUB00074836]].

name: Protein MS5
description: Proteins are known only from species of Brassicaceae. Protein MS5 is essential for pairing of homologues during early prophase stage of meiosis but not necessary for the initiation of DNA double-strand breaks.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF629)
description: This family represents a region of several plant proteins of unknown function. A C2H2 zinc finger is predicted in this region in some family members, but the spacing between the cysteine residues is not conserved throughout the family.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF627)
description: This family represents the N-terminal region of several plant proteins of unknown function.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF632)
description: This plant protein may be a leucine zipper, but there is no experimental evidence for this.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF630)
description: This region is sometimes found at the N-terminus of putative plant bZIP proteins. Its function is not known. Structural modelling suggests this domain may bind nucleic acids [[cite:PUB00070793]].

name: Protein of unknown function, DUF547
description: Family of uncharacterised proteins from C. elegans and A. thaliana.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF620)
description: Family of uncharacterised proteins.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF621)
description: Family of uncharacterised proteins. Some (such as [swissprot:O01625]) are annotated as having possible G-protein-coupled receptor-like activity.

name: Phosphatase 4 regulatory subunit 3
description: This entry represents the Serine/threonine-protein phosphatase 4 regulatory subunit 3 (also known as SMEK homologue) PP4R3, which forms a complex with the phosphatase 4 catalytic subunit (PP4c), localising it to the DNA damage repair machinery [[cite:PUB00101025],[cite:PUB00035452],[cite:PUB00101024],[cite:PUB00101026]] and regulates its activity. PP4c is involved in developmental progression, chemotaxis, expression of stress response genes and cell movement. These proteins contain an N-terminal EVH1 domain and this alpha solenoid region.

name: tRNA (adenine(22)-N(1))-methyltransferase
description: tRNA_MT is a family of bacterial tRNA (adenine(22)-N(1))-methyltransferase enzymes with a Rossmann-like fold. This enzyme carries out the function of N1-adenosine methylation at position 22 of bacterial tRNA [[cite:PUB00057355]].

name: CID domain
description: This domain binds to the phosphorylated C-terminal domain (CTD) of RNA polymerase II [[cite:PUB00051303],[cite:PUB00057474]]. This domain is known as the CTD-interacting domain (CID).

name: Family of unknown function (DUF716)
description: This family is equally distributed in both metazoa and plants. Annotation associated with [swissprot:Q9SLW7] suggest that it may be involved in response to viral attack in plants. However, no clear function has been assigned to this family.

name: Takusan
description: This domain is named takusan, which is a Japanese word meaning 'many'. Members of this family regulate synaptic activity [[cite:PUB00057464]].

name: Armadillo-like
description: This domain contains armadillo-like repeats [[cite:PUB00057475]]. Proteins containing this domain interact with numerous other proteins, through these interactions they are involved in a wide variety of processes including carcinogenesis [[cite:PUB00057476]], control of cellular ageing and survival [[cite:PUB00057475]], regulation of circadian rhythm [[cite:PUB00057477]] and lysosomal sorting of G protein-coupled receptors [[cite:PUB00057478]].

name: Plant transposon protein
description: This family contains plant transposases which are putative members of the PIF / Ping-Pong family [[cite:PUB00033672]][[cite:PUB00033674]].

name: Glutathione-dependent formaldehyde-activating enzyme
description: The GFA enzyme catalyzes the first step in the detoxification of formaldehyde. This domain has a beta-tent fold [[cite:PUB00078711]].

name: Pre-toxin domain with VENN motif
description: This family represents a conserved region found in many bacterial porlymorphic toxins which is located before the C-terminal toxin modules [[cite:PUB00057479]][[cite:PUB00057480]].

name: Possible hemagglutinin (DUF637)
description: This family represents a conserved region found in a bacterial protein which may be a hemagglutinin or hemolysin.

name: Plant protein of unknown function (DUF639)
description: Plant protein of unknown function.

name: Transcriptional repressor, ovate
description: This is a family of transcriptional repressors. In plants, these proteins are important regulators of growth and development [[cite:PUB00057482],[cite:PUB00057483]].

name: ALOG domain
description: The 125-residue ALOG (Arabidopsis LSH1 and oryza G1) domain is rich in basic amino acids, especially arginine, and is highly conserved among land plants. Members of the ALOG family of proteins function as key developmental regulators. It has been proposed that the ALOG domain originated from the N-terminal DNA-binding domains of integrases belonging to the tyrosine recombinase superfamily encoded by a distinct type of DIRS1-like LTR retrotransposon found in several eukaryotes. Secondary structure predictions revealed an all-alpha helical domain with four conserved helices [[cite:PUB00072583],[cite:PUB00072584]]. Some proteins known to contain an ALOG domain are Arabidopsis thaliana LIGHT_DEPENDENT SHORT HYPOCOTYLS1 (LSH1),involved in phytochrome- dependent light signalling; Oryza G1, involved in the specification of sterile lemma identity and Plant defence proteins.

name: Protein of unknown function, DUF624
description: This family includes several uncharacterised bacterial proteins.

name: Plant protein of unknown function (DUF641)
description: Plant protein of unknown function.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF642)
description: This family represents a duplicated conserved region found in a number of uncharacterised plant proteins, potentially in the stem. There is a conserved CGP sequence motif.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF643)
description: Protein of unknown function found in Borrelia burgdorferi, the Lyme disease spirochete.

name: Moulting cycle
description: This family of proteins plays a role in the moulting cycle of nematodes, which involves the synthesis of a new collagen-rich cuticle underneath the existing cuticle and the subsequent removal of the old cuticle [[cite:PUB00057485]].

name: Protein of unknown function, DUF645
description: This family includes several uncharacterised proteins from Vibrio cholerae. There is some doubt regarding the existence of these proteins, they are encoded by open reading frames contained within a repeated region in the Vibrio superintegron.

name: Bacteriophage HK97-gp10, putative tail-component
description: This family of proteins is found in the caudovirales. It may be a tail component.

name: Vitamin B6 photo-protection and homoeostasis domain
description: In plants, this domain plays a role in auxin-transport, plant growth and development [[cite:PUB00057512],[cite:PUB00057513]] and appears to be expressed by all cells in the plant as well as in plastids. The family has been shown to play a role in vitamin B6 photo-protection and homoeostasis in plants [[cite:PUB00066759]]. In line with various literature findings, these proteins likely function as transporters and may be directly involved in the transport of one or more forms of the vitamin.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF648)
description: Family of hypothetical Chlamydia proteins. This family may well comprise of two domains, as some members only match the N-terminus.

name: Yip1 domain
description: The Yip1 integral membrane domain contains four transmembrane alpha helices. The domain is characterised by the motifs DLYGP and GY. The Yip1 protein is a golgi protein involved in vesicular transport that interacts with GTPases [[cite:PUB00020577]].

name: Archaeal Nre, N-terminal
description: This conserved region is found in the N-terminal region of archaeal Nre proteins. While most archaeal organisms encode only a single Nre protein, some encode two, NreA and NreB.

name: Archaeal Nre, C-terminal
description: This conserved region is found in the C-terminal region of archaeal Nre proteins. While most archaeal organisms encode only a single Nre protein, some encode two, NreA and NreB.

name: Fcf1
description: Fcf1 is a nucleolar protein involved in pre-rRNA processing [[cite:PUB00035397]]. Depletion of yeast Fcf1 and Fcf2 leads to a decrease in synthesis of the 18S rRNA and results in a deficit in 40S ribosomal subunits [[cite:PUB00035397]].

name: Transcriptional repressor TCF25
description: Members of this family are transcriptional repressors. They may act by increasing histone deacetylase activity at promoter regions [[cite:PUB00033388]].

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF655)
description: This family includes several uncharacterised archaeal proteins. This protein appears to contain two HHH motifs.

name: Beet necrotic yellow vein virus, p31
description: This is a family of hypothetical proteins known as p31, mostly from Beet necrotic yellow vein virus. P31, encoded by RNA4, is involved in efficient vector transmission, symptom severity and silencing suppression in roots [[cite:PUB00076445]].

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF658)
description: Protein of unknown function found in Lactococcus lactis bacteriophages.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF659)
description: Transposase-like protein with no known function.

name: Ribosome biogenesis regulatory protein (RRS1)
description: This family consists of several eukaryotic ribosome biogenesis regulatory (RRS1) proteins. RRS1 is a nuclear protein that is essential for the maturation of 25 S rRNA and the 60 S ribosomal subunit assembly in Saccharomyces cerevisiae [[cite:PUB00020277]].

name: Transcriptional activator
description: This family of proteins may act as a transcriptional activator. It plays a role in stress response in plants [[cite:PUB00066760]].

name: 40S ribosome biogenesis protein Tsr1 and BMS1 C-terminal
description: RIBIOP_C is a family of eukaryotic proteins from the C-terminus of pre-rRNA-processing protein or ribosome biogenesis proteins BMS1 and TSR1. These proteins act, in the nucleolus, as a molecular switch during maturation of the 40S ribosomal subunit [[cite:PUB00072548],[cite:PUB00072547]]. This domain, domain IV of translation elongation factor selb, adopts the same fold as translation proteins such as domain II of GTP-elongation factor Tu proteins [[cite:PUB00038060]].

name: Mycothiol-S-transferase
description: This entry, previously known as DUF664, represents the Mycothiol S-transferase (MST) from Mycobacterium tuberculosis and related proteins mainly found in Actinobacteria. MST binds to and is responsible for the transfer of Mycothiol (MSH) to xenobiotic acceptors. The ability of MST to catalyse this reaction depends on the presence of divalent metal ions and this enzyme exhibits only a residual activity in metal absence [[cite:PUB00158836]]. MST is a member of the DinB-like superfamily. It folds into a canonical four-helical bundle that creates a metal binding site using a combination of three coordinating highly conserved histidine and aspartate residues. It was shown that MST uses Fe2+ as the catalytic metal in vivo [[cite:PUB00158836]].

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF668)
description: This entry represents the C-terminal domain of PSI proteins from Arabidopsis. This domain is found associated with [pfam:PF11961]. PSI1 was identified as a gene that is co-expressed with the phytosulfokine (PSK) receptor genes PSKR1 and PSKR2 in Arabidopsis thaliana. PSI proteins are plant-specific and promote growth [[cite:PUB00093967]].

name: Per os infectivity factor 3
description: This family contains viral proteins and includes Baculovirus Per os infectivity factor 3 (PIF3). PIF3 forms a complex on the occlusion-derived virus surface with PIF1, PIF2, and P74 which has an essential function in the initial stages of baculovirus oral infection [[cite:PUB00082562]].

name: CFA20 domain
description: This domain is characteristic of cilia- and flagella-associated protein 20 (CFA20). CFA20 is a cilium- and flagellum-specific protein that plays a role in axonemal structure organisation and motility [[cite:PUB00072946],[cite:PUB00072975]]. In Chlamydomonas reinhardtii, it stabilises outer doublet microtubules (DMTs) of the axoneme and may work as a scaffold for intratubular proteins, such as tektin and PACRG, to produce the beak structures in DMT1 [[cite:PUB00072975],[cite:PUB00072976]]. Other proteins contain a domain with homology to CFA20. WDR90/POC16 contains such a domain in its N terminus, followed by a large C-terminal domain with multiple WD40 repeats [[cite:PUB00072975]]. This domain is also present in the N terminus of uncharacterised protein C3orf67.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF669)
description: Members of this family are found in various phage proteins.

name: Methyltransferase FkbM domain
description: This domain is characterised by two well-conserved short regions separated by a variable region in both sequence and length. Proteins containing this domain have been characterised as methyltransferases. FkbM, was shown to be required for a specific methylation in the biosynthesis of the immunosuppressant FK506 in Streptomyces strain MA6548 [[cite:PUB00009583]]. This domain is also found in other methyltransferases such as SdnD from the fungus Sordaria araneosa, involved in the biosynthesis of glycoside antibiotics with tetracyclic diterpene aglycone structure [[cite:PUB00089798]].

name: Autographa californica nuclear polyhedrosis virus (AcMNPV) protein
description: This domain family is found in viral proteins such as Ac109 from Autographa californica nuclear polyhedrosis virus (AcMNPV). The gene (Orf1090) is essential and transcribed late in virus assembly, and protein AC109 has been shown to be important for the transport of the budded virion to the host nucleus. In mutants lacking the AC109 gene, virions are unable to enter the nucleus and remain in the cytoplasm. Although addition of AC109 allowed virions to enter the nucleus, the occlusion bodies were empty, indicating that AC109 is also important for the production of infectious budded virus [[cite:PUB00082303]] [[cite:PUB00082304]]. The exact function of this domain family remains unknown.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF677)
description: This family consists of AT14A like proteins from Arabidopsis thaliana. At14a has a small domain that has sequence similarities to integrins from fungi, insects and humans. Transcripts of At14a are found in all Arabidopsis tissues and localises partly to the plasma membrane [[cite:PUB00010152]].

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF674)
description: This family is found in Arabidopsis thaliana and contains several uncharacterised proteins.

name: Putative serine esterase (DUF676)
description: This domain, whose function is unknown, is found within a group of putative lipases. Proteins containing this domain include YOR059C (Lpl1) from budding yeasts. Lpl1 has been identified as a phospholipase B [[cite:PUB00073522]]. They contain an alpha/beta hydrolase fold.

name: NADH ubiquinone oxidoreductase subunit NDUFA12
description: This family contains the 17.2 kD subunit of complex I (NDUFA12) and its homologues. The family also contains a second related eukaryotic protein of unknown function, e.g. [swissprot:Q9BV02].

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF684)
description: This family contains several uncharacterised proteins from Caenorhabditis elegans. The GO annotation suggests that the protein is involved in nematode larval development and has a positive regulation on growth rate.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF678)
description: This family contains several poxvirus proteins of unknown function.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF679)
description: This family includes members such as plant proteins AtDMPs 1-10 (Arabidopsis thaliana DUF679 domain membrane proteins 1 -10) [[cite:PUB00136742]]. The AtDMP proteins are predicted to have four transmembrane spans, with cytosolic amino- and carboxy-termini. DMP1 is a membrane protein that may be involved in membrane fission during breakdown of the ER and the tonoplast during leaf senescence and in membrane fusion during vacuole biogenesis in roots [[cite:PUB00086645]]. Several DMP proteins are expressed in senescing organs (DMP1, -3, -4) or tissues that will stall later in development (DMP1, -2, -4, -7). These expression patterns strongly suggest involvement of several DMPs in various programmed cell death processes, e.g. senescence, dehiscence and abscission [[cite:PUB00136742]]. AtDMP8 and AtDMP9 however, have been shown to facilitate gamete fusion during double fertilisation in flowering plants [[cite:PUB00093467]].

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF680)
description: This family contains several uncharacterised proteins which seem to be found exclusively in Rhizobium loti.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF681)
description: This family contains several uncharacterised beak and feather disease virus proteins.

name: Autographa californica nuclear polyhedrosis virus (AcMNPV), P18
description: This family is represented by Autographa californica nuclear polyhedrosis virus (AcMNPV), P18; it is a family of uncharacterised viral proteins.

name: Rop-like
description: This family contains several uncharacterised bacterial proteins. These proteins are found in nitrogen fixation operons so are likely to play some role in this process. They consist of two alpha helices which are joined by a four residue linker. The helices form an antiparallel bundle and cross towards their termini. They are likely to form a rod-like dimer [[cite:PUB00052824]]. They have structural similarity to the regulatory protein Rop, [pfam:PF01815].

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF685)
description: This family consists of several uncharacterised proteins from Borrelia burgdorferi (Lyme disease spirochete). There is some evidence to suggest that the proteins may be outer surface proteins.

name: Per os infectivity
description: This is a family of dsDNA Baculovirus proteins. It is required for the infectivity of the OBs or occlusion bodies. It is a structural protein of the ODV envelope required only in the first steps of per os larva infection, as viruses being produced in cells expressing the gene for this protein but not containing it in their genomes are able to produce successful infections. Baculoviruses are large DNA viruses that infect arthropods, mainly members of the order Lepidoptera. In their life cycle, they produce two kinds of particles, a budded, non-occluded virus (BV), which buds out of the infected cell and is responsible for the cell-to-cell transmission of the virus, and an occluded form, the occlusion body (OB), which is responsible for protecting the virus between encounters with larvae. A variable number of virions are included in the para-crystalline structure of the OB, mainly constituted by the virus-encoded polyhedrin protein; these virions are called occlusion body-derived virions or ODVs.

name: Cytokine-induced anti-apoptosis inhibitor 1, Fe-S biogenesis
description: Anamorsin, subsequently named CIAPIN1 for cytokine-induced anti-apoptosis inhibitor 1, in humans is the homologue of yeast Dre2, a conserved soluble eukaryotic Fe-S cluster protein, that functions in cytosolic Fe-S protein biogenesis. It is found in both the cytoplasm and in the mitochondrial intermembrane space (IMS) [[cite:PUB00055951]]. CIAPIN1 is found to be up-regulated in hepatocellular cancer, is considered to be a downstream effector of the receptor tyrosine kinase-Ras signalling pathway, and is essential in mouse definitive haematopoiesis [[cite:PUB00055952]]. Dre2 has been found to interact with the yeast reductase Tah18, forming a tight cytosolic complex implicated in the response to high levels of oxidative stress [[cite:PUB00109169]]. These proteins consist of two domains, the N-terminal well-folded one, with a S-adenosylmethionine methyltransferase-like fold and the C-terminal more flexible domain, represented in this entry, which contains two highly conserved cysteine rich motifs that bind Fe-S clusters [[cite:PUB00067100],[cite:PUB00056284]].

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF687)
description: This family contains several uncharacterised Chlamydia proteins.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF688)
description: This family contains several uncharacterised proteins found in Arabidopsis thaliana.

name: CRISPR-associated protein Cas7
description: CRISPR-associated protein Cas7 is one of the components of the type I-B cascade-like antiviral defence complex. In Haloferax volcanii, Cas5, Cas6 and Cas7 form a small complex that aids the stability of CRISPR-derived RNA [[cite:PUB00071890]].

name: Type VII secretion system ESX-1, transport TM domain B
description: EccB is a family of largely Gram-positive bacterial transmembrane componenets of the type VII secretion system characterised in Mycobacterium tuberculosis, systems ESX1-5. Translocation of virulent peptides through the membranes is thought to be mediated via a complex that includes EccB, EccC, EccD, EccE, and MycP [[cite:PUB00083129],[cite:PUB00106938]]. EccB, EccC, EccD, and EccE form a stable complex in the mycobacterial cell envelope [[cite:PUB00083131]].

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF693)
description: This family consists of several uncharacterised proteins from Borrelia burgdorferi (Lyme disease spirochete).

name: RiPP precursor modification enzyme MbnB/TglH/ChrH
description: This entry represents a family of multinuclear iron-containing proteins which are post-translational modification enzymes involved in the biosynthesis of ribosomally synthesized and post-translationally modified peptide (RiPP) natural products, including the precursor modification enzymes MbnB, TglH, and ChrH, formerly known as DUF692 [[cite:PUB00153337],[cite:PUB00106909]].

name: Family of unknown function (DUF695)
description: Family of uncharacterised bacterial proteins.

name: RNA cytidine acetyltransferase NAT10/TcmA, helicase domain
description: This domain contains a P-loop (Walker A) motif, suggesting that it has ATPase activity, and a Walker B motif. It si found in RNA cytidine acetyltransferase NAT10 from eukaryotes and tRNA(Met) cytidine acetyltransferase TcmA from prokaryotes. NAT10 catalyses the formation of N4-acetylcytidine (ac4C) modification on mRNAs, 18S rRNA and tRNAs [[cite:PUB00050413],[cite:PUB00076725],[cite:PUB00158943],[cite:PUB00158942]]. In tRNA(Met) cytidine acetyltransferase (TmcA) it may function as an RNA helicase motor (driven by ATP hydrolysis) which delivers the wobble base to the active centre of the GCN5-related N-acetyltransferase (GNAT) domain [[cite:PUB00050413]].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF697)
description: Family of bacterial hypothetical proteins that is sometimes associated with GTPase domains.

name: Transcription elongation factor Elf1 like
description: This family of short proteins contains a putative zinc binding domain with four conserved cysteines. [swissprot:P36053] has been identified as a transcription elongation factor in Saccharomyces cerevisiae [[cite:PUB00033659]].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF702)
description: Members of this family are found in various putative zinc finger proteins.

name: Hypothetical methyltransferase
description: This family consists of several uncharacterised eukaryotic proteins which are related to methyltransferases [pfam:PF01209].

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF705)
description: This family contains several uncharacterised Baculovirus proteins.

name: Myo-inositol oxygenase
description: MIOX is the enzyme myo-inositol oxygenase. It catalyses the first committed step in the glucuronate-xylulose pathway, It is a di-iron oxygenase with a key role in inositol metabolism. The structure reveals a monomeric, single-domain protein with a mostly helical fold that is distantly related to the diverse HD domain superfamily. The structural core is of five alpha-helices that contribute six ligands, four His and two Asp, to the di-iron centre where the two iron atoms are bridged by a putative hydroxide ion and one of the Asp ligands. The substrate is myo-inositol is bound in a terminal substrate-binding mode to a di-iron cluster [[cite:PUB00041510]]. Within the structure are two additional proteinous lids that cover and shield the enzyme's active site [[cite:PUB00047694]].

name: Cell division protein ZapA
description: ZapA is a cell division protein which interacts with FtsZ. FtsZ is part of a mid-cell cytokinetic structure termed the Z-ring that recruits a hierarchy of fission related proteins early in the bacterial cell cycle. The interaction of FtsZ with ZapA drives its polymerisation and promotes FtsZ filament bundling thereby contributing to the spatio-temporal tuning of the Z-ring [[cite:PUB00021077]][[cite:PUB00021078]].

name: YcgL domain
description: This family of proteins formerly called DUF709 includes the E. coli gene ycgL. Homologues of YcgL are found in gammaproteobacteria. The structure of this protein shows a novel alpha/beta/alpha sandwich structure [[cite:PUB00041298]].

name: Uncharacterised ACR (DUF711)
description: The proteins in this family are functionally uncharacterised. The proteins are around 450 amino acids long and includes Streptococcus pneumoniae Sp0239 which is structurally similar to ribonucleotide reductase (RNR) and pyruvate formate lyase (PFL). It is likely that this family represents a group of glycerol-3-phosphate dehydrogenases.

name: TRIC channel
description: TRIC (trimeric intracellular cation) channels are differentially expressed in intracellular stores in animal cell types. TRIC subtypes contain three proposed transmembrane segments, and form homo-trimers with a bullet-like structure. Electrophysiological measurements with purified TRIC preparations identify a monovalent cation-selective channel [[cite:PUB00053854]].

name: Methyltransferase TRM13
description: This is a family of eukaryotic proteins which are responsible for 2'-O-methylation of tRNA at position 4 [[cite:PUB00045160]]. TRM13 shows no sequence similarity to other known methyltransferases.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF707)
description: This family consists of several uncharacterised proteins from Arabidopsis thaliana.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF713)
description: This family contains several proteins of unknown function from C.elegans. The GO annotation suggests that this protein is involved in nematode development and has a positive regulation on growth rate.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF735)
description: This family consists of several uncharacterised Borrelia burgdorferi (Lyme disease spirochete) proteins of unknown function.

name: Oligosaccharyltransferase subunit 5
description: Eukaryotic N-glycosylation is catalysed in the ER lumen, where the enzyme oligosaccharyltransferase (OTase) transfers donor glycans from a dolichol pyrophosphate (DolP) carrier (Lipid-linked oligosaccharide; LLO) to polypeptides. The yeast OTase is a hetero-oligomeric complex composed of essential (Ost1, Ost2, Wbp1, Stt3, and Swp1) and nonessential (Ost3, Ost4, Ost5, and Ost6) subunits. This domain family is found in Ost5, [swissprot:Q92316]. The precise function of this subunit is not known, however Ost5 appears to form a sub-complex with Ost1, and this sub-complex associates with the catalytic Stt3 subunit of OTase. Down regulation of Ost5 resulted in a limited effect on glycosylation and no effect on the stability of Ost1 or Stt3 subunits [[cite:PUB00109240],[cite:PUB00109241]].

name: U11-48K-like CHHC zinc finger
description: This zinc binding domain [[cite:PUB00053822]] has four conserved zinc chelating residues in a CHHC pattern. This domain is predicted to have an RNA-binding function [[cite:PUB00053822]].

name: Dna[CI] antecedent, DciA
description: This family contains several actinomycete proteins. Family members such as DciA (dna[CI] antecedent) found in Pseudomonas aeruginosa, has been shown to share a common function with DnaC (in Escherichia coli) and DnaI (in Bacillus subtilis), acting as a replicative helicase. Furthermore, functional analysis revealed that DciA is essential for replication initiation and protein depletion resulted in a blockage of the initiation of replication after the formation of the open complex [[cite:PUB00085163]].

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF722)
description: This family contains several bacteriophage proteins of unknown function.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF723)
description: This family contains several uncharacterised proteins from Neisseria meningitidis. These proteins may have a role in DNA-binding.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF724)
description: This family contains several uncharacterised proteins found in Arabidopsis thaliana and other plants. This region is often found associated with Agenet domains and may contain coiled-coil.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF725)
description: This family contains several Drosophila proteins of unknown function.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF726)
description: This family consists of several uncharacterised eukaryotic proteins.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF736)
description: This family consists of several uncharacterised bacterial proteins of unknown function.

name: MICOS complex subunit MIC19/MIC25
description: MIC19 (also known as ChChd3) and MIC25 (also known as ChChd6) are components of the MICOS complex, a large protein complex of the mitochondrial inner membrane that plays crucial roles in the maintenance of crista junctions, inner membrane architecture, and formation of contact sites to the outer membrane [[cite:PUB00086469],[cite:PUB00086470],[cite:PUB00093460]]. MIC19 plays an important role in the maintenance of the MICOS complex stability and the mitochondrial cristae morphology [[cite:PUB00086469]].

name: GNAT acetyltransferase, Mec-17
description: Mec-17 is the protein product of one of the 18 genes required for the development and function of the touch receptor neuron for gentle touch. Mec-17 is specifically required for maintaining the differentiation of the touch receptor [[cite:PUB00053857]]. The family shares all the residue-motifs characteristic of Gcn5-related acetyl-transferases, though the exact unction is still unknown [[cite:PUB00044970]].

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF720)
description: This family consists of several uncharacterised Chlamydia proteins of unknown function.

name: GSKIP domain
description: This domain is found in GSK3-beta interaction protein (GSKIP), which binds to GSK3beta [[cite:PUB00054079]]. It is also found as a short domain towards the N terminus in clustered mitochondria protein, also known as clueless in Drosophila, which is involved in proper cytoplasmic distribution of mitochondria [[cite:PUB00064791],[cite:PUB00068099],[cite:PUB00068100]].

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF728)
description: This family consists of several uncharacterised tobravirus proteins of unknown function.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF732)
description: This family consists of several uncharacterised Mycobacterium tuberculosis and leprae proteins of unknown function.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF733)
description: This family consists of several uncharacterised Drosophila melanogaster proteins of unknown function.

name: Mitochondrial fission regulator
description: In eukaryotes, this family of proteins induces mitochondrial fission [[cite:PUB00057499],[cite:PUB00057500]].

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF730)
description: This family consists of several uncharacterised Arabidopsis thaliana proteins of unknown function.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF742)
description: This family consists of several uncharacterised Streptomyces proteins as well as one from Mycobacterium tuberculosis. The function of these proteins is unknown.

name: Vesivirus VP2 protein
description: This family consists of several Calicivirus VP2 proteins [[cite:PUB00097361]]. VP2 is a minor capsid protein encoded by all caliciviruses. forms a large portal-like assembly at a unique three-fold axis of symmetry, following receptor engagement. This assembly-which was not detected in undecorated virions-is formed of twelve copies of VP2, arranged with their hydrophobic N termini pointing away from the virion surface.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF719)
description: This family consists of several eukaryotic proteins of unknown function.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF745)
description: This family consists of several uncharacterised Drosophila melanogaster proteins of unknown function.

name: L-rhamnose mutarotase
description: This family contains L-rhamnose mutarotase which is a glycosyl hydrolase that converts the monosaccharide L-rhamnopyranose from the alpha to the beta stereoisomer. In Escherichia coli this enzyme is the product of the rhaM gene (also known as yiiL). The tertiary structure has been solved, in complex with L-rhamnose, and the catalytic mechanism determined. His22 is the proton donor. The enzyme naturally exists as a dimer.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF717)
description: This family consists of several herpesvirus proteins of unknown function.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF739)
description: This family contains several bacteriophage proteins. Some of the proteins in this family have been labeled putative cro repressor proteins.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF740)
description: This family consists of several uncharacterised plant proteins of unknown function.

name: Per os infectivity factor 6
description: Family members include Autographa californica nuclear polyhedrosis virus (AcMNPV) Orf68 (also known as per os infectivity factor 6, PIF6 or ac68). PIF6 is present in both the budded virus (BV) and the occluded-derived virus (ODV). The ac68 gene overlaps the lef3 gene which encodes the single-stranded DNA binding protein, and knockout experiments of ac68 have to ensure that a functional lef3 gene is present. In ac68KO experiments, viral DNA replication and BV levels were unaffected as were mortality rates if caterpillars were injected with BV directly into the hemolymph bypassing the gut. However, in oral bioassays the ac68KO occlusion bodies failed to kill larvae, indicating that PIF6 is a per os infectivity factor [[cite:PUB00082605]].

name: Domain of Unknown Function (DUF746)
description: This is a short conserved region found in some transposons. Structural modelling suggests this domain may bind nucleic acids [[cite:PUB00070793]].

name: Eukaryotic membrane protein family
description: This family is a family of eukaryotic membrane proteins. It was previously annotated as including a putative receptor for human cytomegalovirus gH [[cite:PUB00019476]] but this has has since been disputed [[cite:PUB00044752]]. Analysis of the mouse Tapt1 protein (transmembrane anterior posterior transformation 1) has shown it to be involved in patterning of the vertebrate axial skeleton.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF749)
description: Archaeal domain of unknown function. This domain has been solved as part of a structural genomics project and comprises of segregated helical and anti-parallel beta sheet regions.

name: Viral domain of unknown function (DUF1717)
description: This domain is found in viral proteins of unknown function.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF751)
description: This family contains several plant, cyanobacterial and algal proteins of unknown function. The family is exclusively found in phototrophic organisms and may therefore play a role in photosynthesis (personal obs:Moxon SJ).

name: S-adenosyl-L-methionine-dependent methyltransferase
description: This family is a S-adenosyl-L-methionine (SAM)-dependent methyltransferase. It is often found in association with [pfam:PF01266], where it is responsible for catalysing the transfer of a methyl group from S-adenosyl-L-methionine to 5-aminomethyl-2-thiouridine to form 5-methylaminomethyl-2-thiouridine [[cite:PUB00043072],[cite:PUB00057501]].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF753)
description: This domain contains is found in many copies in a variety of uncharacterised fly proteins. This domain has a Ly6/uPAR/alpha-neurotoxin-like domain structure.

name: Putative 3TM holin, Phage_holin_3
description: This is a family of putative proteobacterial phage three-transmembrane-domain holins.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF755)
description: This family is predominated by ORFs from Circoviridae. The function of this family remains to be determined.

name: Bacterial phospholipase C, C-terminal domain
description: This domain is found, normally as a tandem repeat, at the C-terminus of bacterial phospholipase C proteins.

name: Tumor necrosis factor alpha-induced protein 8-like
description: This family includes human tumor necrosis factor alpha-induced protein 8-like (TNFAIP8) and similar proteins mainly found in animals. TNFAIP8 functions as a negative mediator of apoptosis and may play a role in tumour progression. Proteins in this family adopt an all-alpha configuration.

name: Borrelia burgdorferi protein of unknown function (DUF759)
description: This family consists of several uncharacterised proteins from the Lyme disease spirochete Borrelia burgdorferi.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF760)
description: This family contains several uncharacterised plant proteins.

name: Zinc-binding loop region of homing endonuclease
description: This domain [[cite:PUB00028315]] is the short zinc-binding loops region of a number of much longer chain homing endonucleases. Such loops are probably stabilised by the zinc and may be viewed as small but separate domains. The common structural feature of these domains is that at least three zinc ligands lie very close to each other in the sequence and are not incorporated into regular secondary structural elements. The biological roles played by these small zinc-binding domains are presently unknown [[cite:PUB00053732]].

name: Cotton fibre expressed protein
description: This family consists of several plant proteins of unknown function. Three of the sequences (from Gossypium hirsutum) in this family are described as cotton fibre expressed proteins [[cite:PUB00011314]]. The remaining sequences, found in Arabidopsis thaliana, are uncharacterised.

name: Coxiella burnetii protein of unknown function (DUF762)
description: This family consists several of several uncharacterised proteins from the bacterium Coxiella burnetii. Coxiella burnetii is the causative agent of the Q fever disease.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF763)
description: This family consists of several uncharacterised bacterial and archaeal proteins of unknown function.

name: Borrelia burgdorferi protein of unknown function (DUF764)
description: This family consists of proteins of unknown function from Borrelia burgdorferi (Lyme disease spirochete).

name: Circovirus protein of unknown function (DUF765)
description: This family consists of several short (27-30aa) porcine and bovine circovirus ORF6 proteins of unknown function.

name: JNK1/MAPK8-associated membrane protein
description: This family consists of several eukaryotic proteins including JAMP, a Jun N-terminal kinase 1 (JNK1)-associated membrane protein. It associates with JNK1 through its C-terminal domain and regulates the duration of JNK1 activity in response to diverse stress stimuli [[cite:PUB00086473]]. It is an important component for coordinated clearance of misfolded proteins from the ER [[cite:PUB00086474],[cite:PUB00086475]].

name: Putative peptidase (DUF1758)
description: This is a family of nematode proteins of unknown function. However, it seems likely that these proteins act as aspartic peptidases.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF768)
description: This family consists of several uncharacterised hypothetical proteins from Rhizobium loti.

name: Xylella fastidiosa protein of unknown function (DUF769)
description: This family consists of several uncharacterised hypothetical proteins of unknown function from Xylella fastidiosa, the organism that causes Pierce's disease in plants.

name: Type VI secretion system, VipA, VC_A0107 or Hcp2
description: T6SSs are toxin delivery systems. It is a multiprotein complex requiring numerous core proteins (Tss proteins) including cytoplasmic, transmembrane, and outer membrane components. The needle or tube apparatus is comprised of a phage-like complex, similar to the T4 contractile bacteriophage tail, which is thought to be anchored to the membrane by a trans-envelope complex [[cite:PUB00090998]]. VipA is a family of Gram-negative bacterial proteins that form part of the type VI pathogenic secretion system. Members have been variously defined as VC_A0107 family, Hcp2, TssB and VipA, for ClpV-interacting proteins. VipB and VipA proteins interact very closely to form the shaft of the pathogenic penetrating needle system [[cite:PUB00075705],[cite:PUB00075433],[cite:PUB00075706]]. VipA and VipB (TssB and TssC) proteins were shown to form a cog-wheel like tubular structure in V. cholerae that was noticed to resemble T4 phage gp18 polysheath. Two beta-strands of VipA and four beta-strands of VipB intertwine forming the middle layer of the sheath. The sheath assembles around an inner Hcp tube and is attached to a structure called a baseplate that spans the bacterial membranes. Importantly, VipA/VipB sheath was shown to form a long contractile organelle in V. cholerae and in E. coli, suggesting that sheath contraction powers the secretion [[cite:PUB00091000]].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF771)
description: Family of uncharacterised ORFs found in Bacteriophage and Lactococcus lactis.

name: Transposase domain (DUF772)
description: This presumed domain is found at the N-terminus of many proteins found in transposons.

name: CDK5 regulatory subunit-associated protein 3
description: This family contains several eukaryotic sequences such as CDK5RAP3 (also known as C53 or LZAP) which serves as a probable tumour suppressor. Initially identified as a CDK5R1 interactor controlling cell proliferation [[cite:PUB00086010],[cite:PUB00086014]]. It negatively regulates NF-kappa-B-mediated gene transcription through the control of RELA phosphorylation [[cite:PUB00043152],[cite:PUB00086011]]. It also regulates mitotic G2/M transition checkpoint and mitotic G2 DNA damage checkpoint [[cite:PUB00086012],[cite:PUB00086013]]. It has been shown to bind Wip1 and stimulates its phosphatase activity [[cite:PUB00086015]].

name: Hikeshi-like, N-terminal domain
description: This domain is found at the N-terminal end of Protein Hikeshi from humans and its orthologues OPI10 from other eukaryotes. Hikeshi is an specific nuclear import carrier for HSP70 proteins following heat-shock stress, which is required to protect cells from heat- shock damages. The N-terminal domain shows a jelly-roll/beta- sandwich fold with two layers of beta-sheets consisting of three and five and five antiparallel beta-strands [[cite:PUB00101203]].

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF776)
description: This family consists of several highly related mouse and human proteins of unknown function.

name: Borrelia burgdorferi protein of unknown function (DUF777)
description: This family consists of several hypothetical proteins of unknown function from Borrelia burgdorferi (Lyme disease spirochete).

name: RTE1-like
description: This entry, previously known as DUF778, represents RTE1 (REVERSION-TO-ETHYLENE SENSITIVITY1) from Arabidopsis thaliana. RTE1 is positive regulator of the ETR1 ethylene receptor, leading to negative regulation of ethylene responses.[[cite:PUB00092499],[cite:PUB00092500]]. This entry also includes Arabidopsis RTE1 homologue, RTH, which acts via RTE1 in regulating ethylene responses and signaling [[cite:PUB00092501]]. This domain is also present in TMEM222 from animals which in humans plays a role in brain development and function and mutations result in autosomal recessive neurodevelopmental disorder. This domain has been identified as structurally similar to peptidase C97 domain ([pfam:PF05903]).

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF779)
description: This family consists of several bacterial proteins of unknown function.

name: Caenorhabditis elegans protein of unknown function (DUF780)
description: This family consists of several short C. elegans proteins of unknown function.

name: Leg1
description: Protein liver-enriched gene 1 (Leg1) has been suggested to function as a novel secreted regulator for the liver development [[cite:PUB00074295]].

name: Circovirus ORF3
description: This family consists porcine circovirus ORF3 protein which plays a role in modulating host cell signalling by binding to and degrading host RGS16 [[cite:PUB00097772]]. This protein is not necessary for virus replication [[cite:PUB00097771]].

name: Tho complex subunit 7
description: The Tho complex is involved in transcription elongation and mRNA export from the nucleus.

name: Prolamin-like
description: Prolamin_like (in which DUF784 and DUF1278 have been merged) is found to be expressed in the plant embryo sac and to be regulated by the Myb98 transcription factor. Computational analysis has revealed that members are homologous to the plant prolamin superfamily (Protease inhibitor-seed storage-LTP family, [pfam:PF00234]) [[cite:PUB00057502]]. In contrast to typical prolamin members that have eight conserved Cys residues forming four pairs of disulfide bonds, this domain contains only six conserved Cys residues that may form three pairs of disulfide bonds. The domain may have a potential function in lipid transfer or protection during plant embryo sac development and reproduction [[cite:PUB00057503]].

name: Retropepsin-like aspartic endopeptidase RimB
description: This entry represents a domain found in retropepsin-like bacterial proteases such as RimB from Pseudomonas fluorescens and the related retropepsin-like osmotic stress tolerance peptidases (Rlo) from Pseudomonas aeruginosa [[cite:PUB00161732],[cite:PUB00161733]]. RimB is involved in rhizosphere colonisation and plant infection. It is a bifunctional retropepsin-like aspartic endopeptidase that uniquely recognises and removes glutamate residues from polyglutamated RpsF and stimulates poly-alpha-L-glutamate synthesis by RimK. While Rlo proteases are homologous to RimB, they contain N-terminal signal peptides and perform distinct biological functions. Mutants lacking all three secreted Rlo peptidases show defects in antibiotic resistance, biofilm formation, and cell morphology. Rlo peptidases have been structurally characterised, showing structural features characteristic of retroviral pepsins (PDB:9G59, PDB:9G58) [[cite:PUB00161733]]. Similar to RimB, RloA proteins cleave substrates that become polyglutamated post-translationally.

name: DUF787, N-terminal domain
description: This entry represents the N-terminal domain of a number of hypothetical proteins of unknown function from Borrelia burgdorferi (Lyme disease spirochete).

name: SRP-independent targeting protein 2/TMEM208
description: This family includes SRP-independent targeting protein 2 (SND2) from yeast and transmembrane protein 208 (TMEM208) from mammals. Both are localized to the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) [[cite:PUB00083911],[cite:PUB00083915]]. SND2 works together with SND1 and SND3 in an alternative targeting route to the ER [[cite:PUB00083911]]. TMEM208 regulates both ER stress and autophagy. It contains three predicted transmembrane regions [[cite:PUB00083915]]. SND2 also known as Env10 in Saccharomyces cerevisiae, and its homologue as Mug69 in Schizosaccharomyces pombe. They were identified as proteins involved in vacuolar processing and morphology [[cite:PUB00066964]] and meiosis [[cite:PUB00044889]], respectively.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF789)
description: This family consists of several plant proteins of unknown function.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF790)
description: This family consists of several hypothetical archaeal proteins of unknown function.

name: Sugar-tranasporters, 12 TM
description: MFS_5 is a family of sugar-transporters from both prokaryotes and eukaryotes.

name: Borrelia burgdorferi protein of unknown function (DUF792)
description: This family consists of several hypothetical proteins from the Lyme disease spirochete Borrelia burgdorferi.

name: Protein ROH1-like
description: This family consists of several plant proteins and includes RHO1, an interactor of the exocyst subunit Exo70A1 and has been shown to be required for seed coat mucilage deposition [[cite:PUB00093724]].

name: APO RNA-binding
description: This domain contains conserved cysteine and histidine residues [[cite:PUB00054221]]. It resembles zinc fingers, and binds to zinc [[cite:PUB00057416]]. This domain functions as an RNA-binding domain [[cite:PUB00057416]].

name: HIGH Nucleotidyl Transferase
description: This family consists of HIGH Nucleotidyl Transferases

name: Type VI secretion system effector, Hcp
description: HCP is a family of proteins which are expressed in up to 1000 copies in Gram-negative bacteria. Together these copies aggregate into a needle-like shaft or tube that will penetrate other bacteria via a puncturing protein attached to its head [[cite:PUB00075434]] being part of the type VI secretion system [[cite:PUB00155386],[cite:PUB00054686]]. Initially Hcp forms a hexameric structure with a central channel of 40 Angstroms. These hexamers pile up one on top of each other forming nanotubes resembling the gp19 tail phage tube [[cite:PUB00034462]].

name: Pup-like protein
description: This family consists of several short bacterial proteins formely known as (DUF797). It was recently shown that Mycobacterium tuberculosis contains a small protein, Pup (Rv2111c), that is covalently conjugated to the e-NH2 groups of lysines on several target proteins (pupylation) such as the malonyl CoA acyl carrier protein (FabD) [[cite:PUB00053383]]. Pupylation of FabD was shown to result in its recruitment to the mycobacterial proteasome and subsequent degradation analogous to eukaryotic ubiquitin-conjugated proteins. Searches recovered Pup orthologs in all major actinobacteria lineages including the basal bifidobacteria and also sporadically in certain other bacterial lineages. [[cite:PUB00053382]] The Pup proteins were all between 50-90 residues in length and a multiple alignment shows that they all contain a conserved motif with a G [EQ] signature at the C-terminus. Thus, all of them are suitable for conjugation via the terminal glutamate or the deamidated glutamine (as shown in the case of the Mycobacterium Pup [[cite:PUB00053382]]). The conserved globular core of Pup is predicted to form a bihelical unit with the extreme C-terminal 6-7 residues forming a tail in the extended conformation. Thus, Pup is structurally unrelated to the ubiquitin fold and has convergently evolved the function of protein modifier.

name: Na,K-Atpase Interacting protein
description: NKAIN (Na,K-Atpase INteracting) proteins are a family of evolutionary conserved transmembrane proteins that localise to neurons, that are critical for neuronal function, and that interact with the beta subunits, beta1 in vertebrates and beta in Drosophila, of Na,K-ATPase. NKAINs have highly conserved trans-membrane domains but otherwise no other characterised domains. NKAINs may function as subunits of pore or channel structures in neurons or they may affect the function of other membrane proteins. They are likely to function within the membrane bilayer [[cite:PUB00044756]].

name: Putative lipoprotein GNA1162-like
description: This family of putative lipoproteins mainly found in Proteobacteria includes GNA1162 from Neisseria meningitidis, which shows five alpha-helices and four beta-strands, three of them forming a beta-sheet [[cite:PUB00101016]].

name: Mitochondrial and peroxisomal fission factor Mff
description: This protein has a role in mitochondrial and peroxisomal fission [[cite:PUB00057504]].

name: Tandem-repeating region of mucin, epiglycanin-like
description: The unusual mucin, epiglycanin, is membrane-bound at the C-terminus but has a long region of this tandem-repeat at the N-terminus [[cite:PUB00066740]]. It was the first mucin identified to be associated with the malignant behaviour of carcinoma cells [[cite:PUB00066741]]. Mouse Muc21/epiglycanin is thought to be a highly glycosylated molecule, which makes it likely that its function is dependent on its glycoforms. Cells expressing Muc21 are significantly less adherent to each other and to extracellular matrix components than control cells, and this loss of adhesion is mediated by the TR portion of Muc21 [[cite:PUB00066742]]. This family also now contains the repeat that was the C. elegans protein of unknown function (DUF801).

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF802)
description: This region is found as two or more repeats in a small number of hypothetical proteins.

name: Magnesium transporter NIPA
description: NIPA (nonimprinted in Prader-Willi/Angelman syndrome) is a family of integral membrane proteins which function as magnesium transporters [[cite:PUB00057506],[cite:PUB00057507]].

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF805)
description: This family consists of several bacterial proteins of unknown function.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF806)
description: This family consists of several Siphovirus and Lactococcus proteins of unknown function. The viral sequences are thought to be tail component proteins.

name: Coxiella burnetii protein of unknown function (DUF807)
description: This family consists of several proteins of unknown function from Coxiella burnetii (the causative agent of a zoonotic disease called Q fever).

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF808)
description: This family consists of several bacterial proteins of unknown function.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF809)
description: This family consists of several proteins of unknown function Raphanus sativus (Radish) and Brassica napus (Rape).

name: CCDC22 protein coiled-coil region
description: Human coiled-coil domain-containing protein 22 (CCDC22) is involved in regulation of NF-kappa-B signalling; the function may involve association with COMMD8 and a CUL1-dependent E3 ubiquitin ligase complex [[cite:PUB00077065]]. It is part of the COMMD/CCDC22/CCDC93 (CCC) complex, which interacts with the multisubunit WASH complex required for endosomal deposition of F-actin and cargo trafficking in conjunction with the retromer [[cite:PUB00077066]]. This entry also includes CCDC22 homologues from animals and plants.

name: NFACT protein RNA binding domain
description: This domain occurs in proteins that have been annotated as Fibronectin/fibrinogen binding protein by similarity. This annotation comes from [swissprot:O34693] where the N-terminal region is involved in this activity [[cite:PUB00011315]]. It is an RNA binding domain of the NFACT (NEMF, FbpA, Caliban, and Tae2) proteins. This NFACT-R family is found in two eukaryotic gene contexts: fused to the NFACT-N and NFACT-C domains in the NFACT protein involved in the ribosomal quality control pathway which contributes to CAT-tailing and as a standalone domain [[cite:PUB00091027]]. Additionally this domain contains a conserved motif D/E-X-W/Y-X-H that may be functionally important.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF815)
description: This family consists of several bacterial proteins of unknown function.

name: Baculovirus protein of unknown function (DUF816)
description: This family includes proteins that are about 200 amino acids in length. The proteins are all from baculoviruses. This family includes ORF107 from Orgyia pseudotsugata multicapsid polyhedrosis virus (OpMNPV) and a variety of other numbered ORF proteins, such as ORF52 [swissprot:Q91F03], ORF140 [swissprot:Q9YMI8]. The function of these proteins is unknown.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF817)
description: This family consists of several bacterial proteins of unknown function.

name: Chlamydia CHLPS protein (DUF818)
description: This family consists of several Chlamydia CHLPS proteins, the function of which are unknown.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF819)
description: This family contains proteins of unknown function from archaeal, bacterial and plant species.

name: Putative restriction endonuclease
description: This entry includes a group of putative nuclease, including hypothetical protein TT1808 (also known as Uma2 or TTHA1514), an AT-rich DNA-binding protein from Thermus thermophilus. This domain has a 3-layer alpha/beta/alpha topology similar to that found in restriction endonucleases [[cite:PUB00035698]]. The nuclease domain is ubiquitously found in enzymes involved in metabolism of nucleic acids, mostly in nucleases with diverse biological functions [[cite:PUB00035699]].

name: Glycosyl transferase family 90
description: This family of glycosyl transferases are specifically (mannosyl) glucuronoxylomannan/galactoxylomannan -beta 1,2-xylosyltransferases, [ec:2.4.2.-].

name: BES1/BZR1 plant transcription factor, N-terminal
description: This family consists of the N terminal regions of several plant transcription factors. It is classified as BES1/BZR1, a plant-specific transcription factor that cooperates with transcription factors such as BIM1 to regulate brassinosteroid-induced genes [[cite:PUB00075707]].

name: Bacterial Immunoglobulin-like 21
description: This entry represents BIg21(Bacterial Immunoglobulin-like 21) found in InvasinE (InvE). Invasins are members of the inverse autotransporter (IAT) family also referred to as type Ve secretion system. In general, they consist of an N-terminal beta-barrel-like domain, which is responsible for attachment of invasin to the outer membrane region of bacteria, repetitive Immunoglobuli-like (Ig) domains, which vary significantly in number among all the invasins, and the C-terminal domain/adhesion domain (AD) [pfam:PF05689], which provides invasins with the specificity to bind to its host target molecules. The overall structure of InvE shows that it comprises of three domain architecture in which the domains BIg20 (Bacterial Immunoglobulin-like 20) and BIg21 adopt two layer beta-sandwich fold resembling eukaryotic members of Immunoglobulin-superfamily (IgSF), while the AD is a globular, alpha/beta-domain. The structure of BIg21 belongs to the I2 set of IgSF with a unique modification in the C-E interstrand loop, important for its interaction with AD. BIg21 and AD form a functional super-domain as well, necessary to target the host receptor [[cite:PUB00101290]].

name: Adhesion domain
description: This entry represents the Adhesion domain found in InvasinE (invE). Invasins are members of the inverse autotransporter (IAT) family also referred to as type Ve secretion system. In general, they consist of an N-terminal beta-barrel-like domain, which is responsible for attachment of invasin to the outer membrane region of bacteria, repetitive Immunoglobulin-like (Ig) domains, which vary significantly in number among all the invasins, and the C-terminal domain/adhesion domain (AD), which provides invasins with the specificity to bind to its host target molecules. InvE-AD adopts a C-type lectin-like domain (CTLD)fold with unique modifications. The core structure of the adhesion domain (AD) is made up of a globular alpha/beta fold and can be divided into three sub-sections. The first is a lasso-shaped loop structure termed the \u0022adaptor ring\u0022 since it forms a ring-shaped platform that connects BIg21 [pfam:PF05688] with the two residual sub-sections in the AD. These two residual subsections are the \u0022C-type lectin-like domain\u0022 and the \u0022wedge module\u0022. InvE-CTLD lacks the ability to coordinate Ca2+, and motifs such as EPN, QPD, and WND that are responsible for the specificity of carbohydrate recognition are also absent, giving rise to the notion that the InvE-CTLD is not a carbohydrate binding domain [[cite:PUB00101290]].

name: Ycf2 family
description: This entry, previously known as DUF825, represents Ycf2 protein from Arabidopsis thaliana and related plant proteins. Ycf2 is a component of the Ycf2-FtsHi complex which has been identified as chloroplast import motor. The Ycf2-FtsHi complex is composed of six distinct components. This heterohexameric assembly is organized in a counterclockwise order with components arranged as Ycf2, FtsHi5, FtsHi1, FtsHi2, FtsHi4, and FtsH12 [[cite:PUB00159880]]. A collaborative interplay between the Ycf2-FtsHi complex and the TIC (translocon at the inner chloroplast membrane) complex, contributes to the efficient translocation of preproteins into the chloroplasts [[cite:PUB00159880]].

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF826)
description: This family consists of several enterobacterial and siphoviral sequences of unknown function.

name: Weak chloroplast movement under blue light
description: WEMBL consists of several plant proteins required for the chloroplast avoidance response under high intensity blue light. This avoidance response consists in the relocation of chloroplasts on the anticlinal side of exposed cells. Acts in association with PMI2 to maintain the velocity of chloroplast photo-relocation movement via the regulation of cp-actin filaments [[cite:PUB00066738]]. Thus several member-sequences are described as \u0022myosin heavy chain-like\u0022.

name: Auxin canalisation
description: This domain is frequently found at the N-terminus of proteins containing [pfam:PF08458] at the C-terminus. It is a component of the auto-regulatory loop which enables auxin canalisation by recruitment of the PIN1 auxin efflux protein to the cell membrane [[cite:PUB00090780]].

name: Eukaryotic protein of unknown function (DUF829)
description: This family consists of several uncharacterised eukaryotic proteins.

name: Permuted papain-like amidase enzyme, YaeF/YiiX, C92 family
description: Amidase_YiiX is a family of permuted papain-like amidases. It has amidase specificity for the amide bond between a lipid and an amino acid (or peptide). From the structure, a tetramer, each monomer is made up of a layered alpha-beta fold with a central, 6-stranded, antiparallel beta-sheet that is protected by helices on either side. The catalytic Cys154 in UniProtKB:Q74NK7, PDB:3kw0, is located on the N-terminus of helix alphaF. The two additional helices located above Cys154 contribute to the formation of the active site, where the lysine ligand is bound [[cite:PUB00075488]].

name: Herpesvirus protein of unknown function (DUF832)
description: This family consists of several herpesvirus proteins of unknown function.

name: Transport and Golgi organisation 2
description: In eukaryotes this family is predicted to play a role in protein secretion and Golgi organisation [[cite:PUB00075420]]. In plants this family includes [swissprot:A9X6Y0], which is involved in water permeability in the cuticles of fruit [[cite:PUB00075421]]. [swissprot:P54797] has been found to be expressed during early embryogenesis in mice [[cite:PUB00011316]]. This protein contains a conserved NRDE motif. This gene has been characterised in Drosophila melanogaster and named as transport and Golgi organisation 2, hence the name Tango2.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF834)
description: This short presumed domain is found in a large number of hypothetical plant proteins. The domain is quite rich in conserved glycine residues. It occurs in some putative transposons but currently has no known function.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF835)
description: The members of this archaebacterial protein family are around 250-300 amino acid residues in length. The function of these proteins is not known.

name: Glutaredoxin-like domain (DUF836)
description: These proteins are related to the [pfam:PF00462] family. This entry includes several viral glutaredoxins and many related bacterial and eukaryotic proteins of unknown function. The best characterised member is G4L ([swissprot:P68460]) from Vaccinia virus (strain Western Reserve/WR) (VACV), which is necessary for virion morphogenesis and replication [[cite:PUB00020627]]. This is a cytoplasmic protein which functions as a shuttle in a redox pathway between membrane-associated E10R and L1R or F9L [[cite:PUB00020628]].

name: SIKE family
description: This family consists of several eukaryotic proteins. Suppressor of IKBKE 1 (SIKE) is a physiological suppressor of IKK-epsilon and TBK1, which are two IKK-related kinases involved in virus- and TLR3-triggered activation of interferon regulatory factor 3 (IRF-3). Other members of this family are circulating cathodic antigen (CCA), found in Schistosoma mansoni (Blood fluke) [[cite:PUB00011317],[cite:PUB00059263]], and FGFR1 oncogene partner 2, which may be involved in wound healing pathway [[cite:PUB00059262]].

name: Alkaline phosphatase PhoX
description: This family consists of proteins predominantly found in bacteria, including Alkaline phosphatase PhoX from Pseudomonas fluorescens ([swissprot:Q3K5N8]), a phosphomonoesterase with no phosphodiesterase activity. This protein adopts a six-bladed beta-propeller fold, with the active site located at the bottom of the cavity at the centre of the propeller [[cite:PUB00100675]].

name: Lagovirus minor capsid protein VP2
description: This entry includes minor capsid protein VP2 from Rabbit hemorrhagic disease virus and related lagoviruses. VP2 is minor structural protein that forms a portal-like structure at a unique three-fold axis of symmetry, following binding to the host receptor. The channel formed by VP2 may allow the delivery of the viral genome through the host endosomal membrane.

name: Eukaryotic protein of unknown function (DUF842)
description: This family consists of a number of conserved eukaryotic proteins of unknown function. The sequences carry three sets of CxxxC motifs, which might suggest a type of zinc-finger formation.

name: Orf76 (Ac76)
description: This family consists mainly of baculovirus proteins. Family members include Autographa californica multiple nucleopolyhedrovirus (AcMNPV), protein AC76. Ac76 has been shown to be involved in intranuclear microvesicle formation.
