description: This family consists of several hypothetical bacterial and phage proteins of around 100 residues in length. Members of this family seem to be found exclusively in Lactococcus lactis and the bacteriophages that infect this species. The function of this family is unknown.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1360)
description: This family consists of several bacterial proteins of around 115 residues in length. Members of this family are found in Bacillus species and Streptomyces coelicolor, the function of the family is unknown.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1361)
description: This family consists of several hypothetical bacterial proteins of around 200 residues in length. The function of this family is unknown although some members are annotated as being putative integral membrane proteins.

name: Anabaena sensory rhodopsin transducer
description: The family of bacterial Anabaena sensory rhodopsin transducers are likely to bind sugars or related metabolites. The entire protein is comprised of a single globular domain with an eight-stranded beta-sandwich fold. There are a few characteristics which define this beta-sandwich fold as being distinct from other so-named folds, and these are: 1) a well conserved tryptophan, usually following a polar residue, present at the start of the first strand; this tryptophan appears to be central to a hydrophobic interaction required to hold the two beta-sheets of the sandwich together, and 2) a nearly absolutely conserved asparagine located at the end of the second beta-strand, that hydrogen bonds with the backbone carbonyls of the residues 2 and 4 positions downstream from it, thereby stabilising the characteristic tight turn between strands 2 and 3 of the structure.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1363)
description: This family consists of several Trypanosoma brucei putative variant specific antigen proteins of around 80 residues in length.

name: Putative nuclease YbcO
description: This family includes YbcO (pdbe:3G27), a putative nuclease from E. coli [[cite:PUB00097596]]. Proteins in the entry have been predicted to have the His-Me finger nuclease domain and may act as a Recombinase that participates in DNA repair and replication [[cite:PUB00097591]].

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1365)
description: This family consists of several bacterial and plant proteins of around 250 residues in length. The function of this family is unknown.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1366)
description: This family consists of several hypothetical Streptococcus thermophilus bacteriophage proteins of around 130 residues in length. One of the sequences in this family, from phage Sfi11 ([swissprot:O80186]) is known as Gp149. The function of this family is unknown.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1367)
description: This family consists of several highly conserved, hypothetical phage proteins of around 200 residues in length. The function of this family is unknown. Some proteins are annotated as IrsA (intracellular response to stress).

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF1368)
description: This entry represents a domain found in several proteins that seem to be specific to red algae plasmids.

name: Transmembrane protein 126
description: This entry includes the transmembrane protein 126 A/B (TMEM126A/B) from animals. Human TMEM126B participates in constructing the membrane arm of mitochondrial respiratory complex I [[cite:PUB00077052]].

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1372)
description: This family consists of several Streptococcus bacteriophage sequences and related proteins from Streptococcus species. Members of this family are typically around 100 residues in length and their function is unknown.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1373)
description: This family consists of several hypothetical proteins which seem to be specific to Oryzias latipes (Japanese ricefish). Members of this family are typically around 200 residues in length. The function of this family is unknown.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1374)
description: This family consists of several hypothetical Sulfolobus virus proteins of around 100 residues in length. The function of this family is unknown.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1375)
description: This family consists of several hypothetical, putative lipoproteins of around 80 residues in length. Members of this family seem to be specific to the Class Gammaproteobacteria. The function of this family is unknown.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1376)
description: This family consists of several hypothetical bacterial proteins of around 95 residues in length. The function of this family is unknown.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1378)
description: This family consists of hypothetical bacterial and phage proteins of around 59 residues in length. Bacterial members of this family seem to be specific to Enterobacteria. The function of this family is unknown. Structural modelling suggests this domain may bind nucleic acids [[cite:PUB00070793]].

name: Cell-division protein ZapC, C-terminal
description: ZapC is one of four FtsZ-binding components of the Z ring in bacteria. Formation of the Z ring on the cytoplasmic surface of the membrane is the starting process for assembly of the cell-division apparatus. It binds directly to the Z ring, and although it is not essential for absolute cell division it contributes to it by enhancing the interactions between the FtsZ protofilaments (or polymers) which aggregate to form the ring conformation in the Z ring [[cite:PUB00060666]]. This is the C-terminal domain which contains a pocket with a hydrophobic centre surrounded by conserved basic residues, critical for FtsZ binding [[cite:PUB00101038],[cite:PUB00101039]].

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1380)
description: This family consists of several hypothetical bacterial proteins of around 140 residues in length. Members of this family seem to be specific to Enterobacteria. The function of this family is unknown.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1381)
description: This family consists of several hypothetical Staphylococcus aureus and Staphylococcus aureus bacteriophage proteins of around 65 residues in length. The function of this family is unknown.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1382)
description: This family consists of several hypothetical Escherichia coli and bacteriophage lambda-like proteins of around 60 residues in length. The function of this family is unknown. Structural modelling suggests this domain may bind nucleic acids [[cite:PUB00070793]].

name: Autographa californica nuclear polyhedrosis virus (AcMNPV), Orf18
description: This family is represented by Autographa californica nuclear polyhedrosis virus (AcMNPV), Orf18 (ac18) [[cite:PUB00082301]]; it is a family of uncharacterised viral proteins.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1385)
description: This family contains a number of hypothetical bacterial proteins of unknown function approximately 300 residues in length. Some family members are predicted to be metal-dependent.

name: Baculovirus protein AC11
description: This family of baculovirus proteins is represented by Autographa californica nuclear polyhedrosis virus (AcMNPV) protein AC11 (Orf11). ac11 is an early gene essential for budded-virus production and occlusion-derived-virus envelopment [[cite:PUB00082613]].

name: Spermatogenesis-associated serine-rich protein 2-like
description: This family includes spermatogenesis-associated serine-rich protein 2 (SPATS2) and SPATS2-like proteins from mammals. SPATS2 is involved in spermatogenesis and likely to be a cytoplasmic RNA-binding protein [[cite:PUB00101497],[cite:PUB00101498]]. SPATS2 is highly expressed in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) and may function as an oncogene. It constitutes a novel diagnostic prognostic marker in liver cancer and a potential therapeutic target for the treatment of HCC [[cite:PUB00101499]].

name: Repeat of unknown function (DUF1388)
description: This family consists of several repeats of around 29 residues in length. Members of this family are found in the variable surface lipoproteins in Mycoplasma bovis and in mammalian neurofilament triplet H (NefH or NF-H) proteins. This repeat contains several Lys-Ser-Pro (KSP) motifs and in NefH these are thought to function as the main target for neurofilament directed protein kinases in vivo [[cite:PUB00013013]].

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1389)
description: This family consists of several hypothetical bacterial proteins which seem to be specific to Chlamydia pneumoniae. Members of this family are typically around 400 residues in length. The function of this family is unknown.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1390)
description: This family consists of several Paramecium bursaria chlorella virus 1 (PBCV-1) proteins of around 250 residues in length. The function of this family is unknown.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1391)
description: This family consists of several Enterobacterial proteins of around 50 residues in length. Members of this family are found in Escherichia coli and Salmonella typhi where they are often known as YdfA. The function of this family is unknown.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1392)
description: This family consists of several hypothetical cyanobacterial proteins of around 150 residues in length which seem to be specific to Anabaena species. The function of this family is unknown.

name: ECF-type riboflavin transporter, S component
description: This family is the substrate-binding component (S component) of the energy coupling-factor (ECF)-type riboflavin transporter. It is a transmembrane protein which binds riboflavin, and is responsible for riboflavin-uptake by cells [[cite:PUB00109144],[cite:PUB00057921]].

name: CYRIA/CYRIB Rac1 binding domain
description: This domain has been annotated as Rac1-binding domain [[cite:PUB00093956],[cite:PUB00093955]]. It can be found in human CYRIA/CYRIB and at the N terminus of CYFIP1/2 [[cite:PUB00093957]]. CYFIP proteins are known RAC1 effectors that stimulate actin polymerization [[cite:PUB00093957]]. In mice, CYRIB (also known as CYRI or FAM49B) negatively regulates RAC1-driven cytoskeletal remodelling and plays a role in restricting infection mediated by Mycobacterium tuberculosis and Listeria monocytogenes [[cite:PUB00093957]].

name: Spindle and kinetochore-associated protein 1
description: Spindle and kinetochore-associated protein 1 (SKA1) is a component of the SKA1 complex (consists of Ska1, Ska2, and Ska3/Rama1), a microtubule-binding subcomplex of the outer kinetochore that is essential for proper chromosome segregation [[cite:PUB00061771]]. It is required for timely anaphase onset during mitosis, when chromosomes undergo bipolar attachment on spindle microtubules leading to silencing of the spindle checkpoint [[cite:PUB00061805]].

name: LppX_LprAFG lipoprotein
description: This entry consists of several lipoproteins mainly from Mycobacterium species, collectively known as the LppX_ LprAFG family. Proteins in this entry include LprG, LppX, LprF and lprA [[cite:PUB00020730],[cite:PUB00020731],[cite:PUB00020732],[cite:PUB00039808],[cite:PUB00020734],[cite:PUB00076900]].

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1397)
description: This family consists of several insect specific proteins. [swissprot:Q25513] is annotated as being a haemolymph glycoprotein precursor. The function of this family is unknown [[cite:PUB00013024]].

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1398)
description: This family consists of several hypothetical Enterobacterial proteins of around 130 residues in length. Members of this family seem to be found exclusively in Escherichia coli and Salmonella species. The function of this family is unknown.

name: Glycine-rich domain-containing protein-like
description: This entry includes Arabidopsis Glycine-rich domain- containing protein 1 and 2 (GRDP1/2). They are involved in development and stress responses [[cite:PUB00077560]].

name: Alpha/beta hydrolase of unknown function (DUF1400)
description: This family contains a number of hypothetical proteins of unknown function that seem to be specific to cyanobacteria. Members of this family have an alpha/beta hydrolase fold.

name: CaiF/GrlA transcriptional regulator
description: This is a family of transcriptional regulators. CaiF is involved in carnitine metabolism [[cite:PUB00077941]]. GrlA is encoded within the LEE type III secretion system in the enteropathogenic E. coli O157:H [[cite:PUB00076312]]. GrlR interacts with GrlA at its Helix-Turn-Helix (HTH) motif, preventing GrlA from binding to its target promoter DNA.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1402)
description: This family consists of several hypothetical bacterial proteins of around 310 residues in length. Members of this family seem to be found exclusively in Agrobacterium, Rhizobium and Brucella species. The function of this family is unknown.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1403)
description: This family consists of several hypothetical bacterial proteins of around 320 residues in length. Members of this family are mainly found in Rhizobium and Agrobacterium species. The function of this family is unknown.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1404)
description: This family consists of several archaeal proteins of around 180 residues in length. Members of this family seem to be found exclusively in Sulfolobus tokodaii and Sulfolobus solfataricus. The function of this family is unknown.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1405)
description: This family consists of several bacterial and related archaeal protein of around 180 residues in length. The function of this family is unknown.

name: Tumour necrosis factor receptor, SECRET domain
description: This domain, named as the SECRET domain, is found at the C-terminal end of Tumour necrosis factor receptor (CrmD) from the orthopoxvirus Ectromelia virus. This domain binds a subset of human and mouse CC, CXC and C chemokines. It is thought to be responsible for the anti-chemokine activity of CrmD. The SECRET domain monomer adopts a beta-sandwich fold, consisting of two parallel beta-sheets with five and six anti-parallel strands, and the connecting loops [[cite:PUB00151577]]. This domain is also found in other uncharacterised sequences from poxvirus, including Protein OPG192 and Protein C8 from Vaccinia virus.

name: Double zinc ribbon
description: This family consists of several short, hypothetical bacterial proteins of around 70 residues in length. Members of this family have 8 highly conserved cysteine residues, which form two zinc beta-ribbon domains.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1408)
description: This family consists of several hypothetical Lactococcus lactis and related phage proteins of around 75 residues in length. The function of this family is unknown.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1409)
description: This family represents a short conserved region (approximately 50 residues long), sometimes repeated, within a number of hypothetical Oryza sativa proteins of unknown function.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1410)
description: This family represents a conserved domain approximately 100 residues long, multiple copies of which are found within hypothetical Ureaplasma parvum proteins of unknown function, as well as related species.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1411)
description: This entry represents a domain approximately 150 residues long that is sometimes repeated within some Babesia bovis proteins of unknown function.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1412)
description: This family consists of several Caenorhabditis elegans proteins of around 70-75 residues in length. The function of this family is unknown.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF1413)
description: This family consists of several hypothetical bacterial proteins which seem to be specific to firmicute species. Members of this family are typically around 100 residues in length. The function of this family is unknown.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1414)
description: This family consists of several hypothetical bacterial proteins of around 70 residues in length. Members of this family are often referred to as YejL. The function of this family is unknown.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1415)
description: This family consists of several hypothetical bacterial proteins of around 180 residues in length. The function of this family is unknown.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1416)
description: This family consists of several hypothetical bacterial proteins of around 100 residues in length. Members of this family appear to be Actinomycete specific. The function of this family is unknown.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1418)
description: This family consists of several hypothetical Enterobacterial proteins of around 100 residues in length. Members of this family are often described as YbjC. In E. coli the ybjC gene is located downstream of nfsA (which encodes the major oxygen-insensitive nitroreductase). It is thought that nfsA and ybjC form an operon an its promoter is a class I SoxS-dependent promoter [[cite:PUB00013045]]. The function of this family is unknown.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1419)
description: This family consists of several bacterial proteins of around 110 residues in length. Members of this family seem to be specific to Agrobacterium species and to Rhizobium loti. The function of this family is unknown.

name: DUF1420 N-terminal domain
description: This entry consists of several hypothetical putative lipoproteins which seem to be found specifically in the bacterium Leptospira interrogans. This entry represents the N-terminal domain which may adopt a GT-C-like fold.

name: UBA-like domain (DUF1421)
description: This domain represents a conserved region that has a UBA like fold. It is found in a number of plant proteins of unknown function.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1422)
description: This family consists of several hypothetical bacterial proteins of around 120 residues in length. The function of this family is unknown.

name: PHD - plant homeodomain finger protein
description: PHD_oberon is a plant homeodomain finger domain of Oberon proteins from plants. Oberon is necessary for maintenance and/or establishment of both the shoot and root apical meristems in Arabidopsis. Oberon proteins are made up of a PHD finger domain and a coiled-coil domain. The PHD-finger domain is found in a wide variety of proteins involved in the regulation of chromatin structure [[cite:PUB00067922]]. Oberon proteins mediate the TMO7 (the direct target of MP) expression through modification of, or binding to, chromatin at the TMO7 locus. TMO7 stands for the target of Monopteros 7 (MP) (or Auxin response factor 7) [[cite:PUB00076514]].

name: Putative rep protein (DUF1424)
description: This family consists of several archaeal proteins of around 320 residues in length. Members of this family seem to be found exclusively in Halobacterium and Haloferax species. The function of this family is unknown. This protein is probably a rep protein due to conservation of functional motifs.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1425)
description: This family consists of uncharacterised bacterial proteins mainly found in Proteobacteria, including YcfL from Escherichia coli and Putative lipoprotein from Campylobacter jejuni. This protein adopts a single domain configuration with two beta-sheets formed respectively by three and four beta-strands (beta-sandwich) and contains a Greek key motif, representing a singular variant of the Ig-like fold. Many proteins of this group have a lipid attachment site at the N-terminal of this domain, which together with the structure solved, suggests a role in bacterial lipoproteins [[cite:PUB00100676]].

name: Movement and RNA silencing protein
description: This family consists of several Babuvirus proteins of around 120 residues in length. Proteins in this family include movement and RNA silencing protein (also known as MP) from Banana bunchy top virus. MP acts as a suppressor of RNA-mediated gene silencing, also known as post-transcriptional gene silencing (PTGS), a mechanism of plant viral defense that limits the accumulation of viral RNAs. It transports viral genome to neighbouring plant cells directly through plasmosdesmata, without any budding. The movement protein allows efficient cell to cell propagation, by bypassing the host cell wall barrier [[cite:PUB00070087]].

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1427)
description: This family consists of several bacterial proteins of around 100 residues in length. The function of this family is unknown.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1428)
description: This family consists of several hypothetical bacterial and one archaeal sequence of around 120 residues in length. The function of this family is unknown. The structure of this family shows it to be part of the Dimeric-alpha-beta-barrel superfamily. Many members are annotated as being RNA signal recognition particle 4.5S RNA, but this could not be verified.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1430)
description: This family represents the C-terminus (approximately 120 residues) of a number of hypothetical bacterial proteins of unknown function. These are possibly membrane proteins involved in immunity.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1431)
description: This family contains a number of Drosophila melanogaster proteins of unknown function. These contain several conserved cysteine residues.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1433)
description: This family contains a number of hypothetical bacterial proteins of unknown function approximately 100 residues in length.

name: Membrane-bound toxin component of toxin-antitoxin system
description: CptA is a family of bacterial proteins named for the member of this family, YGFX_ECOLI, Swissprot:Q46824. YgfX was previously thought to be the toxic part of a toxin-antitoxin module [[cite:PUB00075551]] along with the antitoxin, [pfam:PF03937] Sdh5. However, studies have shown that, YgfX interferes with correct cell division and morphology. Furthermore, the function of YgfX-SdhE as a TA system could not be demonstrated in either E. coli or Serratia sp. ATCC 39006. YgfX is predicted to have a short N-terminal cytoplasmic domain followed by two transmembrane helices (TMHs) separated by a short periplasmic loop and finally, a larger C-terminal cytoplasmic domain. The TMHs of YgfX are required for activity, but the sequence of the cytoplasmic 13 N-terminal amino acids is not essential. Furthermore, the amino acids W34 and D117 are not required for localization but are necessary for YgfX multimerization, interaction with SdhE, and YgfX activity. It is proposed that the formation of YgfX multimeric membrane-bound proteins are required to enable the interaction with the cytoplasmic SDH assembly factor SdhE [[cite:PUB00083888]]. Another study has demonstrated that sdhEygfX (bicistronic operon) affects pig biosynthesis, directly or indirectly, at the level of transcription of the biosynthetic operon (pigA-O) [[cite:PUB00066693]]. It has also been suggested that, in addition to indirect transcriptional activation of pigA-O, YgfX might facilitate the formation of a terminal pig biosynthetic complex consisting of PigB and PigC [[cite:PUB00083888]].

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1435)
description: This family consists of several hypothetical Enterobacterial proteins of around 80 residues in length. The function of this family is unknown.

name: CDI immunity protein
description: CdiI immunity proteins function as part of the bacterial contact-dependent growth inhibition (CDI) system. CDI is mediated by the CdiB-CdiA two-partner secretion system. Each CdiA protein exhibits a distinct growth inhibition activity, which resides in the polymorphic C-terminal region (CdiA-CT). Cells with the CDI sytem also express a CdiI immunity protein that blocks the activity of cognate CdiA-CT, thereby protecting the cell from autoinhibition. In many CDI systems the cdiBAI genes are followed by orphan cdiA-CT/cdiI modules, suggesting that these modules are exchanged between the CDI systems of different bacteria [[cite:PUB00074283]].

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1438)
description: This family consists of several hypothetical proteins of around 170 residues in length which appear to be mouse specific. The function of this family is unknown.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1439)
description: This family consists of several hypothetical bacterial proteins of around 190 residues in length. Several members of this family are annotated as being putative lipoproteins and are often known as YceB. The function of this family is unknown.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1440)
description: This family contains a number of bacterial proteins of unknown function approximately 180 residues long. These are possibly integral membrane proteins.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1441)
description: This family consists of several hypothetical Enterobacterial proteins of around 160 residues in length. The function of this family is unknown. However, it appears to be distantly related to other HTH families so may act as a transcriptional regulator.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1442)
description: This family consists of several hypothetical Arabidopsis thaliana proteins of around 225 residues in length. The function of this family is unknown.

name: Per os infectivity factor AC110
description: This family consists of several Baculovirus proteins of around 55 residues in length. Family members include Autographa californica nuclear polyhedrosis virus (AcMNPV) Per os infectivity factor AC110, which is required for oral infectivity. It may play a role after occlusion-derived virions pass through the host's peritrophic membrane [[cite:PUB00082597]].

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1444)
description: This family contains several hypothetical bacterial proteins of unknown function that are approximately 250 residues long.

name: D-glutamate cyclase
description: This family includes mitochondrial D-glutamate cyclase which converts D-glutamate to 5-oxo-D-proline [[cite:PUB00086027]]. This family also includes numerous uncharacterised proteins from bacteria.

name: Acyclic terpene utilisation family protein AtuA
description: This family consists of several bacterial and plant proteins of around 400 residues in length. One member of this family has been characterised in Pseudomonas citronellolis as AtuA, a member of a gene cluster that is essential for the acyclic terpene utilisation (Atu) pathway [[cite:PUB00081891]].

name: RNA polymerase epsilon subunit
description: RNA polymerase in bacteria is a multisubunit protein complex that is essential for gene expression. This entry represents the epsilon subunit encoded by the rpoY gene. The structure of epsilon shows simple beta sheet with an alpha helix running diagonally along the back of the structure forming a beta-beta-alpha-beta fold [[cite:PUB00095126]].

name: Bardet-Biedl syndrome 5 protein N-terminal PH-like domain
description: BBS5 is part of the BBSome complex that may function as a coat complex required for sorting of specific membrane proteins to the primary cilia [[cite:PUB00060532]]. Mutations in the BBS5 gene cause Bardet-Biedl syndrome 5 [[cite:PUB00073459],[cite:PUB00073460]]. This entry represents the N-terminal PH-like domain.

name: Inner membrane protein YqiJ, OB-fold
description: This entry represents the OB-fold domain found in several bacterial proteins, including the inner membrane protein YqiJ from E. coli, whose function is not clear.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1450)
description: This family consists of several hypothetical bacterial proteins of around 80 residues in length. Members of this family contain four highly conserved cysteine residues. The function of this family is unknown.

name: Zinc-ribbon containing domain
description: This family consists of several hypothetical bacterial proteins of around 160 residues in length. Members of this family contain four highly conserved cysteine resides toward the C-terminal region of the protein.

name: CcdC protein
description: This family includes protein CcdC from Bacillus subtilis. The function of Ccdc is not known.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1454)
description: This family consists of several Enterobacterial sequences of around 200 residues in length which are often known as YiiQ proteins. The function of this family is unknown.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1455)
description: This family consists of several hypothetical putative outer membrane proteins which appear to be specific to Anaplasma marginale and Anaplasma ovis.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1456)
description: This family consists of several hypothetical bacterial proteins of around 150 residues in length. The function of this family is unknown.

name: PAS domain
description: This family contains a number of hypothetical bacterial proteins of unknown function approximately 200 residues long. This region is is distantly similar to other PAS domains.

name: Dodecin
description: Dodecin is a flavin-binding protein [[cite:PUB00057445]],found in several bacteria and few archaea and represents a stand-alone version of the SHS2 domain [[cite:PUB00027394]]. It most closely resembles the SHS2 domains of FtsA and Rpb7p, and represents a single domain small-molecule binding form[[cite:PUB00057445]].

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1459)
description: This family consists of several hypothetical Caenorhabditis elegans proteins of around 85 residues in length. The function of this family is unknown.

name: N-acetylmuramoyl-L-alanine amidase-like
description: This family includes N-acetylmuramoyl-L-alanine amidase (AMA) from Bacteroides uniformis and similar bacterial proteins. AmiA hydrolyses GlcNAc-1,6-anhydro-MurNAc-peptide into disaccharide and stem peptide. It shows an alpha/beta/alpha three-layered sandwich fold with a catalytic core that consists of a central five-stranded beta-sheet and four alpha-helices. It is structurally related to NlpC/P60 gamma- D-Glu-meso-diaminopimelic acid amidases [[cite:PUB00100890]].

name: Lipoprotein intramolecular transacylase Lit
description: This entry represents the lipoprotein intramolecular transacylase, Lit [[cite:PUB00158976],[cite:PUB00158977]]. Lit creates a lipoprotein that is less immunogenic, possibly enabling the bacteria to gain a foothold in the host by stealth. The crystal structure of the Lit enzyme from Bacillus cereus ([swissprot:Q813T3]) revealed that it consists of consists of four transmembrane helices with an extracellular cap [[cite:PUB00158977]]. The conserved residues map to the cap-membrane interface and they include two catalytic histidines that function to effect unimolecular transacylation. The reaction involves acyl transfer from the sn-2 position of the glyceryl moiety to the amino group on the N-terminal cysteine of the substrate via an 8-membered ring intermediate.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1462)
description: This family consists of several hypothetical bacterial proteins of around 100 residues in length. The function of this family is unknown.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF1463)
description: This family consists of several hypothetical bacterial proteins of around 140 residues in length. Members of this family seem to be found exclusively in Borrelia burgdorferi (Lyme disease spirochete). The function of this family is unknown.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1464)
description: This family consists of several hypothetical archaeal proteins of around 350 residues in length. The function of this family is unknown.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1465)
description: This family consists of several hypothetical bacterial proteins of around 180 residues in length. The function of this family is unknown.

name: Regulator of chromosome segregation 1
description: This family consists of several mammalian proteins of around 240 residues in length. Family members include regulator of chromosome segregation 1 (RCS1), also known as FAM64A, CATS or PIMREG (PICALM-interacting mitotic regulator). It is a substrate of APC/C. It may control the metaphase to anaphase transition [[cite:PUB00084339]]. It is also a substrate of the Kinase Interacting Stathmin (KIS). RCS1 is highly expressed in cancer cell lines in a cell cycle dependent manner and is induced by mitogens [[cite:PUB00084340]].

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1467)
description: This family consists of several bacterial proteins of around 90 residues in length. The function of this family is unknown.

name: Tripartite tricarboxylate transporter TctB family
description: This family consists of several hypothetical bacterial proteins of around 150 residues in length. This family was formerly known as DUF1468.

name: Putative Actinobacterial Holin-X, holin superfamily III
description: Phage_holin_3_6 is a family of small hydrophobic proteins with two or three transmembrane domains of the Hol-X family. Holin proteins are produced by double-stranded DNA bacteriophages that use an endolysin-holin strategy to achieve lysis of their hosts. The endolysins are peptidoglycan-degrading enzymes that are usually accumulated in the cytosol until access to the cell wall substrate is provided by the holin membrane lesion.

name: Putative stress-induced transcription regulator
description: The structure of one member of the ABATE domain family consists of a two-domain organisation, with the N-terminal domain presenting a new fold called the ABATE domain that may bind an as yet unknown ligand. The C-terminal domain forms a treble-clef zinc-finger that is likely to be involved in DNA binding. suggests a role as stress-induced transcriptional regulator. Further computational analyses sugeests a role as a stress-induced transcriptional regulator [[cite:PUB00054176]]. Members of this family are found in Streptomyces, Rhizobium, Ralstonia, Agrobacterium and Bradyrhizobium species.

name: YdgH/BhsA/McbA-like domain
description: This domain is found in several Enterobacterial proteins of around 90 residues in length, including E. coli YdgH, YhcN, BhsA and McbA, which play a role in stress response, biofilm formation and pathogenesis [[cite:PUB00097758],[cite:PUB00097759]]. BhsA (also known as ComC) reduces the permeability of the outer membrane to copper and may decrease biofilm formation by repressing cell-cell interaction and cell surface interaction [[cite:PUB00097760]]. Members of this entry have one copy of this domain with the exception of YdgH, which has three copies. The function of this domain is unknown, however, it is suggested to be directly involved in host-pathogen interaction [[cite:PUB00097759]].

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1473)
description: This family consists of several hypothetical bacterial proteins of around 150 residues in length. Members of this family seem to be found exclusively in Borrelia burgdorferi (Lyme disease spirochete). The function of this family is unknown.

name: TscT toxin protein
description: This family consists of several bacterial proteins of around 100 residues in length. Members of this family seem to be found exclusively in Staphylococcus aureus. This family includes the TscT protein [[cite:PUB00159162]] which is part of the TscT/TscA toxin-antitoxin system.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1475)
description: This family consists of several hypothetical plant proteins of around 250 residues in length. Members of this family seem to be found exclusively in Arabidopsis thaliana. The function of this family is unknown.

name: ATPase inhibitor subunit zeta
description: This entry represents zeta-subunits, which are found in alpha-proteobacterial F1F0-ATPase regulatory proteins. The zeta subunit is a potent inhibitor of the alpha-proteobacterial F1FO-ATPase. The inhibitory region resides in the first 14 N-terminal residues of the protein, which protrude from the 4-alpha-helix bundle structure of the isolated zeta subunit [[cite:PUB00091055],[cite:PUB00091056],[cite:PUB00091057]].

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1477)
description: This family consists of several hypothetical Nucleopolyhedrovirus proteins of around 100 resides in length. The function of this family is unknown.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1478)
description: This family consists of several hypothetical Sapovirus proteins of around 165 residues in length. The function of this family is unknown.

name: Gig2-like
description: This family includes Gig2 from Candida albicans, YbiU from Escherichia coli and uncharacterised proteins predominantly found in fungi and bacteria. Gig2 is a putative oxidoreductase thought to play a role in the undefined GlcNAc metabolic network. It folds into a single large domain with a cupin like double stranded beta-helix core surrounded by 20 alpha-helices. This protein shows similarity with 2- oxoglutarate dependent Fe containing oxygenases [[cite:PUB00100975]].

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1480)
description: This family consists of several hypothetical Enterobacterial proteins of around 80 residues in length. The function of this family is unknown.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1481)
description: This family consists of several hypothetical bacterial proteins of around 230 residues in length. Members of this family are often referred to as YjaH and are found in the Orders Vibrionales and Enterobacteriales. The function of this family is unknown.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1482)
description: This family consists of several Enterobacterial proteins of around 60 residues in length. The function of this family is unknown.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1484)
description: This family consists of several hypothetical bacterial proteins of around 110 residues in length. Members of this family appear to be found exclusively in Ralstonia solanacearum. The function of this family is unknown.

name: Metallopeptidase family M81
description: This is a family of proteobacterial metallo-peptidases.

name: SnoaL-like polyketide cyclase
description: This family includes SnoaL [[cite:PUB00021066]] a polyketide cyclase involved in nogalamycin biosynthesis. This family was formerly known as DUF1486. The proteins in this family adopt a distorted alpha-beta barrel fold [[cite:PUB00021066]]. Structural data together with site-directed mutagenesis experiments have shown that SnoaL has a different mechanism to that of the classical aldolase for catalysing intramolecular aldol condensation [[cite:PUB00021066]].

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1487)
description: This family consists of several uncharacterised proteins from Drosophila melanogaster. The function of this family is unknown.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1488)
description: This family consists of several hypothetical bacterial proteins of around 85 residues in length. The function of this family is unknown.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1489)
description: This family consists of several hypothetical bacterial proteins of around 150 residues in length. Members of this family seem to be founds exclusively in the Class Alphaproteobacteria. The function of this family is unknown.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1490)
description: This family consists of several hypothetical bacterial proteins of around 90 residues in length. Members of the family seem to be found exclusively in Mycobacterium species. The function of this family is unknown.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1491)
description: This family consists of several bacterial proteins of around 115 residues in length. Members of this family seem to be found exclusively in the Class Alphaproteobacteria. The function of this family is unknown.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1492)
description: This family consists of several hypothetical, highly conserved Streptococcal and related phage proteins of around 100 residues in length. The function of this family is unknown. It appears to be distantly related to [pfam:PF08281].

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1493)
description: This family consists of several bacterial proteins of around 115 residues in length. Members of this family seem to be found exclusively in Salmonella and Yersinia species and several have been described as being putative cytoplasmic proteins. The function of this family is unknown.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1494)
description: This family consists of several bacterial proteins of around 175 residues in length. Members of this family seem to be found exclusively in Chlamydia species. The function of this family is unknown.

name: EarA-like
description: This family includes EarA from Methanococcus maripaludis (MMP1718, [swissprot:Q6LWJ1]) and similar sequences from archaea. EarA is a transcriptional activator that directly regulates the fla operon, which contains genes involved in archaella formation [[cite:PUB00158985],[cite:PUB00158986]]. Proteins in this family possess a winged helix DNA -binding domain.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1496)
description: This family consists of several bacterial proteins of around 90 residues in length. Members of this family seem to be found exclusively in the Orders Vibrionales and Enterobacteriales. The function of this family is unknown.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1497)
description: This family consists of several phage and bacterial proteins of around 59 residues in length. Members of this family seem to be found exclusively in Lactococcus lactis and the bacteriophages that infect this organism. The function of this family is unknown.

name: D-lyxose isomerase
description: Members of this family of sugar isomerases belong to the cupin superfamily and consist of group I and II of D-lyxose isomerases [[cite:PUB00103833]]. The enzyme from Cohnella laevoribosii has been shown to be specific for D-lyxose, L-ribose, and D-mannose [[cite:PUB00075374]]. E. coli sugar isomerase (EcSI) shows a preference for D-lyxose and D-mannose [[cite:PUB00055252]] and its active site is highly similar to YdaE from the sigma B regulon of Bacillus subtilis [[cite:PUB00103833]].

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1499)
description: This family consists of several hypothetical bacterial and plant proteins of around 125 residues in length. The function of this family is unknown.

name: Vaccinia B6 protein
description: This family consists of several Orthopoxvirus specific proteins, which include Vaccinia virus, B6 protein, of around 170 residues in length. The function of this family is unknown.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1501)
description: This family contains a number of hypothetical bacterial proteins of unknown function approximately 400 residues long.

name: Repeat of unknown function (DUF1502)
description: This family consists of a number of repeats of around 34 residues in length. Members of this family seem to be found exclusively in three hypothetical Murid herpesvirus 4 proteins. The function of this family is unknown.

name: Putative Na+/H+ antiporter
description: This family consists of several hypothetical bacterial proteins of around 440 residues in length. The function of this family is unknown. Many members carry 11 or 12 transmembrane regions, suggesting that they might be transporters. One family member, UniProtKB:Q821X2 is classified by TCDB as being an NhaE type of Na+/H+ antiporter.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1505)
description: This family consists of several uncharacterised Caenorhabditis elegans proteins of around 115 resides in length. Members of this family contain 6 highly conserved cysteine residues. The function of this family is unknown.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF1506)
description: This family consists of several bacterial proteins of around 130 residues in length. Members of this family seem to be specific to Borrelia burgdorferi (Lyme disease spirochete). The function of this family is unknown.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1507)
description: This family consists of several hypothetical bacterial proteins of around 90 residues in length. The function of this family is unknown.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF1508)
description: This family represents a series of bacterial domains of unknown function of around 50 residues in length. Members of this family are often found as tandem repeats and in some cases represent the whole protein. All member proteins are described as being hypothetical.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1509)
description: This family consists of several uncharacterised viral proteins from the Marek's disease-like viruses. Members of this family are typically around 400 residues in length. The function of this family is unknown.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF1510)
description: This domain is found in hypothetical bacterial proteins of around 200 residues in length. The function of this domain is unknown.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1512) N-terminal domain
description: This family consists of several archaeal proteins of around 370 residues in length. The function of this family is unknown. This entry corresponds to the N-terminal domain.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1513)
description: This entry represents bacterial proteins that are predicted to be the outer membrane component of an efeUOB-like ferrous iron, uptake system [[cite:PUB00093610],[cite:PUB00070775]].

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1514)
description: This family consists of several Staphylococcus aureus and related bacteriophage proteins of around 65 residues in length. The function of this family is unknown. Structural modelling suggests this domain may bind nucleic acids [[cite:PUB00070793]].

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1515)
description: This family consists of several hypothetical bacterial proteins of around 130 residues in length. Members of this family seem to be found exclusively in Rhizobium species. The function of this family is unknown.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1516)
description: This family contains a number of hypothetical bacterial proteins of unknown function approximately 120 residues long.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1517)
description: This family consists of several hypothetical glycine rich plant and bacterial proteins of around 300 residues in length. The function of this family is unknown.

name: Nuclear receptor coactivator, DUF1518
description: This conserved domain of unknown function is usually found tandemly repeated in the nuclear receptor coactivator family (NCOA1/2/3, also known as the SRC/p160 nuclear receptor coactivator family, which are ligand-dependent transcription factors [[cite:PUB00097822],[cite:PUB00069373]].

name: Domain of Unknown Function (DUF1521)
description: This family of unknown function is found in a limited set of Bradyrhizobium proteins. There appears to be a periodic -DG- motif in it.

name: Domain of Unknown Function (DUF1259)
description: This family is the lppY/lpqO homologue family.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF5131)
description: This is a family of bacterial and phage proteins of unknown function. There are three highly conserved cysteine residues in the disposition, Cx6Cxxc, amongst many highly conserved residues.

name: GmrSD restriction endonucleases, C-terminal domain
description: This entry (previously known as DUF1524) represents a domain found C-terminal in the GmrSD family of modification-dependent restriction endonucleases including SspE proteins [[cite:PUB00155638]]. SspE is a dual-function protein that exerts both N-terminal NTPase and C-terminal DNA nicking nuclease activities to defend against phage infection [[cite:PUB00155272]]. SspE has a phosphorothioate (PT) modification-binding preference and utilises epigenetic PT modification to accomplish self-nonself discrimination and to coordinate its NTPase and DNA nicking activities to fight against phages. The domain represented in this entry has a DNA nicking nuclease activity and belongs to HNH nuclease superfamily.

name: Putative conjugal transfer nickase/helicase TraI C-term
Protein trafficking PGA2
description: A Saccharomyces cerevisiae member of this family (PGA2) is an ER protein which has been implicated in protein trafficking [[cite:PUB00044766]].

name: Heme-binding protein Shr-like, Hb-interacting domain
description: The Hb-interacting domain (HID) is found duplicated in Heme-binding protein Shr from Streptococcus pyogenes, a potentially lethal human pathogen, and in one to six copies in other uncharacterised bacterial proteins. Shr is a virulence factor that captures Hb and binds to the oxidized form of heme through an N-terminal region that contains two copies of this domain. HID shows a beta-sandwich-type fold in which two antiparallel beta-sheets are flanked by an alpha-helix [[cite:PUB00100888]].

name: Host cell surface-exposed lipoprotein
description: This domain is found as 1 to 5 copies in lipoproteins that are involved in superinfection exclusion. Proteins in this group have been shown to act at the stage of DNA release from the phage head into the cell [[cite:PUB00108413]]. This domain shows a three-helix bundle belonging to the HTH superfamily [[cite:PUB00101011]].

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1538)
description: This family contains several conserved glycines and phenylalanines.

name: Domain of Unknown Function (DUF1540)
description: This family has four conserved cysteines, which is suggestive of a metal binding function.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1541)
description: This family consists of several hypothetical bacterial and occurs as a tandem repeat.

name: Domain of Unknown Function (DUF1542)
description: This domain is found in several cell surface proteins, such as extracellular matrix-binding protein ebh [[cite:PUB00014728]]. Some members are involved in antibiotic resistance (e.g [swissprot:Q9RL69] and [swissprot:Q9LCJ9]) [[cite:PUB00014727]] and/or cellular adhesion (e.g. [swissprot:Q931R6]) [[cite:PUB00014728]]. In some proteins it is repeated more than fifteen times, being the most repeated domain in streptococci [[cite:PUB00097824]]. This is a predominantly alpha-helical domain that form a long, thin, fibre-like structure and it has been proposed to function as a stalk that helps the adhesive non-repeat region (NRR) of proteins protrude beyond the cell surface [[cite:PUB00097823],[cite:PUB00065268]].

name: Domain of Unknown Function (DUF1543)
description: This domain is found as 1-2 copies in a small family of proteins of unknown function.

name: TAF6 C-terminal HEAT repeat domain
description: TAF6_C is the C-terminal domain of the TAF6 subunit of the general transcription factor TFIID. The crystal structure reveals the presence of five conserved HEAT repeats. This region is necessary for the complexing together of the subunits TAF5, TAF6 and TAF9 [[cite:PUB00075536],[cite:PUB00099783],[cite:PUB00122818]].

name: Domain of Unknown Function (DUF1547)
description: This domain appears to be found only in a small family of Chlamydia species [[cite:PUB00097825]]. It is usually found repeated. This domain can be found in translocated actin-recruiting phosphoprotein (Tarp) from Chlamydia trachomatis serovar L2. Tarp appears to initiate or participate in signalling events that regulate the actin recruitment, which ultimately leads to internalisation [[cite:PUB00075564]].

name: Domain of Unknown Function (DUF1548)
description: This family appears to be found only in a small family of Chlamydia proteins.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1549)
description: A family of paralogues in the planctomyces.

name: Aerotolerance regulator N-terminal
description: These proteins share a highly-conserved sequence at their N-terminus. They include several proteins from Rhodopirellula baltica and also several from proteobacteria. The proteins are produced by the Batl operon which appears to be important in pathogenicity and aerotolerance. This family is the conserved N-terminus, but the full length proteins carry multiple membrane-spanning domains [[cite:PUB00055562]]. BatA ensures bacterial survival in the early stages of the infection process, when the infected sites are aerobic, and is produced under conditions of oxidative stress [[cite:PUB00055563]].

name: Putative beta barrel porin-7 (BBP7)
description: This is a family of putative beta barrel porin-7 BBP7 proteins identified initially in Rhodopirellula baltica.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1552)
description: A family of proteins identified in Rhodopirellula baltica.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1553)
description: A family of proteins found in Rhodopirellula baltica.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1554)
description: A family of proteins identified in Leptospira interrogans.

name: PEP-CTERM protein-sorting motif
description: This entry describes a 25-residue motif that includes an invariant Pro-Glu-Pro (PEP) motif, a thirteen-residue strongly hydrophobic sequence likely to span the membrane, and a five-residue strongly basic motif that often contains four Arg residues. In most cases, this motif is found within nine residues of the C-terminal end of the protein. Proteins containing this motif typically have signal sequences at the N-terminal [[cite:PUB00034422],[cite:PUB00105164]].

name: Pretoxin HINT domain
description: A member of the HINT superfamily of proteases that is usually found N-terminal to the toxin module in polymorphic toxin systems. The domain is predicted to function in releasing the toxin domain by autoproteolysis [[cite:PUB00057479]].

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1559)
description: A large family of paralogous proteins apparently unique to planctomycetes.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1561)
description: A family of paralogous proteins in Leptospira interrogans.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1563)
description: A small family of short hypothetical proteins in Leptospira interrogans.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1564)
description: A family of paralogous proteins in Leptospira interrogans. Several (e.g. [swissprot:Q8F4V2]) have been annotated as possible CopG-like transcriptional regulators (see [pfam:PF01402]).

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1565)
description: These proteins share a region of homology in their N termini, and are found in several phylogenetically diverse bacteria and in the archaeon Methanosarcina acetivorans. Some of these proteins also contain characterised domains such as [pfam:PF00395] (e.g. [swissprot:Q8YWJ6]) and [pfam:PF03422] (e.g. [swissprot:Q9FBS2]).

name: Lcl C-terminal domain
description: This domain is found C-terminal in the Legionella collagen-like protein (Lcl) and related proteins mainly from bacteria. Lcl is an extracellular peripheral membrane protein that recognises sulphated glycosaminoglycans (GAGs) on the surface of eukaryotic cells, but also stimulates bacterial aggregation in response to divalent cations. This domain has a structural similarity to C-type lectins and is involved in glycan recognition [[cite:PUB00155456]].

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1569)
description: A family of hypothetical proteins identified in Rhodopirellula baltica.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1570)
description: A family of hypothetical proteins in Rhodopirellula baltica. This family carries a highly conserved HExxH sequence motif characteristic of members of the Peptidase clan MA.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1571)
description: A family of paralogous proteins in Rhodopirellula baltica.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1572)
description: These proteins, from several diverse bacteria, share a short conserved sequence towards their N termini.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1573)
description: These hypothetical proteins, from bacteria such as Rhodopirellula baltica, Bacteroides thetaiotaomicron, and Porphyromonas gingivalis, share a region of conserved sequence towards their N-termini.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1574)
description: A family of hypothetical proteins in Leptospira interrogans.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1576)
description: This small family is found in several undescribed proteins. The alignment is distinguished by the frequent occurrence of conserved glycine and aromatic residues.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1577)
description: A family of hypothetical proteins in Leptospira interrogans.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1579)
description: A family of paralogous hypothetical proteins identified in Rhodopirellula baltica that also has members in Gloeobacter violaceus, Sinorhizobium meliloti and Agrobacterium tumefaciens.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1580)
description: A family of short hypothetical proteins found in Rhodopirellula baltica.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1581)
description: Several Rhodopirellula baltica proteins share this probable domain. Most of these proteins are predicted to be secreted or membrane-associated.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1582)
description: A family of hypothetical proteins in Rhodopirellula baltica.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1583) C domain
description: Most of these Rhodopirellula baltica hypothetical proteins also match [pfam:PF07619].

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1585)
description: A conserved sequence region at the C terminus of several cytochrome-like proteins in Rhodopirellula baltica.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1587)
description: A region of similarity shared by several Rhodopirellula baltica cytochrome-like proteins that are predicted to be secreted. These proteins also match [pfam:PF07624].

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1588)
description: A region of similarity shared by several Rhodopirellula baltica cytochrome-like proteins that are predicted to be secreted. These proteins also match [pfam:PF07626] and [pfam:PF07624].

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1589)
description: A family of short hypothetical proteins in Rhodopirellula baltica.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1592)
description: A region of similarity shared by several Rhodopirellula baltica cytochrome-like proteins that are predicted to be secreted. These proteins also match [pfam:PF07627], [pfam:PF07626], and [pfam:PF07624].

name: Cellulose-binding Sde182, nucleoside hydrolase-like domain
description: This Rossmann-related domain is found at the N-terminal end of the C-terminal domain region of the cellulose-binding protein Sde182 from Saccharophagus degradans ([swissprot:Q21PD3]), which seems to have capacity to bind plant carbohydrates. This domain shows an alpha/beta configuration with a central beta-sheet of eight beta-strands and 12 alpha-helices. It is structurally similar to pyrimidine-specific ribonucleoside hydrolases (NH) [[cite:PUB00100688]]. This domain is also found in other uncharacterised bacterial and fungal proteins.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1595)
description: A family of proteins in Rhodopirellula baltica, associated with [pfam:PF07635], [pfam:PF07626], [pfam:PF07631], [pfam:PF07627], and [pfam:PF07624].

name: Putative beta-barrel porin-2, OmpL-like. bbp2
description: BBP2 is a family of putative porin proteins that are likely to be outer membrane beta barrel proteins porins.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1598)
description: A family of Rhodopirellula baltica hypothetical proteins of about 500 amino acids in length.

name: Nucleotide modification associated domain 1
description: An alpha helical domain with conserved polar residues suggestive of enzymatic function. The domain is associated with the 5-hydroxymethyl uridine synthase and is predicted to play a role in modified base biosynthesis pathways [[cite:PUB00091053]].

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1600)
description: These proteins appear to be specific to Mycoplasma species.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1601)
description: This repeat is found in a small number of proteins and is apparently limited to Coxiella and related species.

name: CARDB
description: Cell adhesion related domain found in bacteria.

name: G patch domain-containing protein, N-terminal
description: This domain is found at the N-terminal of several eukaryotic RNA processing proteins, including Arabidopsis TGH, which is involved in microRNA (miRNA) and small interfering RNA (siRNA) biogenesis [[cite:PUB00077126]].

name: Oligonucleotide/oligosaccharide-binding (OB)-fold
description: This family is found towards the C-terminus of the DEAD-box helicases ([pfam:PF00270]). In these helicases it is apparently always found in association with [pfam:PF04408]. There do seem to be a couple of instances where it occurs by itself - e.g. [swissprot:Q84VZ2]. The structure PDB:3i4u adopts an OB-fold. helicases ([pfam:PF00270]). In these helicases it is apparently always found in association with [pfam:PF04408]. This C-terminal domain of the yeast helicase contains an oligonucleotide/oligosaccharide-binding (OB)-fold which seems to be placed at the entrance of the putative nucleic acid cavity. It also constitutes the binding site for the G-patch-containing domain of Pfa1p. When found on DEAH/RHA helicases, this domain is central to the regulation of the helicase activity through its binding of both RNA and G-patch domain proteins [[cite:PUB00092307]].

name: Coatomer beta C-terminal region
description: This family is found at the C-terminus of the coatamer beta subunit proteins (Beta-coat proteins). This C-terminal domain probably adapts the function of the N-terminal [pfam:PF01602] domain.

name: F-box associated beta propeller domain
description: Most of these proteins contain [pfam:PF00646] at the N terminus, suggesting that they are effectors linked with ubiquitination.

name: S-layer protein
description: Archaeal S-layer proteins consist of two copies of this domain [[cite:PUB00060425],[cite:PUB00152243]].

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1609)
description: This region is found in a number of hypothetical proteins thought to be expressed by the eukaryote Encephalitozoon cuniculi, an obligate intracellular microsporidial parasite. It is approximately 200 residues long.

name: Ribosomal protein aS21
description: This entry represents ribosomal protein aS21, an archaea-specific component of the small ribosomal subunit (SSU). The protein was first characterised as HVO_2753 (Small CPxCG-related zinc finger protein) from Haloferax volcanii [[cite:PUB00096940]] and has been identified in ribosome structures from Pyrococcus abyssi [[cite:PUB00114374]] and Pyrobaculum calidifontis [[cite:PUB00161770]], where it is located at a position corresponding to eS21 in eukaryotic ribosomes. NMR 3D structure analysis revealed four C(P)XCG motifs, suggesting the presence of two zinc-binding pockets (ZBPs). While some members of this entry bind two zinc ions [[cite:PUB00161688]], in HVO_2753, only C(P)XCG motifs 2 and 4 (comprising Cys-32 to Cys-35 and Cys-50 to Cys-53) form a ZBP and bind one zinc atom, while C(P)XCG motifs 1 and 3 (comprising Cys-12 to Cys-15 and Cys-39 to Cys-42) form a four-Cys cluster that do not bind zinc. The four C(P)XCG motifs are critical for protein stability, folding and functionality [[cite:PUB00096940]]. Despite structural topology resembling eukaryotic eS21, sequence identities in the structurally superimposed regions are limited, and the archaeal protein contains two zinc knuckles not observed in the eukaryotic version [[cite:PUB00114374]]. The widespread conservation of this protein in archaeal genomes supports its role as a core ribosomal component [[cite:PUB00114374],[cite:PUB00161770]].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF1611_C) P-loop domain
description: This region is found in a number of hypothetical bacterial and archaeal proteins. According to structure it has a P-loop structure.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1612)
description: This family includes sequences of largely unknown function but which share a number of features in common. They are expressed by bacterial species, and in many cases these bacteria are known to associate symbiotically with plants. Moreover, the majority are coded for by plasmids, which in many cases are known to confer on the organism the ability to interact symbiotically with leguminous plants. An example of such a plasmid is NGR234, which encodes Y4CF, a protein of unknown function that is a member of this family [[cite:PUB00004254]]. Other members of this family are expressed by organisms with a documented genomic similarity to plant symbionts [[cite:PUB00015202]].

name: Predicted AdoMet-dependent methyltransferase
description: Proteins in this family have been predicted to function as AdoMet-dependent methyltransferases [[cite:PUB00044770]].

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1614)
description: This is a family of sequences coming from hypothetical proteins found in both bacterial and archaeal species.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1615)
description: This is a family of proteins of unknown function expressed by various bacterial species. Some members of this family (e.g. [swissprot:Q8Z8Z7], [swissprot:Q8ZRF4]) are thought to be lipoproteins. Another member of this family ([swissprot:Q93SV8]) is thought to be involved in photosynthesis [[cite:PUB00015226]]. Based on structure predictions (from AlphaFold and structural comparisons using DALI server), this family may have a lysozyme-like fold.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF1616)
description: This is a domain found at the C-terminal of a group of uncharacterised bacterial and archaeal proteins. It may adopt a Ig-like fold.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1617)
description: This is a family of sequences from hypothetical bacterial and bacteriophage proteins. The region in question is approximately 150 residues long and is highly conserved throughout the family.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1618)
description: The members of this family are mainly hypothetical proteins expressed by grasses.

name: Tectonic domain of DUF1619
description: This is a conserved domain found in tectonic proteins (TCTN1/2/3) which contains conserved cysteine residues predicted to form disulfide bond. This domain is found in two tandem copies. It is predicted to fold into an alpha/beta structure with unique topology composed of a central mixed beta-sheet and alpha-helix packed on it. Although function of this domain is currently unknown, studies on TCTN2 suggest that it is indispensable for its functions [[cite:PUB00097826],[cite:PUB00097827]]. TCTN1, TCTN2, and TCTN3 are members of the tectonic protein family that play crucial roles in ciliogenesis and ciliary function. While they share some common functions, each protein also has specific roles in the process of cilia formation and maintenance. These proteins interact with several other ciliopathy proteins, forming a complex known as the Tectonic ciliopathy complex. This complex is required for hedgehog signalling transduction and regulation of ciliary membrane composition [[cite:PUB00069722],[cite:PUB00160606]].

name: ER membrane protein complex subunit 1, second beta-propeller
description: This is the second beta-propeller domain of ER membrane protein complex subunit 1. ER membrane protein complex subunit 1 is a component of the ER membrane protein complex (EMC, composed of EMC1, EMC2, EMC3, EMC4, EMC5 and EMC6). In Saccharomyces cerevisiae, the EMC seems to be required for efficient folding of proteins in the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) [[cite:PUB00061987]]. EMC1 contains two eight-bladed beta-propellers and stabilises the entire EMC complex, contacting six of the remaining eight subunits [[cite:PUB00096682]]. The beta-propellers are in the lumen and may serve as a platform for recruitment of co-factors at the site of nascent protein insertion [[cite:PUB00096682]].

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1622)
description: This is a family of 14 highly conserved sequences, from hypothetical proteins expressed by both bacterial and archaeal species.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1623)
description: The members of this family are all derived from relatively short hypothetical proteins thought to be expressed by various Nucleopolyhedroviruses.

name: Heparan-alpha-glucosaminide N-acetyltransferase, catalytic
description: This entry includes the catalytic domain of HGSNAT (Heparan-alpha-glucosaminide N-acetyltransferase). It contains the conserved histidine in the active site (His269), thought to hold the acetyl group during the transfer across the membrane and required for its enzymatic activity. HGSNAT transfers an acetyl group from cytoplasmically derived acetyl-CoA to terminal N-glucosamine residues of heparan sulfate within the lysosomes [[cite:PUB00090705]].

name: Transmembrane protein 43
description: This entry represents the transmembrane protein 43 family of proteins, which may function as tetraspanin-like membrane organisers [[cite:PUB00059300]].

name: PD-(D/E)XK nuclease superfamily
description: This family is found to carry modified motifs characteristic of PD-(D/E)XK endonuclease superfamily. These are the conserved Glu of motif I, the Asp surreounded by hydrophobics of motif II, EIKS of motif III, and the lysine of mmotif IV has migrated to an alpha-helix following the third core beta-strand. The conserved patch of positively charged lysine and arginine residues in the motif IV apha-helix might be involved in substrate-binding or be contributing to active site formation [[cite:PUB00044133]]. Members with an additional N-terminal coi9led-coil domain, are annotated as tropomyosin, coiled-coil or microtubule binding proteins [[cite:PUB00016549],[cite:PUB00044133]].

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1627)
description: This is a group of sequences found in hypothetical proteins predicted to be expressed in a number of bacterial species. The region in question is approximately 150 amino acid residues long.

name: Archaeal Type IV pilin, N-terminal
description: This entry represents the N-terminal domain of archaeal pilins, which play important roles in surface adhesion [[cite:PUB00160950]]. Sequences covered by this domain are not mixed up with sequences having such an extremely high sequence conservation as described in [[cite:PUB00069628],[cite:PUB00160950]].

name: Immunity protein family (Imm11)
description: This family formerly known as DUF1629 was identified to be an immunity protein [[cite:PUB00066726]].

name: Docking domain of Afi1 for Arf3 in vesicle trafficking
description: This domain occurs at the N-terminal of Afi1, an Arf3p-interacting protein, is a protein necessary for vesicle trafficking in yeast. This domain is the interacting region of the protein which binds to Arf3, the highly conserved small GTPases (ADP-ribosylation factors). Afi1 is distributed asymmetrically at the plasma membrane and is required for polarized distribution of Arf3 but not of an Arf3 guanine nucleotide-exchange factor, Yel1p. However, Afi1 is not required for targeting of Arf3 or Yel1p to the plasma membrane. Afi1 functions as an Arf3 polarization-specific adapter and participates in development of polarity. Although Arf3 is the homologue of human Arf6 it does not function in the same way, not being necessary for endocytosis or for mating factor receptor internalization. In the S phase, however, it is concentrated at the plasma membrane of the emerging bud. Because of its polarized localisation and its critical function in the normal budding pattern of yeast, Arf3 is probably a regulator of vesicle trafficking, which is important for polarized growth.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1631) N-terminal domain
description: This entry represents the N-terminal helical domain of DUF1631 protein family proteins. The members of this family are sequences derived from a group of hypothetical proteins expressed by certain bacterial species.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1633)
description: This family contains sequences derived from a group of hypothetical proteins expressed by Arabidopsis thaliana. These sequences are highly similar and the region concerned is about 100 residues long.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1635)
description: The members of this family include sequences that are parts of hypothetical proteins expressed by plant species. The region in question is about 170 amino acids long.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1638)
description: This family contains sequences covering an approximately 270 amino acid stretch of a group of hypothetical proteins. These proteins are expressed by archaeal species of the Methanosarcina genus.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1639)
description: This approximately 50 residue region is found in a number of sequences derived from hypothetical plant proteins. This region features a highly basic 5 amino-acid stretch towards its centre.

name: Coiled-coil domain-containing protein 90-like
description: This entry includes coiled-coil domain-containing proteins 90 (CCDC90) and related proteins. CCDC90A is a key regulator of the mitochondrial calcium uniporter (MCU) and hence was renamed MCUR1 [[cite:PUB00097799],[cite:PUB00076354],[cite:PUB00097801]]. A study in mammals and in yeast homologue fmp32 has reported that MCUR1 is a cytochrome c oxidase assembly factor and that it has an indirect role as a regulator of MCU [[cite:PUB00075452]], however, subsequent publications confirmed the function of MCUR1 as a regulator of MCU [[cite:PUB00097799],[cite:PUB00097800]]. The role of CCDC90B proteins is still not known.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1643)
description: The members of this family are all sequences found within hypothetical proteins expressed by various bacterial species. The region concerned is approximately 150 residues long.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1644)
description: This family consists of sequences found in a number of hypothetical plant proteins of unknown function. The region of interest contains nine highly conserved cysteine residues and is approximately 160 amino acids in length, and is probably a zinc-binding domain.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1647)
description: The sequences making up this family are all derived from hypothetical proteins expressed by C. elegans. The region in question is approximately 160 amino acids long. The GO annotation for this protein indicates the protein to be involved in nematode larval development and to have a positive regulation on growth rate.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1645)
description: These sequences are derived from a number of hypothetical plant proteins. The region in question is approximately 270 amino acids long. Some members of this family are annotated as yeast pheromone receptor proteins AR781 but no literature was found to support this.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1634)
description: This family contains many hypothetical bacterial and archaeal proteins. A few members of this family are annotated as being putative transmembrane proteins, and the region in question in fact contains many hydrophobic residues.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1636)
description: The sequences featured in this family are derived from a number of hypothetical prokaryotic proteins. The region in question is approximately 130 amino acids long.

name: PCO_ADO
description: This entry includes cysteine oxidases (PCOs) from plants and 2-aminoethanethiol dioxygenases (ADOs) from animals [[cite:PUB00074379],[cite:PUB00074380]].

name: Helical membrane plugin
description: This entry represents the helical membrane plugin (HMP) domain found in a group of uncharacterised prokaryotic proteins, including the [NiFe]-hydrogenase Huc from Mycobacterium smegmatis [[cite:PUB00161758]]. It is involved in the construction of oxidoreductases in prokaryotes, which allows quinone channelling between the membrane and various redox catalytic subunits [[cite:PUB00161759]]. It was previously known as DUF1641.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1642)
description: The sequences making up this family are derived from various hypothetical phage and prophage proteins. The region in question is approximately 140 amino acids long.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF1648)
description: This domain is found in proteins expressed by bacterial or archaeal species. Some of these are annotated as being transmembrane proteins, and in fact many of these sequences contain a high proportion of hydrophobic residues. One protein containing this domain is immunity protein SdpI (swiss:O32241) from Bacillus subtilis, which provides protection for the cell against the toxic effects of its own SdpC killing factor, and also functions as a receptor/signal transduction protein [[cite:PUB00055038]].

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1646)
description: Some of the members of this family are hypothetical bacterial and archaeal proteins, but others are annotated as being cation transporters expressed by the archaebacterium Methanosarcina mazei ([swissprot:Q8PXG5], [swissprot:Q8PXG7] and [swissprot:Q8PXG8]).

name: Autophagy-related protein 101
description: Atg101 is a critical autophagy factor that functions together with ULK, Atg13 and FIP200 [[cite:PUB00059287],[cite:PUB00078911]]. Atg101 has been shown to be a HORMA (Hop1, Rev7 and MAD2) domain protein with an open conformation [[cite:PUB00109143]].

name: Mediator of CRAC channel activity
description: ORAI-1 is a protein homologue of Drosophila Orai and human Orai1, Orai2 and Orai3. ORAI-1 GFP reporters are co- expressed with STIM-1 (ER CA(2+) sensors) in the gonad and intestine. The protein has four predicted transmembrane domains with a highly conserved region between TM2 ad TM3. This conserved domain is thought to function in channel regulation. ORAI1- related proteins are required for the production of the calcium channel, CRAC, along with STIM1-related proteins [[cite:PUB00055566]].

name: Transmembrane family, TMEM144 of transporters
description: Members of this family fall in to the drug/metabolite transporter (dmt) superfamily. They carry 10xTM domains arranged as 5+5. Although these two sets may originally have arisen by gene-duplication the divergence now is such that the similarity between the two halves is no longer detectable by sequence.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1651)
description: This is a family containing bacterial proteins of unknown function.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1652)
description: This is a family containing hypothetical bacterial proteins.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1653)
description: This is a family of hypothetical bacterial proteins of unknown function.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1654)
description: This family consists of proteins from the Pseudomonadaceae.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1655)
description: This protein is found in some prophages found in Lactobacillales lactis ([[cite:PUB00016516]]).

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1656)
description: This entry represents a putative component of efflux pumps that comprise MFP and FUSC proteins. Several members are in an operon with and have similar mutants phenotypes as an RND efflux pump and a fusaric acid resistance-like protein [[cite:PUB00093610]]. This system is involved in transporting diverse substrates including 4-hydroxybenzoate and octanoate [[cite:PUB00106931]].

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1657)
description: This domain appears to be restricted to the Bacillales.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1659)
