description: This family consists of hypothetical bacterial proteins of unknown function.

name: Prophage protein (DUF1660)
description: This protein is found in Lactobacillae prophages.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1661)
description: This is a family containing bacterial proteins of unknown function. Many of the proteins in this family are hypothetical.

name: CopG-like RHH_1 or ribbon-helix-helix domain, RHH_5
description: This family contains bacterial proteins that form a ribbon-helix-helix fold. This fold occurs in many examples of bacterial antitoxins [[cite:PUB00075548]].

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1664)
description: The members of this family are hypothetical plant proteins of unknown function. The region featured in this family is approximately 100 amino acids long.

name: Rrp15p
description: Rrp15p is required for the formation of 60S ribosomal subunits [[cite:PUB00020276]].

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1666)
description: These sequences are derived from hypothetical plant proteins of unknown function. The region in question is approximately 250 residues long.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1667)
description: Hypothetical archaeal and bacterial proteins make up this family. A few proteins are annotated as being potential metal-binding proteins, and in fact the members of this family have four highly conserved cysteine residues, but no further literature evidence was found in this regard.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1668)
description: The hypothetical proteins found in this family are expressed by Oryza sativa and are of unknown function.

name: Scaffolding anchor of CK1 domain
description: This entry represents the scaffolding anchor of CK1 domain (SACK1 domain) found in the FAM83 family, which includes FAM83A-H. This domain was formerly known as DUF1669 and it has been identified as a CK1 binding domain, which allows the correct subcellular localisation of both FAM83 proteins and the CK1 binding partners and their function [[cite:PUB00155374]]. These proteins are involved in diverse biological processes, depending on their subcellular localisation and binding partners. FAM83A-H interact with the alpha and alpha-like isoforms of CK1, while FAM83A, B, E, and H also interact with the delta and epsilon isoforms of CK1. FAM83 members have function as intermediaries in EGFR/RAS signalling [[cite:PUB00084963]]. FAM83D has been reported to localise to the mitotic spindle and interact with the chromokinesin kinesin family member 22 (KIF22, also called Kid) [[cite:PUB00124155]]. FAM83G, also known as PAWS1 interacts with the transcription factor SMAD1 and promotes the transcription of non-canonical bone morphogenetic protein (BMP) target genes [[cite:PUB00155375]]. FAM83H mutations have been associated with amelogenesis imperfecta [[cite:PUB00092186]].

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1673)
description: This family contains hypothetical proteins of unknown function expressed by two archaeal species.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1674)
description: The members of this family are sequences derived from hypothetical eukaryotic and bacterial proteins. The region in question is approximately 60 residues long.

name: Ethylene-responsive binding factor-associated repression
description: The EAR motif is the ethylene-responsive element binding factor-associated amphiphilic repression motif. This motif binds to the Groucho/Tup1-type co-repressor TOPLESS (TPL) and TPL-related proteins. The motif is frequently to be find at the N-terminus of NINJA, or Novel INteractor of JAZ, proteins [[cite:PUB00066523]]. The EAR motif, defined by the consensus sequence patterns of either LxLxL or DLN xxP, is the most predominant form of transcriptional repression motif so far identified in plants. It is highly conserved in transcriptional regulators that are known to function as negative regulators in a broad range of developmental and physiological processes across evolutionarily diverse plant species [[cite:PUB00075457]]. This family is closely related to family AUX_IAA Pam:PF02309 which also has an LxLxL signature.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1676)
description: This family contains sequences derived from proteins of unknown function expressed by Drosophila melanogaster and Anopheles gambiae.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1670)
description: The hypothetical eukaryotic proteins found in this family are of unknown function.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1672)
description: This family is composed of hypothetical bacterial proteins of unknown function.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1663)
description: The members of this family are hypothetical proteins expressed by Trypanosoma cruzi, a eukaryotic parasite that causes Chagas' disease in humans. This region is found as multiple copies per protein.

name: Peptidase family C78
description: This family formerly known as DUF1671 has been shown to be a cysteine peptidase called (Ufm1)-specific protease [[cite:PUB00034739]].

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1677)
description: The sequences found in this family are all derived from hypothetical plant proteins of unknown function. The region features a number of highly conserved cysteine residues.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1678)
description: This family is composed of uncharacterized proteins expressed by Methanopyrus kandleri, a hyperthermophilic archaebacterium.

name: Uncharacterized oxidoreductase dhs-27
description: The region featured in this family is found in a number of C. elegans proteins, in one case ([swissprot:Q19034]) as a repeat. In many of the family members, this region is associated with the CHK region described by SMART as being found in ZnF_C4 and HLH domain-containing kinases. In fact, one member of this family ([swissprot:Q9GUC1]) is annotated as being a member of the nuclear hormone receptor family, and contains regions typical of such proteins (Interpro:IPR000536, Interpro:IPR008946, and Interpro:IPR001628).

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1684)
description: The sequences featured in this family are found in hypothetical archaeal and bacterial proteins of unknown function. The region in question is approximately 200 amino acids long.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1681)
description: This family is composed of sequences derived from a number of hypothetical eukaryotic proteins of unknown function.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1686)
description: The members of this family are all hypothetical proteins of unknown function expressed by the eukaryotic parasite Encephalitozoon cuniculi GB-M1. The region in question is approximately 250 amino acids long.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1685)
description: The members of this family are hypothetical eukaryotic proteins of unknown function. The region in question is approximately 100 amino acid residues long.

name: Beta-L-arabinofuranosidase, GH127 catalytic domain
description: This entry represents the catalytic domain of Non-reducing end beta-L-arabinofuranosidase from Bifidobacterium longum (Beta -AFase) and similar proteins that belong to the glycoside hydrolase family 127 (GH127). This domain folds into an (alpha /alpha)6 barrel. Beta-AFase has been characterised as an unusual beta-L-arabinofuranosidase enzyme, [ec:3.2.1.185]. It releases l-arabinose from the l-arabinofuranose (Araf)-beta1,2-Araf disaccharide and also transglycosylates 1-alkanols with retention of the anomeric configuration [[cite:PUB00075450],[cite:PUB00151606]].

name: PAT complex subunit CCDC47
description: This family represents CCDC47 proteins which are a component of the PAT complex, an endoplasmic reticulum (ER)-resident membrane multiprotein complex that facilitates multi-pass membrane proteins insertion into membranes [[cite:PUB00097218]]. The PAT complex, formed by CCDC47 and Asterix proteins, acts as an intramembrane chaperone by directly interacting with nascent transmembrane domains (TMDs), releasing its substrates upon correct folding, and is needed for optimal biogenesis of multi-pass membrane proteins [[cite:PUB00097218]]. CCDC47 ([swissprot:Q96A33]) is required to maintain the stability of Asterix [[cite:PUB00097218],[cite:PUB00097217]]. CCDC47 is associated with various membrane-associated processes and is component of a ribosome-associated ER translocon complex involved in multi-pass membrane protein transport into the ER membrane and biogenesis [[cite:PUB00097241]]. It is also involved in the regulation of calcium ion homeostasis in the ER [[cite:PUB00097242]], being also required for proper protein degradation via the ERAD (ER-associated degradation) pathway [[cite:PUB00097243]].

name: MDM10-complementing protein 1, transmembrane domain
description: This entry represents the transmembrane domains found in MDM10-complementing protein 1 from yeast, a mitochondrial protein involved in in mitochondrial lipid homeostasis [[cite:PUB00090363]].

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1689)
description: Family of fungal proteins with unknown function. A member of this family has been found to localise in the mitochondria [[cite:PUB00016470]].

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1687)
description: This is a putative redox protein which is predicted to have a thioredoxin fold containing a single active cysteine [[cite:PUB00033654]].

name: Protein of Unknown function (DUF1690)
description: Family of uncharacterised fungal proteins.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF3294)
description: This family was annotated as mitochondrial Ribosomal protein MRP8, based on the presumed similarity of the S.cerevisiae protein to an E.coli mitochondrial ribosomal protein; however, this similarity is spurious, and the function is not known [Wood, V].

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1688)
description: A family of uncharacterised proteins.

name: Endoplasmic reticulum vesicle transporter
description: This family is conserved from plants and fungi to humans. Erv46 works in close conjunction with Erv41 and together they form a complex which cycles between the endoplasmic reticulum and Golgi complex. Erv46-41 interacts strongly with the endoplasmic reticulum glucosidase II. Mammalian glucosidase II comprises a catalytic alpha-subunit and a 58 kDa beta subunit, which is required for ER localisation. All proteins identified biochemically as Erv41p-Erv46p interactors are localised to the early secretory pathway and are involved in protein maturation and processing in the ER and/or sorting into COPII vesicles for transport to the Golgi [[cite:PUB00063190]].

name: Nucleotidyltransferase
description: This family contains many hypothetical proteins. It also includes four nematode prion-like proteins. This domain has been identified as part of the nucleotidyltransferase superfamily [[cite:PUB00066751]].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF1775)
description: Domain found in bacteria with undetermined function. Its structure has been determined and is an immunoglobulin-like fold.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1694)
description: This family contains many hypothetical proteins.

name: Peptidase family M54
description: This is a family of metallopeptidases. Two human proteins have been reported to degrade synthetic substrates and peptides [[cite:PUB00033883]].

name: Bacterial PH domain
description: This family contains many bacterial hypothetical proteins. The structures of [swissprot:A1SD03], PDB:3hsa, and [swissprot:A3QB43], PDB:3dcx, show similarities to the PH or pleckstrin homology domain. First evidence of PH-like domains in bacteria suggests role in cell envelope stress response [[cite:PUB00054230]].

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1697)
description: This family contains many hypothetical bacterial proteins.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1698)
description: This family contains many hypothetical proteins. It also includes two putative methyltransferase proteins, [swissprot:Q8EEE6] and [swissprot:Q88MX8].

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1699) C-terminal HTH domain
description: This entry represents a C-terminal Helix-turn-helix domain in the DUF1699 family of proteins found in archaeabacterial sequences.

name: HAAS transmembrane region
description: This entry represents the transmembrane region fused to HAAS (HTH-associated alpha-helical signaling) domain (Preprint https://doi.org/10.1101/2020.09.24.301986).

name: JmjC domain
description: This entry includes proteins with a JmjC domain that belong to the cupin superfamily, including Bifunctional lysine-specific demethylase and histidyl-hydroxylase NO66 [[cite:PUB00090402]], Ribosomal oxygenase 1/2 [[cite:PUB00090403],[cite:PUB00090404]], and 50S ribosomal protein L16 3-hydroxylase from Escherichia coli [[cite:PUB00090405],[cite:PUB00099121]]. Proteins are bifunctional, acting as histone lysine demethylases and ribosomal histidine hydroxylases.

name: PD-(D/E)XK nuclease superfamily
description: This family contains many hypothetical bacterial proteins. It has been identified as a member of the PD-(D/E)XK nuclease superfamily through transitive meta profile searches [[cite:PUB00044133]]. DUF1703 has the predicted secondary structure pattern of the restriction endonuclease-like fold core and contains an additional beta-strand at the C-terminus [[cite:PUB00044133]].

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1702)
description: This family of proteins contains many bacterial proteins that are encoded by the UnbL gene. The function of these proteins is unknown.

name: Microtubule-associated tyrosine carboxypeptidase
description: This entry includes microtubule-associated tyrosine carboxypeptidases, proteins that remove the C-terminal tyrosine residue of alpha-tubulin, thereby regulating microtubule dynamics and function [[cite:PUB00101358]]. They are also able to remove the C-terminal phenylalanine residue of alpha-tubulin TUBA8 [[cite:PUB00101358]]. These proteins recognise adjacent tubulin dimers along the same protofilament [[cite:PUB00101358]].

name: Phosphoethanolamine transferase EptA/EptB
description: This entry represents a domain found in a group of bacterial phosphoethanolamine transferases, including eptA from Helicobacter pylori [[cite:PUB00084966]] and eptB from Escherichia coli [ec:2.7.8.42] [[cite:PUB00084967]]. This domain is found immediately N-terminal to the sulphatase domain in many sulphatases.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1706)
description: This family contains many hypothetical proteins from bacteria and yeast.

name: DUF1707 SHOCT-like domain
description: This domain is found in a variety of Actinomycetales proteins. All of the proteins containing this domain are uncharacterised and probably membrane bound or associated. It is unclear to the function of this domain.

name: Meiotically up-regulated protein Msb1/Mug8 domain
description: This domain of unknown function is found in fungal proteins including Mug8 from Schizosaccharomyces pombe which may have a role in meiosis and septation [[cite:PUB00044889]]. Saccharomyces cerevisiae homologue MSB1 (swiss:P21339) may be involved in positive regulation of 1,3-beta-glucan synthesis and the Pkc1p-MAPK pathway [[cite:PUB00087082]].

name: Cell division protein anillin
description: Anillin is a protein involved in septin organisation during cell division. It is an actin binding protein that is localised to the cleavage furrow, and it maintains the localisation of active myosin, which ensures the spatial control of concerted contraction during cytokinesis [[cite:PUB00075569]].

name: INO80 complex subunit Ies4
description: The INO80 ATPase is a member of the SNF2 family of ATPases and functions as an integral component of a multisubunit ATP-dependent chromatin remodelling complex. This family of proteins corresponds to the fungal Ies4 subunit of INO80.

name: Mitochondrial mRNA-processing protein COX24, C-terminal
description: This domain of unknown function is found at the C terminal end of Mitochondrial small ribosomal subunit protein mS38, also known as Mitochondrial mRNA-processing protein COX24 in yeast which is involved in the splicing of the COX1 mRNA [[cite:PUB00076420]]. COX24 is a component of the mitochondrial ribosome (mitoribosome), responsible for the synthesis of mitochondrial genome-encoded proteins, including at least some of the essential transmembrane subunits of the mitochondrial respiratory chain. The mitoribosomes are attached to the mitochondrial inner membrane and translation products are cotranslationally integrated into the membrane [[cite:PUB00089004],[cite:PUB00098057]]. This domain is also found in COX24 mammalian homologue Aurora kinase A-interacting protein [[cite:PUB00078824]]. This entry also includes uncharacterised proteins from bacteria.

name: Histone acetyltransferase KAT11-type domain
description: This entry represents a histone acetyltransferase catalytic domain found in fungal proteins, including RTT109 (also known as KAT11) from budding and fission yeasts and Candida species. This domain catalyses the acetylation of lysine residues on histone H3, including H3K56, H3K9, H3K14, H3K23 and H3K27 [[cite:PUB00045009],[cite:PUB00042670]]. The domain functions within a complex with histone chaperones such as VPS75 that regulate substrate specificity [[cite:PUB00051225]]. Acetylation of H3K56 by this domain promotes nucleosome assembly, DNA repair and transcriptional regulation during S-phase [[cite:PUB00045009],[cite:PUB00042670]]. The domain is also found in other histone acetyltransferases including p300/CBP which share a similar fold but differ in catalytic properties and cofactor requirements [[cite:PUB00051225]]. Members of this family show conservation across most eukaryotic fungi.

name: Catenin-beta-like, Arm-motif containing nuclear
description: CTNNBL is a family of eukaryotic nuclear proteins of the catenin-beta-like 1 type that contain an armadillo motif. A human nuclear protein with this domain ([swissprot:Q8WYA6]) is thought to have a role in apoptosis [[cite:PUB00017164]]. The interaction of CTNNBL1 with its known partners (the Prp19-CDC5L complex and AID) is mediated by recognition of NLS (nuclear localisation signal) motifs. The RNA-splicing factor Prp31 is also an interactor, with recognition also occurring through the NLS. CTNNBL1 uses its central armadillo (ARM) domain to bind NLS-containing partners [[cite:PUB00110056],[cite:PUB00110057]].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF1719)
description: This is a domain of unknown function. It may have a role in ATPase activation.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF1720)
description: This domain is found in different combinations with cortical patch components EF hand, SH3 and ENTH and is therefore likely to be involved in cytoskeletal processes. This family contains many hypothetical proteins.

name: DASH complex subunit Hsk3 like
description: The DASH complex is a ~10 subunit microtubule-binding complex that is transferred to the kinetochore prior to mitosis [[cite:PUB00017174]]. In Saccharomyces cerevisiae DASH forms both rings and spiral structures on microtubules in vitro [[cite:PUB00033281],[cite:PUB00033282]]. This family also includes several higher eukaryotic proteins. However, other DASH subunits do not appear to be conserved in higher eukaryotes.

name: Epoxyqueuosine reductase QueG, DUF1730
description: This domain of unknown function occurs in Epoxyqueuosine reductase QueG, an iron-sulfur cluster-binding protein, together with the 4Fe-4S binding domain ([pfam:PF00037]). QueG catalyses the conversion of epoxyqueuosine (oQ) to queuosine (Q), which is a hypermodified base found in the wobble positions of tRNA(Asp), tRNA(Asn), tRNA(His) and tRNA(Tyr) [[cite:PUB00058202]].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF1731)
description: This domain of unknown function appears towards the C-terminus of proteins of the NAD dependent epimerase/dehydratase family ([pfam:PF01370]) in bacteria, eukaryotes and archaea. Many of the proteins in which it is found are involved in cell-division inhibition.

name: Endoribonuclease YicC-like, C-terminal
description: This domain is found at the C-terminal end of Endoribonuclease YicC from Escherichia coli and similar bacterial sequences. YicC, which is important for cells in the stationary phase, and essential for growth at high temperatures [[cite:PUB00020576]], contributes to degradation of the small RNA (sRNA) RhyB via collaboration with the exoribonuclease PNPase [[cite:PUB00151089]] and seems to generate a 3'-OH and a 5'-phosphate group [[cite:PUB00151088]].

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1722)
description: This domain of unknown function is found in bacteria and archaea and is homologous to the hypothetical protein ybgA from E. coli.

name: Methanogenesis regulatory protein FilR1, middle domain
description: This archaeal domain of unknown function has been found at the middle of Methanogenesis regulatory protein FilR1 [[cite:PUB00091155],[cite:PUB00098067]] and at the C-terminus of archaeal proteins, including several transcriptional regulators of the ArsR family (see [pfam:PF01022]). FilR1 is a member of the two-component regulatory system FilI/FilRs which is involved in the regulation of methanogenesis.

name: tRNA(Met) cytidine acetyltransferase TmcA, N-terminal
description: This domain of unknown function is often found at the N-terminal of the bacterial tRNA(Met) cytidine acetyltransferase TmcA. TmcA catalyses the formation of N(4)-acetylcytidine (ac4C) at the wobble position of tRNA(Met) by using acetyl-CoA as an acetyl donor and either ATP or GTP [[cite:PUB00050413],[cite:PUB00056806],[cite:PUB00107449]]. This modification is thought to ensure precise recognition of the AUG codon by strengthening C-G base-pair interaction and also prevent misrecognition of the near cognate AUA codon [[cite:PUB00050413]]. This domain is also found in mammalian N-acetyltransferase 10 (NAT10) and fungal protein Kre33. Kre33 and NAT10 are RNA cytosine acetyltransferases with specificity toward both 18S rRNA and tRNAs and contain additional putative nuclear and nucleolar localisation signals (NLS and NoLS respectively) [[cite:PUB00076725],[cite:PUB00076726],[cite:PUB00107449]].

name: MurT ligase C-terminal
description: This entry represents the C-terminal domain of MurT ligase from Gram-positive bacteria. MurT is part of the bi-enzymatic complex MurT-GatD involved in the amidation of the alpha-carboxyl group of the D-isoglutamate residue in Lipid II in the peptidoglycan layer to produce D-isoglutamine. This domain contains an aspartate at position 349, the third residue in the catalytic triad GatD-C94, GatD-H189, MurT-D349. This C-terminal domain is built around a central six-stranded, predominantly parallel beta-sheet that is sandwiched between four alpha-helices on one side and two alpha-helices on the other. The MurT-GatD heterodimer adopts a boomerang-shaped conformation, with GatD packing against the C-terminal domain of MurT [[cite:PUB00094480]].

name: Fatty acid synthase subunit beta/Fas1-like, helical
description: This domain has been identified in fungi and bacteria. It is found in fatty acid synthase beta subunit from fungi, including Fas1 from yeasts and aflB from Aspergillus parasiticus. This is an inserted helical domain, whose function is not clear, and is found together with the MaoC-like domain ([pfam:PF01575]) and the acyltransferase domain ([pfam:PF00698]) [[cite:PUB00016843]]. Fas1 is a fatty acid synthetase that catalyses the formation of long-chain fatty acids from acetyl-CoA, malonyl-CoA and NADPH [[cite:PUB00006544]]. AflB is part of the gene cluster that mediates the biosynthesis of aflatoxins [[cite:PUB00083132]].

name: N-terminal domain of anti-restriction factor ArdC
description: This is the ssDNA binding domain of anti-restriction factor ArdC deployed by plasmids and phages in polyvalent proteins related to the BHD domains of XPC/Rad4 and the Tc-38 domain found in kinetoplastid minicircle binding proteins [[cite:PUB00098071],[cite:PUB00091133],[cite:PUB00098072]]. The structure of this domain is composed of three alpha-helices and a three-stranded beta-sheet that supports a long and protuberant beta-hairpin [[cite:PUB00098072]]. This domain is also found in the N-terminal region of the RP4 TraC1 primase [[cite:PUB00043496]], together with the Toprim domain (pfam:PF01751, pfam:PF13362 and pfam:PF13662).

name: Protein O-mannosyl-transferase TMTC, DUF1736
description: This domain of unknown function is found in O-mannosyl -transferases TMTC1-4, and constitutes a loop between TM7 and TM8 located in the ER lumen that contains a small hydrophobic, but not membrane-embedded helix. This loop is critical for catalysis and binding of ligands, especially the lipid-linked sugar moiety [[cite:PUB00098068]]. TMTCs transfers mannosyl residues to the hydroxyl group of serine or threonine residues. The 4 members of the TMTC family are O-mannosyl-transferases acting primarily on the cadherin superfamily; each member has distinct roles in decorating the cadherin domains with O-linked mannose glycans at specific regions. These proteins also act as O-mannosyl-transferase on other proteins such as PDIA3 [[cite:PUB00098069]].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF1737)
description: This domain of unknown function is found at the N-terminus of bacterial and viral hypothetical proteins.

name: NRDE-2, necessary for RNA interference
description: This is a family of eukaryotic proteins. Eukaryotic cells express a wide variety of endogenous small regulatory RNAs that regulate heterochromatin formation, developmental timing, defence against parasitic nucleic acids, and genome rearrangement. Many small regulatory RNAs are thought to function in nuclei, and in plants and fungi small interfering (si)RNAs associate with nascent transcripts and direct chromatin and/or DNA modifications. This family protein, NRDE-2, is required for small interfering (si)RNA-mediated silencing in nuclei. NRDE-2 associates with the Argonaute protein NRDE-3 within nuclei and is recruited by NRDE-3/siRNA complexes to nascent transcripts that have been targeted by RNA interference, RNAi, the process whereby double-stranded RNA (dsRNA) directs the sequence-specific degradation of mRNA [[cite:PUB00057435]].

name: Armadillo-like helical domain-containing protein 3, C-terminal
description: This is the C-terminal domain of Armadillo-like helical domain- containing protein 3 (ARMH3), the previously uncharacterised peripheral Golgi protein C10orf76. ARMH3 interacts with and is involved in GBF1 recruitment, Golgi maintenance and protein secretion [[cite:PUB00098076]]. The function of this domain is unknown.

name: AAA-ATPase Vps4-associated protein 1
description: Vps Four-Associated 1, Vfa1, in yeast, is an endosomal protein that interacts with the AAA-ATPase Vps4. It would seem to be involved in regulating the trafficking of other proteins to the endocytic vacuole [[cite:PUB00066734]]. There is a CCCH zinc finger at the N-terminus.

name: TiaS FLD domain
description: This is the FLD domain found in tRNA(Ile2) 2-agmatinylcytidine synthetase TiaS. TiaS is an archaeal ATP-dependent agmatine transferase that catalyses the formation of 2-agmatinylcytidine (agm2C) at the wobble position (C34) of tRNA(Ile2) [[cite:PUB00056803],[cite:PUB00154283],[cite:PUB00106019]]. This modified base specifically recognises AUA codons. TiaS consists of four domains, the TCKD domain ([pfam:PF22641]) at the N-terminal followed by the FLD domain, an OB fold domain and a zinc ribbon domain (ZRD) domain at the C-terminal [[cite:PUB00154283]]. This domain is responsible for agmantine binding [[cite:PUB00056803]].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF1744)
description: This domain is found at the C-terminal of the epsilon catalytic subunit of DNA polymerase. It is found C terminal to [pfam:PF03104] and [pfam:PF00136].

name: FIST N domain
description: The FIST N domain is a novel sensory domain, which is present in signal transduction proteins from Bacteria, Archaea and Eukarya. Chromosomal proximity of FIST-encoding genes to those coding for proteins involved in amino acid metabolism and transport suggest that FIST domains bind small ligands, such as amino acids [[cite:PUB00044261]].

name: Fungal domain of unknown function (DUF1746)
description: This is a fungal domain of unknown function. This domain can be found in DSC E3 ubiquitin ligase complex subunit 4 (Dsc4) from S. pombe, a component of the DSC E3 ubiquitin ligase complex required for the sre1 transcriptional activator proteolytic cleavage to release the soluble transcription factor from the membrane in low oxygen or sterol conditions. The complex plays also an important role in the multivesicular body (MVB) pathway and functions in a post-endoplasmic reticulum pathway for protein degradation [[cite:PUB00075404]]. This domain is also found in GLD1 from S. cerevisiae, also a component of the DSC E3 ubiquitin ligase complex involved in the targeting of the DSC complex to the Golgi apparatus and endosome membranes via the AP3 pathway to ubiquitinate Golgi/endosome membrane proteins [[cite:PUB00098082]].

name: Histone chaperone Rttp106-like, middle domain
description: This Pleckstrin homology (PH) domain is found in the middle region of Rttp106, a histone chaperone involved in heterochromatin-mediated silencing [[cite:PUB00033392]]. It is also found in the final part of the middle domain of various FACT (facilitates chromatin transactions) complex subunits, such as Spt16 and either Pob3 (yeast) or the related SSRP1 (higher eukaryotes). This domain plays a role in DNA binding [[cite:PUB00101033],[cite:PUB00101035],[cite:PUB00101032]].

name: Mitofissin
description: This is a family of fungal proteins identified as mitochondrial fission factors (mitofissin, also referred to as Atg44) which are essential for mitophagy. Mitofissin directly binds to lipid membranes to drive mitochondrial fission required for mitophagy [[cite:PUB00151415]].

name: BT_3987-like, N-terminal domain
description: This domain, previously known as DUF1735, is found in a number of proteins mainly found in firmicutes, including BT_3987 from Bacteroides thetaiotaomicron, which displays hydrolytic activity against Hy-type N-glycans, probably initiating the degradation of this type of glycan in the human gut [[cite:PUB00152803]]. This domain adopts a beta-sandwich fold.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1749)
description: This is a plant and fungal family of unknown function. This family contains many hypothetical proteins.

name: SWI/SNF and RSC complexes subunit Ssr4 N-terminal
description: This entry represents the N-terminal domain of SWI/SNF and RSC complexes subunit Ssr4 from S. pombe, a essential member of the chromatin structure remodelling complex (RSC) and the SWI/SNF complex [[cite:PUB00066307],[cite:PUB00101211]]. The structure of this domain revealed that it has a novel fold comprising an antiparallel beta-sheet of seven strands with alpha-helices on one side and random coil on the other [[cite:PUB00101211]]. It contains the highly conserved motif WxxxxxPxxGxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxDG. RSC is involved in transcription regulation and nucleosome positioning which controls, particularly, membrane and organelle development genes. The ATP-dependent chromatin remodelling complex SWI/SNF is required for the positive and negative regulation of gene expression of a large number of genes through the regulation of nucleosome remodelling [[cite:PUB00066307]].

name: Nitrogen regulatory protein areA, GATA-like domain
description: This entry represents fungal proteins containing GATA domains, including nitrogen regulatory protein areA, a transcription activator that binds the consensus DNA element 5'-CGATAG-3' and mediates nitrogen metabolite repression [[cite:PUB00089490]]. This entry also contains the Negative regulator of RAS-cAMP pathway MKS1 from yeast that is thought to be a negative regulator of RAS-cAMP pathway.

name: Eukaryotic integral membrane protein (DUF1751)
description: This entry represents an integral membrane domain found in eukaryotic proteins. [swissprot:Q12239], a Saccharomyces cerervisiae protein, has been shown to localise COP II vesicles [[cite:PUB00016470]]. This protein has a predicted structure which shows similiarity to the rhomboid proteases.

name: Inositolphosphorylceramide synthase subunit Kei1
description: Kei1 is a subunit of Saccharomyces cerevisiae inositol phosphorylceramide (IPC) synthase [[cite:PUB00092487]]. It is localised to the Golgi and is cleaved by the late Golgi processing endopeptidase Kex2 [[cite:PUB00092487]]. Kei1 is essential for both the activity and the Golgi localization of IPC synthase [[cite:PUB00092487]].

name: FAM32A
description: FAM32A, also known as OTAG12, has been linked to ovarian tumour in humans and mice [[cite:PUB00092488]].

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1757)
description: This family of proteins are about 150 amino acids in length and have no known function.

name: Uncharacterised protein family, YAP/Alf4/glomulin
description: This entry contains a number of protein families with apparently unrelated functions. These include the YAP binding proteins of yeasts. These are stress response and redox homeostasis proteins, induced by hydrogen peroxide or induced in response to alkylating agent methyl methanesulphonate (MMS) [[cite:PUB00053725]] [[cite:PUB00053726]]. The family includes Aberrant root formation protein 4 (Alf4) of Arabidopsis thaliana (Mouse-ear cress), which is required for the initiation of lateral roots independent from auxin signalling. It may also function in maintaining the pericycle in the mitotically competent state needed for lateral root formation [[cite:PUB00053727]]. The family includes glomulin (FAP68), which is essential for normal development of the vasculature and may represent a naturally occurring ligand of the immunophilins FKBP59 and FKBP12 [[cite:PUB00044263]] [[cite:PUB00053728]].

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1761)
description: Family of conserved fungal and bacterial membrane proteins with unknown function.

name: Transcription factor Iwr1
description: Iwr1 is involved in transcription from polymerase II promoters; it interacts with with most of the polymerase II subunits [[cite:PUB00054162]]. Deletion of this protein results in hypersensitivity to the K1 killer toxin [[cite:PUB00033286]].

name: Eukaryotic protein of unknown function (DUF1764)
description: This is a family of eukaryotic proteins of unknown function. This family contains many hypothetical proteins.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1765)
description: This region represents a conserved region found in hypothetical proteins from fungi, mycetozoa and entamoebidae.

name: Cytochrome c oxidase biogenesis protein Cmc1 like
description: Cmc1 is a metallo-chaperone like protein which is known to localise to the inner mitochondrial membrane in Saccharomyces cerevisiae. It is essential for full expression of cytochrome c oxidase and respiration [[cite:PUB00044676]]. Cmc1 contains two Cx9C motifs and is able to bind copper(I). Cmc1 is thought to play a role in mitochondrial copper trafficking and transfer to cytochrome c oxidase [[cite:PUB00044676]].

name: RMI1, N-terminal OB-fold domain
description: This is the OB-fold domain found at the N-terminal of RecQ-mediated genome instability protein 1 (RMI1), which forms a stable complex with Bloom syndrome protein BLM and DNA topoisomerase 3-alpha [[cite:PUB00075424],[cite:PUB00075425],[cite:PUB00058799]].

name: Domain of unknown function at the cortex 1 (Duc1)
description: This entry represents the Duc1 (Domain of Unknown Function at the Cortex 1) protein, which is involved in maintaining proper plasma membrane lipid composition and cytokinetic ring anchoring in Schizosaccharomyces pombe [[cite:PUB00155608]]. Duc1 localizes to the plasma membrane, except at the cell division site, and its localization is controlled by interactions with the ER-PM contact site proteins Scs2 and Scs22 through a FFAT-like motif. Duc1 promotes proper localization of the PI-5 kinase Its3, thereby maintaining appropriate levels of PI(4,5)P2 at the plasma membrane. This function is important for proper anchoring of the cytokinetic ring during cell division. Duc1 contains a conserved domain previously known as the DUF1769 domain of unknown function.

name: Autophagy receptor ATG43
description: This family represents the autophagy receptor ATG43 from fungi. It is a mitochondrial outer membrane protein which serves as a mitophagy receptor to promote the selective degradation of mitochondria.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF1771)
description: This domain is highly charged and may represent a small helical extension of the Smr domain ([pfam:PF01713]), known as N-ext, whose function is not yet clear [[cite:PUB00098095]].

name: Anthrone oxygenase
description: This family consists of anthrone oxygenases found in bacteria and fungi, and involved in the synthesis of different products. GedH from Aspergillus terreus is part of the gene cluster that mediates the biosynthesis of geodin [[cite:PUB00081405]], EncC from Neosartorya fumigata is involved in the biosynthesis of endocrocin [[cite:PUB00081406]], and MdpH from Aspergillus nidulans in the biosynthesis of monodictyphenone [[cite:PUB00081407]].

name: Mug135-like, C-terminal domain
description: This entry represents the C-terminal domain found in Meiotically up-regulated gene 135 protein from Schizosaccharomyces pombe (Mug135, also known as Tdk1, O74876) and similar fungal proteins that are annotated as meiotically up-regulated gene products. Mug135 is a killer meiotic driver (KMD), a selfish genetic element that by selectively kills meiotic products lacking its gene, thereby promoting its own propagation. This protein exists in a nontoxic tetrameric form during vegetative growth and meiosis but transforms into a distinct toxic form in spores [[cite:PUB00159004],[cite:PUB00159007]]. These proteins generally contain a long coiled-coil region with this domain found at the C-terminus.

name: Fungal protein of unknown function (DUF1774)
description: This is a fungal family of unknown function.

name: Fungal family of unknown function (DUF1776)
description: This is a fungal family of unknown function. One of the proteins in this family [swissprot:P32792] has been localised to the mitochondria [[cite:PUB00033287]].

name: U4/U6.U5 small nuclear ribonucleoproteins
description: This is a family of eukaryotic proteins including U4/U6.U5 small nuclear ribonucleoprotein 27 kDa protein may play a role in mRNA splicing [[cite:PUB00084347]].

name: Sporulation protein SpoIIT
description: This entry represents sporulation protein SpoIIT and related proteins. TATA-box_bdg is a family of bacterial proteins.SpoIIT from Bacillus subtilis contains a circularly permuted TATA-box binding protein-like fold. It participates in cell-cell signalling pathways during sporulation. It functions in the SpoIIGA-dependent proteolytic activation of sigma E in the mother cell [[cite:PUB00162567]].

name: Antitoxin TacA 1-like
description: This protein family includes Antitoxin TacA 1 from Salmonella typhimurium and similar short sequences mainly found in bacteria. TacA1, the antitoxin component of a type II toxin -antitoxin (TA) system, counteracts the toxic effect of cognate toxin TacT1. TacT1 is active in complex with its antitoxin, acetylation of this antitoxin upregulates the acetylation of tRNAs by TacT1 [[cite:PUB00158919],[cite:PUB00158918]].

name: Putative endonuclease, protein of unknown function (DUF1780)
description: This is a family of uncharacterised proteins. The structure of a hypothetical protein from Pseudomonas aeruginosa has shown it to adopt an alpha/beta fold, placing it in the Endonuclease superfamily/clan of restriction endonucleases.

name: Microtubule-binding calmodulin-regulated spectrin-associated
description: This is the C-terminal domain of a family of eumetazoan proteins collectively defined as calmodulin-regulated spectrin-associated, or CAMSAP, proteins. CAMSAP proteins carry an N-terminal region that includes the CH domain, a central region including a predicted coiled-coil and this C-terminal, or CKK, domain - defined as being present in CAMSAP, KIAA1078 and KIAA1543, The C-terminal domain is the part of the CAMSAP proteins that binds to microtubules. The domain appears to act by producing inhibition of neurite extension, probably by blocking microtubule function. CKK represents a domain that has evolved with the metazoa. The structure of a murine hypothetical protein from RIKEN cDNA has shown the domain to adopt a mainly beta barrel structure with an associated alpha-helical hairpin.

name: Ubiquitin-fold modifier-conjugating enzyme 1
description: Ubiquitin-like (UBL) post-translational modifiers are covalently linked to most, if not all, target protein(s) through an enzymatic cascade analogous to ubiquitylation, consisting of E1 (activating), E2 (conjugating), and E3 (ligating) enzymes. Ubiquitin-fold modifier 1 (Ufm1) a ubiquitin-like protein is activated by a novel E1-like enzyme, Uba5, by forming a high-energy thioester bond. Activated Ufm1 is then transferred to its cognate E2-like enzyme, Ufc1, in a similar thioester linkage. This family represents the E2-like enzyme.

name: Cytochrome oxidase complex assembly protein 1
description: Coa1 is an inner mitochondrial membrane protein that associates with Shy1 and is required for cytochrome oxidase complex IV assembly. It contains a conserved hydrophobic segment (amino acids 74-92) with the potential to form a membrane-spanning helix. The N-terminus of Coa1 is rich in positively charged amino acids and could form an amphipathic alpha helix, characteristic of a mitochondrial presequence. A cleavage site for the mitochondrial processing peptidase is predicted adjacent to the presequence. Upon in vitro import into mitochondria, Coa1 is processed to a mature form, indicating that it possesses a cleavable presequence [[cite:PUB00053933]]. The eukaryotic cytochrome oxidase complex consists of 12-13 subunits, with three mitochondrial encoded subunits, Cox1-Cox3, forming the core enzyme. Translation of the Cox1 transcript requires the two promoters, Pet309 and Mss51, and the latter has an additional role in translational elongation. Coa1 is necessary for linking the activity of Mss51 to Cox1 insertion into the assembly complex [[cite:PUB00053932]].

name: Fcf2 pre-rRNA processing
description: This is a family of eukaryotic nucleolar proteins that are involved in pre-rRNA processing [[cite:PUB00035397]].

name: Argonaute linker 1 domain
description: ArgoL1 is a region found in argonaute [[cite:PUB00035384]] proteins. It normally co-occurs with [pfam:PF02179] and [pfam:PF02171]. It is a linker region between the N-terminal and the PAZ domains. It contains an alpha-helix packed against a three-stranded antiparallel beta-sheet with two long beta-strands (beta8 and beta9) of the sheet spanning one face of the adjacent N and PAZ domains. L1 together with linker 2, L2, PAZ and ArgoN forms a compact global fold [[cite:PUB00038652]].

name: NADAR domain
description: This is a domain of unknown function, it has been named been named the NADAR (NAD and ADP-ribose) domain [[cite:PUB00079392]].

name: Putative pyruvate format-lyase activating enzyme (DUF1786)
description: This family is annotated as pyruvate formate-lyase activating enzyme ([ec:1.97.1.4]) in UniProt. It is not clear where this annotation comes from.

name: C8 domain
description: This domain contains 8 conserved cysteine residues, but this family only contains 7 of them to overlaps with other domains. It is found in disease-related proteins including von Willebrand factor, Alpha tectorin, Zonadhesin and Mucin. It is often found on proteins containing [pfam:PF00094] and [pfam:PF01826].

name: PINc domain ribonuclease
description: This is a family of bacterial and archaeal PINc domains. PIN domains are characterised by the conservation of three acidic residues, possibly four, an Asp at residue 13, a Glu at 63, and then Asps at 172 and 194 in UniProtKB:Q58360. Family members include Homologs of Aquifex RNase P (HARP) proteins [[cite:PUB00091006]].

name: BREX protein BrxB
description: This family includes BREX protein BrxB from Bacillus cereus, which is part of a type 1 BREX (bacteriophage exclusion) system, a system that provides immunity against bacteriophage, which allows phage adsorption but prevents phage DNA replication, without degradation of the phage DNA [[cite:PUB00093365]]. The exact function of BrxB is not clear.

name: Phage tail assembly chaperone
description: This is a family of phage tail assembly chaperone proteins largely from phage T1 Gp40.

name: Glycosyltransferase GT-D fold
description: This domain is found at the C terminus of proteins such as the probable glycosyltransferase Gly ([swissprot:Q9AEU2]) that also contain the glycosyl transferase domain at the N terminus. It is also found N-terminal in numerous putative glycosyltransferases such as GalT1. GalT1 has been shown to catalyse the third step of Fap1 glycosylation [[cite:PUB00081880]]. This domain is structurally distinct from all known GT folds of glycosyltransferases and contains a metal binding site. This new glycosyltransferase fold has been named GT-D [[cite:PUB00081880]].

name: THAP4-like, heme-binding beta-barrel domain
description: This domain can be found in THAP4 from mammals and At1g79260 from Arabidopsis. THAP4 catalyzes the heme-based conversion of peroxynitrite into nitrate-NO3- in vitro [[cite:PUB00095798]]. At1g79260 is a nitrophorin-like heme-binding protein that may reversibly bind nitric oxide (NO) and be involved in NO transport [[cite:PUB00063678]]. This entry also includes the beta-barrel domain of Caenorhabditis elegans protein male abnormal 7 (Mab-7) which plays an important role in determining body shape and sensory ray morphology [[cite:PUB00095799]]. Nitrobindins (Nbs), constituting a heme-protein family spanning from bacteria to Homo sapiens, display an all-beta-barrel structural organisation. Proteins containing this domain are putatively related to fatty acid-binding proteins (FABPs) [[cite:PUB00040845]].

name: DcrB
description: DcrB is a bacterial protein required for phages C1 and C6 adsorption [[cite:PUB00063631],[cite:PUB00063632]]. It may be involved in the opening or formation of diffusion channels in the outer membrane [[cite:PUB00063632]]. Structurally, it consist of an antiparallel beta sheet with some alpha helical regions.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1797)
description: This is a domain of unknown function. It forms a central anti-parallel beta sheet with flanking alpha helical regions.

name: Bacterial domain of unknown function (DUF1798)
description: This domain is found in many hypothetical proteins. The structure of one of the proteins in this family has been solved and it adopts an all alpha helical fold.

name: Phage related hypothetical protein (DUF1799)
description: Members of this family are about 100 amino acids in length and are uncharacterised.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1800)
description: This is a family of large bacterial proteins of unknown function.

name: Domain of unknown function (DU1801)
description: This domain is found in the Intracellular iron chaperone frataxin YdhG [[cite:PUB00098100]] and the uncharacterised protein YdeI from Bacillus subtilis.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF1802)
description: The function of this family is unknown. This region is found associated with a [pfam:PF04471] suggesting they could be part of a restriction modification system..

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF1803)
description: This small domain is found in one or two copies in proteins from bacteria. The function of this domain is unknown.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1804)
description: This family of bacterial protein is uncharacterised.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF1805)
description: This domain is found in bacteria and archaea and has an N terminal tetramerisation region that is composed of beta sheets.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1806)
description: This is a bacterial family of uncharacterised proteins. The structure of one of the proteins in this family has been solved and it adopts a beta barrel-like structure.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1810)
description: This is a family of uncharacterised proteins. The structure of one of the members in this family has been solved and it adopts a mainly alpha helical structure.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1811)
description: This family includes uncharacterised proteins predominantly found in Firmicutes, including Uncharacterized protein YfhH from Bacillus subtilis and protein GK0453 from Geobacillus kaustophilus. GK0453 shows two small domains: an helix-turn-helix like motif is found in its N-terminal domain while an SH3-like beta-barrel like structure is observed its C-terminal region. Its specific function is unknown [[cite:PUB00100670]]. Some of the members of this protein family are annotated as transcriptional regulators (see Q3EXU7, Q81I96).

name: Fimbrillin-A associated anchor proteins Mfa1 and Mfa2
description: This family of proteins may be lipoproteins principally from bacilli. They are between 300 and 400 residues. Many Bacteroides-like bacterial species, including Porphyromonas gingivalis, the causal agent of periodontal infection, carry at least two types of fimbriae, namely FimA and Mfa1 fimbriae, following the names of their major subunit proteins [[cite:PUB00055567]]. Normally, FimA fimbriae are long filaments that are easily detached from cells, whereas Mfa1 fimbriae are short filaments that are tightly bound to cells; however, in the absence of Mfa2 protein, the Mfa1 fimbriae are also very long and are not attached. Mfa2 and Mfa1 are associated with each other in whole P. gingivalis cells to the extent that Mfa2 is located on the cell surface and probably associated with Mfa1 fimbriae in such a way that it anchors the Mfa1 fimbriae to the cell surface and regulates Mfa1 filament length [[cite:PUB00055568]].

name: Nucleotidyl transferase AbiEii toxin, Type IV TA system
description: This family was recently identified as belonging to the nucleotidyltransferase superfamily [[cite:PUB00066751]]. AbiEii is the cognate toxin of the type IV toxin-antitoxin 'innate immunity' bacterial abortive infection (Abi) system that protects bacteria from the spread of a phage infection. The Abi system is activated upon infection with phage to abort the cell thus preventing the spread of phage through viral replication. There are some 20 or more Abis, and they are predominantly plasmid-encoded lactococcal systems. TA, toxin-antitoxin, systems on plasmids function by killing cells that lose the plasmid upon division. AbiE phage resistance systems function as novel Type IV TAs and are widespread in bacteria and archaea. The cognate antitoxin is [pfam:PF13338] [[cite:PUB00075538]].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF1815)
description: This presumed domain is about 100 amino acids in length and is functionally uncharacterised.

name: Toxin SymE, type I toxin-antitoxin system
description: SymE (SOS-induced yjiW gene with similarity to MazE ) is an SOS-induced toxin. It inhibits cell growth, decreases protein synthesis and increases RNA degradation. It may play a role in the recycling of RNAs damaged under SOS response-inducing conditions. It is predicted to have an AbrB fold, similar to that of the antitoxin MazE. Its translation is repressed by the antisense RNA SymR, which acts as an antitoxin [[cite:PUB00064452],[cite:PUB00053151]].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF1816)
description: [swissprot:Q4C9H3] is associated with the [pfam:PF01383] domain suggesting this presumed domain could have a role in phycobilisomes.

name: Chlororespiratory reduction 6
description: Chlororespiratory reduction 6 (Crr6) is a factor required for the assembly or stabilisation of the chloroplast NAD(P)H dehydrogenase complex in Arabidopsis [[cite:PUB00075334]].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF1818)
description: This presumed domain is found in a small family of cyanobacterial protein. These proteins are functionally uncharacterised.

name: BrxA
description: BrxA is part of the phage resistance system BREX (Bacteriophage Exclusion). It shares structural homology with the RNA-binding antitermination protein NusB [[cite:PUB00093365]].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF1820)
description: This family includes small functionally uncharacterised proteins around 100 amino acids in length.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1822)
description: This family of proteins are functionally uncharacterised.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF1823)
description: This presumed domain is functionally uncharacterised.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF1824)
description: This uncharacterised family of proteins are principally found in cyanobacteria.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF1825)
description: This uncharacterised family of proteins are principally found in cyanobacteria.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1826)
description: These proteins are functionally uncharacterised.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF1827)
description: This presumed domain has no known function.

name: Domain of unknown function DUF1828
description: This presumed domain is functionally uncharacterised.

name: Domain of unknown function DUF1829
description: This short domain is usually associated with [pfam:PF08861].

name: ReoY-like, N-terminal domain
description: This entry represents the N-terminal domain of Peptidoglycan synthesis regulatory protein ReoY ([swissprot:Q8Y5Y2]) which is involved in the PASTA kinase-mediated signalling pathway regulating peptidoglycan synthesis to maintain cell wall integrity [[cite:PUB00104135]]. It modulates peptidoglycan (PG) synthesis pathway committed-step enzyme MurA [[cite:PUB00104135]]. ReoY positively modulates ClpCP-dependent proteolysis of MurA, thereby regulating PG synthesis and inhibiting intrinsic cephalosporin resistance [[cite:PUB00104135]].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF1830)
description: This family of short proteins is functionally uncharacterised.

name: Putative amino acid metabolism
description: Solution of the structure of the Lactobacillus plantarum protein from this family has indicated a potential new fold with remote similarities to TBP-like (TATA-binding protein) structures. This similarity, in combination with genomic context analysis, leads us to propose an involvement in amino-acid metabolism. The potentially novel fold is an alpha + beta fold comprising two beta sheets packed against a single helix. The enzyme is present in the cytosol.

name: DNA sulphur modification protein DndE
description: DndE is a small protein of 126 residues. It is a putative carboxylase homologous to NCAIR synthetase. It is encoded by an operon that is associated with a sulphur-based modification to DNA [[cite:PUB00042946]].

name: Bacteriophage Mu, Gp37
description: This family is represented by Bacteriophage Mu, Gp37 (also known as Probable tail terminator protein) which may stop tail tube polymerization by capping the rapidly polymerising tail tube once it has reached its requisite length and prevent its depolymerization [[cite:PUB00052083]]. This family also has prophages matches, such as the Gp37 protein from the FluMu prophage.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF1835)
description: This family of proteins are functionally uncharacterised.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF1833)
description: This family of proteins are functionally uncharacterised and are predicted to adopt an all-beta fold [[cite:PUB00034476]]. They are often found in gene neighborhoods containing genes for an NlpC peptidase and a Ubiquitin domain predicted to be involved in tail assembly [[cite:PUB00034476]].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF1836)
description: This protein family appears to be primarily involved in transcriptional regulation and cellular processes. Members of this family, such as the one represented by [swissprot:Q8E4L3] (gene gbs1388), exhibit high levels of transcriptional activity and may be regulated by factors like the rex gene, indicating a role in significant cellular processes [[cite:PUB00156067]]. Another member, [swissprot:A6M310], gene name cbei_4884), is implicated in strain degeneration and regulatory functions linked to sporulation and solvent formation in Clostridium beijerinckii, suggesting conservation among clostridial species [[cite:PUB00156068]]. The sgo_1308 gene encodes a protein [swissprot:A8AXS9] containing the DUF1836 domain which belongs to the helix-turn-helix (HTH) clan, hinting at its role in transcriptional regulation, specifically influencing bacterial hemolysin III [[cite:PUB00156066]].

name: HamA
description: Hachiman antiphage defense system has been described in Ralstonia solanacearum species complex (RSSC), and is composed of two genes, hamAB, which encode a protein of unknown function HamA, represented in this entry, and an helicase (HamB). Only one strain (KACC10722) from phylotype IV shows this system complete and both genes are organised in an operon [[cite:PUB00097806],[cite:PUB00097805]].

name: DUF1839 N-terminal domain
description: This entry represents a domainfound in proteins that are functionally uncharacterised. It is likely to adopt papain-like fold.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1838)
description: This family of proteins are functionally uncharacterised.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF1840)
description: This family of proteins are functionally uncharacterised.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF1842)
description: This domain is found at the N-terminus of proteins that are functionally uncharacterised.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF1841)
description: This family of proteins are functionally uncharacterised.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF1843)
description: This domain is found at the C-terminus of a family of proteins that are functionally uncharacterised. The presumed domain is about 60 amino acid residues in length and is found independently in some proteins.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF1844)
description: This family of proteins are functionally uncharacterised.

name: Transcriptional regulator AcaB
description: This family of proteins is found in the IncC family of broad-host-range plasmids which enables the spread of antibiotic resistance genes among human enteric pathogens. Recently, AcaB member has been characterised as a transcriptional regulator that plays a crucial role in the regulation of IncC conjugation. It is a DNA binding protein which binds upstream of the acaDB promoter to increase its transcription and, in turn, acaDB activates the transcription of IncC conjugation genes. Structurally, AcaB consists of two helical hairpins in tandem which assemble into an anti-parallel four-helix bundle to form a two-stranded antiparallel beta-sheet positioned parallel to the helices. This is structurally similar to bacterial transcription factors from the ribbon-helix-helix (RHH) superfamily [[cite:PUB00098625]].

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1847)
description: This family of proteins are functionally uncharacterised. THey contain 4 N-terminal cysteines that may form a zinc binding domain.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF1848)
description: This family of proteins are functionally uncharacterised. The C-terminus contains a cluster of cysteines that are similar to the iron-sulfur cluster found at the N-terminus of [pfam:PF04055].

name: Domain of unknown function DUF1846, N-terminal
description: This domain is found in a family of proteins that are functionally uncharacterised, known as UPF0371. Some members of the family are annotated as ATP-dependent peptidases. This is a P-loop-like domain (pdbe:3BH1).

name: EipB-like
description: This entry includes a group of bacterial proteins, including EipB from Brucella. EipB is a periplasmic protein that functions as part of a system required for cell envelope homeostasis. It adopts a beta-spiral fold, consisting of 14 beta-strands and 2 alpha-helices [[cite:PUB00092848]].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF1850)
description: This family of proteins are functionally uncharacterised. Some members of this family appear to be misannotated as RocC an amino acid transporter from B. subtilis.

name: T6SS immunity protein Tdi1, C-terminal
description: This domain is found at the C-terminal region of the type VI secretion system (T6SS) immunity protein Tdi1 from Agrobacterium tumefaciens (Atu4351, [swissprot:Q7CUQ2]) and similar bacterial proteins Tdi1 is organised into a N-terminal GAD-related domain ([pfam:PF08887]) and a C-terminal domain likely to exist as an insertion in the GAD-like domain. This domain shows a two-stranded antiparallel beta-sheet and four helices. A positive groove that extends to both domains may be associated with nucleotide binding [[cite:PUB00100858]].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF1853)
description: This family of proteins are functionally uncharacterised.

name: Putative oxygenase MesX
description: This family represents MesX, the putative oxygenase component of an oxygen-dependent methionine synthase MesD. It is required for MesD for activity [[cite:PUB00097274]].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF1854)
description: This potential domain is functionally uncharacterised. It is found at the C-terminus of a number of ATP transporter proteins suggesting this domain may be involved in ligand binding.

name: Aida N-terminus
description: This is the N-terminal domain of the axin interactor, dorsalization-associated protein family [[cite:PUB00053882]].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF1904)
description: This domain is found in a set of hypothetical bacterial proteins.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF1905)
description: This domain is found in a set of hypothetical bacterial proteins.

name: Rv2525c-like, glycoside hydrolase-like domain
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised bacterial proteins, including the putative peptidoglycan hydrolase Rv2525c from Mycobacterium tuberculosis [[cite:PUB00100887],[cite:PUB00100886]]. It has been proposed to function as a peptidoglycan hydrolase with glycosidase activity regarding structural studies showed that this domain has a typical TIM-barrel-like fold, characteristic of glycoside hydrolases [[cite:PUB00100887]]. However, it displays esterase activity toward p-nitrophenyl esters of various acyl chain length in vitro [[cite:PUB00100886]].

name: Domain of Unknown Function (DUF1907)
description: The structure of this domain displays an alpha-beta-beta-alpha four layer topology, with an HxHxxxxxxxxxH motif that coordinates a zinc ion, and an acetate anion at a site that likely supports the enzymatic activity of an ester hydrolase [[cite:PUB00035389]].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF1908)
description: This domain is found in a set of hypothetical/structural eukaryotic proteins.

name: PoNe immunity protein (PoNi), N-terminal
description: This entry represents the N-terminal domain of the PoNe immunity proteins (PoNi) which antagonise the DNAse toxin PoNe (Polymorphic Nuclease effector) [[cite:PUB00099821]]. PoNi proteins may directly interact with PoNe.

name: PoNe immunity proteins (PoNi), C-terminal
description: This entry represents the C-terminal domain of the PoNe immunity proteins (PoNi), which antagonize the DNAse toxin PoNe (Polymorphic Nuclease effector) [[cite:PUB00099821]]. PoNi proteins may directly interact with PoNe.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF1912)
description: This domain has no known function. It is found in various Streptococcal proteins.

name: Lactophage receptor-binding protein C-terminal head domain
description: Caudo_bapla_RBP is a family of proteins expressed from ORF18 of the Lactococcus P2-like phage. This is one of three protein domains, shoulders, neck, and head, that form the phage tail base-plate. In the overall structure this head domain exists as six trimers, and is necessary for specific recognition of the receptors at the host cell surface. Siphoviridae are the P2-like Caudovirales of Lactococcus [[cite:PUB00054437]]. This family now includes DUF1914. Family Baseplate, [pfam:PF16774], is the ORF15 or shoulder component of the base-plate complex.

name: Monodechloroaminopyrrolnitrin synthase PrnB
description: This protein family includes Monodechloroaminopyrrolnitrin synthase PrnB from Pseudomonas fluorescens and similar bacterial proteins. PrnB is involved in the biosynthesis of the antifungal compound pyrrolnitrin. It is organised into two domains: a small N-terminal capping domain that consists of 7 alpha-helices and the core helical domain, which is related to myoglobin. PrnB shows structural homology to the heme b-dependent two-domain indoleamine 2,3-dioxygenase enzyme (IDO, [pfam:PF01231]) and to the tryptophan 2,3-dioxygenase (TDO, [pfam:PF03301]) family [[cite:PUB00049615],[cite:PUB00054440]].

name: Viral protein VP4 subunit
description: This domain is predominantly found in viral proteins from the family Picornaviridae. It is VP4 of the viral polyprotein which, in poliovirus, is part of the capsid that consists of 60 copies each of four proteins VP1, VP2, VP3, and VP4 arranged on an icosahedral lattice [[cite:PUB00109098]]. VP4 is on the inside and differs from the others in being small, myristoylated and having an extended structure. Productive infection involves the externalisation of the VP4, which is cleaved from the rest, along with the N-terminus of VP1. There thus seem to be three stages of the virus, ie a multi-step process for cell entry involving RNA translocation through a membrane channel formed by the externalised N termini of VP1 [[cite:PUB00109099]].

name: Thoeris protein ThsB, TIR-like domain
description: Thoeris is a bacterial antiphage defense system, which consists of two genes, thsA and thsB, via NAD+ degradation [[cite:PUB00097806],[cite:PUB00101118],[cite:PUB00101117]]. ThsA has robust NAD+ cleavage activity and and a two-domain architecture containing a N-terminal NAD-binding domain (denoted as sirtuin-like or Macro) and C-terminal SLOG-like domain. In some instances, such as in B. amyloliquefaciens ThsA has an N-terminal transmembrane domain [[cite:PUB00097806]]. ThsB (also referred to as TIR1 and TIR2) is structurally similar to TIR domain proteins but without enzymatic activity. This is the TIR-like domain of ThsB proteins, which adopts a Rossmann-like fold. ThsB is responsible for recognizing phage infection [[cite:PUB00101118]].

name: HBS1 N-terminus
description: This domain is found at the N-terminus of HBS1 proteins. It interacts with the ribosomal protein rpS3 at the mRNA entry site [[cite:PUB00066737]].

name: Basophilic leukemia-expressed protein Bles03
description: This domain is found in Basophilic leukemia-expressed protein Bles03 from humans (also known as UPF0696 protein C11orf68, [swissprot:Q9H3H3]) and various proteins from eukaryotes, bacteria and archaea. Bles03 has been suggested to have phosphothreonine lyase activity and to play a role in the biosynthesis of dehydro amino acids [[cite:PUB00039014]]. It shows a two-layer sandwich architecture with a a nine-stranded beta-sheet and three alpha-helices on each side [[cite:PUB00100679]].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF1918)
description: This domain, found in various hypothetical bacterial proteins, has no known function.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF1919)
description: This domain has no known function. It is found in various hypothetical and putative bacterial proteins. The structure of this domain is known (PDB:2g6t).

name: Bacteriophage PRD1, P5, spike N-terminal
description: The spike structure of bacteriophage PRD1 is comprised of proteins P2, P5, and P31. P5 is an elongated multidomain trimer. This domain is found at the N-terminal of bacteriophage PRD1 spike protein P5 and mediates the interaction with protein P31. The C-terminal domain appears to contain the residues responsible for the trimerization of the protein [[cite:PUB00032209],[cite:PUB00088279]].

name: Bacteriophage PRD1, spike protein P5, C-terminal
description: This domain is found at the C-terminal of bacteriophage PRD1 spike protein P5. [[cite:PUB00032209]]. The spike structure of bacteriophage PRD1 is comprised of proteins P2, P5, and P31. P5 is an elongated multidomain trimer. This C-terminal domain appears to contain the residues responsible for the trimerization of the protein [[cite:PUB00032209],[cite:PUB00088279]].

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1861)
description: This hypothetical protein, found in bacteria and in the eukaryote Leishmania, has no known function.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF1866)
description: This domain, found in Synaptojanin, has no known function.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF1899)
description: This set of domains is found in various eukaryotic proteins. Function is unknown.

name: Trimerisation motif
description: This domain is predominantly found in the structural protein coronin, and is duplicated in some sequences. It appears to have the function of stabilising the topology of short coiled-coils in proteins [[cite:PUB00035387]].

name: BofC C-terminal domain
description: The C-terminal domain of the bacterial protein 'bypass of forespore C' contains a three-stranded beta-sheet and three alpha-helices. Its exact function is, as yet, unknown [[cite:PUB00035362]].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF1869)
description: This domain is found in a set of hypothetical bacterial proteins.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF1871)
description: This set of hypothetical proteins is produced by prokaryotes pertaining to the Bacillus genus.

name: STIV B116-like
description: The sulfolobus turreted icosahedral virus (STIV) infects Sulfolobus species found in the hot springs of Yellowstone National Park. It has 37 ORFs including B116, whose function is unknown. The structure of B116 reveals a fold consisting of a five-stranded beta-sheet flanked on one side by three alpha helices. Two subunits come together to form a homodimer with a 10-stranded mixed beta-sheet, where the topology of the central strands resembles an unclosed beta-barrel [[cite:PUB00041899]].

name: Nuclear receptor-binding factor 2, autophagy regulator
description: NRBF2 plays an essential role in autophagy, the cellular pathway that degrades long-lived proteins and other cytoplasmic contents through lysosomes. NRBF2 binds Atg14L - a Beclin-binding protein - directly via the MIT domain and enhances Atg14L-linked Vps34 kinase (a class III phosphatidylinositol-3 kinase) activity and autophagy induction [[cite:PUB00078728]].

name: Rv2632c-like
description: This entry includes a set of Actinobacterial proteins, including Rv2632c from Mycobacterium tuberculosis that is strongly implicated in the onset of non-replicating persistence, and thereby latent tuberculosis. Rv2632c contains a dsRBD-like (2 layers alpha/beta) fold (PDBe:2fgg). It shares remarkable similarity with bacterial hibernation factors, despite very low sequence similarity. Based on this structure it was predicted that Rv1738, highly up-regulated in conditions that mimic the onset of persistence, helps trigger dormancy by association with the bacterial ribosome [[cite:PUB00097447]].

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1878)
description: This domain is found in a set of hypothetical bacterial proteins.

name: Beta/Gamma crystallin
description: This family of beta/gamma crystallins includes the N-terminal domain of Dictyostelium discoideum Calcium-dependent cell adhesion molecule 1 ([swissprot:P54657]), which mediates cell-cell adhesion through homophilic interactions [[cite:PUB00038511]].

name: Aca2/YdiL-like
description: This domain is found in Aca2 repressor from Pectobacterium phage ZF40, the uncharacterised protein YdiL from Escherichia coli and related sequences. Aca2 regulates the transcription and translation of phage anti-CRISPR acrIF8 gene through DNA binding and translationally by binding conserved RNA stem-loops on mRNAs. This protein contains six alpha-helices and two parallel beta-strands [[cite:PUB00160094],[cite:PUB00158951],[cite:PUB00158952]].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF1882)
description: This domain is found in a set of hypothetical bacterial proteins.

name: Putative type 4B encapsulin shell protein
description: Proteins in this entry may be the encapsulin shell protein in a type 4 A-domain encapsulin nanocompartment system. It has been shown that bacterial/archaeal encapsulin-like systems and HK97-type viruses share a common ancestor and it is likely that encapsulins have evolved from HK97-type phages [[cite:PUB00100782]].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF1885)
description: This domain is found in a set of hypothetical proteins produced by bacteria of the Bacillus genus.

name: USP8 dimerisation domain
description: This domain is predominantly found in the amino terminal region of Ubiquitin carboxyl-terminal hydrolase 8 (USP8). It forms a five helical bundle that dimerises [[cite:PUB00039203]].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF1902)
description: Members of this family of prokaryotic proteins adopt a fold consisting of one alpha-helix and four beta-strands. Their function has not, as yet, been elucidated [[cite:PUB00035388]].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF1893)
description: A member of the deaminase fold that binds an unknown ligand in the crystal structure. The protein is ADP-ribosylated at a conserved aspartate [[cite:PUB00046766]]. Contextual analysis suggests that the domain is likely to bind NAD or ADP ribose either to sense redox states or to function as a regulatory ADP ribosyltransferase [[cite:PUB00057473]].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF1877)
description: This domain is found in a set of hypothetical bacterial proteins.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF1868)
description: This group of 2H-phosphodiesterases comprises a single family typified by the protein mlr3352 from M.loti. Members are also present in various alpha-proteobacteria, Synechocystis, Streptococcus and Chilo iridescent virus. The presence of a member of this predominantly bacterial group in a large eukaryotic DNA virus represents a potential case of horizontal transfer from a bacterial source into a virus. Several proteins of bacterial origin have been noticed in the insect viruses (L.M.Iyer, E.V.Koonin and L.Aravind, unpublished observations and these appear to have been acquired from endo-symbiotic or parasitic bacteria that share the same host cells with the viruses. Presence of 2H proteins in the proteomes of large DNA viruses (e.g. T4 57B protein and the Fowl-pox virus FPV025) may point to some role for these proteins in regulating the viral tRNA metabolism. Each member of this family contains an internal duplication, each of which contains an HXTX motif that defines the family.

name: EF-hand domain
description: This domain is found predominantly in DJ binding proteins.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF1894)
description: Members of this family have an important role in methanogenesis. They assume an alpha-beta globular structure consisting of six beta-strands and three alpha-helices forming the secondary structural topological arrangement of alpha1-beta1-alpha2-beta2-beta3-beta4-beta5-beta6-alpha3 [[cite:PUB00035386]].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF1883)
description: Predicted ligand-binding domain of the PPC-like beta-sandwich fold. Observed in conserved gene neighbourhoods with diverse nucleotide-activated effector and related conflict systems, potentially recognises invasive molecules and initiates system responses or directly triggers directly-associated effector domains [[cite:PUB00097693]].

name: Acetylaranotin biosynthesis cluster protein L
description: This entry includes acetylaranotin biosynthesis cluster protein L (AtaL) from Aspergillus terreus, which is a non-ribosomal peptide synthetase. It is required for the biosynthesis of the toxin acetylaranotin, which is a disulfide bridged cyclic dipeptide [[cite:PUB00086035]]. There are a number of steps in the biosyntheis of this epipolythiodioxopiperazine toxin from two phenylananines, but the specific function of AtaL has yet to be determined [[cite:PUB00086035]]. Homologues are also known from bacteria.

name: Vasopressin V1 receptor, C-terminal
description: This is the conserved C-terminal domain of Vasopressin V1a/b receptors (V1R), which is involved in receptor trafficking and facilitates the interaction between the intracellular loops of the receptor, the G proteins and coupling to phospholipase C [[cite:PUB00038629],[cite:PUB00098105]]. This domain is unstructured and may reflect its conformational plasticity that may be necessary for proper function of V1R [[cite:PUB00038629]].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF1858)
description: This domain has no known function. It is found in various hypothetical bacterial proteins.

name: DP-EP family
description: The DP-EP family of proteins, formerly known as DUF1888 have been shown to catalyse a cleavage of an internal peptide bond [[cite:PUB00062632]].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF1889)
description: This domain is found in a set of hypothetical bacterial proteins. They are probably cytoplasmic proteins.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1892)
description: Members of this family, that are synthesised by Saccharomycetes, adopt a structure consisting of a four-stranded beta-sheet, with strand order beta2-beta1-beta4-beta3, and two alpha-helices, with an overall topology of beta-beta-alpha-beta-beta-alpha. They have no known function [[cite:PUB00029007]].

name: Type III secretion system, cytoplasmic E component of needle
description: T3SS_needle_E is a family of proteins from the operon that builds and controls the needle of the injection system of type III secretion. The YscE protein, produced by the pathogen Yersinia, assumes a secondary structure composed of two anti-parallel alpha-helices separated by a flexible loop [[cite:PUB00049490]]. The family is cytoplasmic and may help to stabilise and prevent early polymerisation of the needle-protein F [[cite:PUB00048615],[cite:PUB00109133]].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF1896)
description: This domain is found in a set of hypothetical bacterial proteins.

name: Cx9C motif-containing protein 4
description: Members of this family adopt a coiled coil structure, with two antiparallel alpha-helices that are tightly strapped together by two disulfide bridges at each end. The protein sequence shows a cysteine motif, required for the stabilisation of the coiled-coil-like structure. Additional inter-helix hydrophobic contacts impart stability to this scaffold [[cite:PUB00024565]]. The precise function of this eukaryotic domain is, as yet, unknown [[cite:PUB00013217]]. Cx9C motif-containing protein 4 (CMC4, also known as Mature T-cell proliferation 1 neighbor protein) is found in mitochondria. CMC4 is the first gene unequivocally identified in the group of uncommon leukemias with a mature phenotype [[cite:PUB00075489]].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF1890)
description: This domain is found in a set of hypothetical archaeal proteins.

name: Card1-like, endonuclease domain
description: This is the endonuclease domain found in a set of bacterial proteins, including Card1 (cyclic-oligoadenylate-activated single-stranded ribonuclease and single-stranded deoxyribonuclease 1) from Treponema succinifaciens ([swissprot:F2NWD3]), a protein that is part of type III CRISPR-Cas immune response system.
