This protein consists of a CARF (CRISPR-associated Rossman fold) domain at the N-terminal, an helical hinge domain and a C-terminal endonuclease domain [[cite:PUB00153094]].

name: Alkylated DNA repair protein alkB homolog 8, N-terminal
description: This domain is the N-terminal domain of Alkylated DNA repair protein alkB homolog 8 (ALKBH8) and its homologues. This domain corresponds to the basic alpha-helix located at the N-terminal of the RRM domain, which enhances its RNA binding affinity [[cite:PUB00062550]].

name: Far upstream element-binding protein, C-terminal
description: This entry represents the transactivation domain of Far upstream element-binding protein 1/2 (FUBP1/2) which is found at the C-terminal. FUBP1 regulates MYC expression by binding to a single-stranded far-upstream element (FUSE) upstream of the MYC promoter. FUBP2, also known as KSRP (K homology-type splicing regulatory protein), is a single-strand-RNA binding protein that integrate different levels of gene expression and is required for proper immune response, lipid metabolism, cell fate decisions, and tissue regeneration [[cite:PUB00084324]]. This domain contains the tyrosine residues required for transactivation and adopts an alpha-helical configuration [[cite:PUB00159898]].

name: HMG-box domain
description: This short 71 residue domain is an HMG-box domain. HMG-box domains mediate re-modelling of chromatin-structure. Mammalian HMG-box proteins are of two types: those that are non-sequence-specific DNA-binding proteins with two HMG-box domains and a long highly acidic C-tail; and a diverse group of sequence-specific transcription factor-proteins with either a single HMG-box or up to six copies, and no acidic C-tail [[cite:PUB00109134]].

name: FeoC like transcriptional regulator
description: This family contains several transcriptional regulators, including FeoC, which contain a HTH motif. FeoC acts as a [Fe-S] dependent transcriptional repressor [[cite:PUB00035969]].

name: Glucan 1,4-alpha-maltotetraohydrolase, domain C
description: This entry represents Domain C from Glucan 1,4-alpha- maltotetraohydrolase, which consists of five antiparallel beta-strands [[cite:PUB00025232],[cite:PUB00098204]].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF1922)
description: This entry represents a putative zinc finger domain. Proteins containing this domain typically consist of a beta-sheet region followed by an alpha-helix and an unstructured C-terminus. The beta-sheet region contains a CXCX...XCXC sequence with Cys residues located in two proximal loops and pointing towards each other. The precise function of this set of bacterial proteins is, as yet, unknown [[cite:PUB00008047]].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF1923)
description: Members of this family are found in maltosyltransferases, and adopt a secondary structure consisting of eight antiparallel beta-strands, which form an open-sided 'jelly roll' Greek key beta-barrel. Their exact function is, as yet, unknown [[cite:PUB00025274]].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF1924)
description: This domain is found in a set of bacterial proteins, including Cytochrome c-type protein. It is functionally uncharacterised.

name: Alpha-amylase/4-alpha-glucanotransferase, middle domain
description: This entry represents a domain found in prokaryotic alpha-amylase and 4-alpha-glucanotransferase. It is adjacent to the C-terminal domain ([pfam:PF09095]). This domain adopts an immunoglobulin/ albumin-binding domain-like fold, with a bundle of three alpha-helices. Their function is, as yet, unknown [[cite:PUB00014074]].

name: Alpha-amylase/4-alpha-glucanotransferase, C-terminal
description: This entry represents a domain found in prokaryotic alpha-amylase and 4-alpha-glucanotransferase. It adopts a beta-sandwich fold, in which two layers of anti-parallel beta-sheets are arranged in a nearly parallel fashion. The exact function of this family is, as yet, unknown, however it has been proposed that they may play a role in transglycosylation reactions [[cite:PUB00014074]].

name: Quinohemoprotein amine dehydrogenase, alpha subunit domain III
description: Members of this family, which are predominantly found in the prokaryotic protein quinohemoprotein amine dehydrogenase, adopt an immunoglobulin-like beta-sandwich fold, with seven strands arranged into two beta sheets; the fold is possibly related to the immunoglobulin and/or fibronectin type III superfamilies. The precise function of this domain has not, as yet, been defined [[cite:PUB00022422],[cite:PUB00013277]].

name: Quinohemoprotein amine dehydrogenase, alpha subunit domain IV
description: Members of this family, which are predominantly found in the prokaryotic protein quinohemoprotein amine dehydrogenase, adopt an immunoglobulin-like beta-sandwich fold, with seven strands arranged into two beta sheets; the fold is possibly related to the immunoglobulin and/or fibronectin type III superfamilies. The precise function of this domain has not, as yet, been defined [[cite:PUB00022422],[cite:PUB00013277]].

name: Galactose oxidase-like, Early set domain
description: E or 'early' set domains are associated with the catalytic domain of galactose oxidase at the C-terminal end. Galactose oxidase is an extracellular monomeric enzyme which catalyzes the stereospecific oxidation of a broad range of primary alcohol substrates, and possesses a unique mononuclear copper site essential for catalysing a two-electron transfer reaction during the oxidation of primary alcohols to corresponding aldehydes. The second redox active centre necessary for the reaction was found to be situated at a tyrosine residue. The C-terminal domain of galactose oxidase may be related to the immunoglobulin and/or fibronectin type III superfamilies. These domains are associated with different types of catalytic domains at either the N-terminal or C-terminal end, and may be involved in homodimeric/tetrameric/dodecameric interactions. Members of this family adopt a secondary structure consisting of a bundle of seven, mostly antiparallel, beta-strands surrounding a hydrophobic core. The 7 strands are arranged in 2 sheets, in a Greek-key topology [[cite:PUB00014151]]. This domain is found in sugar-utilising enzymes, such as galactose oxidase or chitinase [[cite:PUB00028414],[cite:PUB00044942],[cite:PUB00080765],[cite:PUB00080766],[cite:PUB00003324]].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF1930)
description: Members of this family are found in 3-mercaptopyruvate sulfurtransferase, and have no known function. They adopt a structure consisting of a four-stranded antiparallel beta-sheet and an alpha-helix, arranged in a beta(2)-alpha-beta(2) fashion, and bearing a remarkable structural similarity to the FK506-binding protein class of peptidylprolyl cis/trans-isomerase [[cite:PUB00029481]].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF1931)
description: Members of this family, which are found in a set of hypothetical bacterial proteins, contain a core of six alpha-helices, where one central helix is surrounded by the other five. The exact function of this family has not, as yet, been determined [[cite:PUB00035390]]. The known structure shows this domain contains two copies of the histone fold [[cite:PUB00035390]].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF1932)
description: This domain is found in a set of hypothetical prokaryotic proteins. Its exact function has not, as yet, been described.

name: Carbapenam-3-carboxylate synthase, N-terminal
description: This domain is found in the N-terminal of carbapenam-3-carboxylate synthase (carA), and is composed of two antiparallel six-stranded beta-sheets that form a sandwich, flanked on each side by two alpha-helices [[cite:PUB00022497]]. carA is involved in the biosynthesis of carbapenam-3-carboxylate, a beta-lactam antibiotic of the carbapenem class. It catalyses the ATP-dependent formation of (3S,5S)-carbapenam-3-carboxylate from (2S,5S)-5-carboxymethylproline [[cite:PUB00069787],[cite:PUB00069788],[cite:PUB00069789]].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF1934)
description: Members of this family are found in a set of hypothetical bacterial proteins. Their precise function has not, as yet, been defined.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF1935)
description: Members of this family are found in various Trypanosomatida hypothetical proteins, as well as in the cysteine protease calpain. Their exact function has not, as yet, been defined. This domain adopts a jelly-roll fold.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF1936)
description: This domain is found in a set of hypothetical Archaeal proteins. Its exact function has not, as yet, been defined. It possesses a zinc ribbon fold.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF1937)
description: This domain is found in a set of hypothetical bacterial proteins. Their exact function has not, as yet, been described.

name: Methylated DNA-protein cysteine methyltransferase, N-terminal
description: This domain is found in the archaeal protein O6-alkylguanine-DNA alkyltransferase (also known as Methylated DNA-protein cysteine methyltransferase MGMT), adopt a secondary structure consisting of a three stranded antiparallel beta-sheet and three alpha helices. This entry represents the N-terminal ribonuclease H-like domain, associated with 6-O-methylguanine DNA methyltransferase activity. The exact function has not, as yet, been defined, though it has been postulated that they confer thermostability to the archaeal protein [[cite:PUB00027330]].

name: Alpha-amylase C-terminal
description: This entry represents a C-terminal domain associated with prokaryotic alpha-amylases, which adopt a secondary structure consisting of an eight-stranded antiparallel beta-sheet containing a Greek key motif. Their exact function has not, as yet, been determined [[cite:PUB00027474]].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF1940)
description: Members of this family adopt a secondary structure consisting of six alpha helices, with four long helices (alpha1, alpha2, alpha5, alpha6) form a left-handed, antiparallel alpha helical bundle. The function of this family of Archaeal hypothetical proteins has not, as yet, been defined [[cite:PUB00035391]].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF1942)
description: Members of this family of bacterial proteins assume a beta-sandwich structure consisting of two antiparallel beta-sheets similar to an immunoglobulin-like fold, with an additional small, antiparallel beta-sheet. The longer-stranded beta-sheet is made up of four antiparallel beta-strands. The shorter-stranded beta-sheet consists of five beta-strands, four of these beta-strands form an antiparallel beta-sheet. The exact function of this family of proteins is unknown, though a putative role includes involvement in host-bacterial interactions involved in endocytosis or phagocytosis, possibly during bacterial internalisation [[cite:PUB00028893]].

name: CST, complex subunit STN1, C terminal
description: STN1 is a component of the CST complex, a complex that binds to single-stranded DNA and is required for protecting telomeres from DNA degradation. The CST complex binds single-stranded DNA with high affinity in a sequence-independent manner, while isolated subunits bind DNA with low affinity on their own. In addition to telomere protection, the CST complex probably has a more general role in DNA metabolism at non-telomeric sites. This entry represents the C-terminal region of Stn1 which has two winged helix-turn-helix (wHTH) motifs, wHTH1 and wHTH2 [[cite:PUB00053885],[cite:PUB00097419]]. wHTH1 is structurally similar to that in RPA32 with a large insertion between helices alpha2 and alpha3, unique to Stn1, that may allow interaction with a different set of proteins that function at telomeres such as Ctc1 [[cite:PUB00097419]]. wHTH2 is most similar to the DNA-binding wHTH motifs of the pur operon repressor and RepE replication initiator, but it does not bind double-stranded DNA [[cite:PUB00057805]].

name: N-glycosylase/DNA lyase
description: This domain is predominantly found in the Archaeal protein N-glycosylase/DNA lyase.

name: Vitellinogen, open beta-sheet
description: This entry represents the open beta-sheet domain found in vitellinogen, which generally corresponds to a domain within the lipovitellin-1 peptide product. This domain adopts a structure consisting of several large open beta-sheets [[cite:PUB00007158]].

name: Vitellinogen, beta-sheet shell
description: This entry represents the beta-sheet shell domain found in vitellinogen, which generally corresponds to the lipovitellin-2 peptide product. This domain consists of several large open beta-sheets [[cite:PUB00007158]].

name: 4-alpha-glucanotransferase, C-terminal
description: Members of this family, which are predominantly found in prokaryotic 4-alpha-glucanotransferase, adopt a structure composed of six antiparallel beta-strands, four of which form a beta-sheet and another two form a type I' beta-hairpin. The role of this family of domains, has not, as yet, been defined [[cite:PUB00027143]].

name: TilS substrate binding domain
description: This domain is found in the tRNA(Ile) lysidine synthetase (TilS) protein.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF1947)
description: Members of this family are found in a set of hypothetical Archaeal proteins. Their exact function has not, as yet, been defined.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF1948)
description: Members of this family of Mycoplasma hypothetical proteins adopt a helical structure, with one central alpha-helix surrounded by five others, in a NusB-like fold. Their function has not, as yet, been determined [[cite:PUB00030162]].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF1949)
description: Members of this family pertain to a set of functionally uncharacterised hypothetical bacterial proteins. They adopt a ferredoxin-like fold, with a beta-alpha-beta-beta-alpha-beta arrangement [[cite:PUB00032088]].

name: RNA-directed DNA methylation 1
description: This family of plant proteins includes RDM1 from Arabidopsis, which is a component of the RNA-directed DNA methylation (RdDM) effector complex and may have a role in linking siRNA production with pre-existing or de novo cytosine methylation [[cite:PUB00057309]]. As part of the DDR complex with two other RdDM components, it has been shown to facilitate association of PolV to chromatin [[cite:PUB00109101],[cite:PUB00096469]].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF1951)
description: Members of this family of Mycoplasma hypothetical proteins adopt a helical structure, with a buried central helix. Their function has not, as yet, been determined.

name: Archaeal MoaD-like protein
description: This entry represents an archaeal MoaD-like domain with a ubiquitin-like fold found in various archaebacterial proteins. These proteins have a highly conserved Gly-Gly motif at their C-terminus, a hallmark of the MoaD/ThiS/ubiquitin superfamily [[cite:PUB00011756],[cite:PUB00035630]]. The bacterial MoaD protein functions as a sulfur carrier in molybdenum cofactor (Moco) biosynthesis, with the C-terminal Gly-Gly motif being essential for activation by the MoeB enzyme. After activation, MoaD receives a sulfur atom to form a thiocarboxylate intermediate that acts as a sulfur donor. Based on the conserved Gly-Gly motif and association with ThiS genes and MoaB-like proteins, these archaeal proteins likely function as sulfur carriers in cofactor biosynthesis pathways, similar to their bacterial counterparts.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF1953)
description: This domain is found in the Archaeal protein maltooligosyl trehalose synthase produced by Sulfolobus spp. Its function has not, as yet, been defined.

name: Staphylococcal superantigen-like OB-fold domain
description: This OB-fold domain folds into a five-stranded beta-barrel [[cite:PUB00018994]]. Members of this family are found in various staphylococcal toxins described as staphylococcal superantigen-like (SSL) proteins that are related to the staphylococcal enterotoxins (SEs) or superantigens. These SSL proteins of which 11 have so far been characterised have a typical SE tertiary structure consisting of a distinct oligonucleotide/oligosaccharide binding (OB-fold), this domain, linked to a beta-grasp domain, family Stap_Strp_tox_C, [pfam:PF02876]. SSLs do not bind to T-cell receptors or major histocompatibility complex class II molecules and do not stimulate T cells. SSLs target components of innate immunity, such as complement, Fc receptors, and myeloid cells 2,3,4,5,6,7,8]. SSL protein 7 (SSL7) is the best characterised of the SSLs and binds complement factor C5 and IgA with high affinity and inhibits the end stage of complement activation and IgA binding to FcalphaR [[cite:PUB00065773]].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF1955)
description: Members of this family are found in hypothetical proteins synthesised by the Archaeal organism Sulfolobus. Their exact function has not, as yet, been determined.

name: HTH-type transcriptional dual regulator CecR, C-terminal domain
description: This entry represents the C-terminal domain found in CecR (regulator of cefoperazone and chloramphenicol sensitivity), previously known as YbiH. CecR has been shown to control sensitivity to cefoperazone and chloramphenicol through regulating the transcription of the cecR-ybhGFSR operon and the rhlE gene [[cite:PUB00104740]].

name: 1,4-alpha-glucan branching enzyme, C-terminal
description: This entry represents the C-terminal domain found in bacterial 1,4-alpha-glucan branching enzymes, such as TTHA1902 from Thermus thermophilus and TK1436 from Thermococcus kodakarensis, which belong to the glycoside hydrolase family 57 (GH57). These enzymes catalyse the formation of branch points in alpha-glucans by cleavage of an alpha-1,4 glycosidic bond and subsequent transfer of the cleaved-off oligosaccharide to a new alpha-1,6 position. This is an alpha-helical domain composed of a four alpha-helical bundle. It plays a role in the formation of the active-site cleft, being essential for substrate binding and catalysis [[cite:PUB00090452],[cite:PUB00058786]].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF1958)
description: Members of this functionally uncharacterised family are found in prokaryotic penicillin-binding protein 4.

name: EhaM-like
description: This domain covers most of the sequence in the uncharacterised protein MJ0517 from Methanocaldococcus jannaschii and similar archaeal proteins. Members of this family are predicted to be the hydrophilic EhaM subunits of Eha-type energy-converting [NiFe] hydrogenase complexes [[cite:PUB00096941],[cite:PUB00161043]].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF1961)
description: Members of this family are found in a set of hypothetical bacterial proteins. Their exact function has not, as yet, been determined.

name: Bubble protein
description: Members of this family of fungal domains are functionally uncharacterised. They may act as toxins [[cite:PUB00031842]].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF1963)
description: This domain is found in a set of hypothetical bacterial proteins. Its exact function has not, as yet, been described.

name: Sucrose phosphorylase, C-terminal
description: This domain is C-terminal to the catalytic sucrose phosphorylase beta/alpha barrel domain which adopts a beta-sandwich fold with Greek-key topology [[cite:PUB00030562],[cite:PUB00041019],[cite:PUB00151581]].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF1965)
description: Members of this family of fungal domains adopt a structure that consists of an alpha/beta motif. Their exact function has not, as yet, been determined [[cite:PUB00027613]].

name: Alpha-amylase, domain C
description: This domain is found at the C-terminal of various fungal alpha-amylase proteins [[cite:PUB00027691]]. It has been identified as a secondary binding site, which might be part of a starch interaction site [[cite:PUB00097489]]. It has a beta- sandwich fold comprising an antiparallel beta-sheet with eight strands [[cite:PUB00097489],[cite:PUB00097488]].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF1967)
description: Members of this family contain a four-stranded beta sheet and three alpha helices flanked by an additional beta strand. They are predominantly found in the bacterial GTP-binding protein Obg, and are still functionally uncharacterised [[cite:PUB00022779]].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF1968)
description: Members of this family are found in mammalian T-cell antigen receptor, and adopt an immunoglobulin-like beta-sandwich fold, with seven strands in two beta-sheets in a Greek-key topology. Their exact function has not, as yet, been determined.

name: Fumarylacetoacetase N-terminal
description: The N-terminal domain of fumarylacetoacetate hydrolase is functionally uncharacterised, and adopts a structure consisting of an SH3-like barrel [[cite:PUB00025833]].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF1970)
description: Members of this family consist of various uncharacterised viral hypothetical proteins.

name: TehB-like domain
description: This domain, previously known as DUF1971, is found at the N-terminal associated with [pfam:PF03848], and covering the whole length of the sequence in other bacterial uncharacterised proteins. TehB plays a role in both resistance to oxidative damage and haem uptake/utilisation, and is important for virulence of this organism in an animal model of invasive disease. It also protects H.influenzae from tellurite exposure in vitro [[cite:PUB00161042]]. In Escherichia coli, TehB is thought to utilise a methyltransferase activity in the detoxification of tellurite [[cite:PUB00014885]].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF1972)
description: Members of this family of functionally uncharacterised domains are found in bacterial glycosyltransferases and rhamnosyltransferases.

name: Acyl-CoA dehydrogenase, C-terminal, bacterial type
description: This C-terminal domain is functionally uncharacterised and is predominantly found in various prokaryotic acyl-coenzyme A dehydrogenases and seems to be essential for its function [[cite:PUB00101040]].

name: Glycosyl transferase 1 domain A
description: Glyco_trans_A_1 is family of found predominantly at the N-terminus of various prokaryotic alpha-glucosyltransferases. According to whether the domain exists as a whole molecule or as a half molecule determines the number of sugar residues that the molecule transfers. Two-domain proteins are processive in that they transfer more than one sugar residue, processively; single domain proteins transfer just one sugar moiety [[cite:PUB00075675],[cite:PUB00064844]].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF1977)
description: Members of this family of functionally uncharacterised domains are predominantly found in dnaj-like proteins.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF1978)
description: Members of this family are found in various hypothetical proteins produced by the bacterium Chlamydia pneumoniae. Their exact function has not, as yet, been identified.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF1979)
description: Members of this family of functionally uncharacterised domains are found in various Oryza sativa mutator-like transposases.

name: DUF1980 N-terminal domain
description: Members of this family are found in a set of prokaryotic hypothetical proteins. Their exact function, has not, as yet, been defined. This entry represents the N-terminal 3-transmembrane helical domain.

name: Mon2/Sec7/BIG1-like, HDS
description: This entry represents a HDS (homology downstream of Sec7) domain found towards the C-terminal of guanine nucleotide exchange factors involved Golgi transport, such as budding yeast protein Sec7, protein Mon2 and BIG1-like proteins [[cite:PUB00101185],[cite:PUB00101184]]. Sec7 is involved in the secretory pathway as a protein binding scaffold for the COPII-COPI protein switch for maturation of the VTC intermediate compartments for Golgi compartment biogenesis [[cite:PUB00076747]]. Sec7 has four HDS1-4 domains, which act to integrate the signals from several small GTPases, including Arf1 itself, to switch Sec7 from a strongly autoinhibited to a strongly auto activated form [[cite:PUB00101184]].

name: NADH-ubiquinone oxidoreductase subunit G, C-terminal
description: Members of this family of are found at the C-terminus of NADH dehydrogenases subunit G or NADH-ubiquinone oxidoreductase subunit G. [ec:1.6.99.5].

name: Bacteriophage tail tip fiber protein
description: The Tail Tip Fiber Protein family includes proteins involved in the attachment and penetration of bacteriophages into host cells. Members of this family are responsible for recognizing and irreversibly binding to specific host receptors, which triggers structural changes in the viral tail necessary for the injection of viral DNA into the host. This process is critical for the successful infection and propagation of the virus. The family includes proteins that initiate distal tail tip assembly during phage tail assembly and play a key role in the virus entry by mediating the attachment to the host receptor and inducing DNA ejection through the receptor's pore. This entry represents the beta prism domain which is formed from a homotrimeric complex of members of this family.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF1984)
description: Members of this family of functionally uncharacterised domains are found at the C-terminus of plant phytochelatin synthases.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF1985)
description: Members of this family of functionally uncharacterised domains are found in a set of Arabidopsis thaliana hypothetical proteins.

name: Nudel, serine protease domain
description: This domain is found in Nudel from Drosophila melanogaster and related proteins. Nudel is involved in defining embryonic dorsoventral polarity. Three proteiases ndl, gd and snk process easter to create active easter. Active easter defines cell identities along the dorsal-ventral continuum by activating the spz ligand for the Tl receptor in the ventral region of the embryo. Nudel, pipe and windbeutel together trigger the protease cascade within the extraembryonic perivitelline compartment which induces dorsoventral polarity of the Drosophila embryo [[cite:PUB00054161]].

name: Conserved hypothetical protein 2217 (DUF2460)
description: This model represents a family of conserved hypothetical proteins. It is usually (but not always) found in apparent phage-derived regions of bacterial chromosomes.

name: SiaC family regulatory phosphoprotein
description: This entry represents the SiaC family regulatory phosphoprotein which undergoes a regulatory phosphorylation at Thr-68 of founder protein PA0170 from Pseudomonas aeruginosa, but in more distant homologs, T can be S. Also, it is part of motif NTSS, so may contain more than one phosphorylation site. Phosphorylation causes regulatory change to protein-protein interaction, in a pathway that seems broadly distributed, involves a diguanylate cyclase, and in the case of Pseudomonas aeruginosa affects aggregation and biofilm formation responses.

name: SMI1 / KNR4 family (SUKH-1)
description: Proteins in this family are involved in the regulation of 1,3-beta-glucan synthase activity and cell-wall formation [[cite:PUB00044491]][[cite:PUB00013613]]. Genome contextual information showed that SMI1 are primary immunity proteins in bacterial toxin systems [[cite:PUB00057479]].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF1989)
description: This family of proteins are functionally uncharacterised.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF1990)
description: This family of proteins are functionally uncharacterised. They are presicted to adopt a structure with similarity to members of the Bet v 1-like superfamily.

name: OHCU decarboxylase
description: The proteins in this family are OHCU decarboxylase - enzymes of the purine catabolism that catalyse the conversion of OHCU into S(+)-allantoin [[cite:PUB00042841]]. This is the third step of the conversion of uric acid (a purine derivative) to allantoin. Step one is catalysed by urate oxidase ([pfam:PF01014]) and step two is catalysed by HIUases ([pfam:PF00576]).

name: DnaJ homologue, subfamily C, member 28, conserved domain
description: This domain is found in proteins that may have a role in protein folding or as a chaperone, including DnaJ homolog subfamily C member 28. DnaJ is a member of the J-protein family (also known as HSP40), which are defined by the presence of a J domain that regulate the activity of 70kDa heat-shock proteins [[cite:PUB00109020]]. The function of this domain is not yet known.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF1993)
description: This family of proteins are functionally uncharacterised.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF1995)
description: This family of proteins are functionally uncharacterised.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF1996)
description: This family of proteins are functionally uncharacterised.

name: Conserved hypothetical protein (DUF2461)
description: Members of this family are widely (though sparsely) distributed bacterial proteins, about 230 residues in length. All members have a motif RxxRDxRFxxx[DN]KxxY. The function of this protein family is unknown.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1997)
description: This family of proteins are functionally uncharacterised.

name: MrfA Zn-binding domain
description: This is the C-terminal MrfA Zn+2-binding domain (MZB, also referred to as DUF1998) which contains a conserved four-cysteine signature motif. These four Cys reside in a short coil between two alpha-helices and form a metal ion-binding site [[cite:PUB00098193]]. This domain is frequently found at the C-terminal of ndNTPases, however, it is also found encoded in a standalone gene, downstream of putative helicase domain-encoding genes associated with bacterial anti-phage defense system DISARM. MrfA (Mitomycin repair factor A, also known as YprA in Bacillus subtilis) is a DNA helicase that supports repair of mitomycin C-induced DNA damage. MrfA homologues are widely distributed in bacteria and are also present in archaea, fungi and plants. The MrfA-homologue in yeast, Hrq1, also reduces mitomycin C sensitivity. Hrq1 has high similarity to human RecQ4 and was therefore assigned to the RecQ-like helicase family. MrfA homologues appear to be missing in Enterobacteria, however, certain pathogenic Escherichia coli and Salmonella strains harbour Z5898-like helicases with this domain [[cite:PUB00098193]].

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1999)
description: This family contains a putative Fe-S binding reductase ([swissprot:Q72J89]) whose structure adopts an alpha and beta fold.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF2000)
description: This is a family of proteins of unknown function. The structure of one of the proteins in this family has been shown to adopt an alpha beta fold.

name: Phage tail tube protein
description: This is a family of phage tail tube proteins including protein XkdM from phage-like element PBSX protein ([swissprot:P54332]) whose structure adopts a beta barrel flanked with alpha helical regions.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF2002)
description: This is a family of putative cytoplasmic proteins. The structure of these proteins form an antiparallel beta and sheet and contain some alpha helical regions.

name: KICSTOR complex C12orf66 like
description: This entry includes C12orf66-like proteins. Human C12orf66 is part of the KICSTOR complex that functions in the amino acid-sensing branch of the TORC1 signaling pathway [[cite:PUB00085648]].

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF2004)
description: This is a family of proteins with unknown function. The structure of one of the proteins in this family has revealed a novel alpha-beta fold [[cite:PUB00039229]].

name: AbiEi antitoxin C-terminal domain
description: AbiEi_1 is the cognate antitoxin of the type IV toxin-antitoxin 'innate immunity' bacterial abortive infection (Abi) system that protects bacteria from the spread of a phage infection. The Abi system is activated upon infection with phage to abort the cell thus preventing the spread of phage through viral replication. There are some 20 or more Abis, and they are predominantly plasmid-encoded lactococcal systems. TA, toxin-antitoxin, systems on plasmids function by killing cells that lose the plasmid upon division. AbiE phage resistance systems function as novel Type IV TAs and are widespread in bacteria and archaea. The cognate antitoxin is [pfam:PF13338] [[cite:PUB00075538]].

name: Putative prokaryotic signal transducing protein
description: This is a family of putative prokaryotic signal transducing proteins of Pii-type.

name: CENP-S associating Centromere protein X
description: The centromere, essential for faithful chromosome segregation during mitosis, has a network of constitutive centromere-associated (CCAN) proteins associating with it during mitosis. So far in vertebrates at least 15 centromere proteins have been identified, which are divided into several subclasses based on functional and biochemical analyses. These provide a platform for the formation of a functional kinetochore during mitosis. CENP-S is one that does not associate with the CENP-H-containing complex but rather interacts with CENP-X to form a stable assembly of outer kinetochore proteins that functions downstream of other components of the CCAN. This complex may directly allow efficient and stable formation of the outer kinetochore on the CCAN platform.

name: Non-canonical E2 ubiquitin-conjugating enzyme, DUF2009 family
description: This entry represents a novel family of non-canonical E2 ubiquitin-conjugating enzymes that lack the typical HPN motif found in other E2 enzymes. The domain contains a highly conserved catalytic cysteine (C572 in PF3D7_0811400) that forms a thioester bond with ubiquitin. This was experimentally validated through mutational analysis and biochemical assays [[cite:PUB00160741]]. The domain is found in the C-terminal region of proteins, while the N-terminal region contains coiled helices involved in protein-protein interactions with other ubiquitin pathway components like Rbx1. The domain represents a new class of E2 enzymes particularly found in Apicomplexan parasites.

name: Mitochondrial PGP phosphatase
description: This is a family of proteins that acts as a mitochondrial phosphatase in cardiolipin biosynthesis. Cardiolipin is a unique dimeric phosphoglycerolipid predominantly present in mitochondrial membranes. The inverted phosphatase motif includes the highly conserved DKD triad [[cite:PUB00066452]].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF2014)
description: This domain is found at the C terminal of a family of ER membrane bound transcription factors called sterol regulatory element binding proteins (SREBP).

name: Fungal protein of unknown function (DUF2011)
description: This is a family of fungal proteins whose function is unknown. They are distantly related to CUSTOS proteins [pfam:PF23999] from animals.

name: ER membrane protein complex subunit 7, beta-sandwich domain
description: This is the beta-sandwich domain found in ER membrane protein complex subunit 7 (EMC7) [[cite:PUB00096682],[cite:PUB00096681]], which is an integral membrane component of the EMC. EMC is widely conserved and involved in membrane protein biogenesis. It mediates the insertion into endoplasmic reticulum membranes of newly synthesized membrane proteins in an energy-independent manner, both post-translational insertions of tail-anchored proteins and co-translational insertion of multipass membrane proteins [[cite:PUB00096679],[cite:PUB00096678]]. This entry includes UPF0620 protein C83.10 from S. pombe, an orthologue of animal EMC7. This domain is also found in nodal modulators, which have been identified as part of a protein complex that participates in the nodal signalling pathway during vertebrate development [[cite:PUB00054165]].

name: SPIN90/Ldb17, leucine-rich domain
description: This is the conserved leucine-rich domain (LRD) within the C-terminal domain of SPIN90 (also known as NCK interacting protein with SH3 domain (NCKIPSD)) from animals, Ldb17 from budding yeasts and Dip1 from fission yeasts [[cite:PUB00098231]]. Ldb17 is involved in the regulation of endocytosis in yeast [[cite:PUB00054166]]. SPIN90 is an F-actin binding protein that regulates actin polymerization and endocytosis [[cite:PUB00085468]]. It associates with and activates the Arp2/3 complex, without requiring a preformed actin filament [[cite:PUB00054166],[cite:PUB00033588],[cite:PUB00054167]]. This LRD, within the C-terminal armadillo repeat (ARM) domain of SPIN90, is important for activation of Arp2/3 complex [[cite:PUB00098231]].

name: Fungal protein of unknown function (DUF2015)
description: This is a fungal family of uncharacterised proteins.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF2016)
description: A predicted alpha+beta domain that is usually fused N-terminal to the JAB metallopeptidase. This protein in turn is found in conserved gene neighborhoods that include genes encoding the bacterial homologs of the ubiquitin modification system such as the E1, E2 and Ub proteins [[cite:PUB00034476]]. The domain is also known as the JAB-N domain. An AlphaFold3 prediction with A0A375JCV4 suggests that this domain likely mediate dimerisation (iPTM=0.87).

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF2017)
description: This is an alpha-helical domain found in gene neighborhoods that contain genes encoding ubiquitin, cysteine synthases and JAB peptidases [[cite:PUB00034476]].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF2018)
description: Acid-adaptive protein possibly of physiological significance when H.pylori colonises the human stomach, which adopts a unique four alpha-helical triangular conformations. The biologically active form is thought to be a tetramer. The protein is expressed along with six other proteins, some of which are related to iron storage and haem biosynthesis [[cite:PUB00039697]].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF2020)
description: Protein of unknown function found in bacteria.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF2019)
description: Protein of unknown function found in bacteria.

name: Tryptophan-rich protein (DUF2389)
description: Members of this family are small hypothetical proteins of 60 to 100 residues from Cyanobacteria and some Proteobacteria. Prochlorococcus marinus strains have two members, other species one only. Interestingly, of the eight most conserved residues, four are aromatic and three are invariant tryptophans. It appears all species that encode this protein can synthesise tryptophan de novo.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF2462)
description: This protein is highly conserved, but its function is unknown. It can be isolated from HeLa cell nucleoli and is found to be homologous with Leydig cell tumour protein whose function is unknown [1, supplementary Table I].

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF2388)
description: This family consists of small hypothetical proteins, about 100 amino acids in length. The family includes five members (three in tandem) in Pseudomonas aeruginosa PAO1 and in Pseudomonas putida (strain KT2440), four in Pseudomonas syringae DC3000, and single members in several other Proteobacteria. The function is unknown.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF2390)
description: Members of this family are bacterial hypothetical proteins, about 160 amino acids in length, found in various proteobacteria, including members of the genera Pseudomonas and Vibrio. The C-terminal region is poorly conserved and is not included in the model.

name: Probable metal-binding protein (DUF2387)
description: Members of this family are small proteins, about 70 residues in length, with a basic triplet near the N-terminus and a probable metal-binding motif CPXCX(18)CXXC. Members are found in various proteobacteria.

name: Predicted lipoprotein of unknown function (DUF2380)
description: This family consists of at least 9 paralogs in Myxococcus xanthus, a member of the Deltaproteobacteria. One appears truncated toward the N-terminus; the others are predicted lipoproteins. The function is unknown.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF2378)
description: This family consists of a set of at least 17 paralogous proteins in Myxococcus xanthus DK 1622 and and 12 in Stigmatella aurantiaca DW4/3-1. Members are about 200 amino acids in length. The function is unknown.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF2383)
description: This domain is found in found in uncharacterised proteins predominantly from bacteria. The uncharacterised [swissprot:Q9I1U6] from Pseudomonas aeruginosa shows a ferritin-like topology with a four-helix-bundle fold that lacks metal-ion-binding site typical of the ferritin family ([pfam:PF00210]) but has a potential metal-binding site [[cite:PUB00065044]]. The function is unknown.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF2385)
description: Members of this uncharacterised protein family are found in a number of alphaproteobacteria, including root nodule bacteria, Brucella suis, Caulobacter crescentus, and Rhodopseudomonas palustris. Conserved residues include two well-separated cysteines, suggesting a disulfide bond. The function is unknown.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF2379)
description: This family consists of at least 7 paralogs in Myxococcus xanthus and 6 in Stigmatella aurantiaca, both members of the Deltaproteobacteria. The function is unknown.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF2381)
description: This family consists of at least 8 paralogs in Myxococcus xanthus, a member of the Deltaproteobacteria. The function is unknown.

name: Phage tail assembly chaperone protein, TAC
description: This is a family of phage tail assembly chaperone proteins largely derived from the Rhodobacter species viral agent GTA (gene transfer agent) gp10.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF2382)
description: This entry describes an uncharacterized domain, sometimes found in association with a PRC-barrel domain [pfam:PF05239] which is also found in rRNA processing protein RimM and in a photosynthetic reaction centre complex protein). This domain is found in proteins from Bacillus subtilis, Deinococcus radiodurans, Nostoc sp. PCC 7120, Myxococcus xanthus, and several other species. The function is not known.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF2375)
description: Two members of this family are found in Colwellia psychrerythraea (strain 34H / ATCC BAA-681) and one each in various other species of Colwellia and Shewanella. One member from C. psychrerythraea is of special interest because it is preceded by the same cis-regulatory site as a number of genes that have the PEP-CTERM domain described by PEP_anchor (IPR013424).

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF2374)
description: This very small protein (about 46 amino acids) consists largely of a single predicted membrane-spanning region. It is found in Photobacterium profundum SS9 and in three species of Vibrio, always near periplasmic nitrate reductase genes, but far from the periplasmic nitrate reductase genes in Aeromonas hydrophila ATCC 7966.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF2463)
description: This protein is found in eukaryotic, parasitic microsporidia. Its function is unknown.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF2031)
description: This protein is expressed in Plasmodium; its function is unknown. It may be the product of gene family pyst-b [[cite:PUB00044233]].

name: Glycosyltransferase family 87
description: The enzymes in this family are glycosyltransferases. PimE is involved in phosphatidylinositol mannoside (PIM) synthesis, a major class of glycolipids in all mycobacteria. PimE is a polyprenol-phosphate-mannose-dependent mannosyltransferase that transfers the fifth mannose of PIM [[cite:PUB00075385]]. The family also includes alpha(1-->3) arabinofuranosyltransferase, invloved in the synthesis of of mycobacterial arabinogalactan [[cite:PUB00075386]].

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF2459)
description: This conserved hypothetical protein of unknown function is found in several Proteobacteria. Its function is unknown and its genome context is not well-conserved. It is found amid urease genes in at least one species.

name: Putative integral membrane protein (DUF2391)
description: This entry is found in Nostoc sp. PCC 7120, Agrobacterium tumefaciens, Rhizobium meliloti, and Gloeobacter violaceus in a conserved two-gene neighbourhood. Proteins containing this entry appear to span the membrane seven times.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF2393)
description: The function of this protein is unknown. It is always found as part of a two-gene operon with IPR013416, a protein that appears to span the membrane seven times. It has so far been found in the bacteria Nostoc sp. PCC 7120, Agrobacterium tumefaciens, Rhizobium meliloti, and Gloeobacter violaceus.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF2024)
description: This protein of 86 residues is expressed in bacteria. It consists of four alpha helices and two beta strands. Its function is unknown. One UniProt entry gives the gene name as Traf5.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF2023)
description: This protein of approx.120 residues consists of three beta strands and five alpha helices, thought to fold into a homo-dimer. It is expressed in bacteria.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF2025)
description: This protein is produced from gene PA1123 in Pseudomonas. It contains three alpha helices and six beta strands and is thought to be monomeric. It appears to be present in the biofilm layer and may be a lipoprotein.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF2027)
description: This protein domain is of unknown function. though putatively involved in DNA mismatch repair. It is associated with [pfam:PF01713].

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF2026)
description: This protein of approx. 100 residues is found in bacteria. It contains up to five alpha helices and up to seven beta strands and is probably monomeric. Its function is unknown. It is cited as a major prophage head protein [[cite:PUB00044231]], so might generally be of viral origin.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF2396)
description: These conserved hypothetical proteins have so far been found only in the Cyanobacteria. They are about 170 amino acids long and contain a CxxCx(14)CxxH motif near the N-terminus.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF2397)
description: Proteins in this entry are encoded within a conserved gene four-gene neighbourhood found sporadically in a phylogenetically broad range of bacteria including: Nocardia farcinica, Symbiobacterium thermophilum, and Streptomyces avermitilis (Actinobacteria), Geobacillus kaustophilus (Firmicutes), Azoarcus sp. EbN1 and Ralstonia solanacearum (Betaproteobacteria).

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF2398)
description: Proteins in this entry are encoded within a conserved gene four-gene neighbourhood found sporadically in a phylogenetically broad range of bacteria including: Nocardia farcinica, Symbiobacterium thermophilum, and Streptomyces avermitilis (Actinobacteria), Geobacillus kaustophilus (Firmicutes), Azoarcus sp. EbN1 and Ralstonia solanacearum (Betaproteobacteria).

name: Protein of unknown function C-terminus (DUF2399)
description: Proteins in this entry are encoded within a conserved gene four-gene neighbourhood found sporadically in a phylogenetically broad range of bacteria including: Nocardia farcinica, Symbiobacterium thermophilum, and Streptomyces avermitilis (Actinobacteria), Geobacillus kaustophilus (Firmicutes), Azoarcus sp. EbN1 and Ralstonia solanacearum (Beta-proteobacteria). Just the C-terminal region is ioncluded here.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF2028)
description: This region of similarity is found in the vertebrate homologues of the drosophila Bobby Sox.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF2400)
description: Members of this uncharacterised protein family are found sporadically, so far only among spirochetes, epsilon and delta proteobacteria, and Bacteroides. The function is unknown and its gene neighbourhoods show little conservation.

name: Magnetosome magnetite crystal formation protein family
description: This entry represents the magnetosome MamF/MmsF protein family found in magnetotactic bacteria. These membrane proteins are involved in magnetite crystal formation within magnetosome organelles. They are not essential for biomineralization, but play a major role in controlling the size and shape of magnetite crystals. Loss of these proteins results in crystals that are approximately 75% of wild-type size with altered morphology. They are multi-pass membrane proteins associated with the magnetosome membrane and exhibit cumulative, partially redundant functions in regulating crystal growth. This family includes proteins from organisms that are not known to contain magnetosomes suggesting that this family of proteins have a broader function.

name: Plasmodium RESA N-terminal
description: The short, four-helical domain first identified in the Plasmodium export proteins PHISTa and PHISTc [[cite:PUB00053439]] has been extended to become this six-helical PRESAN domain identified in the P. falciparum-specific RESA-type (Ring-infected erythrocyte surface antigen) proteins in association with the DnaJ domain. Overall, at least 67 proteins have been detected in P. falciparum with complete copies of the PRESAN domain. No versions of this domain were detected in other apicomplexan genera, suggesting that the domain was 'invented' after the divergence of the lineage leading to the genus Plasmodium undergoing a dramatic proliferation only in P. falciparum. A secondary structure-prediction derived from the multiple alignment of the PRESAN family reveals that it is composed of an all-helical fold with six conserved helical segments. There is some evidence it might localise to membranes [[cite:PUB00055558]].

name: Antitoxin Xre/MbcA/ParS C-terminal toxin-binding domain
description: This entry represents the C-terminal domain of antitoxin components of a type II toxin-antitoxin (TA) system, including Xre from Pseudomonas putida, MbcA from Mycobacterium sp. and ParS from Sphingobium sp. [[cite:PUB00098292],[cite:PUB00098291],[cite:PUB00093678],[cite:PUB00098290]]. This domain interacts with the toxin component and sterically blocks its active site, neutralising its effect [[cite:PUB00098291],[cite:PUB00093678]]. These antitoxins also have a HTH domain at the N-terminal.

name: Sister chromatid cohesion protein Dcc1
description: Sister chromatid cohesion protein Dcc1 is a component of the Ctf18-RFC complex. This complex is required for the efficient establishment of chromosome cohesion during S-phase and for loading the replication clamp Pol30/PCNA, which functions in DNA replication and repair [[cite:PUB00045276],[cite:PUB00109231]]. Ctf18-RFC loads PCNA onto DNA in an ATP-dependent manner. It may also have PCNA-unloading activity [[cite:PUB00045277]].

name: Pre-mRNA-splicing factor of RES complex
description: This entry is characterised by proteins with alternating conserved and low-complexity regions. Bud13 together with Snu17p and a newly identified factor, Pml1p/Ylr016c, form a novel trimeric complex. called The RES complex, pre-mRNA retention and splicing complex. Subunits of this complex are not essential for viability of yeasts but they are required for efficient splicing in vitro and in vivo. Furthermore, inactivation of this complex causes pre-mRNA leakage from the nucleus. Bud13 contains a unique, phylogenetically conserved C-terminal region of unknown function [[cite:PUB00042559]].

name: LRRFIP family
description: LRRFIP1 is a transcriptional repressor which preferentially binds to the GC-rich consensus sequence (5'- AGCCCCCGGCG-3') and may regulate expression of TNF, EGFR and PDGFA [[cite:PUB00078055]]. LRRFIP2 may function as activator of the canonical Wnt signalling pathway, in association with DVL3, upstream of CTNNB1/beta-catenin [[cite:PUB00078057]].

name: Mini-chromosome maintenance replisome factor
description: This entry is of proteins of approximately 600 residues in length containing alternating regions of conservation and low complexity. The Arabidopsis protein is a replisome factor found to bind with the mini-chromosome maintenance, MCM-binding, complex and is crucial for efficient DNA replication. The family now spans the full-length proteins.

name: Uncharacterized conserved protein (DUF2043)
description: This is a 100 residue conserved region of a family of proteins found from fungi to humans. This region contains three conserved Cysteines and a motif of {CP}{y/l}{HG}.

name: Uncharacterized conserved protein (DUF2045)
description: This entry represents Uncharacterized protein KIAA0930 homolog found in animals. KIAA0930 is localised in the cytosol and not secreted from cells. Expression of KIAA0930 (C22orf9) is significantly higher in pancreatic, colorectal, gastric, and tongue cancer tissues than in normal tissues [[cite:PUB00163385]].

name: E3 UFM1-protein ligase 1
description: The ubiquitin fold modifier 1 (Ufm1) is the most recently discovered ubiquitin-like modifier whose conjugation (ufmylation) system is conserved in multicellular organisms. Ufm1 is known to covalently attach with cellular protein(s) via a specific E1-activating enzyme (Uba5), an E2-conjugating enzyme (Ufc1), and a E3-ligating enzyme [[cite:PUB00054168]].

name: Nuclear speckle splicing regulatory protein 1, N-terminal
description: This domain is found at the N-terminal of Nuclear speckle splicing regulatory protein 1 (NRP1, also known as Nuclear speckle-related protein 70 and Coiled-coil domain-containing protein 55) and contains a coiled-coil domain that plays a critical role in NRP1 alternative splicing activity and self-oligomerization. NRP1 is a RNA-binding protein that mediates pre-mRNA alternative splicing regulation [[cite:PUB00093376],[cite:PUB00093375]].

name: Coiled-coil domain containing protein 97-like, C-terminal
description: This domain is found at the C-terminal of CCD97. In some proteins, this domain is found as two conserved domains separated by a region of low complexity, spanning some 200 residues. The function is unknown.

name: Alpha/beta hydrolase domain containing 18
description: This entry represents alpha/beta hydrolase domain-containing protein 18 (ABHD18). Its function is not clear.

name: Uncharacterized conserved protein H4 (DUF2046)
description: This is the conserved N-terminal 350 residues of a family of proteins of unknown function possibly containing a coiled-coil domain.

name: Predicted membrane protein (DUF2053)
description: This entry is of the conserved N-terminal 150 residues of proteins conserved from plants to humans. The function is unknown although some annotation suggests it to be a transmembrane protein.

name: Ima1 N-terminal domain
description: This domain occurs at the N-terminus of the Schizosaccharomyces pombe inner nuclear membrane (INM) protein, Ima1. Ima1 interacts with other inner nuclear membrane proteins [[cite:PUB00066721],[cite:PUB00066722],[cite:PUB00097072]].

name: Coiled-coil domain-containing protein 149-A
description: Members of this family have been annotated as being coiled-coil domain-containing protein 149, however they currently have no known function.

name: Ubiquitin 3 binding protein But2 C-terminal domain
description: This family is of proteins conserved in yeasts. It binds to Uba3 and is involved in the NEDD8 signalling pathway [[cite:PUB00044177]]. This family represents a presumed C-terminal domain.

name: Pet100
description: Pet100 is a chaperone required for the assembly of cytochrome c oxidase [[cite:PUB00075399]]. The human Pet100 homologue (also known as C19orf79) has been shown to be located in the mitochondrial inner membrane and forms a ~300 kDa subcomplex with mitochondrial complex IV subunits [[cite:PUB00075400]].

name: DENN domain-containing protein 11
description: DENN domain-containing protein 11 (also known as LCHN) is thought to play a role in neuritogenesis, as well as in neuronal recovery and/or restructuring in the hippocampus following transient cerebral ischemia [[cite:PUB00092489]].

name: Elongation complex protein 6
description: ELP6 is a subunit of the RNA polymerase II elongator complex. The Elongator complex promotes RNA-polymerase II transcript elongation through histone acetylation in the nucleus and tRNA modification in the cytoplasm. ELP5 and ELP6 play a major role in the migration, invasion and tumorigenicity of melanoma cells, as integral subunits of Elongator [[cite:PUB00075653]]

name: HECT-like Ubiquitin-conjugating enzyme (E2)-binding
description: HECT_2 is a family of UbcH10-binding proteins.

name: RZZ complex, subunit zwilch
description: The protein Zwilch is an essential component of the mitotic checkpoint, which prevents cells from prematurely exiting mitosis. It is required for the assembly of the dynein-dynactin, Mad2 complexes and spindly/CG15415 onto kinetochores [[cite:PUB00054075],[cite:PUB00054076],[cite:PUB00044111]].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF2357)
description: This entry was previously the N terminal portion of DUF524 ([pfam:PF04411]) before it was split into two. This domain has no known function. It is predicted to adopt an all beta secondary structure pattern followed by mainly alpha-helical structures [[cite:PUB00044133]].

name: Uncharacterized protein conserved in bacteria (DUF2057)
description: This domain, found in various prokaryotic proteins, has no known function.

name: Uncharacterized protein conserved in bacteria (DUF2058)
description: This domain, found in various prokaryotic proteins, has no known function.

name: Uncharacterized protein conserved in bacteria (DUF2059)
description: This domain, found in various prokaryotic proteins, has no known function.

name: Predicted membrane protein (DUF2061)
description: This domain, found in various prokaryotic proteins, has no known function.

name: Uncharacterized protein conserved in bacteria (DUF2062)
description: This domain, found in various prokaryotic proteins, has no known function.

name: HvfC C-terminal domain
description: This entry describes the N-terminal domain in HvfC ([swissprot:Q4QL34]), NGO_1945 ([swissprot:Q5F5I0], [pdbe:3dee]), BufC1 and various other proteins partnered with MNIO family peptide modification enzymes. HvfC, as described in Haemophilus influenzae, is a partner protein to the multinuclear nonheme iron-dependent oxidase (MNIO) enzyme HvfB [swissprot:Q4QL34], and participates in post-translational modification that converts the precursor protein HvfA (Haemophilus virulence factor A) into a copper-binding metallophore and a contributor to the cell's ability to invade host cells and survive as an intracellular pathogen [[cite:PUB00161768],[cite:PUB00161749],[cite:PUB00161769]]. The related protein NGO_1945 occurs in a similar genomic context and was previously suggested to be a DNA-binding protein [[cite:PUB00057687]]. It comprises residues 31 to 117 as a helical bundle with 4 main helices [[cite:PUB00057687]]. The C-terminal is represented by [[pfam:PF22106]].

name: Uncharacterized protein conserved in bacteria (DUF2064)
description: This family has structural similarity to proteins in the nucleotide-diphospho-sugar transferases superfamily. The similarity suggests that it is an enzyme with a sugar substrate.

name: Uncharacterized protein conserved in bacteria (DUF2065)
description: This domain, found in various prokaryotic proteins, has no known function.

name: DUF2066
description: This domain, found in various prokaryotic proteins, has no known function.

name: Uncharacterized protein conserved in archaea (DUF2067)
description: This domain, found in various archaeal proteins, has no known function.

name: Predicted membrane protein (DUF2069)
description: This domain, found in various prokaryotes, has no known function.

name: Predicted membrane protein (DUF2070)
description: This is a family of Archaeal 7-TM proteins. There are 6 closely assembled TM-regions at the N-terminus followed by a long intracellular, from residues 220-590, highly conserved region, of unknown function, terminating with one more TM-region. The short 25 residue section between TMs 5 and 6 might lie on the outer surface of the membrane and be acting as a receptor (from TMHMM).

name: Uncharacterized conserved protein (COG2071)
description: This conserved protein (similar to YgjF), found in various prokaryotes, has no known function.

name: Origin-associated protein OapC
description: This entry includes archaeal Zinc-ribbon containing proteins which are mostly uncharacterised. Some members of this entry have been described as OapC/ArvC, encoded by oapC gene which is part of the three-gene cluster oapABC, involved in generation of extracellular vesicles (arv, archaeal vesiculating GTAse). Knockout of OapC/ArvC leads to over vesiculation, possibly due to dysregulation of OapA/ArvA, a small GTPase, therefore, it has been suggested that OapC/ArvC may represent a GAP [[cite:PUB00154442],[cite:PUB00154443]].

name: Origin-associated protein OapB
description: This entry includes archaeal proteins whose function is unclear. Some members of this entry have been described as OapB/Arvb, encoded by oapB gene which is part of the three-gene cluster oapABC, involved in generation of extracellular vesicles (arv, archaeal vesiculating GTAse) [[cite:PUB00154442],[cite:PUB00154443]]. It has been suggested that OapB/ArvB could be a guanine nucleotide exchange factor (GEF), however, further experimental research is required to confirm this [[cite:PUB00154443]].

name: Membrane protein of 12 TMs
description: This family carries twelve transmembrane regions. It does not have any characteristic nucleotide-binding-domains of the GxSGSGKST type. so it may not be an ATP-binding cassette transporter. However, it may well be a transporter of some description. ABC transporters always have two nucleotide binding domains; this has two unusual conserved sequence-motifs: 'KDhKxhhR' and 'LxxLP'.

name: Schlafen group 3, DNA/RNA helicase domain
description: This domain is found in at the C terminus of group 3 Schlafen proteins from mammals, and represents the DNA/RNA helicase domain [[cite:PUB00070629]]. Schlafen proteins are involved in the control of cell proliferation, induction of immune responses, and in the regulation of viral replication [[cite:PUB00070625],[cite:PUB00070629],[cite:PUB00098266]]. These proteins inhibit DNA replication and promote cell death in response to DNA damage. They play a role in genome surveillance to kill cells with defective replication [[cite:PUB00098266]]. This domain is also found in various uncharacterised prokaryotic proteins fused to a DNA helicase, GIY-YIG or PD-(D/E)XK catalytic domain or HsdR-N(terminal) domain, which are similar to AAA DNA helicase, Type III restriction enzyme ATPase, RecD and RuvB helicase [[cite:PUB00098266]].

name: Uncharacterized protein conserved in bacteria (DUF2076)
description: This domain, found in various hypothetical prokaryotic proteins, has no known function. The domain, however, is found in various periplasmic ligand-binding sensor proteins.

name: Type VI secretion system protein DotU
description: DotU is a family of Gram-negative bacterial proteins that form part of the membrane-joining complex of the type VI secretion system. DotU binds tightly to IcmF and together they are tethered to the inner membrane at one end and the peptidoglycan layer at the other; they interact with Lip1 which then tethers the peptidoglycan layer to the outer membrane [[cite:PUB00075434]].

name: Predicted membrane protein (DUF2079)
description: This domain, found in various hypothetical prokaryotic proteins, has no known function.

name: Putative transposon-encoded protein (DUF2080)
description: This domain, found in various hypothetical archaeal proteins, has no known function.

name: Nucleic-acid-binding protein containing Zn-ribbon domain (DUF2082)
description: This domain, found in various hypothetical prokaryotic proteins, as well as some Zn-ribbon nucleic-acid-binding proteins has no known function.

name: Short-chain fatty acyl coenzyme A regulator, C-terminal
description: This entry includes short-chain fatty acid regulators such as RAMB (regulator of acetate metabolism B), PCCR (Propionyl-CoA carboxylase regulator), PrpR (Propionate regulator). RamB is a negative transcriptional regulator of genes involved in acetate metabolism of C. glutamicum. It is responsible for expression control of the AK, PTA, ICL, and MS genes and, thus, for the proper adaptation to acetate as carbon and energy source. Nucleotide sequence analysis indicate the RamB protein consists of 469 aa with a putative HTH motif at the N terminus [[cite:PUB00074928]]. PCCR prevents the accumulation of propionyl-CoA by controlling expression of the gene encoding propionyl-CoA carboxylase, which is responsible for propionyl-CoA consumption by Rhodobacter sphaeroides. Many other Proteobacteria and Actinomycetales contain one or several PccR homologs that group into distinct clades on the basis of the pathway of acyl-CoA metabolism that they control [[cite:PUB00076849]]. PrpR is a transcriptional activator controlling prpDBC2 operon which encodes enzymes 2-methylcitrate dehydratase (PrpD2), 2-methylisocitrate lyase (PrpB2) and 2-methylcitrate synthase (PrpC2). They are essential for growth with propionate as carbon source. The regulatory protein belongs to the HTH_XRE regulator family. It has a length of 441 amino acids and an N-terminal lamda repressor-like DNA-binding domain [[cite:PUB00106935]]. This is the C-terminal domain, which is likely an iron sensor domain that adopts a GAF-like fold [[cite:PUB00100702]].

name: Putative toxin of bacterial toxin-antitoxin pair
description: YjhX_toxin is a putative toxin of a bacterial toxin-antitoxin pair, which is neutralised by the proteins YjhQ in family [pfam:PF00583].

name: Predicted membrane protein (DUF2085)
description: This domain, found in various hypothetical prokaryotic proteins, has no known function.

name: Oxygenase, catalysing oxidative methylation of damaged DNA
description: This family of bacterial sequences is predicted to catalyse oxidative de-methylation of damaged bases in DNA.

name: Uncharacterized protein conserved in bacteria (DUF2087)
description: This domain, found in various hypothetical prokaryotic proteins and transcriptional activators, has no known function. Structural modelling suggests this domain may bind nucleic acids [[cite:PUB00070793]].

name: Lactate racemase N-terminal domain
description: This is the N-terminal domain found in Lactate racemase enzymes [ec:5.1.2.1]. LarA is a nickel-dependent lactate racemase from the larA-E operon of Lactobacillus plantarum, whereas LarB, LarC and LarE are accessory proteins required for the incorporation of Ni in the lactate racemase apoprotein. LarA contains 18 beta-strands and 16 alpha-helices arranged in a novel fold composed of two domains of similar size. This entry represents the N-terminal domain of LarA and related proteins [[cite:PUB00085157]].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF2089)-HTH
description: This domain, found in various hypothetical prokaryotic proteins, has no known function. It occurs as a fusion of ZnR+HTH+SHOCT-like.

name: Uncharacterized protein conserved in bacteria (DUF2090)
description: This domain, found in various prokaryotic carbohydrate kinases, has no known function.

name: Membrane-bound lysozyme-inhibitor of c-type lysozyme
description: Lysozymes are ancient and important components of the innate immune system of animals that hydrolyse peptidoglycan, the major bacterial cell wall polymer. Various mechanisms have evolved by which bacteria can evade this bactericidal enzyme, one being the production of lysozyme inhibitors. MliC (membrane bound lysozyme inhibitor of c-type lysozyme) of E. coli and Pseudomonas aeruginosa, possess lysozyme inhibitory activity and confer increased lysozyme tolerance upon expression in E. coli [[cite:PUB00054072]]. Structural analyses show that the invariant loop of MliC plays a crucial role in the inhibition of the lysozyme by its insertion into the active site cleft of the lysozyme, where the loop forms hydrogen and ionic bonds with the catalytic residues [[cite:PUB00051886]].

name: Predicted periplasmic protein (DUF2092)
description: This domain, found in various hypothetical prokaryotic proteins, has no known function.

name: Uncharacterized protein conserved in bacteria (DUF2093)
description: This domain, found in various hypothetical prokaryotic proteins, has no known function.

name: TagF N-terminal domain, Type VI secretion system-associated
description: This is the N-terminal domain of the T6S-associated protein, TagF. A post-translational repressor of the hemolysin co-regulated secretion island I (HSI-I)-encoded type VI secretion system (H1-T6SS) found in Pseudomonas aeruginosa. The type VI secretion system (T6SS) is found broadly among the Proteobacteria and is implicated in diverse processes including host-cell interactions, biofilm formation and gene regulation. Furthermore, studies indicate that the T6SS plays a critical role in interbacterial interactions. TagF has been shown to regulate the activity of the H1-T6SS in a manner that does not require phosphorylated-Fha1, PpkA, or other Tag proteins. Additionally TagF is found to associate as a homodimer with nearly identical monomers composed of alpha and beta elements assembled as a three-layer sandwich (alpha-beta-alpha) [[cite:PUB00086563]].

name: Uncharacterized protein conserved in archaea (DUF2095)
description: This domain, found in various hypothetical prokaryotic proteins, has no known function.

name: DUF2096 C-terminal KH-like domain
description: This domain, found in various hypothetical archaeal proteins, has no known function. The domain shows structural similarity to KH domains suggesting it may have an RNA-binding function.

name: Uncharacterized protein conserved in archaea (DUF2097)
description: This domain, found in various hypothetical prokaryotic proteins, has no known function.

name: Uncharacterized protein conserved in archaea (DUF2098)
description: This domain, found in various hypothetical prokaryotic proteins, has no known function.

name: Uncharacterized protein conserved in archaea (DUF2099)
description: This domain, found in various hypothetical prokaryotic proteins, has no known function.

name: SepCysE-like
description: This family includes MJ1481 from Methanocaldococcus jannaschii and similar archaeal proteins. MJ1481 has been reported to be SepCysE, a translation factor, essential for the methanococcal Cys biosynthesis. SepCysE forms a bridge between Sep-tRNA:Cys -tRNA synthase (SepCysS) and O-phosphoseryl-tRNA synthetase (SepRS), forming the transsulfursome complex, enabling substrate channelling of Sep-tRNACys [[cite:PUB00093677],[cite:PUB00093676]].

name: Predicted membrane protein (DUF2101)
description: This domain, found in various archaeal and bacterial proteins, has no known function.

name: Uncharacterized protein conserved in archaea (DUF2102)
description: This domain, found in various hypothetical archaeal proteins, has no known function.

name: Predicted metal-binding protein (DUF2103)
description: This domain, found in various putative metal binding prokaryotic proteins, has no known function.

name: Energy-converting hydrogenase subunit EhaL
description: This family of archaeal proteins represents the Energy-converting hydrogenase subunit EhaL [[cite:PUB00096941],[cite:PUB00014600]]. Eha is the essential conduit of electrons from H2 and supports methanogenesis [[cite:PUB00096941]].

name: EhaG-like

The Abi system is activated upon infection with phage to abort the cell thus preventing the spread of phage through viral replication. There are some 20 or more Abis, and they are predominantly plasmid-encoded lactococcal systems. TA, toxin-antitoxin, systems on plasmids function by killing cells that lose the plasmid upon division. AbiE phage resistance systems function as novel Type IV TAs and are widespread in bacteria and archaea. The cognate antitoxin is [pfam:PF13338] [[cite:PUB00075538]].

name: Bacterial antitoxin of type II TA system, VapB
description: VapB is the antitoxin of a bacterial toxin-antitoxin gene pair. The cognate toxin is VapC, [pfam:PF05016]. The family contains several related antitoxins from Cyanobacteria and Actinobacterial families. Antitoxins of this class carry an N-terminal ribbon-helix-helix domain, RHH, that is highly conserved across all type II bacterial antitoxins, which dimerises with the RHH domain of a second VapB molecule. A hinge section follows the RHH, with an additional pair of flexible alpha helices at the C-terminus. This C-terminus is the Toxin-binding region of the dimer, and so is specific to the cognate toxin, whereas the RHH domain has the specific function of lying across the RNA-binding groove of the toxin dimer and inactivating the active-site - a more general function of all antitoxins.

The structure of a member from Bacteroides has been crystallised and modelled onto the luminal region of the human member of the family, the transmembrane glycoprotein N-acetylglucosamine-1-phosphodiester alpha-N-acetylglucosaminidase. There is some conservation of potentially functional residues, implying that in the bacterial members this family acts in some way as a phosphodiester glycosidase [[cite:PUB00078675]]. The human protein is also present, so the eukaryotic members are likely to be catalysing the second step in the formation of the mannose 6-phosphate targeting signal on lysosomal enzyme oligosaccharides [[cite:PUB00108993]].

name: T6SS, Phospholipase effector Tle1-like, catalytic domain

Tle1 is organised into two distinct parts, the phospholipase catalytic module (this entry) and the putative membrane-anchoring module ([pfam:PF22137]). This domain adopts a compact conformation with a classical mixed alpha/beta-hydrolase fold that shows of seven central parallel beta-sheets and 13 alpha-helices [[cite:PUB00154252]].

name: ER-bound oxygenase mpaB/B'/Rubber oxygenase, catalytic domain

Structural analysis from Lcp revealed that Arg164, Thr168 and His198 are crucial active site residues [[cite:PUB00087009]]. The mpaB and mpaB' are part of the gene cluster that mediates the biosynthesis of mycophenolic acid (MPA) [[cite:PUB00096709]]. Lcp (Latex clearing proteins) is a rubber oxygenase that catalyses the extracellular cleavage of poly (cis-1,4-isoprene) [[cite:PUB00087009],[cite:PUB00096710]]. This domain is also present in uncharacterised proteins from Mycobacterium sp. and hypothetical proteins, mainly from bacteria and fungi.

name: Q-cell neuroblast polarisation
description: Dyp-19, formerly known as DUF2211, is a transmembrane domain family that is required to orient the neuroblast cells, QR and QL accurately on the anterior-posterior axis: QL and QR are born in the same anterior-posterior position, but polarise and migrate left-right asymmetrically, QL migrating towards the posterior and QR migrating towards the anterior. It is also required, with unc-40, to express mab-5 correctly in the Q cell descendants [[cite:PUB00044879]]. The Dpy-19 protein derives from the C. elegans DUMPY mutant, [swissprot:P34413].

description: Cas6 is a member of the RAMP (repeat-associated mysterious protein) superfamily [[cite:PUB00043288]]. It is among the most widely distributed Cas proteins and is found in both bacteria and archaea [[cite:PUB00020781]]. Cas6 functions in the generation of CRISPR-derived guide RNAs for invader defense in prokaryotes [[cite:PUB00054084]].

name: BufA1 family periplasmic bufferin-type metallophore
description: BufA1 family periplasmic bufferin-type metallophore belongs to a family of ribosomally synthesised and post-translationally modified peptide (RiPP) precursors that are modified by multinuclear nonheme iron-dependent oxidase (MNIO) enzymes. Unusual among RiPPs, these peptides have an Sec-dependent N-terminal signal peptide, and are delivered to the periplasm. Members of this family act as metallophores, analogous to methanobactin, can be induced by stress from excess concentrations of copper or other metals, reduce metal toxicity by sequestration, and are termed bufferins [[cite:PUB00161747],[cite:PUB00161748],[cite:PUB00161749]].

name: ER junction formation factor lunapark, zinc ribbon finger
description: This zinc ribbon domain is found in Endoplasmic reticulum junction formation protein (LNP1) and other related eukaryotic proteins. LNP1 plays a role in endoplasmic reticulum (ER) network formation [[cite:PUB00155939]]. It binds to the reticulons and Yop1p and resides at ER tubule junctions in both yeast and mammalian cells [[cite:PUB00155939]]. Lnp1 dimerises in vitro via this zinc finger domain and this is required for proper ER structure but not for the nuclear pore complex (NPC) integrity [[cite:PUB00155940]]. The latter role is determined by the interactions with other ER components, including Rtn1, Yop1, Pom33, and Per33 [[cite:PUB00155940]].
