description: This domain family is found in viruses, and is approximately 40 amino acids in length.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF3757)
description: This family of proteins is found in bacteria. Proteins in this family are typically between 94 and 154 amino acids in length.

name: TRAPPC10 C-terminal domain
description: This domain forms part of the TRAPP complex for mediating vesicle docking and fusion in the Golgi apparatus. The fungal version is referred to as Trs130, and an alternative vertebrate alias is TMEM1 [[cite:PUB00020479],[cite:PUB00055557]].

name: Virulence factor CipC-like
description: This entry (ex DUF3759) represents virulence factors and related proteins in fungi including Concanamycin-induced protein C. Virulence factor cipC is involved in host Brassica napus (canola) leaf infection [[cite:PUB00163274]].

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF3760)
description: This domain family is found in eukaryotes, and is typically between 46 and 64 amino acids in length.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF3761)
description: This family of proteins is found in bacteria. Proteins in this family are typically between 100 and 157 amino acids in length. This entry represents a likely zinc-binding domain.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF3762)
description: This domain family is found in viruses, and is approximately 80 amino acids in length. The family is found in association with [pfam:PF05533].

name: ATPase, RavA, C-terminal
description: This domain is found at the C-terminal of bacterial regulatory ATPase RavA (Regulatory ATPase variant A) [[cite:PUB00091615],[cite:PUB00097491]] and is the second subdomain that forms the discontinuous triple helical domain [[cite:PUB00091615]]. RavA forms an hexamer in which the triple helical domain mediates the lateral interactions between neighbouring RavA monomers [[cite:PUB00097491]].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF3764)
description: This family of proteins is found in bacteria. Proteins in this family are typically between 89 and 101 amino acids in length. AlphaFold 3 prediction shows these proteins form a confident homodimer structure which adopts a dimeric Alpha/Beta barrel structure.

name: Cytochrome c oxidase assembly protein COX20
description: Complex IV (CIV) is a copper-heme oxidase that couples electron transfer from cytochrome c to oxygen with proton extrusion across the inner membrane to contribute to the proton gradient required for ATP generation. This entry includes fungal mitochondrial complex IV assembly factor Cox20 [[cite:PUB00053731]] and its homologues (also known as FAM36A in metazoa [[cite:PUB00086694]]. Human CIV is formed by three catalytic core subunits (COX1/2/3). COX20 has been found to form a complex with SCO1, SCO2, and newly synthesized COX2. It may act as a chaperone in the early steps of COX2 maturation [[cite:PUB00088297]].

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF3768)
description: This family of proteins is found in bacteria. Proteins in this family are typically between 108 and 129 amino acids in length. There are two conserved sequence motifs: NDP and RVLT.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF3769)
description: This family of proteins is found in bacteria and eukaryotes. Proteins in this family are typically between 560 and 931 amino acids in length.

name: RNA-directed RNA polymerase L, PA-C-like domain
description: This domain is found in RNA-directed RNA polymerase L from from Bunyavirales. It has been described as the PA-C-like domain which forms a narrow and positively charged cleft with the thumb domain, where the 3' RNA is likely bound [[cite:PUB00101134]]. It is found in association with [pfam:PF04196].

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF3772)
description: This domain family is found in bacteria, and is approximately 60 amino acids in length. The family is found in association with [pfam:PF00924].

name: Type IVb secretion, IcmS, effector-recruitment
description: This is a family of Gram-negative bacterial proteins involved in the Dot/Icm type IVb transport system. Members are small acidic cytoplasmic proteins required for Dot/Icm-dependent activities. Binary complexes of IcmW-IcmS and of IcmS-LvgA have been consistently reported, suggestive of the binary WXG100 system. The IcmW-IcmS complex may play a role in recruitment of effector proteins to the transport apparatus [[cite:PUB00075640]].

name: Wound-induced protein
description: This family of proteins is found in eukaryotes. Proteins in this family are typically between 81 and 97 amino acids in length. The proteins in the family are often annotated as wound-induced proteins however there is little accompanying literature to confirm this.

name: Putative flagellar
description: Proteins in this entry are encoded in a subset of bacterial flagellar operons, generally between genes designated flgD and flgE, in species as diverse as Bacillus halodurans and various other Firmicutes, Geobacter sulfurreducens, and Bdellovibrio bacteriovorus.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF3775)
description: This domain family is found in bacteria, and is approximately 80 amino acids in length. There is a single completely conserved residue G that may be functionally important.

name: PHD finger protein 20, AT-hook
description: PHD finger protein 20 (PHF20) is a Methyllysine-binding protein, component of the MOF histone acetyltransferase protein complex. It consists of tandem Tudor domains at the N-terminal, an AT hook, a C2H2-type zinc finger, and a plant homeodomain (PHD) finger [[cite:PUB00059425],[cite:PUB00094038],[cite:PUB00061037]]. This entry represents the AT-hook domain, a putative DNA-binding domain [[cite:PUB00059425],[cite:PUB00094038],[cite:PUB00061037]].

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF3778)
description: This domain family is found in eukaryotes, and is typically between 48 and 61 amino acids in length. There is a conserved LRF sequence motif.

name: Extracellular tail, of 10TM putative phosphate transporter
description: This PHM7_ext family is found in plants and fungi. It represents the C-terminal extracellular domain of the putative phosphate transporter, PHM7 [[cite:PUB00063120]]. The three N-terminal TMS are found in family RSN1_TM, [pfam:PF02714]; the cytoplssmic domain is [pfam:PF14703], and the remaining 7TM region is in [pfam:PF02714].

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF3780)
description: This family of proteins is functionally uncharacterised.This family of proteins is found in bacteria. Proteins in this family are typically between 189 and 206 amino acids in length. There are two conserved sequence motifs: PEERWWL and GWR. This family is found in a very sporadic set of bacterial species, suggesting that it may have been horizontally transferred. One protein is annotated as plasmid borne.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF3781)
description: This family of proteins is functionally uncharacterised. This family of proteins is found in bacteria and archaea. Proteins in this family are typically between 82 and 98 amino acids in length. There are two conserved sequence motifs: GKNWY and ITA.

name: Peptide arginase FlmR/OhkR-like, N-terminal domain
description: This entry represents a domain found at the N-terminal end of FlmR from Flagellimonas meridianipacifica (Swiss A0A2T0MFS9), OhkR from Ohtaekwangia koreensis (Swiss A0A1T5M544) and similar uncharacterised proteins found in animals and bacteria. FlmR and OhkR have been reported to be peptide arginases that modify Arg residues to ornithine in bioactive RiPP peptides [[cite:PUB00162570]]. This domain is predicted to adopt an alpha/beta arginase-like fold.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF3782)
description: This family of proteins is functionally uncharacterised. This family of proteins is found in bacteria and archaea. Proteins in this family are typically between 91 and 186 amino acids in length.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF3783)
description: This presumed domain is functionally uncharacterised. This domain family is found in bacteria, archaea and eukaryotes, and is approximately 60 amino acids in length.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF3784)
description: This family of proteins is functionally uncharacterised. This family of proteins is found in bacteria and archaea. Proteins in this family are typically between 96 and 110 amino acids in length.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF3785)
description: This family of proteins is functionally uncharacterised.This family of proteins is found in bacteria. Proteins in this family are approximately 140 amino acids in length. These proteins share two CXXC motifs suggesting these are zinc binding proteins. This protein is found in clostridia in an operon with three signalling proteins, suggesting this protein may be a DNA-binding transcription regulator downstream of an as yet unknown signalling pathway (Bateman A pers obs).

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF3786)
description: This presumed domain is functionally uncharacterised. This family of proteins is found in bacteria. Proteins in this family are typically between 201 and 257 amino acids in length. Some proteins also contains an iron-sulfur cluster.

name: Spore surface protein CDIF630_02480
description: This family of proteins, previously known as DUF3787, represents the spore surface protein CDIF630_02480 from Clostridioides difficile and related proteins found in Clostridia. CDIF630_02480 contribute to maintain proper thickness of the spore coat and exosporium layers [[cite:PUB00152825]]. Members of this family contain a conserved TAAW sequence motif that may be functionally important.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF3788)
description: This family of proteins is functionally uncharacterised. This family of proteins is found in bacteria and archaea. Proteins in this family are typically between 137 and 149 amino acids in length. This family may be distantly related to RelE proteins.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF3789)
description: This family of proteins is functionally uncharacterised. This family of proteins is found in bacteria. Proteins in this family are approximately 40 amino acids in length. There are two completely conserved residues (V and C) that may be functionally important.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF3791)
description: This family of proteins is functionally uncharacterised. This family of proteins is found in bacteria. Proteins in this family are typically between 71 and 125 amino acids in length.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF3792)
description: This family of proteins is functionally uncharacterised. This family of proteins is found in bacteria. Proteins in this family are approximately 130 amino acids in length. These proteins are integral membrane proteins.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF3793)
description: This family of proteins is functionally uncharacterised. This family of proteins is found in bacteria. Proteins in this family are typically between 187 and 211 amino acids in length. There are two conserved sequence motifs: PHE and LGYP.

name: SipL, SPOCS domain
description: This is the SPOCS domain found in three copies in SipL from C. difficile, N-terminal to the LysM domain ([pfam:PF01476]) [[cite:PUB00101296]]. SipL (for SpoIVA-interacting protein) is involved in coat localization, and, together with SpoIVA, is a critical spore morphogenetic protein [[cite:PUB00101297]].

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF3795)
description: This family of proteins is functionally uncharacterised. This family of proteins is found in bacteria and archaea. Proteins in this family are typically between 99 and 171 amino acids in length. This protein is likely to be zinc binding given the conserved cysteines.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF3797)
description: This presumed domain is functionally uncharacterised. This domain family is found in bacteria and viruses, and is approximately 50 amino acids in length. There is a conserved CGN sequence motif.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF3798)
description: This family of proteins is functionally uncharacterised. This family of proteins is found in bacteria. Proteins in this family are typically between 247 and 417 amino acids in length. Most of the proteins in this family have an N-terminal lipoprotein attachment site. These proteins have distant similarity to periplasmic ligand binding families such as [pfam:PF02608], which suggests that this family have a similar role.

name: PDDEXK-like domain of unknown function (DUF3799)
description: This family of proteins is functionally uncharacterised. This family of proteins is found in bacteria and viruses. Proteins in this family are typically between 265 and 420 amino acids in length. It appears that these proteins are distantly related to the PDDEXK superfamily and so these domains are likely to be nucleases. This family has a C-terminal cysteine cluster similar to that found in [pfam:PF01930].

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF3800)
description: This family of proteins is functionally uncharacterised. This family of proteins is found in bacteria, archaea, eukaryotes and viruses. Proteins in this family are typically between 215 and 302 amino acids in length. There is a DE motif at the N-terminus and a QXXD motif at the C-terminus that may be functionally important.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF3801)
description: This family of proteins is functionally uncharacterised. This family of proteins is found in bacteria. Proteins in this family are typically between 158 and 187 amino acids in length. This family includes the PcfB protein.

name: Lipocalin-like
description: This is a family of proteins of 115 residues on average. The family has two highly conserved tryptophan residues. The fold is very similar to the lipocalin-like fold from several comparable structures.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF3804)
description: This family is approximately 130 residues. Dali search indicates this protein carries a NTF2-fold with a hydrophobic cavity as a structural homologue to 1JB2, 2R4I, 3FSD and 2UX0. In this hydrophobic cavity, Arg 118 provides the H-bonding force to hold a PEG molecule from crystallisation. The interface interaction suggests that the biomolecule of [swissprot:Q46KI2] is a dimer. Two members of the family are annotated as putative EF-Tu domain 2 but there is no match to this family so this is likely to be a false assignment. There are two highly conserved tryptophan residues towards the C-terminal end of the family.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF3805)
description: This family represent the N-terminal domain of the structure. In two related Bacteroides species the gene lies immediately upstream from a putative ATP binding component of an ATP transporter and a putative histidinol phosphatase. The structure of this domain is strikingly similar to the N-terminal structure of 1tui, also of unknown function. The domain carries four conserved tryptophan residues.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF3806)
description: This family represent the C-terminal domain of the structure. In two related Bacteroides species the gene lies immediately upstream from a putative ATP binding component of an ATP transporter and a putative histidinol phosphatase. The structure of this domain is strikingly similar to the N-terminal structure of 1ma7 whose C-terminal domain is a phage integrase, [pfam:PF00589].

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF3807)
description: This is a family of conserved fungal proteins of unknown function.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF3809)
description: This family of proteins is functionally uncharacterised. This family of proteins is found in Deinococci bacteria. Proteins in this family are typically between 117 and 157 amino acids in length.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF3810)
description: This family of proteins is functionally uncharacterised. This family of proteins is found in bacteria. Proteins in this family are typically between 333 and 377 amino acids in length. There is a conserved HEXXH sequence motif that is characteristic of metallopeptidases. This family may therefore belong to an as yet uncharacterised family of peptidase enzymes.

name: Eisosome protein 1
description: Eisosome protein 1 is required for normal formation of eisosomes, large cytoplasmic protein assemblies that localize to specialised domains on plasma membrane and mark the site of endocytosis [[cite:PUB00056207]].

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF3813)
description: This is an uncharacterised family of Bacillus proteins.

name: 4TM region of pyridine nucleotide transhydrogenase, mitoch
description: PNTB_4TM is the region upstream of family PNTB, [pfam:PF02233], that carries four of this transporters transmembrane regions. PNTB is the beta-subunit of pyridine nucleotide transhydrogenase. This family forms part of the Proton-translocating Transhydrogenase (PTH) Family.

name: Threonine/Serine exporter, ThrE
description: ThrE_2 is a family of membrane proteins involved in the export of threonine and serine. L-threonine, L-serine are both substrates for the exporter. The exporter exhibits nine-ten predicted transmembrane-spanning helices with long charged C and N termini and an amphipathic helix present within the N terminus [[cite:PUB00075687]]. L-Threonine can be made by the amino acid-producing bacterium Corynebacterium glutamicum, but the potential for amino acid formation can be considerably improved by reducing its intracellular degradation into glycine and increasing its export by this exporter [[cite:PUB00075540]]. Members of the family are found in Bacteria, Archaea, and the fungal kingdoms, and the family can exist either as a single long polypeptide chain or as two short polypeptides [[cite:PUB00075540]]. All family members show an extended hydrophilic N-terminal domain with weak sequence similarity to portions of hydrolases (proteases, peptidases, and glycosidases); this suggests that since this region is cytoplasmic to the membrane it may be generating the transport substrate, so may imply that threonine may not be the primary substrate and the ThrE has a subsidiary function [[cite:PUB00075688]].

name: ECF transporter, substrate-specific component
description: Energy-coupling factor (ECF) transporters consist of a substrate-specific component (known as the S component), and an energy-coupling module [[cite:PUB00056162]]. The substrate-binding component is a small integral membrane protein which captures specific substrates and forms an active transporter in the presence of the energy-coupling AT module.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF3817)
description: This domain is of unknown function. It is sometimes found adjacent to [pfam:PF07690] and [pfam:PF03176] which are both transporter domains.

name: Domain of unknown function in PX-proteins (DUF3818)
description: This domain is found on proteins carrying a PX domain. Its function is unknown.

name: CCR4-Not complex, Not1 subunit, domain of unknown function DUF3819
description: This is an uncharacterised domain that is found on the CCR4-Not complex component Not1. Not1 is a global regulator of transcription that affects genes positively and negatively and is thought to regulate transcription factor TFIID [[cite:PUB00010586]].

name: Putative quorum-sensing-regulated virulence factor
description: QSregVF_b is a family of short Pseudomonas proteins that are potential virulence factors. The structure of UniProtKB:Q9HY15 a secreted protein has been solved and deposited as PDB:3npd, from [pfam:PF13652]. It is predicted that these two adjacent proteins form a single transcriptional unit based on the prediction that together they interact with their adjacent protein PotD, which is the putrescine-binding periplasmic protein in the polyamine uptake system comprising PotABCD. These two adjacent proteins are predicted to be quroum-sensing-regulated virulence factors [[cite:PUB00075641]].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF3821)
description: This is a domain largely confined to sequences from Methanomicrobiales found on putative lipases. The function is not known.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF3822)
description: This is a family of uncharacterised bacterial proteins. However, structural-similarity searches indicate the family takes on an actin-like ATPase fold.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF3823) N-terminal domain
description: This is a family of uncharacterised proteins from Bacteroidetes. This domain has a beta-sandwich prealbumin-like fold.

name: Domain of unknwon function (DUF3824)
description: This is a repeating domain found in fungal proteins. It is proline-rich, and the function is not known.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF4878)
description: This is a family of putative lipoproteins from bacteria. The family is probably related to the NTF2-like transpeptidase family.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF3825)
description: Potential uncharacterized enzymatic domain associated with bacterial [pfam:PF12872] domains. Has conserved residues suggestive of an enzymatic role probably related to RNA metabolism.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF3826)
description: This is a putative sugar-binding family.

name: UPF0606 protein KIAA1549 alpha/beta domain 2
description: This entry represents an alpha/beta domain found in the KIAA1549 protein from human ([swissprot:Q9HCM3]) which has been implicated in pilocytic astrocytomas [[cite:PUB00056166],[cite:PUB00056167],[cite:PUB00056168]]. It has been found to be fused to BRAF gene in many cases of pilocytic astrocytomas. The fusion is due mainly to a tandem duplication of 2 Mb at 7q34 [[cite:PUB00056166],[cite:PUB00056167]]. The BRAF protein is a well characterised oncoprotein. It is a serine/threonine protein kinase which is implicated in MAP/ERK signalling, a critical pathway for the regulation of cell division, differentiation and secretion [[cite:PUB00056166],[cite:PUB00056167],[cite:PUB00056168]]. More recently, KIAA1549 has been described to play a role in photoreceptor function [[cite:PUB00101492]]. This protein contains three homologous domains of this type found in tandem.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF3828)
description: This is a family of bacterial proteins of unknown function.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF3829)
description: This is a small family of proteins from several bacterial species, whose function is not known. It may, however, be related to the GvpL_GvpF family of proteins, [pfam:PF06386].

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF3830)
description: This is a family of bacterial and archaeal proteins, the structure for one of whose members has been characterised. PDB:3kop from [swissprot:A0JVT3] probably adopts a new hexameric form compared to previous structures. The putative active is near the domain interface. 3kop is most closely related, structurally to PDB:1zx8, where the potential active site is located near residues E51 and Y53 (conserved in 1zx8). name: Endospore appendages
description: The surface of Bacillus and Clostridium endospores is decorated with long filamentous endospores appendages that resemble pili from Gram- negative and Gram-positive bacteria. They show two morphologies, the main or Staggered-type (S-Ena) which accounts for 90% of the fibres, and the Ladder-like (L-Ena) which is smaller and less abundant. They are a novel class of Gram-positive pili, consisting in single domain subunits with a jellyroll topology comprised by two juxtaposed beta-sheets. This domain represents the S-Ena core. Disulfide bonding through the N-terminal connector peptide that precedes this domain stabilizes longitudinally the fibres, bridging the helical turns. name: MBH, subunit D
description: Hydrogen gas-evolving membrane-bound hydrogenase (MBH) is a respiratory complex homologous to the quinone-reducing Complex I. Like Complex I, MBH has peripheral and membrane arms. MBH is made of 14 subunits (MbhA-N). MbhJ, K, L, N and M form the Membrane-anchored hydrogenase module. MbhJ, K, L, N are predicted to be exposed to the cytoplasm and form the peripheral arm. The remaining 10 subunits are predicted to be integral membrane proteins forming the membrane arm, made of 44 transmembrane helices (TMH) [[cite:PUB00098955],[cite:PUB00098954]]. MbhA, B, C and F form the Sodium translocation module. MbhD, E, G and H form the Proton translocation module. MbhI is the linker between the hydrogenase module and the proton-translocating membrane module. It anchors the discontinuous TMH7 of MbhH via its middle lateral helix and the C-terminal of TMH2, found in MbhE. MbhD and MbhE together are equivalent to Nqo10 of Complex I [[cite:PUB00098952]]. MbhD has three TM helices.

description: This domain is found at the C terminus of protein members of the glycoside hydrolase family 123, including N-acetylgalactosaminidase from Clostridium perfringens. This enzyme removes specific terminal N-D-acetylgalactosamine from glycosphingolipids. This catalytic domain adopts an alpha/beta barrel configuration with a two-stranded beta sheet and a pair of alpha-helices at the C-terminal end [[cite:PUB00100654],[cite:PUB00151590]].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF4084)
description: This family of Firmicute proteins is frequently associated with the EAL, GGDEF and PAS families, [pfam:PF00563], [pfam:PF00990], and [pfam:PF00989]. The exact function is not known.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF4092)
description: This family is found in Proteobacteria. The function is not known.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF4093)
description: This domain lies at the C-terminus of primase proteins carrying the TOPRIM, [pfam:PF01751], domain. The exact function of the domain is not known.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF4094)
description: This domain is found in plant proteins that often carry a galactosyltransferase domain, [pfam:PF01762], at their C-terminus.

name: Transcriptional regulator, AbiEi antitoxin
description: AbiEi_4 is the cognate antitoxin of the type IV toxin-antitoxin 'innate immunity' bacterial abortive infection (Abi) system that protects bacteria from the spread of a phage infection. The Abi system is activated upon infection with phage to abort the cell thus preventing the spread of phage through viral replication. There are some 20 or more Abis, and they are predominantly plasmid-encoded lactococcal systems. TA, toxin-antitoxin, systems on plasmids function by killing cells that lose the plasmid upon division. AbiE phage resistance systems function as novel Type IV TAs and are widespread in bacteria and archaea. The cognate antitoxin is [pfam:PF13338] [[cite:PUB00075538]].

name: Toastrack DUF4097
description: This an all-beta structure with a twenty-residue repeat with a highly conserved repeating GD, gly-asp, motif that has been described as Toastrack DUF4097, whose function is unknown. It has been suggested to form part of a bacterial adhesin. Toastrack has been transferred from bacteria to certain eukaryotes, such as FAM185A from human and its orthologues in animals and other eukaryotes.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF4099)
description: A family of uncharacterized proteins found by clustering human gut metagenomic sequences [[cite:PUB00055601]]. The C-terminal repeat region of this family is DUF4098, [pfam:PF13345].

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF4100)
description: This is a family of uncharacterised proteins. Some members have an aspartic peptidase domain at the C-terminal ([pfam:PF13650]).

name: ARC6-like, IMS domain
description: This domain corresponds to the C-terminal intermembrane space (IMS) region from protein accumulation and replication of chloroplasts 6 (ARC6) and its paralogue PARC6 [[cite:PUB00096838]]. ARC6 and PARC6 are components of the plastid division machinery which are essential for the chloroplast replication process [[cite:PUB00096838],[cite:PUB00096839]], which implies the assembly and constriction of the tubulin-like FtsZ ring on the stromal surface of the inner envelope membrane (IEM) and the dynamin-like ARC5 ring on the cytosolic surface of the outer envelope membrane (OEM). ARC6 is evolutionarily related to the cyanobacterial cell division protein Ftn2/ZipN [[cite:PUB00096838]], having similar structures. This domain from ARC6 and PARC6 interacts with PDV2 and PDV1 respectively. PDV proteins recruit dynamin-like ARC5 ring to the chloroplast surface and mediates its constriction. ARC6/PARC6 are key to connect and coordinate Fst and ARC5 rings during fission [[cite:PUB00096837],[cite:PUB00096840]].

name: Arm DNA-binding domain
description: This DNA-binding domain is found at the N-terminus of a wide variety of phage integrase proteins.

name: Alginate export
description: This domain forms an 18-stranded beta-barrel pore which is likely to act as an alginate export channel [[cite:PUB00056376]].

name: DSC E3 ubiquitin ligase complex subunit 3, C-terminal domain
description: This is the C-terminal domain of DSC E3 ubiquitin ligase complex subunit 3 (Dsc3), which contains two transmembrane helices and a characteristic GFDRL sequence motif. Dsc3 is a component of the DSC E3 ubiquitin ligase complex (a Golgi-specific protein ubiquitination system) that functions in protein homeostasis under non-stress conditions, playing a role in protein quality control [[cite:PUB00098312],[cite:PUB00098082],[cite:PUB00098314]]. Yeast DSC E3 ubiquitin ligase complex is the homologue of Hrd1 E3 ligase complex from mammals, in which Dsc1, Dsc2 and Dsc3 corresponds to Hrd1, Der1, and Usa1, respectively. Dsc3 is a Herp-like protein that acts as a bridge between Dsc1 and Dsc2 for their interaction [[cite:PUB00075404]].

name: Lnb N-terminal periplasmic domain
description: This domain, previously known as DUF4105, is found N-terminal in Lipoprotein N-acyltransferase Lnb from Bacteroides and related uncharacterised bacterial proteins. Lnb functions as a lipoprotein N-acyltransferase in its native cell background [[cite:PUB00158892]]. It is composed of two domains, N-terminal (this entry) and C-terminal alpha- helical transmembrane domain. The domain represented by this entry contains a highly conserved histidine residue and a well-conserved NCT motif. Its predicted structure has a significant similarity to the papain-like cysteine peptidases. In addition, the putative catalytic triad Asn-His-Cys is highly conserved. This domain is also found in combination with other domains.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF4106)
description: This family of proteins are found in large numbers in the Trichomonas vaginalis proteome. The function of this protein is unknown.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF4107)
description: This family of putative proteins are found in Trichomonas vaginalis in large numbers. The function of this protein is unknown.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF4108)
description: This family of putative proteins are found in Trichomonas vaginalis in large numbers. The function of this protein is unknown.

name: RNA polymerase-binding protein
description: RbpA is a family bacterial RNA polymerase-binding proteins. RbpA acts as a transcription factor by binding to the sigma subunit of RNA polymerase [[cite:PUB00069577],[cite:PUB00152374],[cite:PUB00152372],[cite:PUB00152371],[cite:PUB00152373],[cite:PUB00067238],[cite:PUB00069578]].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF4110)
description: This is a family that is found predominantly at the C-terminus of Kelch-containing proteins. However, the exact function of this region is not known.

name: Aminoglycoside adenylyltransferase, C-terminal domain
description: This domain is found at the C-terminal end of Aminoglycoside adenylyltransferase from Salmonella typhimurium (AadA) and other proteins associated with methicillin-resistant bacteria. AadA adenylates the 3''-hydroxyl group of the streptomycin glucosamine ring and the 9-hydroxyl group of the spectinomycin actinamine ring, mediating bacterial resistance to these antibiotics. This enzyme is organised into two domains: a N-terminal domain with a nucleotidyltransferase fold ([pfam:PF01909]) and a C-terminal domain (this entry) which consists of five alpha-helices forming an up-and-down alpha-helical bundle. This domain undergoes small conformational changes upon binding of ATP and magnesium that play a key role in the binding of the antibiotic compounds [[cite:PUB00091136],[cite:PUB00100854]].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF4112)
description: This family has several highly conserved GD sequence-motifs of unknown function. The family is found in bacteria, archaea and fungi.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF4113)
description: Although the function is not known this domain occurs almost invariably at the very C-terminus of the IMS family DNA-polymerase repair proteins, IMS, [pfam:PF00817].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF4114)
description: This is a repeated domain that is found towards the C-terminal of many different types of bacterial proteins. There are highly conserved glutamate and aspartate residues suggesting that this domain might carry enzymic activity.

name: RodZ C-terminal domain
description: This short domain is often found at the C-terminus of RodZ cytoskeletal proteins. These proteins usually contain a helix-turn-helix domain.

name: 4TM region of DNA translocase FtsK/SpoIIIE
description: 4TM_FtsK is the integral membrane domain of the FtsK DNA tranlocases. During sporulation in Bacillus subtilis, the SpoIIIE protein is believed to form a translocation pore at the leading edge of the nearly closed septum. The E. coli FtsK protein is homologous to SpoIIIE, and can free chromosomes trapped in vegetative septa.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF4118)
description: This domain is found in a wide variety of bacterial signalling proteins. It is likely to be a transmembrane domain involved in ligand sensing.

name: Domain of unknown function, B. Theta Gene description (DUF4119)
description: Based on Bacteroides thetaiotaomicron gene BT_0594, a putative uncharacterised protein. As seen in gene expression experiments (http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE2231), it appears to be upregulated in the presence of host or vs when in culture [[cite:PUB00056011],[cite:PUB00056012]]

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF4120)
description: Based on Bacteroides thetaiotaomicron gene BT_2585, a putative uncharacterised protein. As seen in gene expression experiments (http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE2231), it appears to be upregulated in the presence of host or vs when in culture [[cite:PUB00056011],[cite:PUB00056012]].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF4121)
description: Based on Bacteroides thetaiotaomicron gene BT_2588, a putative uncharacterised protein. As seen in gene expression experiments (http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE2231), it appears to be upregulated in the presence of host or vs when in culture [[cite:PUB00056011],[cite:PUB00056012]].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF4122)
description: Based on Bacteroides thetaiotaomicron gene BT_2607, a putative uncharacterized protein. As seen in gene expression experiments (http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE2231), it appears to be upregulated in the presence of host or vs when in culture [[cite:PUB00056011],[cite:PUB00056012]].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF4123)
description: This presumed domain is functionally uncharacterised. It is about 120 amino acids in length and contains several conserved motifs that may be functionally important. This domain is sometimes associated with the FHA domain.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF4124)
description: This presumed domain is found in a variety of bacterial proteins. It is found associated at the N-terminus associated with other domains such as the SLT domain and glutaredoxin domains in some proteins. The function of this domain is unknown, but it may have an Ig-like fold.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF4127)
description: This family of uncharacterised bacterial proteins are about 500 amino acids in length.

name: Phage tail terminator protein
description: The three-dimensional structure of NP_888769.1, PDB:2L25, reveals a tail terminator protein gpU fold, which suggests that the protein could have a bacteriophage origin.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF4129)
description: This presumed domain is found at the C-terminus of proteins that contain a transglutaminase core domain. The function of this domain is unknown. The domain has a conserved TXXE motif.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF4131)
description: This domain is frequently found to the N-terminus of the Competence domain, [pfam:PF03772].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF4132)
description: This domain might be involved in the biosynthesis of the molybdopterin cofactor in E.coli.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF4133)
description: Based on Bacteroides thetaiotaomicron gene BT_0094, a putative uncharacterized protein as seen in gene expression experiments (http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE2231), It appears to be upregulated in the presence of host or vs when in culture [[cite:PUB00056011]][[cite:PUB00056012]].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF4134)
description: Based on Bacteroides thetaiotaomicron gene BT_0095, a putative uncharacterized protein As seen in gene expression experiments (http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE2231), It appears to be upregulated in the presence of host or vs when in culture [[cite:PUB00056011]][[cite:PUB00056012]].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF4135)
description: This presumed domain is functionally uncharacterised. This domain family is found in bacteria and archaea, and is approximately 380 amino acids in length. The family is found in association with [pfam:PF05147]. This domain may be involved in synthesis of a lantibiotic compound.

name: BatD DUF11 like domain
description: This domain that probably has an Ig-like fold is found in three copies in BatD proteins that are involved in tolerance to oxygen in in Bacteroides spp.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF4136)
description: This domain is found in bacterial lipoproteins. The function is not known.

name: SBF-like CPA transporter family (DUF4137)
description: These family members are 7TM putative membrane transporter proteins. The family is similar to the SBF family of bile-acid symporters, [pfam:PF01758].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF4138)
description: Based on Bacteroides thetaiotaomicron gene BT_4780, a putative uncharacterized protein. As seen in gene expression experiments (http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE2231), it appears to be upregulated in the presence of host or vs when in culture [[cite:PUB00056011],[cite:PUB00056012]]. This entry represents the C-terminal domain which may have a Ig-like fold.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF4139)
description: This family is usually found at the C-terminus of proteins.

name: N-terminal domain of unknown function (DUF4140)
description: This family is often found at the N-terminus of its member proteins, with DUF4139, [pfam:PF13598], at the C-terminus.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF4141)
description: Based on Bacteroides thetaiotaomicron gene BT_4772, a putative uncharacterized protein. As seen in gene expression experiments (http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE2231), it appears to be upregulated in the presence of host or vs when in culture [[cite:PUB00056011],[cite:PUB00056012]].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF4142)
description: This is a bacterial family of unknown function.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF4143)
description: This domain is almost always found C-terminal to an ATPase core family.

name: protein structure with unknown function
description: A family based on the three-dimensional structure of YP_926445.1 (PDB:2L6O)

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF4145)
description: This domain is found in a variety of restriction endonuclease enzymes. The exact function of this domain is uncertain.

name: Putative quorum-sensing-regulated virulence factor
description: This is a family of short ~14 kDa proteins from Psuedomonas. The structure of UniProtKB:Q9HY15 a secreted protein has been solved and deposited as PDB:3npd. It comprises one structural domain with five beta-strands and five alpha-helices. Various comparative structural prediction methods plus its genomic location point to the protein forming a functional dimer with its adjacent genomic partner, UniProtKB:Q9HY14, in [pfam:PF12843]. Together these might be regulated by the other product from the PotABCD operon, namely the putrescine-binding periplasmic protein UniProtKB:Q9HY16. which has been implicated in quorum-sensing. QSregVF is certainly up-regulated in quorum-sensing, and is predicted to be a virulence factor [[cite:PUB00075641]].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF4147)
description: This domain is frequently found at the N-terminus of proteins carrying the glycerate kinase-like domain MOFRL, [pfam:PF05161].

name: Toxin PAAR-like domain
description: This domain is found at the N-terminal of bacterial toxin systems, including Tse7 (type IV secretion exported 7) from Pseudomonas aeruginosa, a type VI secretion exported toxin with DNase activity that induces growth arrest and ultimately DNA degradation within target cell [[cite:PUB00098743]]. The structure of this domain has a PAAR-like organisation necessary for interaction with T6SS VgrG tip and correct toxin delivery [[cite:PUB00098743],[cite:PUB00098744]].

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF4152)
description: This family of proteins is functionally uncharacterised. This family of proteins is found in archaea. Proteins in this family are approximately 230 amino acids in length. The structure of PF2046 from pyrococcus furiosus has been solved. It shows an RNaseH like fold that conserves critical catalytic residues [[cite:PUB00057311]]. This suggests that these proteins may cleave nucleic acid.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF4153)
description: Members of this family are annotated as putative inner membrane proteins.

name: YfiR/HmsC-like
description: This family of proteins is found in bacteria and includes YfiR from E. coli. YfiR has been shown to regulate YfiN, a diguanylate cyclase and a bifunctional protein that produces c-di-GMP in response to reductive stress and then dynamically relocates to the division site to arrest cell division in response to envelope stress in Escherichia coli. YfiR may serve as a periplasmic redox sensor that regulates YfiN activity in response to reducing conditions [[cite:PUB00088310],[cite:PUB00088309]]. HmsC in Yersinia Pestis is the orthologue of YfiR from E. coli [[cite:PUB00091013]]. HmsC is a periplasmic protein that interacts directly with the periplasmic domain (PD) of HmsD and causes proteolytic degradation of HmsD, which in turn negatively regulates Y. pestis biofilm formation [[cite:PUB00091014]].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF4156)
description: The function of this family is unknown but members are annotated as putative lipoprotein outer membrane proteins.

name: eCIS core domain
description: This entry represents a domain found in a group of prokaryotic proteins that was previously known as DUF4157. This domain has been recently identified as a highly conserved eCIS (extracellular Contractile Injection System) core domain [[cite:PUB00154361]]. eCIS is a cell-free toxin-delivery system that evolved from a bacteriophage tail and is prevalent in prokaryotes. This eCIS core DUF4157 domain contains an HEXXH motif that is characteristic of many families of metallopeptidases and a putative metal-binding site for a divalent cation such as zinc. Proteobacterial members of this family are thought to be related to the type VI secretion system (T6SS). This region is responsible for the toxicity of the protein in the bacterial periplasm [[cite:PUB00100134]]. eCIS-associated toxins carry DUF4157 domains in their N-terminus or are found adjacent to genes with this domain [[cite:PUB00154361]]. No peptidase activity has been reported for this domain so far.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF4158)
description: The exact function of this domain is not clear, but it frequently occurs as an N-terminal region of transposase 3 or IS3 family of insertion elements.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF4942)
description: The function of this family is not known.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF4159)
description: Members of this family are hypothetical proteins.

name: CarboxypepD_reg-like domain
description: This domain family is found in bacteria, archaea and eukaryotes, and is approximately 90 amino acids in length. The family is found in association with [pfam:PF07715] and [pfam:PF00593].

name: ATP-binding protein DrrA1-3-like, C-terminal domain
description: This domain is found at the C-terminal end of Daunorubicin resistance ATP-binding protein DrrA1-3 from Streptomyces coeruleorubidus and related prokaryotic sequences. DrrA1-3 are part of the ABC transporter complex DrrA3B3 involved in daunorubicin efflux [[cite:PUB00158909]].

name: Deacetylase PdaC
description: This domain forms an alpha-beta-two layer sandwich. It is found in the Bacillus subtilis proteins anti-sigma-V factor RsiV, which downregulates SigV activity [[cite:PUB00084362]], and peptidoglycan-N-acetylmuramic acid deacetylase PdaC, which catalyzes the deacetylation of N-acetylmuramic acid which makes the peptidoglycan resistant to lysosyme [[cite:PUB00084363]]. It is found in association with Heat-shock cognate 70kd protein 44kd ATPase, [pfam:PF11738].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF4164)
description: This is a family of short, approx 100 residue-long, bacterial proteins of unknown function. There is several conserved LE/LD sequence pairs.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF4166)
description: This domain is often found at the C-terminus of proteins containing [pfam:PF03435].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF4171)
description: This short family is frequently found at the N-terminus of Homeobox proteins.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF4172)
description: The family is often found in association with [pfam:PF02661].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF4174)
description: This domain of unknown function is found in a putative tumour suppressor gene [[cite:PUB00057318]] and in a ligand for the the urokinase-type plasminogen activator receptor, which plays a role in cellular migration and adhesion [[cite:PUB00057319],[cite:PUB00057320]].

name: SR1 protein
description: This family of proteins is encoded by the dual function SR1 RNA. SR1 is a sRNA which regulates arginine metabolism [[cite:PUB00075682]], it also encodes a short protein that binds to glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate dehydrogenase (GapA) and stabilises the gapA operon mRNAs [[cite:PUB00075683]].

name: Fibrillar ENdospore Appendages
description: This entry, previously known as DUF4183, represents the so-called Fibrillar ENdospore Appendages or F-ENAs found mainly in Bacilli lineage. F-ENA subunits assemble into trimeric units that stack axially into a helical ultrastructure fibers [[cite:PUB00163791]]. F-ENAs contribute to spore clustering. At the spore distal terminus, F-ENAs are decorated with a flexible tip fibrillum that consists of the collagen-like protein F-BclA [[cite:PUB00163791]].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF4184)
description: This domain of unknown function contains several highly conserved histidines.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF4187)
description: This family is found at the very C-terminus of proteins that carry a G-patch domain, [pfam:PF01585]. The domain is short and cysteine-rich.

name: Monooxygenase af470-like
description: This entry includes Monooxygenase af470-like from Aspergillus fumigatus, which is part of the fma gene cluster that mediates the biosynthesis of fumagillin, a meroterpenoid with numerous biological activities [[cite:PUB00081410]]. It has been suggested that af470 mediates the oxidative cleavage of the terminal alkene of the dodecapentaenoate side chain into the carboxylic acid present in fumagillin [[cite:PUB00081411]].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF4189)
description: This domain of unknown function contains six well-conserved cysteine residues.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF4190)
description: This integral membrane domain is functionally uncharacterised. One of the membrane helices contains two GXXG motifs that are usually associated with dimerisation.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF4193)
description: This domain of unknown function contains four conserved cysteines and a conserved histidine, including a CXXXXH motif.

name: Wadjet protein JetB
description: This family includes Wadjet protein JetB, a component of anti plasmid transformation system Wadjet type I, composed of JetA, JetB, JetC and JetD. Expression of Wadjet type I in B.subtilis (strain BEST7003) reduces the transformation efficiency of plasmid pHCMC05 [[cite:PUB00097806]]. The Wadjet proteins JetA, JetB, and JetC show sequence similarity to subunits of the bacterial condensin complex MukBEF, a member of the SMCs complex superfamily. The overall structure of JetB and its interaction with JetA is very similar to that of MukE, and the overall positioning of the JetB dimer with respect to JetA is also similar to the MukF-MukE complex [[cite:PUB00163953]]. JetB is composed of two winged helix domains.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF4195)
description: This family is found at the N-terminus of metazoan proteins that carry PHD-like zinc-finger domains. The function is not known.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF4196)
description: This is a short region of ccdc82_homologues that is conserved from Schizo. pombe up to humans. The function is not known.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF4197)
description: This family of proteins is functionally uncharacterised. This family of proteins is found in bacteria. Proteins in this family are typically between 228 and 249 amino acids in length.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF4199)
description: This family of proteins is functionally uncharacterised. This family of proteins is found in bacteria. Proteins in this family are typically between 167 and 182 amino acids in length.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF4200)
description: This family is found in eukaryotes. It is a coiled-coil domain of unknwon function.

name: CCDC113/CCDC96, coiled-coil
description: This entry represents the coiled-coil region of Coiled-coil domain-containing protein 113 (CCDC113, also known as cilia- and flagella-associated protein 263, CFAP263) and coiled-coil domain-containing protein 96 (CCDC96, also known as cilia- and flagella-associated protein 184, CFAP184) [[cite:PUB00159884],[cite:PUB00153410]]. These proteins form a complex and regulate ciliary beating that connects radial spoke 3 (RS3) to the inner dynein arm (IDA) and the nexin-dynein regulatory complex (N-DRC). The complex is positioned parallel to N-DRC and forms a connection between the arch at the base of RS3, the IDA tail and N-DRC [[cite:PUB00159884]].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF4202)
description: This family of proteins is found in bacteria, archaea and eukaryotes. Proteins in this family are typically between 187 and 205 amino acids in length. There are two conserved sequence motifs: LED and KMS. The function of these proteins is unknown, although many are incorrectly annotated as glutamyl tRNA synthetases.

name: TM7S3/TM198-like domain
description: This domain is found at the C-terminal end of human Transmembrane 7 superfamily member 3 (TM7SF3), which is is involved in the inhibition of cytokine-induced death of pancreatic beta cells, towards the N terminus of human Transmembrane protein 198 (TM198), which plays a role in Wnt signalling and in similar proteins mainly found in animal, fungi and bacteria. This domain is predicted to adopt an all alpha-helical structure.

name: Chromosome segregation during meiosis
description: The proteins come from eukaryotes, plants and animals, and are necessary for chromosome segregation during meiosis.

name: Deubiquitinating enzyme MINDY-3/4, conserved domain
description: Deubiquitinating enzymes (DUBs) remove ubiquitin (Ub) from Ub-conjugated substrates to regulate the functional outcome of ubiquitination. This entry includes MINDY-3/4. They belong to the MINDY (motif interacting with Ub-containing novel DUB) family (peptidase family C121), whose members are deubiquitinating enzymes releasing Lys48-linked ubiquitin [[cite:PUB00081935]]. This is a conserved domain found in deubiquitinating enzymes, MINDY-3 and MINDY-4.

name: Rubicon Homology Domain
description: This is the Rubicon homology domain (RH) characterised at the C-terminal of Rubicon, PLEKHM1 and Pacer, proteins that modulate late steps in autophagy [[cite:PUB00100995],[cite:PUB00100997]]. Rubicon (RUBCN) negatively regulates autophagy and endolysosomal trafficking by inhibiting PI3K complex II (PI3KC3-C2), which impairs autophagosome maturation process. PLEKHM1 is an adapter protein that regulates Rab7-dependent and HOPS complex-dependent fusion events in the endolysosomal system and couples autophagic and the endocytic trafficking pathways [[cite:PUB00100999],[cite:PUB00100998]]. On the other hand, Pacer positively regulates autophagy, promoting autophagosome maturation by facilitating the biogenesis of phosphatidylinositol 3-phosphate (PtdIns3P) in late steps of autophagy; it antagonises RUBCN [[cite:PUB00101000]]. This domain contains nine conserved cysteines and one conserved histidine, which have been predicted to bind divalent zinc cations being required for Rubicon and PLEKHM1 to interact with Rab7.

name: Coiled-coil domain-containing protein 34
description: This family is found in eukaryotes; it has several conserved tryptophan residues. The function is not known.

name: Chromodomain-helicase-DNA-binding protein 1-like, C-terminal
description: This domain is found at the C-terminus of chromodomain-helicase-DNA-binding proteins, including Chromodomain-helicase-DNA-binding protein 1 from humans (CHD1), an ATP-dependent chromatin-remodeling factor which acts as substrate recognition component of the transcription regulatory histone acetylation (HAT) complex SAGA. This helical domain consists of five alpha-helices organised in a variant helical bundle topology. Its surface is positively charged and can bind dsDNA and nucleosomes, but its specific function remains unknown [[cite:PUB00100856],[cite:PUB00100857],[cite:PUB00091268]].

name: EMARD, N-terminal domain
description: This entry represents the KEN domain found at the N-terminal of Endoplasmic reticulum membrane-associated RNA degradation protein (EMARD, also known as C6orf70 in human), which belongs to the HEPN superfamily. It carries the characteristic, highly conserved RxxxxHG sequence motif [[cite:PUB00091124]]. This domain may be a RNase that is involved in the degradation of rRNAs, mRNAs associated with the endoplasmic reticulum membrane. EMARD may play a role in neuronal migration during embryonic development [[cite:PUB00089893]].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF4210)
description: This short domain is found in fungi, plants and animals, and the proteins appear to be necessary for chromosome segregation during meiosis.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF4212)
description: This family includes several putative integral membrane proteins which have been predicted as the putative subunit of transporters for D-alanine or lactate (See Supplementary note 5 in [[cite:PUB00093610]]).

name: Putative heavy-metal chelation
description: This domain of unknown function has an enolase N-terminal domain-like fold. Its genomic context suggests that it may have a role in anaerobic vitamin B12 biosynthesis. This domain is often found at the N-terminus of proteins containing DUF364, [pfam:PF04016]. name: Tuberculosis necrotizing toxin
description: This is the C-terminal domain secreted by Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb). It induces necrosis of infected cells to evade immune responses. Mtb utilizes the protein CpnT to kill human macrophages by secreting its C-terminal domain (CTD), named tuberculosis necrotizing toxin (TNT) that induces necrosis. It acts as a NAD+ glycohydrolase which hydrolyzes the essential cellular coenzyme NAD+ in the cytosol of infected macrophages resulting in necrotic cell death [[cite:PUB00082601]]. CpnT transports its toxic CTD from the cell surface of M. tuberculosis by proteolytic cleavage, where the toxin is cleaved to induce host cell death [[cite:PUB00082600]]. Structural analysis determined that the TNT core contains only six beta-strands as opposed to seven found in all known NAD+-utilizing toxins, and is significantly smaller, with only two short alpha-helices and two 3/10 helices. Furthermore, the putative NAD+ binding pocket identified Q822, Y765 and R757 as residues possibly involved in NAD+-binding and hydrolysis based on similar positions of catalytic amino acids of ADP-ribosylating toxins. While glutamine 822 residue was detected to be highly conserved among TNT homologs [[cite:PUB00082601]].

Yet, bacterial resistance to phage is taking place in similar fashion to antibiotic resistance. This might be, in part due to temperate phages that are stably associated with their host.
