name: Protein of unknown function (DUF4427)
description: This domain is often found at the C-terminal of proteins with [pfam:PF10899] domain, for instance in STY1911 protein from a multiple drug resistant Salmonella enterica serovar Typhi CT18.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF4428)
description: This putative zinc finger domain is found in uncharacterised bacterial proteins.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF4429)
description: This presumed domain is functionally uncharacterised. This domain family is found in bacteria, archaea and viruses, and is approximately 90 amino acids in length. This domain is often found in two tandem copies.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF4430)
description: Although this family has overlaps with SLBB, the majority of its sequences are unique. Several family members, eg UniProtKB:A0RGA8, that do not overlap have an LPXTG-cell wall anchor at their C-terminus, a SSF_Family 10_polysaccharide_lyase or Glycosyltransferase structure associated with them in the middle region, as shown by InterPro, as well as this domain at the N-terminus.

name: ssDNA thymidine ADP-ribosyltransferase, DarT
description: This family of proteins is found in bacteria, archaea and eukaryotes. Proteins in this family are typically between 201 and 230 amino acids in length. There is a single completely conserved residue E that may be functionally important. This family is distantly similar to [pfam:PF01885]. Studies in search for novel ADP-ribosylation systems in bacterial genomes have identified an operon that encodes a conserved protein containing a distinct type of macrodomain associated with this family. This led to the identification of a toxin-antitoxin (TA) system, with DarT acting as the toxin. It is an enzyme that specifically modifies thymidines on single-stranded DNA in a sequence-specific manner by a nucleotide-type modification called ADP-ribosylation. This modification in turn can be removed by DarG, the antitoxin macrodomain protein. In addition, it was illustrated that substitution of the single completely conserved glutamate residue resulted in attenuation of function where DarT was non-toxic [[cite:PUB00091008]].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF4434)
description: This family has a TIM-barrel structure and appears to be related to a variety of glycosyl hydrolase enzymes.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF4435)
description: This presumed domain is functionally uncharacterised. This domain is found in bacteria, archaea and eukaryotes. Proteins in this family are typically between 285 and 362 amino acids in length. This domain is sometimes associated with AAA domains.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF4436)
description: This entry represents a domain found in a family of membrane and transmembrane proteins from mycobacterial and related species. This domain has similarity to the ligand-binding domains of neurotransmitter ligand-gated ion channels and sensory receptors and it is likely to have similar function.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF4437)
description: This family of proteins is found in bacteria. Proteins in this family are typically between 152 and 283 amino acids in length.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF4438), N-terminal
description: This is the N-terminal domain of TM_1086 and related proteins.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF4439)
description: This domain has a ferritin-like fold.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF4440)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised proteins from bacteria, archaea and eukaryotes, including NTF2-Like SgcJ protein from Streptomyces carzinostaticus, which plays a role in the biosynthesis of the 9-membered enediyne antitumor antibiotic C-1027. It shows a cone-like alpha+beta barrel structure with a long N-terminal alpha- helix, a curved six-stranded antiparallel beta-sheet and two additional shorter alpha-helices. Its specific function is still unkown [[cite:PUB00100883]].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF4441)
description: This family is largely made up of uncharacterised proteins from the Ciliophora. The function is not known.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF4442)
description: This family of proteins is found in bacteria, archaea and eukaryotes. Proteins in this family are typically between 139 and 165 amino acids in length. There is a conserved PYF sequence motif. There is a single completely conserved residue N that may be functionally important.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF4443)
description: This is a family of archaeal proteins. The domain is a putative gyrase domain.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF4444)
description: This domain family is found in bacteria, and is approximately 40 amino acids in length. There is a conserved LIPL sequence motif. There are two completely conserved G residues that may be functionally important.

name: C-terminal domain of RACo the ASKHA domain
description: This family includes reductive activator of CoFeSP (RACo) proteins, [swissprot:Q3ACS2]. Structure analysis of RACo indicate that it contains 4 regions: N-terminal region [pfam:PF00111] (residues 3-94) binding the [2Fe-2S] cluster, a linker region (residues 95-125), the middle region (residues 126-206), and the large C-terminal domain (residues 207-630). This entry is specific for the C-terminal domain which harbors the ATP-binding site. Structural studies show that the C-terminal domain contains the conserved beta-beta-beta-alpha-beta-alpha-beta-alpha topology characteristic of the ASKHA (acetate and sugar kinases/heat shock protein 70/actin). Despite the low-sequence identity shared between members of the ASKHA super family, they show a common central fold. Members of the ASKHA include proteins that catalyze phosphoryl transfers or hydrolysis of ATP in a variety of biological contexts. Asp, Asn, Glu, and Gln residues are well conserved in the core of the ASKHA proteins, where they interact with the phosphates of ATP and the bound Mg2+ ions.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF4446)
description: This family of proteins is functionally uncharacterised. This family of proteins is found in bacteria and eukaryotes. Proteins in this family are typically between 165 and 176 amino acids in length.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF4447)
description: This family of proteins is found in bacteria. Proteins in this family are approximately 170 amino acids in length.

name: Ykl077w/Psg1 (Pma1 Stabilization in Golgi)
description: Ykl077w/Psg1 (Pma1 Stabilization in the Golgi) physically interacts with Exp1 (for ER eXport of Pma1). Psg1 can be found in the Golgi and coat protein I (COPI) vesicles but does not directly bind Pma1. Loss of Psg1 causes enhanced degradation of Pma1 in the vacuole. Psg1 is 392aa protein with a predicted signal sequence at its N-terminus and a single TMD near the C-terminus. The short cytosolic region bears 2 putative retrieval motifs KRR and KKxxKxx. It was previously shown to be cleaved by the Ca+ dependent serine protease, Kex2 [[cite:PUB00093685]].

name: HAM1-like, C-terminal domain
description: This is a domain found at the C-terminal end of the putative cell signalling protein HAM1 from Cryptococcus neoformans and similar fungal sequences. HAM1 may act as a negative regulator of mating during vegetative growth [[cite:PUB00110896]]. Proteins with this domain often also contain an N-terminal domain [pfam:PF19343]. The member [swissprot:Q7SB48], named HAM-13, is thought to associate with MAPKs and to be required for proper cell communication but it is also possible to be involved in other processes such as cell signalling or trafficking [[cite:PUB00110895]].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF4450)
description: This is a family of bacterial proteins of unknown function.

name: Transcription regulator Rua1, C-terminal
description: This entry represents a domain that can be found at the C terminus f fungal proteins such as meiotic expression up-regulated protein 26 from Schizosaccharomyces pombe [[cite:PUB00034710]], Ecm8 from Saccharomyces cerevisiae and Rua1 from Ustilago maydis. Rua1 is a transcription factor and part of the gene cluster that mediates the biosynthesis of the glycolipid biosurfactant ustilagic acid (UA) [[cite:PUB00097885],[cite:PUB00097886]].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF4452)
description: This fungal family has no known function. However, it is rich in paired, as CXXC, cysteines and histidines, but these do not fall in the conformation that might suggest zinc-binding.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF4453)
description: This short domain is found only on a small subgroup of proteins from Gram-negative Proteobacteria that also carry a YARHG domain, [pfam:PF13308]. They carry three conserved tryptophan and three conserved cysteine residues.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF4454)
description: This C-terminal domain is found only on a small subgroup of proteins from Gram-positive Clostridiales that also carry a YARHG domain, [pfam:PF13308].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF4455)
description: This domain family is found in bacteria and eukaryotes, and is approximately 480 amino acids in length. There are two completely conserved residues (W and P) that may be functionally important.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF4456)
description: This domain family is found in eukaryotes, and is approximately 210 amino acids in length. There is a single completely conserved residue E that may be functionally important.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF4457)
description: This family of proteins is found in eukaryotes. It is found repeated several times in the vertebrate KIAA0556 proteins.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF4458)
description: this domain is found in tandem repeats on the N-terminus of secreted LRR proteins from human associated Bacteroidetes domain boundaries are based on the JCSG solved 3D structure of JCSG target SP16667A (BT_0210)

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF4459)
description: This family appears only on sequences from Salmonella spp. These sequences also all carry a YARHG domain, [pfam:PF13308].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF4460)
description: This domain family is found in eukaryotes, and is typically between 103 and 119 amino acids in length. There is a conserved HPD sequence motif. There are two completely conserved residues (N and F) that may be functionally important.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF4461)
description: This domain family is found in eukaryotes, and is approximately 310 amino acids in length.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF4462)
description: This domain family is found in eukaryotes, and is approximately 30 amino acids in length.

name: Cytosolic domain of 10TM putative phosphate transporter
description: PHM7_cyt is the predicted cytosolic domain of integral membrane proteins, such as yeast PHM7 and TM63A_HUMAN TRANSMEMBRANE PROTEIN 63A, SwissProt:O94886. This domain usually precedes the 7TM region, [pfam:PF02714], and follows a RSN1_TM, [pfam:PF13967]. Fold recognition programs consistently and with high significance predict this domain to be distantly homologous to RNA binding proteins from the RRM clan.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF4464)
description: This family of proteins is found in eukaryotes. Proteins in this family are typically between 224 and 241 amino acids in length. There is a conserved YID sequence motif.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF4465)
description: A large family of uncharacterized proteins mostly from human gut bacteroides, but also some environmental and water bacteria (Planctomycetes) as well as metagenomic samples Most proteins from this family are secreted or located on the outer surface and may participate in cell-cell interactions or cell-nutrient interactions This function is supported by a solved structure of a Bacteroides ovatus homolog, which adapts a galactose binding (jelly-roll) beta barrel structure

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF4466)
description: This is a domain of unknown function found in bacteroidetes.

name: Domain of unknown function with cystatin-like fold (DUF4467)
description: Large family of predicted lipoproteins from Gram-positive bacteria Experimentally determined structure shows a cystatitin-like fold, allowing us to classify this family in the NFT2 clan, despite lack of any detectable sequence similarity between members of this family and other families in this clan

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF4468) with TBP-like fold
description: A large family of (predicted) secreted proteins with unknown functions from human gut and oral cavity. Typically forms a N-terminal domain with FMN binding domain at the C-terminus. Experimentaly determined 3D structure of this domain shows a variant of a TATA box binding - like fold, but no detectable sequence similarity to other proteins with this fold

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF4469) with IG-like fold
description: A C-terminal domain in a large family of (predicted) secreted proteins with unknown functions from human gut bacteroides

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF4470)
description: This family is conserved from fungi to Metazoa and includes plants. The function is not known, but several members have zinc-finger domain, zf-MYND, [pfam:PF01753], at their very C-terminus. Others are also associated with DUF1279, [pfam:PF06916].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF4472)
description: This family is specific to the Chordates. Some members also carry Kinesin-motor domains at their N-terminus, Kinesin, [pfam:PF00225].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF4471)
description: This family is conserved from fungi to Metazoa and includes plants. The function is not known, but several members have zinc-finger domain, zf-MYND, [pfam:PF01753], at their very C-terminus. Others are also associated with DUF1279, [pfam:PF06916]. This domain is more C-terminal in many members to DUF4470, [pfam:PF14737].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF4473)
description: This short family is largely confined to Caenorhabditis proteins. The function is not known. There are two well-conserved aspartate residues.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF4474)
description: Domain found on N-termina of few families of uncharacterized Clostridia proteins. Typically followed by a proline-rich domain or other kinds of repeats

name: Protein FAM221A/B
description: This family of proteins is found in eukaryotes. Proteins in this family are typically between 99 and 305 amino acids in length.

name: Nucleolus and neural progenitor protein, N-terminal
description: This domain is found at the N-terminal of nucleolus and neural progenitor protein (NEPRO) which may play a role in cortex development as part of the Notch signalling pathway. Downstream of Notch may repress the expression of proneural genes and inhibit neuronal differentiation thereby maintaining neural progenitors [[cite:PUB00101272]]. NEPRO may also play a role in preimplentation embryo development [[cite:PUB00101273]]. NEPRO interacts with multiple protein subunits of RMRP and is implicated in Anauxetic dysplasia 3 [[cite:PUB00101274]]. NEPRO is likely the human orthologue of RMP1 subunit from yeast and they share a four-helix bundle domain structure.

name: Pyrimidine/purine nucleotide 5'-monophosphate nucleosidases
description: This is an N-terminal domain found in pyrimidine/purine nucleotide 5'-monophosphate nucleosidases (PpnN) in bacteria. PpnN catalyzes the hydrolysis of the N-glycosidic bond of diverse pyrimidine and purine nucleotide 5'-monophosphates, to form ribose 5-phosphate and the corresponding free base. It can use AMP, GMP, IMP, CMP, dTMP and UMP as substrates [[cite:PUB00084997]]. It is found in association with [pfam:PF03641] and [pfam:PF11892].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF4479)
description: This domain family is found in bacteria, and is approximately 70 amino acids in length. The family is found in association with [pfam:PF01588].

name: SOGA 1/2-like, coiled-coil
description: This entry represents a coiled-coil region found in microtubule cross-linking factors 1 and 2 (also known as SOGA1/2), which are members of the SOGA (suppressor of glucose by autophagy) family and in the uncharacterised human protein KIAA0408. SOGA1 regulates autophagy by playing a role in the reduction of glucose production in an adiponectin- and insulin-dependent manner [[cite:PUB00067397]]. SOGA1/2 are required for faithful chromosome segregation during mitosis [[cite:PUB00153172]]. These proteins contain long coiled-coils that dimerize and holds two N-terminal domains that bind to microtubules [[cite:PUB00153172]]. This region is found in association with [pfam:PF11365].

name: Cilia- and flagella-associated protein 77
description: This family of proteins is found in flagella [[cite:PUB00086673]]. Proteins in this family are typically between 203 and 326 amino acids in length. There is a single completely conserved residue N that may be functionally important.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF4484)
description: This domain is found, in a few members, a the the C-terminus of family Avl9, [pfam:PF09794]. The function is not known.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF4485)
description: This family is found in eukaryotes, and is approximately 90 amino acids in length.

name: Cilia- and flagella-associated protein 54
description: This domain family is found in eukaryotes, and is typically between 542 and 565 amino acids in length. This entry represents the N-terminal region of the cilia- and flagella-associated protein 54 which is required for assembly and function of cilia and flagella.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF4487)
description: This family of proteins is found in eukaryotes. Proteins in this family are typically between 209 and 938 amino acids in length. There is a conserved WCF sequence motif. There is a single completely conserved residue W that may be functionally important.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF4488)
description: In most members this domain covers almost the whole sequence, but a few member-sequences also carry a TonB_C domain, PF03544. This domain has a lipocalin fold.

name: Piercer of microtubule wall 1/2
description: This family of proteins is found in eukaryotes and includes Piercer of microtubule wall 1/2 proteins (PIRC1/2). In mice PIRC1 expression is induced by p53 may play a role in DNA damage response and has been shown to function at the initial step of left-right asymmetry specification of the visceral organs [[cite:PUB00111186]]. PIRC1/2 are microtubule inner proteins involved in the attachment of outer dynein arms (ODAs) to dynein-decorated doublet microtubules (DMTs) in cilia axoneme [[cite:PUB00100771]].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF4491)
description: This family of proteins is found in bacteria. Proteins in this family are typically between 94 and 107 amino acids in length. There is a conserved EYY sequence motif.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF4492)
description: This family of proteins is found in bacteria. Proteins in this family are approximately 80 amino acids in length. The function of these proteins is unknown.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF4493)
description: This family of proteins is found in bacteria. Proteins in this family are typically between 264 and 710 amino acids in length. Many of these proteins have a lipid attachment site suggesting they are lipoproteins.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF4494)
description: This family of proteins is found in bacteria. Proteins in this family are typically between 154 and 172 amino acids in length. There are two conserved sequence motifs: VDA and EAE. This entry contains two domains which share a similar topology. AlphaFold3 prediction suggests this family may form a DNA-binding homotetrameric complex.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF4495)
description: This domain family is found in eukaryotes, and is typically between 322 and 336 amino acids in length. There are two conserved sequence motifs: QMW and DLW. Proteins in this family vary in length from 793 to 1184 amino acids.

name: CCDC81 eukaryotic HU domain 1
description: This is the first of two HU domains found in the CCDC81-like proteins. CCDC81 has been experimentally linked to the centrosome; eukaryotic CCDC81 HU domains are predicted to function in protein-protein interactions in centrosome organization and potentially contribute to cargo-binding in conjunction with Dynein-VII. A striking lineage-specific expansion of the domain is observed in birds, where the HU domains could function in recognition of non-self molecules [[cite:PUB00091007]].

name: Microtubule associated protein 10, N-terminal domain
description: This domain is found at the N-terminal of MAP10 (Microtubule associated protein 10, also known as MTR120/KIAA1383) from mammals. There are two completely conserved G residues that may be functionally important. It adopts a C2-like fold. MAP10 localises to stabilised MTs during interphase and to the mitotic apparatus during mitosis. It may promote microtubule stability and ensures normal progress of cytokinesis [[cite:PUB00068314]].

name: Cilia- and flagella-associated protein 300
description: CFAP300 is a cilia- and flagella-associated protein that is essential for assembly of dynein arms. Mutations in the CFAP300 gene (C11orf70) cause defective cilia motility and primary ciliary dyskinesia [[cite:PUB00089790],[cite:PUB00089791]].

name: Transmembrane protein 254
description: This family contains proteins found in eukaryotes, including human Transmembrane protein TMEM254 (C10orf57). The exact function of this protein is still unknown, however it is thought to be an integral membrane protein. The protein sequence is 123 amino acids in length and has a mass of approximately 14.2 kDa. The family also includes some longer proteins that possess an N-terminal dehydrogenase domain, [pfam:PF01073].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF4500)
description: This family is found in eukaryotes. The function of this protein remains unknown. The gene which encodes for this protein is named chromosome 6 open reading frame 162 (C6orf162) and is found between the chromosomal positions 6q15-q16.1. It is thought that this protein may be an important part of membrane function.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF4501)
description: This family of proteins is found in eukaryotes. Proteins in this family are typically between 167 and 308 amino acids in length. The exact function of this protein remains unknown, but it is thought to be a single-pass membrane protein. This family contains many highly conserved cysteine residues.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF4502)
description: This family of proteins is found in eukaryotes. Proteins in this family are typically between 181 and 876 amino acids in length.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF4503)
description: This family of proteins is found in eukaryotes. Proteins in this family are typically between 313 and 876 amino acids in length.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF4504)
description: This family of proteins is found in eukaryotes. Proteins in this family are typically between 253 and 329 amino acids in length. There are two conserved sequence motifs: LLGYP and SFS.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF4505)
description: This family of proteins is found in bacteria and eukaryotes. Proteins in this family are typically between 166 and 225 amino acids in length.

name: ATPase PAAT-like
description: This family is found in eukaryotes. It represents the ATPase protein associated with ABC transporters (PAAT) and related proteins. PAAT is formed of a nucleotide-binding domain (NBD)-like domain and a signal for intramitochondrial sorting. PAAT interacts with the mitochondrial inner membrane ABC proteins: ABCB7, ABCB8 and ABCB10. It is involved in maintenance of mitochondrial homeostasis and cell survival [[cite:PUB00093681]].

name: Integrator complex subunit 15
description: Integrator complex subunit 15 (C7orf26) is likely a component of the Integrator (INT) complex, which is involved in the small nuclear RNAs (snRNA) U1 and U2 transcription and in their 3'-box-dependent processing [[cite:PUB00100760]].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF4508)
description: This family of proteins is found in eukaryotes. Proteins in this family are typically between 117 and 253 amino acids in length.

name: Tubulin epsilon and delta complex protein 1
description: This family represents the tubulin epsilon and delta complex protein 1 (TEDC1). This complex is required for centriole maintenance and it is a component of several ciliary structures. It acts as a positive regulator of hedgehog signalling, which play key roles in embryonic development and in cancers [[cite:PUB00094182]]. Additionally, this protein may play a role in counteracting perturbation of actin filaments, such as after treatment with the actin depolymerising microbial metabolite Chivosazole F [[cite:PUB00094181]].

name: Protein C10
description: The function of this protein family is unknown. Mutations in protein C (C12orf57) are implicated in the pathogenesis of colobomatous microphthalmia [[cite:PUB00069935],[cite:PUB00069936]].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF4512)
description: This family of proteins is found in eukaryotes. Proteins in this family are typically between 74 and 104 amino acids in length. There are two completely conserved residues (C and P) that may be functionally important.

name: Sperm-associated microtubule inner protein 10
description: This family (previously DUF4513) represents homologs of Sperm-associated microtubule inner protein 10 (SPMIP10). SPMIP10 is a microtubule inner protein (MIP) part of the axonemal dynein-decorated doublet microtubules (DMTs). It plays a role in the stabilisation of the interacting protomers of TEKTL1 - a tektin-like molecule that forms a filament in the cleft between protofilaments A11 and A12 . In the EM structure of sperm DMTs, SPMIP10 cradles the inter-TEKTL1 interface while interacting with protofilaments A11 and A12 [[cite:PUB00151496]].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF4514)
description: This family of uncharacterised proteins are found in mammals.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF4515)
description: This family of proteins is found in bacteria and eukaryotes. Proteins in this family are typically between 198 and 469 amino acids in length. There are two completely conserved L residues that may be functionally important.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF4516)
description: This family of proteins is found in eukaryotes. Proteins in this family are typically between 56 and 69 amino acids in length.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF4517)
description: The function of this protein remains unknown. This family of proteins is found in eukaryotes and are typically between 160 and 182 amino acids in length.

name: DUF4518 C-terminal domain
description: This entry represents the C-terminal beta sheet domain of the DUF4518 family of proteins. This domain has an NTF2-like fold. The function of this domain is unknown.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF4519)
description: This family of proteins is found in eukaryotes. Proteins in this family are typically between and 59 amino acids in length. There are two conserved sequence motifs: KET and VLP. There is a single completely conserved residue P that may be functionally important.

name: C5orf34 C-terminal domain
description: This is the C-terminal Polo-like domain of C5orf34 from human and its homologues. C5orf34 has been associated with an unfavourable prognosis of patients from a variety of human malignancies [[cite:PUB00154384],[cite:PUB00154383]].

name: Shieldin complex subunit 1, C-terminal domain
description: SHLD1, also known as RINN3, is a component of the shieldin complex, a vertebrate-specific protein complex which functions as a downstream effector in the 53BP1 pathway, regulates NHEJ (non-homologous end joining) [[cite:PUB00089626],[cite:PUB00154232]]. This entry represents a conserved helical domain found at the C-terminal of SHLD1.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF4522)
description: This family of proteins is functionally uncharacterised. This family of proteins is found in mammals. In human this protein is known as C4orf36.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF4523)
description: This family of proteins is functionally uncharacterised. This family of proteins is found in mammals.

name: C5orf34-like, N-terminal
description: This entry represents the N-terminal domain of a family of eukaryotic proteins, including the human uncharacterised protein C5orf34, which has been reported to be correlated with an unfavourable prognosis of patients from a variety of human malignancies [[cite:PUB00154384]]. This domain is predicted to show an alpha-beta structure with high structural similarity to a polo box.

name: MGT5A-like, N-terminal
description: This domain is found at the N-terminal end of human Alpha-1,6 -mannosylglycoprotein 6-beta-N-acetylglucosaminyltransferase A (MGT5A) [[cite:PUB00155403]] and similar sequences mainly found in vertebrates. MGT5A is a glycosyltransferase family 18 enzyme that also has the catalytic region [pfam:PF15024]. This domain, which shows an all helical structure, plays a critical role in the recognition of glycoprotein substrates [[cite:PUB00155403],[cite:PUB00155404],[cite:PUB00155405]]. It is also found in Coiled -coil domain-containing protein 126, a smaller sequence that only contains this domain.

name: Transmembrane protein 174
description: This family of proteins is found in chordates and includes the human integral membrane protein TMEM174 protein.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF4527)
description: This family of proteins is functionally uncharacterised. This family of proteins is found in vertebrates.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF4528)
description: This family of proteins is found in eukaryotes. Proteins in this family are typically between 95 and 154 amino acids in length. This family includes Human C15orf61.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF4529)
description: This family of proteins is functionally uncharacterised. This family of proteins is found in eukaryotes. The proteins contain a conserved VLPPLK sequence motif.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF4530)
description: This family of proteins is found in eukaryotes. Proteins in this family are typically around 140 amino acids in length. The human member of this family is C19orf69.

name: Tektin bundle interacting protein 1
description: This family includes Tektin bundle interacting protein 1 (TKTI1) which has been recently characterised as a microtubule inner protein (MIP) part of the dynein-decorated doublet microtubules (DMTs) in cilia axoneme, which is required for motile cilia beating. It is located at the center of the tektin bundle where may function to recruit tektins or stabilize the bundle [[cite:PUB00100771]].

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF4532)
description: This family of proteins is functionally uncharacterised. This family of proteins is found in eukaryotes.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF4533)
description: This family of proteins is functionally uncharacterised. This family of proteins is found in mammals. This family includes two human proteins: C12orf60 and C12orf69.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF4534)
description: This family of proteins is functionally uncharacterised. This family of proteins is found in mammals. Proteins in this family are typically between 170 and 190 amino acids in length. The protein includes the human integral membrane TMEM217 protein.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF4535)
description: This family includes the uncharacterised protein C7orf73 that is found in eukaryotes. Members are generally less than 100 residues in length. Although the precise function of the domain is still unknown, members have a predicted N-terminal signal peptide sequence which suggests they are short secreted peptides.

name: DMAC1/Dmo2-like domain
description: This domain is found in human Distal membrane-arm assembly complex protein 1 (DMAC1), which is required for the assembly of the mitochondrial NADH:ubiquinone oxidoreductase complex, Tam6 from Schizosaccharomyces pombe (also known as Dmo2), which is required for the stability and maturation of Cox2p, the second subunit of the COX complex, and similar eukaryotic proteins. This domain is predicted to show two alpha helices.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF4537)
description: The function of this domain family is unknown. It is found in eukaryotes, and is typically between 119 and 141 amino acids in length. In humans, it is found in the chromosomal position C11orf16.

name: MITRAC7/Phoenixin family
description: This entry represents the Small Integral Membrane Protein 20/Phoenixin family, which contains proteins with dual functions. The full-length protein (SMIM20/MITRAC7) is a mitochondrial inner membrane protein that acts as a component of the MITRAC (mitochondrial translation regulation assembly intermediate of cytochrome c oxidase) complex, regulating cytochrome c oxidase assembly. It functions as a chaperone-like assembly factor required to stabilize newly synthesized MT-CO1/COX1 and prevent its premature turnover. The C-terminal region of this protein is also processed to produce bioactive peptides known as phoenixin-14 and phoenixin-20, which were first identified through a bioinformatic approach. These secreted peptides are involved in multiple physiological functions. They act as ligands for the G protein-coupled receptor GPR173. Phoenixin peptides regulate gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH) signaling in the hypothalamus and pituitary, augmenting luteinizing hormone release. They delay the appearance of estrus when reduced in vivo and modulate GnRH receptor expression. Additionally, phoenixin peptides regulate vasopressin secretion by hypothalamic neurons and have roles in memory retention, anxiety reduction, food intake regulation, granulosa cell proliferation, heart function, and islet cell proliferation.

name: Homologous recombination OB-fold protein

name: Spermatogenesis-associated protein 48
description: Spermatogenesis-associated protein 48 is also known as post-meiotic spermatogenesis protein 1 [[cite:PUB00087304]]. Proteins in this family are typically between 109 and 302 amino acids in length. In humans, it is found in the chromosomal position, C7orf72.

name: Cilia and flagella associated protein 90
description: This family represents the homologues of Cilia and flagella associated protein 90 (CFAP90, also known as C5orf49). CFAP90 is a microtubule inner protein (MIP) part of the doublet microtubules (DMTs) in cilia and sperm axoneme [[cite:PUB00103594],[cite:PUB00151496]]. It belongs to the core-MIPs and binds to protofilament B09 in the sperm DMTs. Members of this family contain a conserved KLHRDDR sequence motif.

name: Sperm microtubule associated protein 1
description: This family (previously DUF4542) represents the homologs of Sperm microtubule associated protein 1 (SPMAP1 also known as C17orf98). These proteins contain a conserved IPPYN sequence motif. The EM structure of sperm DMTs shows that SPMAP1 interacts directly with the tubulin lattice at the A-tubule seam (between protofilaments A09/A10) where outer dense fibers (ODFs) are connected to dynein-decorated doublet microtubules (DMTs) [[cite:PUB00151496]].

name: Membrane-anchored junction protein
description: Membrane-anchored junction protein (MAJIN) is a meiosis-specific telomere-associated protein involved in meiotic telomere attachment to the nucleus inner membrane, a crucial step for homologous pairing and synapsis. It is a component of the MAJIN-TERB1-TERB2 complex, which promotes telomere cap exchange by mediating attachment of telomeric DNA to the inner nuclear membrane and replacement of the protective cap of telomeric chromosomes [[cite:PUB00077546]].

name: Regulator of DNA class I crossover intermediates 1-like
description: This family of proteins mainly found in vertebrates includes mouse Regulator of DNA class I crossover intermediates 1 (Redic1). Redic1 is involved in recombination, probably acting by stabilising recombination intermediates during meiotic crossover formation. It is required for normal germline development and fertility as well as for meiotic progression, complete chromosomal synapsis and crossover formation [[cite:PUB00153152],[cite:PUB00153151]]. This protein binds double-stranded DNA [[cite:PUB00153152]].

name: Sperm-associated microtubule inner protein 4
description: This family (previously DUF4555) includes the homologs of human sperm-associated microtubule inner protein 4 (SPMIP4) that is found predominantly in testis [[cite:PUB00151495]]. SPMIP4 is a microtubule inner protein (MIP) part of the axonemal dynein-decorated doublet microtubules (DMTs). Members of this family adopt rather extended conformation and contain a single or multiple Mn motifs. Each Mn motif consists of a 5- to 6-residue helix flanked by a Tyr/Phe residue on one end and by a Ser/Thr on the other that binds the shoulder of the alpha-tubulin S9/S10 loop [[cite:PUB00151502]]. Members of this family are likely to stabilise the microtubule structure in the sperm flagella [[cite:PUB00151496]].

name: Sperm acrosome-associated protein 9
description: This family of proteins found in eukaryotes represents sperm acrosome-associated protein 9 (SPACA9, previously known as C9orf9 or MAST). Sperm acrosome-associated protein 9 has been suggested to form a complex with calcium-binding proteins calreticulin and caldendrin localised to the acrosome. Despite this, no known protein interaction motifs have been identified in MAST/SPACA9 [[cite:PUB00080694]].

name: Small membrane A-kinase anchor protein
description: SmAKAP is a small membrane-bound PKA-RI-specific protein kinase A-anchoring protein, referred to as small membrane-AKAP. It is probably tethered to the plasma membrane most through a dual acylation of its N-terminal Met-Gly-Cys- motif (myristoylation and palmitoylation, respectively). It specifically targets PKA-RI isoforms to the plasma membrane. It localizes to plasma membranes, is enriched at cell-cell junctions and associates with filopodia [[cite:PUB00067440]].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF4566)
description: This entry represents a domain covering the whole length in Uncharacterized protein C6orf62 from metazoa. C6orf62 is ubiquitously expressed, including in brain tissue, which led to its inclusion in neurogenetic linkage studies, particularly in the region associated with developmental dyslexia. Though C6orf62 itself was not confirmed as causal, it lies adjacent to dyslexia-associated genes such as KIAA0319 and DCDC2, both of which are involved in neuronal migration and axonal growth [[cite:PUB00162470]]. name: TLR adaptor interacting with SLC15A4 on the lysosome
description: In humans, TASL (TLR adaptor interacting with SLC15A4 on the lysosome) is encoded by CXorf21 that is associated with systemic lupus erythematosus [[cite:PUB00093601]]. It is an immune adaptor that is required for recruitment and activation of IRF5 by TLR7, TLR8 and TLR9, in mechanistic analogy to IRF3 and its three adaptors STING, MAVS and TRIF. TASL interacts with the endolysosomal transporter SLC15A4 forming the SLC15A4-TASL complex, which is required for endolysosomal TLR signalling. TASL contains a pLxIS motif that is important for its function [[cite:PUB00095082]].

name: Protein SPO16 homolog

It plays a key role in reinforcing the integrity of the central element of the synaptonemal complex (SC), resulting in the SC stabilization which ensures the progression of meiotic prophase I in male and female germ cells [1. It promotes homologous recombination and crossing-over in meiotic prophase I via its association with SHOC1 [[cite:PUB00096701]]. It is also required for the localization of TEX11 and MSH4 to recombination intermediates [[cite:PUB00096701]].

name: Elongin BC and Polycomb repressive complex 2-associated protein
description: This family of proteins is found in eukaryotes. Family members are approximately 835 amino acids in length and include the polycomb repressive complex 2-associated factor EPOP (Elongin BC and Polycomb Repressive Complex 2 (PRC2) Associated Protein, also termed C17orf96, esPRC2p48, E130012A19Rik), a scaffold protein expressed in the inner cell mass of the mouse blastocyst serving as a bridging partner between the PRC2/EED-EZH2 complex and the elongin BC complex, and fine-tuning the transcriptional status of Polycomb group (PcG) target genes in embryonic stem cells. Both EPOP and Elongin BC are required to maintain low levels of expression at PRC2 genomic targets [[cite:PUB00083907]]. EPOP interacts with the H2B deubiquitinase USP7 to modulate transcriptional processes in mESCs similar to MYC [[cite:PUB00083908]]. Functional studies found that the C-terminal region of EPOP directly interacts with PRC2 and that this region associates with the VEFS-box of the PRC2 core member SUZ12. Thus, suggesting that EPOP may directly affect PRC2 chromatin binding by altering the functionality of Suz12. This region is proposed to have evolved in early vertebrates and is also present in the paralog SKIDA1 (C10orf140) another novel PRC2-interacting protein, supporting the idea that proteins possessing this sequence are PRC2 regulators in the entire vertebrate branch [[cite:PUB00111127]]. The family is found in association with [pfam:PF02437].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF4585)
description: The function of this protein domain family is yet to be characterised. It is putatively thought to lie in the C-terminal domain of the DNA nucleotide repair protein, Xeroderma pigmentosa complementation group A (XPA). The function of XPA is to bind to DNA and repair any mismatched base pairs. This domain family is often found in eukaryotes, and is approximately 70 amino acids in length. There is a conserved DPE sequence motif. In humans, this protein is encoded for in the chromosomal position, Chromosome 5 open reading frame 65. Mutations in the gene lead to myelodysplastic syndromes, where there is inefficient stem cell production in the bone marrow. This suggests that the protein may have a role in forming blood cells [[cite:PUB00067380]].

The EM structure of sperm DMTs shows that CFAP96 binds to tubulin and, similarly to other axonemal wedge-MAPs, binds deeper into the inter-protofilament cleft making extensive contacts with flanking protofilaments [[cite:PUB00151496]].

name: Telomere attrition and p53 response 1 protein-like

It may attenuate p53/TP53 activation through the E3 ubiquitin ligase HUWE1 which also promotes TAPR1's degradation [[cite:PUB00100199],[cite:PUB00101217]]. This family also includes uncharacterised proteins from fungi, such as YJR056C from yeast.

BTBD8 is involved in clathrin-mediated endocytosis at the synapse and plays a role in neuronal development and in synaptic vesicle recycling in mature neurons, a process required for normal synaptic transmission [[cite:PUB00090548]]. SAXO5 is a filamentous SAXO protein that binds along protofilament A04 with 96-nm periodicity [[cite:PUB00151496]]. A typical feature of SAXO proteins is the presence of Mn motif which forms a 5- to 6-residue helix flanked by a Tyr/Phe residue on one end and by a Ser/Thr on the other that binds the shoulder of the alpha-tubulin S9/S10 loop [[cite:PUB00151502]]. description: This family includes WD repeat and coiled-coil-containing protein (WDCP, previously known as C2orf44), which is found in eukaryotes and consists of around 721 amino acids. The N-terminal contains two WD (tryptophan-aspartic acid) repeats (WD1 and WD2). WD repeats may be involved in a range of biological functions including apoptosis, transcriptional regulation and signal transduction. The C-terminal contains a proline-rich sequence (PPRLPQR), and is predicted to have leucine-rich coiled coil region (CC) [[cite:PUB00080737]]. WDCP was identified in a proteomic screen to find signalling components that interact with Hck (hematopoietic cell kinase), a non-receptor tyrosine kinase. WDCP was shown to bind tightly and specifically to the SH3 domain of Hck in U937 human monocytic cells. WDCP was also shown to exist as an oligomer when expressed in mammalian cells. While the function of WDCP is unknown, it has been identified in a gene fusion event with anaplastic lymphoma kinase (ALK) in colorectal cancer patients [[cite:PUB00080737]].

An activating ligand named GPR15L is shown to bind GPR15 and attract GPR15-expressing T cells including lymphocytes in colon-draining lymph nodes and thymic precursors of dermal epithelial T cell. In humans GPR15L, is encoded by the gene C10ORF99 and has some features similar to the CC family of chemokines [[cite:PUB00088053]]. Furthermore, the activating peptides of CC chemokines are typically located at the N-terminus, while that of GPR15L is C-terminal, a feature that it shares with some other GPCR ligands like chemerin and apela [[cite:PUB00088054]].

The predicted structure of the VASt domain is a two-layer sandwich alpha beta fold, also called 'helix grip fold', containing three alpha helices (alpha1 to 3), six beta-sheets (beta1 to 6) and two loops (omega1 and 2) numbered from N to C terminus [[cite:PUB00084279]]. Some proteins known to contain a VASt domain are : Plant vascular associated death1 (VAD1), a regulator of programmed cell death (PCD) harboring a GRAM putative lipid-binding domain. Yeast SNF1 Interacting Protein 3 (SIP3), may be involved in sterol transfer between intracellular membranes. Yeast Suicide Protein 1 (YSP1), a mitochondrial protein specifically required for the mitochondrial thread-grain transition, de-energization, and the cell death. May be involved in sterol transfer between intracellular membranes. Yeast Suicide Protein 2 (YSP2), a mitochondrial membrane protein involved in mitochondrial fragmentation and may be involved in sterol transfer between intracellular membranes.It is also found in human GramD1a-c.

DSE converts D-glucuronic acid to L-iduronic acid (IdoUA) residues. It plays an important role in the biosynthesis of the glycosaminoglycan/mucopolysaccharide dermatan sulfate [[cite:PUB00162452],[cite:PUB00109125]]. HepB cleaves both heparin and heparan sulfate glycosaminoglycans through a beta-elimination mechanism. It cleaves heparin at alpha-D-GlcNp2S6S(1->4) alpha-L-IdoAp2S and heparan sulfate at alpha-D-GlcNp2Ac(or 2S)6OH(1->4)beta-D-GlcAp [[cite:PUB00016410]]. This domain is composed of helical hairpins.

LRP1 is involved in cellular lipid homeostasis and in the plasma clearance of chylomicron remnants and activated LRPAP1 (alpha 2-macroglobulin), as well as the local metabolism of complexes between plasminogen activators and their endogenous inhibitors. It acts as an LRPAP1 alpha-2-macroglobulin receptor [[cite:PUB00151934],[cite:PUB00151933]].

name: 3'-5' exoribonuclease Rv2179c-like domain
description: This is a highly divergent 3' exoribonuclease family. The proteins constitute a typical RNase fold, where the active site residues form a magnesium catalytic centre. The protein of the solved structure readily cleaves 3' overhangs in a time-dependent manner. It is similar to DEDD-type RNases and is an unusual ATP-binding protein that binds ATP and dATP. It forms a dimer in solution and both protomers in the asymmetric unit bind a magnesium ion through Asp-6 in SwissProt:P9WJ73 [[cite:PUB00074134]]. Proteins containing this domain also include 3'-5' exonuclease dexA from bacteriophage T4. It may play a role in the final step of host DNA degradation, by scavenging DNA into mononucleotides [[cite:PUB00078716],[cite:PUB00078717]].

name: Nucleotide-binding C-terminal domain
description: This is the C-terminal domain found in proteins in a range of Proteobacteria as well as the Gram-positive Oceanobacillus iheyensis. Structural analysis of the whole protein indicates the N- and C-termini act together to produce a surface into which a threonate-ADP complex is bound, demonstrating that a sugar binding site is on the N-terminal domain, and a nucleotide binding site is in the C-terminal domain [[cite:PUB00085179]]. There is a critical motif, DDXTG, at approximately residues 22-25. Proteins containing this domain have been predicted as kinases. Some members are associated with PdxA2 by physical clustering and gene fusion with PdxA2. Some members that are fused with PdxA2 have been shown to be involved in L-4-hydroxythreonine (4HT) phosphorylation, part of the alternative pathway to make PLP (pyridoxal 5'-phosphate) out of a toxic metabolite, 4HT. However, 4HT phosphorylation might not be the main function of this group of proteins. Moreover, some members that are not associated with pdxA2, and even one that is associated with pdxA2, have lost 4HT kinase activity [[cite:PUB00083215]]. Functional analysis demonstrate that family members include D-Threonate kinases (DtnK), D-Erythronate kinases (DenK) and 3-Oxo-tetronate kinases (OtnK) [[cite:PUB00085179]].

name: ERMES regulator 1

NUP160 plays a role in normal auxin signalling, which works in synergy with ethylene to control various ethylene-dependent phenomena [[cite:PUB00155768]]. Also, it contributes to pathogen defense [[cite:PUB00085247]], nucleocytoplasmic mRNA export [[cite:PUB00155768]], and is required for disease resistance [[cite:PUB00085246]].

name: Cas6b C-terminal domain
description: Clustered, regularly interspaced, short palindromic repeat (CRISPR) loci play a pivotal role in the prokaryotic host defense system against invading genetic materials. Four Cas proteins (Cas5, Cas6b, Cas7 and Cas8b) are proposed to form a Type I-B Cascade complex that mediates the antiviral defense [[cite:PUB00085160]]. This is the C-terminal domain found in Cas6b proteins. Cas6b is a member of Cas6 RNA processing endoribonucleases found in bacteria and archaea whose RNA substrates have a wide range of structural features. Cocrystal structures of Cas6 from Methanococcus maripaludis (MmCas6b) bound with its repeat RNA revealed a dual-site binding structure and a cleavage site conformation poised for phosphodiester bond breakage [[cite:PUB00085376]].

name: Type VI secretion system TssC/VipB, central domain
description: This entry represents the central domain of TssC-like proteins. T6SSs are toxin delivery systems. It is a multiprotein complex requiring numerous core proteins (Tss proteins) including cytoplasmic, transmembrane, and outer membrane components. The needle or tube apparatus is comprised of a phage-like complex, similar to the T4 contractile bacteriophage tail, which is thought to be anchored to the membrane by a trans-envelope complex [[cite:PUB00090998]]. VipB is a family of Gram-negative type VI secretion system components of the tail sheath. They have been known as COG3517. These sheath-components, of which there are many copies in the sheath, are also variously referred to as TssC. On contact with another bacterial cell the sheath contracts and pushes the puncturing device and tube through the cell envelope and punches the target bacterial cell [[cite:PUB00090998]]. VipA and VipB (TssB and TssC) proteins were shown to form a cog-wheel like tubular structure in V. cholerae that was noticed to resemble T4 phage gp18 polysheath. Two beta-strands of VipA and four beta-strands of VipB intertwine forming the middle layer of the sheath. The sheath assembles around an inner Hcp tube and is attached to a structure called a baseplate that spans the bacterial membranes. Importantly, VipA/VipB sheath was shown to form a long contractile organelle in V. cholerae and in E. coli, suggesting that sheath contraction powers the secretion [[cite:PUB00091000]].

name: Luciferase domain
description: This entry describes the luciferase domain found in fungi. This entry also includes uncharacterised bacterial sequences. Fungal luciferase is part of the gene cluster that mediates the fungal bioluminescence cycle [[cite:PUB00101065]]. It may use the fungal luciferin 3-hydroxyhispidin as a substrate to produce an endoperoxide as a high-energy intermediate with decomposition that yields oxyluciferin (also known as caffeoylpyruvate) and light emission. The fungal bioluminescence cycle begins with the hispidin synthetase that catalyses the formation of hispidin which is further hydroxylated by the hispidin-3-hydroxylase, yielding the fungal luciferin 3-hydroxyhispidin. The luciferase then produces an endoperoxide as a high-energy intermediate with decomposition that yields oxyluciferin and light emission. Oxyluciferin can be recycled to caffeic acid by caffeoylpyruvate hydrolase [[cite:PUB00101065]].

In nematoda, it is found on the N-terminal side of ribosomal protein family L14 [pfam:PF00238]. It is also found on the N-terminal of Cob(I)alamin adenosyltransferase [pfam:PF01923] in other eukaryotes. Family members found in homo sapiens such as [swissprot:Q5VUE5], have been shown to be highly expressed in 15 high-grade neuroendocrine tumor cell lines and YAP1-positive small-cell lung cancer cell lines [[cite:PUB00091275]] as well as being up-regulated in two human Multiple Myloma cell lines in response to selective nuclear export inhibitor KPT-276 [[cite:PUB00091276]]. description: This entry represents the N-terminal domain of a family of proteins that includes RPA-related protein RADX from animals, the human member is also known as CXorf57. High-throughput sequencing used to identify genes driving tumorigenesis in Avian leukosis virus (ALV)-induced B-cell lymphomas, showed CXorf57 as the 10th most frequently targeted common integration site by ALV. ALV induces B-cell lymphoma and other neoplasms in chickens by integrating within or near cancer genes and perturbing their expression [[cite:PUB00138338]]. RADX is a replication factor A protein-like (RPA-like), single-stranded DNA binding protein recruited to replication forks to maintain genome stability [[cite:PUB00091321]]. description: RAB7A-interacting MON1-CCZ1 complex subunit 1 (RIMC1, previously known as UPF0600 protein C5orf51) plays an important role in the removal of damaged mitochondria via mitophagy by controlling the stability and localization of RAB7A. It is required for the recruitment of RAB7A and ATG9A vesicles to damaged mitochondria and promotes the stability of RAB7A by inhibiting its proteasomal degradation during mitophagy [[cite:PUB00100228]].

name: RNA ligase 1
description: This entry includes RNA ligase 1 from animals (RLIG1), which functions as an RNA ligase in vitro [[cite:PUB00151146]]. This protein catalyses ATP-dependent RNA ligation via a three-step mechanism, involving tandem auto- and RNA AMPylation. It exhibits selectivity for single-stranded RNA substrates. RLIG1 may play a role in maintaining RNA integrity under stress conditions, such as in response to reactive oxygen species (ROS) [[cite:PUB00151146]].

name: POU domain class 2-associating factor 2
description: POU domain class 2-associating factor 2 (also known as Protein OCA-T1) is a transcriptional coactivator that specifically associates with POU2F3 [[cite:PUB00101325]], forming a complex that drives the development of tuft cells, a rare chemosensory cells that coordinate immune and neural functions within mucosal epithelial tissues [[cite:PUB00101325]].

name: Intraflagellar transport-associated protein
description: Intraflagellar transport-associated protein (IFTAP, C11ORF74) interacts with the IFT-A complex and is accumulated at the distal tip in the absence of an IFT-A subunit IFT139. In IFTAP-knockout (KO) cells, the BBSome components cannot enter cilia. However, IFTAP-KO mice demonstrated no obvious anatomical abnormalities associated with ciliary dysfunctions [[cite:PUB00093954]].

name: PEX14-like KPWE domain
description: This domain, previously known as DUF5572, is found in Peroxisomal membrane protein PEX14 from Arabidopsis thaliana and other eukaryotic proteins. PEX14 is a component of the PEX13-PEX14 docking complex, a translocon channel that specifically mediates the import of peroxisomal cargo proteins bound to PEX5 receptor. This domain carry a highly conserved KPWE sequence at the C-terminal.

Family members have one predicted transmembrane region which is not included in this entry. The C19orf38 protein is also known as HIDE1 after Highly expressed in Immature DEndritic cell transcript 1 protein.

name: DUF5575 central RNaseH like domain
description: This entry represents the central domain from a family of Chordate proteins that includes C19orf68. These proteins appear to be transposon related. This domain appears to be closely related to the MULE RNaseH domain [pfam:PF10551].

name: YchJ, middle NTF2-like domain
description: This entry represents the NTF2-like domain found in the functionally uncharacterised YchJ family protein from Psychrobacter arcticus and related proteins. This domain is usually found flanked by either ([pfam:PF21612]) and ([pfam:PF02810]) at the N and C terminus or flanked on both sides by ([pfam:PF02810]]). The structure of YchJ shows that this domain adopts structure typical for Nuclear transport factor 2 (NTF2) that consists of a curved three-stranded beta-sheet and array of alpha-helices packed on one side of it. The function of this domain is unknown.

name: Testis-specific expressed protein 55
description: This family includes testis-specific expressed protein 55 (also known as TSCPA in human), which is involved in normal in normal spermatogenesis [[cite:PUB00092766],[cite:PUB00101403]].

name: SHOC1 ATPase domain
description: This domain is found in the human Protein shortage in chiasmata 1 ortholog (SHOC1) and related proteins from chordate. SHOC1 is an integral to the formation of crossover recombination intermediates during mammalian meiosis [[cite:PUB00090399]]. SHOC1 preferentially binds branched DNA molecules but apparently lacks in vitro endonuclease activity [[cite:PUB00090399]]. The core of SHOC1 resembles the DNA repair endonuclease XPF. This domain has significant similarity to P-loop AAA ATPase domains. This aligns with the SHOC1 ATPase activity, which is stimulated by the presence of single-stranded DNA [[cite:PUB00090399]].

name: Family of unknown function (DUF5588)
description: This is a family of unknown function found in chordata.

name: NIP7/UPF0113, pre-PUA domain
description: This entry represents the N-terminal, pre-PUA domain of yeast 60S ribosome subunit biogenesis protein NIP7 and homologues, some uncharacterised proteins from the UPF0113 family and similar sequences from eukaryotes and some archaeal species. NIP7 is required for proper 27S pre-rRNA processing and 60S ribosome subunit assembly. This domain is found associated with [pfam:PF03657].

name: Cell wall elongation regulator TseB-like domain
description: This domain is found in the probable cell wall elongation regulator TseB from Bacillus subtilis and similar sequences from firmicutes. TseB is required for normal cell shape. It plays an important role in cell wall elongation during exponential phase and spore outgrowth [[cite:PUB00105892]]. This domain shows an alpha-beta structure.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF5591)
description: This is a domain of unknown function found in archaeal tRNA-guanine transglycosylase ([ec:2.4.2.48]) and in archaeosine synthase ([ec:2.6.1.97]) proteins.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF3823_C)
description: This is a family of uncharacterised proteins from Bacteroidetes. This domain has an Ig-like fold.

name: Rv3651-like, N-terminal
description: This domain is found in Rv3651 from Mycobacterium tuberculosis ([swissprot:I6YCP0]) and similar proteins from Actinobacteria. Rv3651 adopts a three-domain configuration. This entry represents the N-terminal domain, a GAF domain that shows a central antiparallel beta-sheet of six beta-strands [[cite:PUB00100971]].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF5594)
description: This domain was first discovered in BPSL1050, a highly immunoreactive protein found in Burkholderia pseudomallei. The domain's structure consists of three helical regions which pack onto an antiparallel beta sheet, formed by four strands. The beta sheet is solvent exposed on one side and packs tightly against the three helices on the other side, generating a network of hydrophobic and aromatic interactions that contribute to tight packing of the protein. Is is thought that the small loop L1, the main loop L2, and part of helix alpha-3 extending until Leu120 are the three main immunogenic sequences [[cite:PUB00091370]].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF5595)
description: This domain is found in Nude C 80 (Ndc80) proteins which can be found in species such as Homo sapiens. Ndc80 protein complexes are a core component of the end-on attachment sites for kinetochore microtubules. Ndc80 is also known as Hec1, for highly expressed in cancer 1 [[cite:PUB00049694]].

name: N-acyltransferase N-terminal domain
description: This is the N-terminal all helix domain found in N-acyltransferases (NATs), the gene products orf11 and dbv8. The all-helix domain is composed of eight helices with two helix-turn-helix motifs in tandem. It is structurally akin to the AAA+ protein family (ATPases associated with diverse cellular activities) [[cite:PUB00091662]].

name: Carbohydrate binding module (family 35)
description: This is a delta4,5-anhydrogalacturonic acid-specific carbohydrate-binding module family 35, which is found in several prokaryotic proteins. Its crystal structure shows a jelly roll/beta-sandwich fold with 2 antiparallel sheets made of 4 and 5 antiparallel beta-strands [[cite:PUB00054441]]. It is also found at the end of a family of putative glycosyl hydrolases.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF5597)
description: This is the C-terminal domain of xyloglucan utilization locus (XyGUL) present in Cellvibrio japonicas. XyGUL is required for xyloglucan utilization. It is also the C-terminal domain of PF02449 and PF01301 [[cite:PUB00091233]].

name: Nicotinamide phosphoribosyltransferase, N-terminal domain
description: This is the N-terminal domain found in Nicotinamide phosphoribosyltransferase (NAMPT) present in Homo sapiens. NAMPT captures nicotinamide (NAM) and replenish the nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD+) pool during ADP-ribosylation and transferase reactions [[cite:PUB00059630]].

name: RNA helicase UPF1, 1B domain
description: UPF1 (or regulator of nonsense transcripts 1 homologue) is an essential RNA helicase that detects mRNAs containing premature stop codons and triggers their degradation. Together with UPF2 and UPF3, forms a surveillance complex, in which UPF2 acts as a bridge between UPF1 and UPF3. UPF2 and UPF3 are non-enzymatic components of the complex that stimulate the activity of UPF1 [[cite:PUB00050141],[cite:PUB00095891]]. UPF1 has a N-terminal cysteine/histidine-rich zinc-binding domain (CH/ZBD), a regulatory 1B domain, followed by a helicase core that belongs to superfamily 1 (SF1). This entry represents 1B domain of UPF1 which has a regulatory role. It suffers conformational changes from an inhibitory state to a transition-state complex that modulate RNA binding [[cite:PUB00050141],[cite:PUB00095891]].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF5600)
description: This domain can be found in EH-domain-containing ATPase 2 (EHD2) present in Mus musculus. The domain is helical in nature and has extensive contacts with the G-domain [[cite:PUB00049104]].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF5601)
description: This domain is found in the catalytic core RABEX-5 present in Homo sapiens. RABEX, also known as Rab GTPase exchange factors, regulate endocytic trafficking through activation of the Rab families RAB5, RAB21 and RAB22. The domain is helical in nature [[cite:PUB00042275]].

name: Hypothetical protein TTHB210
description: This domain is found in TTHB210 protein present in Thermus thermophilus. TTHB210 is a Sigma-E factor regulated gene product that forms a homodecamer. This domain is chain G and can be classified with chains A, C, E and I based on its folds [[cite:PUB00058436]].

name: L-serine kinase SerK, C-terminal domain
description: This domain is found in the C-terminal region of free serine kinase (SerK) in the hyperthermophilic archaeon Thermococcus kodakarensis. SerK converts ADP and l-serine (Ser) into AMP and O-phospho-l-serine (Sep), which is a precursor of l-cysteine. The domain is not conserved in the ParB/Srx family. The differences between SerK and the other members of the ParB/Srx family is concentrated in the C-terminal region, which may include residues involved in the Sep binding [[cite:PUB00091306]]. Members of this group are mainly found in archaea.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF5604)
description: This domain is often found in the N-terminal region of proteins carrying the SET domain ([pfam:PF00856]), such as the SETDB1 protein present in Homo sapiens. SETDB1 is a histone methyltransferase that suppresses gene expression and modulates heterochromatin formation through H3K9me2/3 [[cite:PUB00091314]].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF5605)
description: This domain is found in the C-terminal region of proteins carrying [pfam:PF16586] and [pfam:PF13204]. The C-terminal domain is carried by species such as Bacteroides vulgatus.

description: This entry represents a domain from ORF137 from Pyrobaculum spherical virus. This protein contains two domains with Sm-like fold which relative orientation is very similar to the relative orientation of individual subunits in the Sm-like assembly rings.

description: This entry represents a domain from ORF137 from Pyrobaculum spherical virus. This protein contains two domains with Sm-like fold which relative orientation is very similar to the relative orientation of individual subunits in the Sm-like assembly rings.

The structure displays an alpha/beta two-layer sandwich architecture formed by three alpha-helices and five beta-strands. Furthermore, structural homologs indicate that the TA0095 structure belongs to the TBP-like fold [[cite:PUB00047999]].

Individual blade consist of a three-stranded antiparallel beta-sheet and an alpha-helix packed on it. In some members this helix may have transitioned to a random coil.

name: Recombination directionality factor-like

Gp3 is a recombination directionality factor that interacts directly with the integrase tetramer to activate excision and inhibit integration [[cite:PUB00094660]]. name: Sublancin
description: This family represents sublancin, a small bacteriocin active against Gram-positive bacteria. This family appears to be restricted to Bacilli. Sublancin was thought to be a lantibiotic but was later shown to be an S-linked glycopeptide [[cite:PUB00060499],[cite:PUB00094614]]. Glycosylation is essential for its antimicrobial activity. Sublancin is biosynthesised as a precursor peptide bearing an N-terminal leader peptide, and a C-terminal core peptide that is converted into the mature peptide [[cite:PUB00060499]]. Sublancin comprises two alpha helices and a well-defined inter-helical loop [[cite:PUB00094615]]. Sublancin inhibits B.cereus spore outgrowth, after the germination stage, approximately 1000-fold better than it inhibits exponential growth of the same cells and inhibits B.subtilis strain ATCC6633 and B. megaterium strain 14581 [[cite:PUB00094614]].

Anaclyclamides are a type of cyanobactin produced in strains of the cyanobacteria Anabaena [[cite:PUB00060495]]. AcyE is a 49-amino-acid protein with N-terminal homology to the peptide precursor proteins in the other cyanobactin pathways [[cite:PUB00094616]]. The core peptide of AcyE is cleaved during post-translational processing of the precursor peptide [[cite:PUB00094616]].

name: 6-phospho-N-acetylmuramidase, N-terminal
description: This domain represents the N-terminal domain of 6-phospho-N-acetylmuramidase (MupG) from Staphylococcus aureus [[cite:PUB00097906]], also found in putative phospho sugar glycosidases from Gram-negative and -positive species, but mainly firmicutes. MupG [[cite:PUB00097906]], specifically cleaves MurNAc 6P-GlcNAc, a product of cell wall turnover, into the sugars MurNAc 6P and GlcNAc, involved in cell wall turnover and recycling. Since some species, for example Lactobacillus plantarum, possess several putative paralogs, the substrate specificity of the proteins containing this domain may not be limited to cell wall sugars, but may include phosphorylated disaccharides in general. Most of these proteins appear to consist of two structural subdomains, as it can be seen in the two available crystal structures of Enterococcus faecalis (PDB:2p0o) and Bacillus cereus (PDB:1X7F). This entry is the larger N-terminal domain that constitutes a TIM-barrel like structure and the C-terminal domain is similar to the cyclophilin family. It should be noted that some proteins lack the C-terminal domain.

name: Coronavirus replicase NSP6
description: This entry represents proteins found in Coronaviruses and includes the Non-structural Protein 6 (NSP6). Coronaviruses encode large replicase polyproteins which are proteolytically processed by viral proteases to generate mature Nonstructural Proteins (NSPs) [[cite:PUB00094417]]. NSP6 is a membrane protein containing 6 transmembrane domains with a large C-terminal tail [[cite:PUB00094417]]. NSP6 from the avian coronavirus, infectious bronchitis virus (IBV) and the mouse hepatitis virus (MHV) have been shown to localise to the ER and to generate autophagosomes [[cite:PUB00094416]]. Coronavirus NSP6 proteins have also been shown to limit autophagosome expansion. This may favour coronavirus infection by reducing the ability of autophagosomes to deliver viral components to lysosomes for degradation [[cite:PUB00094416]]. NSP6 from IBV, MHV and severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus (SARS-CoV) have also been found to activate autophagy [[cite:PUB00094416],[cite:PUB00094418]].

The AH domain interacts with A/R tRNA and links the very C-terminal subdomains with TGS domain. RelA/SpoT-homologue proteins (RHS) mediate the stringent response in bacteria which enables its metabolic adaptation under stress conditions. These enzymes synthesise the second messenger (p)ppGpp, which is a regulatory metabolite of the stringent response characterised by growth arrest and the modulation of gene expression in response to various nutritional stresses [[cite:PUB00095792],[cite:PUB00098872],[cite:PUB00059269]].

TEP1 is also a component of the vault particle, a cytoplasmic ribonucleoprotein complex, in which it is required for vault RNA stability and its association with the vault particle [[cite:PUB00035328]]. This domain is localised between the TROVE ([pfam:PF05731]) and DUF4062 ([pfam:PF13271]) domains.

TFIIIC is a multisubunit complex that directly recognises promoter elements and recruits TFIIIB and RNA polymerase III, being absolutely required for RNA polymerase III transcription. TFIIIC90 has an intrinsic histone acetyltransferase activity with a substrate specificity for histone H3 [[cite:PUB00056254]]. Duramycin binds phosphatidylethanolamine (PE), a major structural phospholipid in mammalian and microbial cell membranes which contains 19 amino acids and 5 post-translational modifications (PTMs). This entry represents DurN, an enzyme that forms (2S,9S)-Lal one of the two last PTMs. DurN catalyses stereospecific and diastereoselective Lal formation in an unusual substrate-assisted mechanism in which the active site residues that make the reaction proceed come from the substrate itself, manoeuvred into position by DurN [[cite:PUB00152101]].

name: 7(1) septoil knot domain
description: This entry represents a small protein domain with a 7(1) septoil knot topology, one of the most complex protein knots known. The structured core consists of a beta-barrel with six beta-strands and two short alpha-helices. The domain contains a conserved SFPD tetrapeptide motif in the loops between beta-strands, resulting in a pseudo fivefold symmetry with conserved phenylalanine side chains pointing outward. The domain is exceptionally stable against chemical denaturation and shows high mechanical resistance. name: Cell division protein PerM
description: PerM is an integral membrane protein containing 8-10 transmembrane helices that is highly conserved amongst mycobacteria and actinobacteria but absent from other bacterial lineages. The protein functions as an essential component of the mycobacterial divisome complex, directly interacting with FtsB through conserved hydrophobic residues. PerM localises to division septa where it modulates cell wall synthesis, with activity critically dependent on magnesium availability. Disruption results in magnesium-dependent growth defects, cell elongation, hypersensitivity to beta-lactam antibiotics, and severe attenuation during chronic infections. The protein appears to integrate environmental stress signals, enabling mycobacteria to regulate cell division in response to host-induced stress during persistent infection.

name: RZ type zinc finger domain
description: This entry represents the RZ type zinc finger domain, found in NFX1-type zinc finger-containing protein 1 (ZNFX1) and E3 ubiquitin-protein ligase RNF213 from humans. It contains two conserved histidine residues and four conserved cysteine residues in a CHC3H motif. It can bind divalent transition metals, with a preference for Zn2+. ZNFX1 is an RNA-binding protein that initiates the antiviral response and is required to restrict the replication of RNA viruses [[cite:PUB00100916],[cite:PUB00100918]]. RNF213 is a giant E3 ubiquitin ligase that can catalyse ubiquitination of both proteins and lipids, which is involved in various processes, such as lipid metabolism, angiogenesis and cell-autonomous immunity. It functions as a key immune sensor by catalysing ubiquitination of the lipid A moiety of bacterial LPS via its RZ-type zinc-finger and restricts the proliferation of cytosolic bacteria [[cite:PUB00100919],[cite:PUB00100915]]. RNF213 is a major susceptibility factor of Moyamoya disease [[cite:PUB00100917]].

name: Pediocin PA-1 biosynthesis protein PedC-like
description: This family of proteins, previously known as DUF6568, represents the Pediocin PA-1 biosynthesis protein PedC and related proteins, including Protein MesC, that are mainly found in firmicutes. PedC is probably involved in pediocin PA-1 biosynthesis , a class II bacteriocin produced by the bacterium Pediococcus acidilactici [[cite:PUB00034683]]. Member of this family contain two conserved motifs, CxxF and YxN, and two conserved residues, Tyr at the N-terminal and a Gly at the C-terminal end. Many members of this family are thought to belong to the Thioredoxin superfamily.

name: ARG and Rhodanese-Phosphatase-superfamily-associated Protein domain
description: ARPP-1 shows a distinguishing group of absolutely conserved residues, including a cysteine and a glutamine, suggestive of enzymatic activity. Structural predictions reveal a core beta-sheet comprised of a duplicated four-stranded beta-meander with a beta-barrel domain bearing the absolutely conserved residues inserted into the first repeat. The unifying biochemical theme across its conserved contextual genome linkages is the presence of molecules with sugar moieties (ADPr, nucleotides, and polysaccharides). In genome contexts linking ARPP-1 with ARG and other counter viral ribosylation domains, ARPP is predicted to act on ribose moieties coming from ADPr. The presence of the conserved cysteine suggests that it could function analogous to the recently characterized SRAP domain by forming covalent cross-links with sugars [[cite:PUB00153825],[cite:PUB00153826]].

SutA interacts directly with RNAP holoenzyme and the RNAP-beta protrusion is its primary anchor site. This domain comprises an alpha-helix and a beta-strand and is responsible for interaction with RNAP-beta protrusion [[cite:PUB00152756]]. It contains a conserved FLxxGG sequence motif that appears to be located near the C-terminal helix cap. The SutA-RBD alpha-helix binds to a hydrophobic groove on RNAP-beta protrusion [[cite:PUB00152756]].

name: Family of unknown function (DUF6814)
description: This family of proteins is functionally uncharacterised. Proteins in this family are predominantly found in Bacteroidetes and are approximately 80 amino acids in length. There are several conserved motifs: IxxGL, FGxY and GEY.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF6815)
description: This presumed domain is functionally uncharacterised and is found in bacteria and eukaryotes. It may contain an ATP-grasp-like fold which suggest an ATP-binding function. There are several conserved motifs: EGxxR, PxxWxxDF and ExNCSCV.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF6816)
description: This presumed domain is functionally uncharacterised and it is found in bacterial (predominantly in cyanobacteria) and eukaryotic (mainly from plants) sequences. Structure prediction using AlphaFold resource, suggest that this domain may have a START-like (StAR-related lipid-transfer) fold consisting of an alpha/beta structure of a helix-grip fold, that forms cavities for hydrophobic substrates or ligands which may indicate a possible function for this domain.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF6817)
description: This presumed domain is functionally uncharacterised, found in bacteria and plants. It is approximately 160 amino acids in length and it has two conserved sequence motifs, HL and GLxHxxY. Several members of this entry also has TPR regions.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF6818)
description: This presumed domain is functionally uncharacterised. It is found in proteins from eukaryotes, and is typically between 39 and 76 amino acids in length. There are several conserved motifs, Y/FxN, KF and KPTG and a highly conserved W residue at the N-terminal. Structural predictions indicate this domain may fold into three alpha helices.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF6819)
description: This domain of unknown function is found at the C-terminal of [pfam:PF16314] and it may have an alpha-helical fold.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF6820)
description: This domain is functionally uncharacterised. It is found in eukaryotes (predominantly in the marine diatom Thalassiosira) and is approximately 50 amino acids in length. There are several conserved motifs: TSAGR/QARxM, FAV and DNxGRRAM/IG.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF6821)
description: This presumed domain is functionally uncharacterised. This family is found mainly in plants, and is approximately 300 amino acids in length. It contains a predicted transmembrane helix.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF6822)
description: This family of proteins is functionally uncharacterised. This family of proteins is found in eukaryotes (predominantly in the Dinoflagellate Symbiodinium microadriaticum). There are several highly conserved W residues.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF6823)
description: This family of proteins is functionally uncharacterised. This protein family is found in eukaryotes. There are highly conserved motifs: QQE and RFDLR.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF6824)
description: This presumed domain is functionally uncharacterised. This domain family is found in eukaryotes. There are highly conserved motifs: DxxxGR/KG, HxGN and GRFL; and three highly conserved residues: W, K and R at the C-terminal.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF6825)
description: This family of proteins is functionally uncharacterised. This family of proteins is found in plants and cyanobacteria. Proteins in this family are typically between 108 and 202 amino acids in length.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF6826)
