description: This presumed domain is functionally uncharacterised and is found in fungal sequences, N-terminal to a kinase domain. There are two conserved motifs: PD and QPxR.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF6827)
description: This presumed domain is functionally uncharacterised. This domain is predominantly found in sequences from Apicomplexa. There are highly conserved motifs: NWxD, EDxxDH and GxGLAI/LLRQ.

name: ATPTG10-like
description: This entry, previously known as DUF6828, represents a domain found in the T. gondii ATP synthase subunit 10 (ATPTG10) and related proteins from Apicomplexan species. This domain adopts an alpha-helical structure consisting of five helices [[cite:PUB00152764]]. It contains two highly conserved sequence motifs: FSWxD and MxLWI/LKxRI/L. The formation of the T.gondii ATP synthase hexamer involves two contact sites in the lumenal region. ATPTG10 contributes to the the second site via interaction with ATP synthase subunit 11 (ATPTG11).

name: Family of unknown function (DUF6829)
description: This family is functionally uncharacterised. This domain family is found in eukaryotes, and is around 420 amino acids in length. Structurally, this family is made of alpha helices.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF6830)
description: This presumed domain is functionally uncharacterised. This domain family is predominantly found in Basidiomycetes. There are several highly conserved residues: P, W, Q and G.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF6831)
description: This domain s is functionally uncharacterised. It is predominantly found in eukaryotic sequences mostly from Alveolata. There are several highly conserved motifs, including YxKHxR and WPPE at the C terminus. The domain is predicted to adopt an alpha-beta fold.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF6832)
description: This domain is functionally uncharacterised. It is predominantly found in eukaryotic sequences mostly from Alveolata. There are several highly conserved motifs: FGFNSFWS, FKxxxYD, PRxxY and YRC. Predictions of its structure suggest it folds into seven alpha helices.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF5580) middle domain
description: This is a family of unknown function found in metazoa. This entry represents the central globular domain of the protein related to the calmodulin domain.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF5580) C-terminal domain
description: This is a family of unknown function found in metazoa. This entry represents the C-terminal domain.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF6833)
description: This presumed domain predominantly is found in sequences from tailed bacteriophages and proteobacterial prophages, including Pseudomonas phage LUZ7. Its function is unknown.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF6834), C-terminal domain
description: This presumed domain is found at the C terminus of Uncharacterized protein AF_2093 from Archaeoglobus fulgidus and similar proteins of unknown function from archaea.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF6835)
description: This domain of unknown function is found in proteins from bacteria, including the product of the gene SO_2669 from Shewanella oneidensis. Its structure has been solved and shows 16 alpha helices ([swissprot:Q8EDS4]).

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF6836)
description: This domain is predominantly found in proteins from bacteria, including CLOLEP_02462 from Clostridium leptum. The function of this protein is unknown.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF6837)
description: This domain is found in proteins from tailed bacteriophages and eukaryotes, including 201phi2-1p060 from Pseudomonas phage 201phi2-1 Its function is unknown.

name: Phage tail terminator protein
description: This entry represents a family of likely phage tail terminator proteins which form a hexameric complex that joins the phage neck to the tail.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF447)
description: This entry represents a spectrin-like domain found in the DUF447 family of proteins.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF6839)
description: This entry represents a domain of unknown function found in a range of bacteria and phage.

name: DUF5575 N-terminal domain
description: This entry represents the N-terminal domain from a family of Chordate proteins that includes C19orf68. These proteins appear to be transposon related. This domain appears to be related to the WRKY-like DNA-binding domains.

name: DUF5575 C-terminal domain
description: This entry represents the C-terminal domain from a family of Chordate proteins that includes C19orf68. These proteins appear to be transposon related.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF6840)
description: This uncharacterised protein family is predominantly found in Leptospirillum sp. Its function is unknown. There are some conserved motifs: SRD, AGGL and some highly conserved Y, H and W residues.

name: NTF2-like protein (DUF6841)
description: This entry represents a family of NTF2-like proteins of unknown function.

name: Dot/Icm T4SS effector Lem25 domain
description: This domain is found in Dot/Icm T4SS effector Lem25 from Legionella pneumophila. It adopts an helical bundle fold. Its function is unknown.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF5382) C-terminal domain
description: This is a domain of unknown function found in Caenorhabditis. It has an NTF2-like fold.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF5382) N-terminal domain
description: This is a domain of unknown function found in Caenorhabditis. It has an NTF2-like fold.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF6843)
description: This protein family includes Putative lipoprotein BA_2398 from Bacillus anthracis and similar proteins from bacteria, predominantly Firmicutes and Bacteroidetes.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF6844)
description: This domain is found in proteins predominantly found in Gammaproteobacteria such as Hypothetical protein FTT_1539c from Francisella tularensis. It is located in the centre of the proteins included in this entry.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF6845)
description: This domain is found at the N-terminal end of uncharacterized DUF3829-like proteins. It might be related to [pfam:PF12889]. Its function is unknown.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF6846)
description: This domain is found at the N-terminal end of Uncharacterized protein AF_2093 from Archaeoglobus fulgidus and similar proteins from archaea. Its function is unknown.

name: S-Me-THD-like, C-terminal domain
description: This beta barrel domain is found at the C-terminal of S-methyl thiohydantoin desulfurase from Variovorax sp. (S-Me-THD) and similar sequences mainly found in bacteria and fungi. S-Me-THD catalyses the hydrolysis of S-methyl -thiohydantoin-5-propanoate into hydantoin-5-propanoate and methanethiol, the third step in S-methyl ergothioneine degradation [[cite:PUB00155448]].

name: Domain of unknown function DUF1846, C-terminal
description: This is the C-terminal domain found in the uncharacterised protein family UPF0371. It has a cytidine deaminase-like fold (pdbe:3bh1).

name: Family of unknown function (DUF6847)
description: This family represents bacterial uncharacterised proteins such as Uncharacterized conserved protein Dip1984 from Corynebacterium diphtheriae, which shows an all-alpha structure. Some members of this family are annotated as septicolysin, such as [swissprot:H6NMB2], a cholesterol-dependent pore-forming cytolysin that acts to facilitate the infection of certain pathogenic gram-positive bacteria.

name: DUF2264 C-terminal domain
description: This domain is found at the C-terminus of DUF2264 family proteins. This domain adopts a beta sandwich domain that is structurally related to [pfam:PF07940], suggesting that DUF2264 proteins are oligosaccharide degrading enzymes.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF6848)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised protein rbstp2171 from Bacillus stearothermophilus and similar proteins found in bacteria and tailed bacteriophages.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF4785) central domain
description: This family of proteins is found in bacteria. Proteins in this family are typically between 392 and 442 amino acids in length. This entry represents the central immunoglobulin-like domain.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF4785) C-terminal domain
description: This family of proteins is found in bacteria. Proteins in this family are typically between 392 and 442 amino acids in length. This entry represents the C-terminal immunoglobulin-like domain.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF4931) C-terminal domain
description: This family consists of uncharacterized proteins around 270 residues in length and is mainly found in various Bacillus cereus species. Some members of this family are annotated as Galactose-1-phosphate uridylyltransferases, but the specific function of this family is unknown.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF6849)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised archaeal proteins. It is found C-terminal to [pfam:PF02933], in CDC48 proteins. Its function is unknown.

name: Predicted membrane protein (DUF2207) C-terminal domain
description: This domain, found in various hypothetical bacterial proteins, has no known function.

name: Type VI lipase adapter protein Tla3, C-terminal
description: This entry represents the the C-terminal domain of Type VI lipase adapter protein Tla3, an adapter protein that targets and loads the Tle3 toxin onto the H2 type VI secretion system (H2-T6SS) machinery through an interaction with the TTR domain of VgrG2b [[cite:PUB00100136]] and it seems to be specific for Tle3 [[cite:PUB00100136]]. This domain and its N-terminal ([pfam:PF11394]) are both required for the interaction with the toxin [[cite:PUB00100136]].

name: Family of unknown function (DUF5581) N-terminal domain
description: This entry represents the N-terminal helical domain found in C20orf195 and its homologues found in chordates.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF3195) C-terminal domain
description: This archaeal family of proteins has no known function. This entry represents the C-terminal THUMP-like domain.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF4438), C-terminal
description: This is the C-terminal domain of TM_1086 which consists of a 3-layer sandwich.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF6850)
description: This bacterial protein forms a likely integral membrane beta barrel domain.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1285), C-terminal domain
description: This domain is found at the C-terminal end of several hypothetical bacterial proteins. The structure revealed a superficial similarity of this domain to pleckstrin homology-like folds [[cite:PUB00062529]].

name: Biogenesis factor required for ATP synthase 1, C-terminal domain
description: This domain is predominantly found at the C-terminal end of proteins from cyanobacteria and plants, including Biogenesis factor required for ATP synthase 1 (BFA1, [swissprot:F4J1U2]) from Arabidopsis thaliana. BFA1 promotes the assembly of the CF1 subcomplex of the chloroplast ATP synthase by specifically interacting with the gamma and beta subunits. This domain consists of ten beta-sheets and one alpha- helix forming a typical beta-barrel, which locates perpendicularly to [pfam:PF12204] [[cite:PUB00100989]].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF6851)
description: This domain of unknown function is found in the N-terminal region of a group of bacterial proteins, including Haloperoxidase from Muricauda lutaonensis. In this protein, this domain is found associated to [pfam:PF01569]. Its specific function is unknown.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF6852)
description: This domain is found at the C-terminal end of BVU_3817 from Phocaeicola vulgatus ([swissprot:A6L6W4]) and similar proteins mostly found in Bacteroidetes. This domain shows an alpha/beta structure and is normally found associated with [pfam:PF18347]. Its function is unknown.

name: DUF3108-like
description: This is a domain found in bacteria which adopts a beta-barrel fold of the YmcC-like type.

name: DUF3860-like
description: This protein family includes [swissprot:Q6N4D8] from Rhodopseudomonas palustris, an uncharacterized protein that shows an alpha-beta structure and has some similarity with the structure predicted for members of [pfam:PF12976].

name: DUF1980 C-terminal domain
description: Members of this family are found in a set of prokaryotic hypothetical proteins. Their exact function, has not, as yet, been defined. This entry represents the C-terminal domain.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF6853)
description: This protein family includes NMB0500 from Neisseria meningitidis and similar bacterial uncharacterised proteins. NMB0500 has an all-alpha structure. Its function is unknown.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF6854)
description: This domain is found usually twice in a group of uncharacterised bacterial proteins. It shows a four-stranded beta-sheet and two alpha-helices.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF6855)
description: This single domain protein is found a range of bacteria such as actinobacteria, bacteroidetes and firmicutes. It is functionally uncharacterised. The proteins are about 130 amino acids in length.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF6856)
description: This entry includes a set of mycoplasma lipoproteins related to uncharacterized Mycoplasma genitalium lipoprotein MG348.

name: CORD, C-terminal domain
description: This domain is found at the C-terminal in Protein CORTICAL MICROTUBULE DISORDERING (CORD) proteins found in plants. This domain may consist of 5-6 alpha-helices. CORD proteins are microtubule-associated proteins that are required, redundantly with CORD2, for the formation of the pitted secondary cell wall of metaxylem vessels [[cite:PUB00163241]]. CORD1 from Arabidopsis thaliana controls the disorganisation of the parallel cortical microtubule network by modulating microtubule attachment to the plasma membrane in metaxylem vessel cells; this mechanism probably relies on disruption of interactions between ARAC10/ROP11 and cortical microtubules [[cite:PUB00163241]5].

name: Family of unknown function (DUF6858)
description: This family of proteins are distantly related to [pfam:PF03625]. Their function is as yet unknown.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF6859)
description: This domain is found at the N-terminal of fungal proteins, such as SwissProt:O74728 from S.pombe, a protein thought to be localised in the ER. From AlphaFold structure prediction, it can be inferred that this domain may adopt an alpha/beta structure consisting of six antiparallel beta-strands surrounded by three or four alpha-helices.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF6860)
description: This is the N-terminal domain of uncharacterised proteins such as YhiJ from E.coli. According to AlphaFold model, this domain may have an alpha/beta structure consisting of five beta-sheets and three short alpha-helices.

name: Domain of unknown function DUF4246, N-terminal
description: This presumed domain is found N-terminal of [pfam:PF14033]) which may consist of four helices.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF6861)
description: This domain is a likely integral membrane domain that contains a glycine-zipper motif. This domain is found associated with toxin domains.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF6862)
description: This entry represents a small domain that is found in a variety of toxin proteins. The precise function of this domain is uncertain. It often follows [pfam:PF04829].

name: Family of unknown function (DUF6863)
description: This entry represents an alpha helical bundle domain found at the N-terminus of a small group of putative bacterial toxins. The function of this domain is unknown.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF6864)
description: This entry represents a family of bacterial proteins that adopt a beta-sandwich domain. The function of these proteins is currently unknown.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF6865)
description: This entry represents a short family of uncharacterised proteins from plants. AlphaFold predictions suggest that the protein contains two non-contacting alpha-helices.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF6866) N-terminal domain
description: This entry represents the N-terminal alpha+beta domain found in DUF6866 family proteins. The function of these proteins is unknown. Proteins in this family are primarily found in Proteobacteria.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF6866) C-terminal domain
description: This entry represents the C-terminal alpha-helical domain found in DUF6866 family proteins. The function of these proteins is unknown. Proteins in this family are primarily found in Proteobacteria.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF6867)
description: This entry represents a likely integral membrane protein. These proteins are composed of three alpha helices followed by a short beta hairpin. This family is called DUF6867. Proteins in this family are found in Proteobacteria.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF6868)
description: This entry represents a small bacterial integral membrane protein of unknown function that is composed of two transmembrane helices. The function of this protein is unknown.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF6869)
description: This short family of bacterial proteins contains a potential alpha helical solenoid structure. The function of these proteins is unknown. Proteins in this family are primarily found in Proteobacteria.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF6870)
description: This entry represents a small bacterial protein o unknown function. Proteins in this family are primarily found in Firmicutes.

name: CFAP58 central coiled coil
description: This domain is found in Cilia- and flagella-associated protein 58 (CFAP58) and related eukaryotic proteins. The human CFAP58 protein has an essential role in the assembly and organisation of the sperm flagellar axoneme [[cite:PUB00151877]]. This domain forms a parallel coiled coil that in the C. reinhardtii axonemal structure lays on the doublet microtubule surface and interacts with the N terminus of the MIA coiled coil [[cite:PUB00152767]].

name: ODAD1 central coiled coil region
description: This domain, previously know as DUF6872, is found in Outer dynein arm-docking complex subunit 1 (ODAD1, CCDC114) from humans and similar eukaryotic proteins. In mammals, CCDC114 forms a hetero-coiled coil with ODAD1/CCDC151 within the A07/A08 interprotofilament cleft, analogous to the DC1/2 coiled coil of the trimeric ODA-DC observed in C. reinhardtii axoneme [[cite:PUB00152762],[cite:PUB00100771]]. DC2 is a homolog of the human ODAD1/CCDC151 and in C.reinhardtii it is a part of the ODA-DC that consists of three proteins: DC1, DC2, and DC3. The N-terminal halves of DC1 and DC2 form a microtubule-bound heteromeric coiled-coil [[cite:PUB00152762],[cite:PUB00152763]].

name: Family of unknown function (DUF6873)
description: This entry represents a family of uncharacterised proteins that have a five fold symmetric alpha/beta propeller fold belonging to the GME (guanidino-group modifying enzymes) superfamily [[cite:PUB00009967],[cite:PUB00151878]].

name: Family of unknown function (DUF6874)
description: This entry represents a family of uncharacterised proteins that contain a small alpha helical bundle domain.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF6875)
description: This entry represents family of uncharacterised proteins. They share an N-terminal CPF/Y motif that is characteristic of the NCPF superfamily of proteins.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF6876)
description: This entry represents a family of uncharacterised proteins that show structural similarity to [pfam:PF06124].

name: Family of unknown function (DUF6877)
description: This entry represents a small family of short uncharacterised proteins. They are predicted to adopt a three helical structure.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF6878)
description: This entry represents an uncharacterised protein that adopts a beta-grasp fold.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF6879)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised proteins. However, they fold into a compact domain that is structurally related to the Phospholipase D protein family ([pfam:PF13091]). This suggests they may have an enzymatic activity.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF6880)
description: This entry represents a family of proteins that form an alpha-helical solenoid structure of HEAT-like repeats. Proteins in this family are found in various bacterial species, but most commonly in proteobacteria.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF6881)
description: This entry represents a small bacterial protein of unknown function. Its predicted structure shows a 6 stranded beta sheet with a C-terminal helix packed on one side. In a few proteins this domain is associated with [pfam:PF15595] a presumed immunity protein, which could suggest this domain may have a toxin function or be involved in a toxin/antitoxin system or in phage defence.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF6882)
description: This family of bacterial proteins is uncharacterised.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF6883)
description: This entry represents a protein domain that is often found in single domain proteins. It is also sometimes found in larger multi-domain proteins. The function of this domain is unknown.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF6884)
description: This is a domain of unknown function that is found either as a standalone protein or in combination with other domains. Members of this family possess a highly conserved LSAXXG motif that may constitute an active site. This domain may be distantly related to oxidative stress response YaaA proteins.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF6885)
description: This is a small family of proteins that are likely to adopt a papain-like fold. Most members of this family have conserved residues in equivalent positions as the residues that constitute the active site of cysteine proteases.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF6886)
description: This is a family of proteins whose function is unknown. They may be distantly related to ADP-ribosylating toxins.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF6887)
description: This entry represents a family of uncharacterised cyanobacterial proteins.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF6888)
description: This family of proteins is found in bacteria. Proteins in this family are approximately 60 amino acids in length. There is a conserved N-terminal MPT sequence motif. AlphaFold predicts that this protein is composed of an N-terminal alpha helix followed by a four stranded beta sheet. AlphaFold also predicts the protein forms a strong dimer interface. It shows some weak structural similarity to the N-terminal domain of RnlA toxin.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF6889)
description: This entry represents a family of small proteins that are largely composed of a single alpha helix. Some members of the family are found on phage. The function of these proteins is unknown.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF6890)
description: This entry represents a family of small proteins composed largely of a single alpha helix. Some proteins in this family are annotated as from phage. The function of these proteins is unknown.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF6891)
description: This entry represents a bacterial protein of unknown function.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF6892)
description: This entry represents a family of uncharacterised bacterial proteins.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF6893)
description: This entry represents a small protein that has a likely signal peptide that takes up most of the sequence. Thus a small peptide might be released from these proteins.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF6894)
description: This entry represents a small protein domain found in alpha proteobacteria. Its structure is composed of a four stranded sheet packed on one side by an alpha helix. The function of these proteins is unknown.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF6895)
description: This entry contains a set of proteins that have a predicted 6-helical hairpin fold found in a wide range of glycosyl hydrolase enzymes, suggesting a potential function for these proteins. These proteins are largely found in actinobacteria and Alphaproteobacteria.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF6896)
description: This entry represents a family of bacterial proteins of unknown function. The domain structure includes a four stranded beta sheet which has two conserved aspartates in a DXDXG motif close to a highly conserved histidine. These three residues may for the potential active site.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF6897)
description: This entry represents a family of small bacterial and archaeal proteins that have an SH3 like barrel structure that shows most similarity to the C-terminal domain of the ribosomal chaperone RimP [pfam:PF17384].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF6898)
description: This entry represents a small protein that has a domain with a structure resembling a double stranded RNA-binding domain such as [pfam:PF00035]. Thus suggesting this protein may also have a dsRNA binding function. This is supported by the presence of several conserved positively charged residues.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF6899)
description: This entry represents a bacterial protein of unknown function.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF6900)
description: This entry represents a small domain found in a range of bacterial and phage proteins. In a few proteins it is associated with [pfam:PF11994]. This region is composed of two alpha helices.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF6901)
description: This entry represents a family of uncharacterised proteins. The possess a beta sheet packed against an alpha helical subdomain. This alignment contains three fully conserved cysteines that look like they form an Fe-S cluster or zinc binding site in the predicted structures.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF6902)
description: This entry represents a family of bacterial proteins that have an alpha/alpha(6) toroid structure. This suggests that these proteins are likely to be an as yet uncharacterised family of glycosyl hydrolases.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF6903)
description: This entry represents a family of small putative integral membrane proteins with two transmembrane helices.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF6904)
description: This entry represents an uncharacterised family of bacterial proteins. Members of the family are about 250 residues in length.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF6905)
description: Members of this family are annotated in SwissProt as Putative glycerol transporters SwissProt:Q92EU1. Members of the family contain four potential transmembrane helices.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF6906)
description: This entry represents a small domain found in a range of phage and bacterial proteins. Structurally it is composed of a three stranded beta meander packed against an alpha helix. The function of these proteins is unknown.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF6907)
description: This entry represents a family of Actinobacterial proteins of unknown function. AlphaFold predicts a confident dimeric arrangement. This family appears to be distantly related to [pfam:PF19887].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF6908)
description: This family of proteins are uncharacterised. This family is distantly related to [pfam:PF06853] currently known as DUF1249.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF6909)
description: This is a family of uncharacterised proteins. They are predicted to adopt a globular structure consisting of two domains. The predicted C-terminal domain share similarity with the catalytic domains of purine and uridine phosphorylases.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF6910)
description: The function of this family of proteins is unknown. They are predicted to adopt a five-bladed beta-propeller and are probably distantly related to apyrase.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF6911)
description: This entry represents a family of uncharacterised proteins. Proteins in this family are primarily found in Proteobacteria. The structure of these proteins contains a six stranded beta sheet.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF6912)
description: This is a family of uncharacterized proteins.Their predicted structure shows some similarity to ADP-rybosylating toxins.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF6913)
description: This is a family of uncharacterized proteins. They share remote similarity to both domains of proteins members of UDP-glycosyltransferase superfamily. In contrast to them, these proteins are predicted to consist of a single standalone domain.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF6914)
description: This is a family of uncharacterized proteins. They are predicted to adopt a globular structure that resembles the conserved core of the PPPDE superfamily (after Permuted Papain fold Peptidases of DsRNA viruses and Eukaryotes) consisting of thiol peptidases with a circularly permuted papain-like fold.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF6915)
description: This family of proteins is primarily found in proteobacteria. Proteins in this family are typically between 124 and 153 amino acids in length. Proteins in this family has several conserved histidine residues that may form zinc binding sites.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF6916)
description: This is a domain of unknown function found in bacterial proteins. It is predicted to adopt a RIFT-type beta(6)-barrel topology with a greater similarity to FAD-binding domains.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF6917)
description: This family of proteins is found in bacteria. Proteins in this family are typically between 135 and 154 amino acids in length. These proteins share significant sequence similarity to the central part of mammalian cell entry (MCE) protein MlaD.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF6918)
description: This is a family of uncharacterized bacterial proteins with a length of ~140-150 residues. They are predicted to adopt an alpha-helical structure consisting of two structural repeats.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF6919)
description: This domain is found standalone in bacteria. Its function is unknown but it has a significant sequence similarity to the C-terminal SAM-binding regulatory domain of 5,10-methylenetetrahydrofolate reductase (MTHFR).

name: Family of unknown function (DUF6920)
description: This entry represents a set of uncharacterised proteins found in prokaryotes. They share remote similarity to LolA and LolB outer-membrane lipoproteins. Similar to LolA and LolB these proteins are predicted to have a hydrophobic cavity consisting of an unclosed beta-barrel and an alpha-helical lid.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF6921)
description: This family of proteins is based on the known structure of a protein from Ruminococcus gnavus PDB:3noh. The structure shows similarity to solute binding proteins. The exact function of these proteins is not yet known.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF6922)
description: This family is found in bacterial proteins either as a standalone domain or in combination with an HTH domain that resembles lambda C1 repressor DNA-binding domain. This family has a partial sequence similarity to the RAP1 C-terminal (RCT) domain.

name: Repeat of unknown function (DUF6923)
description: This entry represents a beta propeller domain composed of five blades. It is often found in large extracellular proteins in one or more copies. It is uncertain whether this domain might have an enzymatic function or a ligand binding function. Structurally this domain appears to have a sixfold symmetry, but one of the blades takes up the space of normal repeats. This unusual blade is composed of three strands of the first repeat and a final C-terminal strand from the last repeat.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF6924)
description: This domain of unknown function is found mainly in bacterial proteins, either standalone or in combination with other domains. It is probably remotely related to the anticodon binding domain observed in histidyl, glycyl, threonyl and prolyl tRNA synthetases.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF6925)
description: This is a family of uncharacterised bacterial proteins. They are probably distantly related to heme-binding proteins PhuS, ChuS, HmuS.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF6926)
description: This domain of unknown function is found in bacterial proteins. It is probably distantly related to dodecin. It is predicted to adopt a simple fold consisting of a core of 3 strands, forming a curved sheet, and two short helices.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF6927)
description: This domain is found C-terminal in uncharacterised bacterial proteins. It is probably remotely related to PemK-like, MazF-like toxins and is predicted to adopt SH3-like fold.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF6928)
description: This is a family of uncharacterised bacterial proteins. They are predicted to adopt alpha/beta structure with a central nine-stranded antiparallel beta-sheet with helices packed on both sides. The predicted structure has some partial structural similarity to bacterial S-adenosylmethionine decarboxylases.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF6929)
description: This is a family of uncharacterised bacterial proteins. They are predicted to fold into five-bladed beta-propeller that has similarity to apyrase but it is circularly permuted. The C-terminal two beta-strands of this domain occupy the position of the two N-terminal beta-strands in apyrase.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF6930)
description: This domain is found C-terminal in uncharacterised bacterial proteins. It is remotely related to the integrase core domain with a partly conserved active site architecture.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF6931)
description: This is a family of uncharacterised bacterial proteins. They share significant sequence similarity with immunity protein Imm5 and are predicted to adopt similar alpha-helical structure.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF6932)
description: This is a family of uncharacterised bacterial proteins. They are remotely related to nucleotidyltransferases and share similar active site architecture.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF6933)
description: This domain is found in bacterial and archaeal uncharacterised proteins. It is typically between 150 and 160 amino acids in length. It is remotely related to ribonuclease H-like nucleases but it is unlikely to possess any enzymatic activity.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF6934)
description: This is a family of uncharacterised bacterial proteins. They are predicted to adopt an alpha/beta structure consisting of a central mixed beta-sheet packed on both sides with alpha-helices that is reminiscent to the common structural core of N-acetyltransferases (NAT).

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF6935)
description: This is a domain found in uncharacterised bacterial proteins either as standalone or in combination with other domains. It is remotely related to soluble lipid-binding protein MlaC and it is predicted to adopt a similar structure with a typical NTF2-like topology.

name: Enoyl-acyl carrier protein reductase FabMG
description: This entry, previously known as DUF6936, represents FabMG enoyl-acyl carrier protein reductase (ENR) and related proteins. This enzyme is a FabI-type ENR that employs NADH as a coenzyme and mediates resistance to triclosan. FabMG adopts an alpha/beta structure, with a central parallel beta-sheet elaborated with alpha-helices on both sides. FabMG differs from other related ENRs in sequence and structure. These differences, in particular in the substrate-binding loop and pocket regions in which triclosan binds, could be responsible for the triclosan resistance [[cite:PUB00154385]].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF6937)
description: This domain is found N-terminal in a family of uncharacterised bacterial proteins. This domain has a significant sequence similarity to the N-terminal domains of a number of proteins members of UDP-Glycosyltransferase/glycogen phosphorylase superfamily. It is predicted to adopt the same alpha/beta structure.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF6938)
description: This domain is found C-terminal in a family of uncharacterised bacterial proteins. This domain has a significant sequence similarity to the C-terminal domains of a number of proteins members of UDP-Glycosyltransferase/glycogen phosphorylase superfamily. It is predicted to adopt the same alpha/beta structure.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF6939)
description: This is a family of bacterial proteins with unknown function. They share sequence similarity with the N-terminal part of NADAR domain and are predicted to adopt structure that is globally similar to the structure of E.coli protein YbiA, a member of the NADAR domain family.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF6940)
description: This is a family of uncharacterised proteins found in bacteria and eukaryotes. These proteins are probably distantly related to HIT-containing uridylyltransferases and are likely to adopt the same structure.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF6941)
description: This is a family of uncharacterised bacterial proteins. They share sequence similarity to Ig-like domains found in a number of proteins such as xylosyltransferase, alkylpurine DNA glycosylase, cycloisomaltooligosaccharide glucanotransferase and are predicted to adopt the same structure.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF6942)
description: This is a family of uncharacterised bacterial proteins. They are probably distantly related to uracil-DNA glycosylases and other related DNA glycosylases given their predicted structure.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF6943)
description: This is a family of uncharacterised bacterial proteins. They share significant sequence similarity with each of the specificity subunit target recognition domains of type I restriction-modification enzymes and are predicted to adopt the same structure.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF6944)
description: This is a family of uncharacterised proteins found mainly in Gram-positive bacteria. They are predicted to be associated with the membrane and to adopt structure that has topological similarity to the common structural core of Succinate-acetate permease (SatP) superfamily proteins.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF6945)
description: This entry represents a WH-like domain (PDB:4ro3) found at the N-terminal of an uncharacterised protein from Vibrio cholerae ([swissprot:M1RHE3]), whose function is unknown. This domain is also found in phage proteins.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF6946)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised bacterial proteins either standalone or in combination with other domains. It is distantly related to the type II restriction endonucleases with predicted similar active site architecture. These proteins are most likely endonucleases based on the strict conservation of the putative active site residues.

name: DUF3829-like, C-terminal domain
description: This domain is found at the C-terminal end of uncharacterised DUF3829-like proteins. It is often found associated to [pfam:PF20893]. Its function is unknown. It shows four alpha-helices.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF6947)
description: This is a domain found in a group of uncharacterised bacterial sequences whose function is unknown. This domain adopts a galactose-binding-like structure (PDBe:4lr4).

name: DUF5018-related
description: This domain is found in the putative secreted protein BF4250 from Bacteroides fragilis ([swissprot:Q5L7M9]) and similar bacterial functionally uncharacterised proteins. This domain seems to be related to [pfam:PF16410].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF6948)
description: This domain is found either as standalone or in combination with other domains in a group of uncharacterised proteins. It is distantly related to EDC3 mRNA-decapping protein 3 and it could be involved in RNA-binding. It is predicted to adopt a barrel-like structure with a typical Sm-like fold. The pair of glycines responsible for maintaining the Sm-barrel curvature are also conserved in the members of this family.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF6949)
description: This is a family of uncharacterised bacterial proteins. These proteins are enriched with hydrophobic residues and it is quite likely to be associated with the membrane.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF6950)
description: This domain if found in a group of uncharacterised bacterial proteins. It is related to NlpC/P60 domains and it is likely to adopt similar structure as well as to possess an endopeptidase activity. All members of this family contain a conserved cysteine residue that is predicted to occupy equivalent spatial position as in the NlpC/P60 domains.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF6951)
description: This is a family of uncharacterised proteins found in archaea and bacteria. These proteins are predicted to adopt similar structure to the members of SufE/NifU superfamily. They contain three invariant cysteine residues and a fourth semi-conserved residue either cysteine or histidine. These residues are likely to define a potential Zn-binding site similar to the binding site observed in SufU.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF6952)
description: This is a family of uncharacterised bacterial proteins. They contain highly conserved acidic residues and G[S/A]ID motif at the C terminus.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF6953)
description: This is a family of uncharacterised bacterial proteins. They share significant sequence similarity to HTH winged helix domains, in particular to the N-terminal domain of transcriptional regulator BrxR and RNA polymerase III subunit RPC82.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF6954)
description: This is a family of uncharacterised bacterial proteins. They are enriched in hydrophobic residues and are likely associated with the membrane.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF6955)
description: This is a family of small uncharacterised proteins found in bacteria and archaea. They are predicted to adopt an alpha/beta globular structure consisting of a cradle-like beta-sheet and alpha-helices packed on the convex side of the sheet.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF6956)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised bacterial proteins either as standalone or in combination with other domains. It is predicted to adopt an alpha-beta structure with ferredoxin-like topology.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF6957)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised bacterial proteins. It is predicted to fold into a beta-barrel that has some similarity to the replication focus targeting sequence (RFTS) domain of Dnmt1 methyltransferase 1.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF6958)
description: This family is found in uncharacterised bacterial proteins. They share sequence similarity with several HTH winged helix domains, one of which Zinc uptake regulation protein FurB.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF6959)
description: This is a family of uncharacterised bacterial proteins. They contain conserved Pro-Gly-rich motif with a semi- conserved pattern PGRxFPGx3QGD.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF6960)
description: This is a family of uncharacterised bacterial proteins. They are composed of two tandem domains with similarity to SH3 domains, in particular to YorP.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF6961)
description: This is a family of small, about 60 residues in length, bacterial proteins. They are predicted to adopt a globular structure consisting of three helices. The N- and C-terminal helices contain highly conserved aromatic residues in addition to the nearly invariant glycines located at the interhelical connecting loops.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF6962)
description: This is a family of uncharacterised bacterial proteins. They are related to HlyIII family [pfam:PF03006] and are predicted to adopt the same structure consisting of seven transmembrane helices. Their predicted structure, suggests that, similarly to HlyIII, they may contain a Zn-binding site, albeit slightly rearranged as only two of the Zn-coordinating residues are in conserved positions.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF6963)
description: This domain is found N-terminal in uncharacterised bacterial proteins. It is distantly related to class-II glutamine amidotransferase domains [pfam:PF13522].

name: Family of unknown function (DUF6964)
description: This short helical domain is found in a small set of ribosomal S1 proteins. It's function is unknown.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF6965)
description: This entry represents a family of uncharacterised proteins which are predicted to form a small three helical bundle containing a beta hairpin between helices 1 and 2.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF6966)
description: This is a domain found in uncharacterised bacterial proteins that is predicted to be helical. It contains a nearly invariant tryptophan toward the N terminus and a highly conserved motif [F/Y]GGMGSx(2)D toward the C-terminus.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF6967)
description: This family of proteins is found in bacteria. Proteins in this family are approximately 70 amino acids in length. They are predicted to fold into a four-stranded beta-sheet meander and an alpha-helix. One face of this beta-sheet is enriched with conserved positively charged arginine and lysine residues.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF6968)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised bacterial proteins either standalone or C-terminal to HTH winged helix domains. It has a partial sequence similarity to ribosome associated factors that are members of [pfam:PF02482].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF6969)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised proteins from Proteobacteria. It is predicted to adopt an alpha/beta globular structure. It has three highly conserved histidines that are predicted to cluster together in space and are likely involved in metal coordination.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF6970)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised proteins from bacteria and protostome animals. It is predicted to fold into a curved meander beta-sheet. It contains four highly conserved cysteine residues, two of which are predicted to cluster together in space and are likely involved in disulfide bond formation.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF6971)
description: This is a domain of unknown function found at the N-terminal end.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF6972)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised bacterial proteins either standalone or in combination with other domains. It is probably distantly related to the C-terminal domain of CdiA toxin (CdiA-CT), known member of RNase A superfamily.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF6973)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised proteins. It is predicted to adopt a globular structure consisting of five alpha-helices. It is probably distantly related to Wnt domains.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF6974)
description: This entry represents a dimeric alpha/beta barrel domain from an uncultured marine organism (PDB:2op5). The function of this family is unknown.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF6975)
description: This family of uncharacterised proteins is found in Proteobacteria. It shares significant sequence similarity with enzymes members of Heme oxygenase-like superfamily and are predicted to adopt similar structure consisting of a bundle of six alpha-helices.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF6976)
description: This family of uncharacterised proteins is found mainly in Proteobacteria. It is likely to consists of two domains that engage in extensive contacts mainly via hydrophobic residues. The predicted structure of the N-terminal domain has similarity to chorismatases.

name: DarT1-associated NADAR antitoxin
description: This entry, previously known as DUF6977, represents the DarT1-associated NADAR antitoxin and related proteins. The DarT-NADAR system is a TA system catalysing the specific and reversible ADP-ribosylation of guanosine bases in which DarT1-associated NADARs reverse guanine ADP-ribosylation catalysed by DarT1. DarT1-associated NADAR antitoxin adopts an alpha/beta globular structure characterised by an alpha-helical core that forms the active site flanked by two small beta sheet regions, comprising two and three strands [[cite:PUB00154386]]. Its structural core is globally similar to the structure of E.coli protein YbiA, a member of the NADAR domain family.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF6978)
description: This is a family of uncharacterised proteins. They are predicted to adopt a globular alpha/beta structure consisting of a meander beta-sheet and two helices packed on one side on the sheet. These proteins contain three highly conserved histidines that in the predicted structure cluster close in space and could potentially form a metal binding site.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF6979)
description: This is a family of uncharacterised proteins. They are predicted to fold into a globular structure consisting mainly of alpha-helices.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF6980)
description: This is a domain found in uncharacterised bacterial proteins. This domain occurs either standalone or in combination with other domains. It contains conserved cysteines and histidine that may be involved in Zn2+ coordination.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF6981)
description: This entry represents an alpha-lytic protease prodomain-like domain present in a protein of unknown function from Desulfovibrio piger. It structure has been characterized (PDB:4HLB).

name: Family of unknown function (DUF6982)
description: This family of proteins is found in bacteria. Proteins in this family are typically between 135 and 1024 amino acids in length. This family of proteins are structurally related to [pfam:PF03614] a family of transcriptional repressors of phase-1 flagellin genes. The family appears to contain two related subdomains with Sm-like topology.

name: Cyanophage baseplate Pam3 plug gp18
description: This family, previously known as DUF6983, represents Cyanophage baseplate Pam3 plug gp18 and related proteins. Gp18 has structural similarity to a component of the baseplate Complex for Myoviridae Phage XM1. The cyanophage Pam3 has a substantially simpler molecular organisation than the prototypical, contractile-tail bacteriophage T4, but it retains the essential elements required for DNA injection. The baseplate of Pam3 contains six protein components: the trimeric spike gp20, the trimeric hub gp19, the baseplate wedge (six heterotriplexes of gp22-gp23), the plug of six gp18 monomers, and the fibers (12 trimers of gp24) [[cite:PUB00154413]]. The plug gp18 consists of two-layered beta-sheets and a C-terminal alpha-helix, resembling the immunoglobin fold. Each plug monomer is embedded between the two C-terminal helices of the tube initiator, forming a 'plug' to fix the core helical bundle of the wedge onto the hub [[cite:PUB00154413]]

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF6984)
description: This entry represents a bacterial family of unknown function.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF6985)
description: This entry represents a family of bacterial domains of unknown function.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF6986)
description: This entry represents a family of TIM barrel proteins that are most closely related to [pfam:PF03328]. This strongly suggests that these proteins are enzyme with a possibly related function.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF6987)
description: This alpha helical domain is usually found at the C-terminus of proteins containing repeats of [pfam:PF12396].

name: Family of unknown function (DUF6988)
description: This family of uncharacterised proteins is found mainly in Proteobacteria. These proteins are predicted to adopt an alpha-helical structure. They contain a highly conserved RXXXE-motif and an invariant histidine that may have a functional role.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF6989)
description: This domain is found in a number of uncharacterised bacterial proteins that are likely associated with the membrane.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF6990)
description: This family of proteins is found in bacteria. Proteins in this family are typically between 185 and 199 amino acids in length. There are two semi-conserved sequence motifs: HLA and GFVPYI.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF6991)
description: This entry represents a C-terminal domain of a functionally unknown conserved protein from Bacillus anthracis (PDB:4fca).

name: Family of unknown function (DUF6992)
description: This is a family of uncharacterised bacterial proteins. They are enriched with hydrophobic residues and are likely associated with the membrane. These proteins contain two conserved motifs GLDxxYxxxG and FLxxFD.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF6993)
description: This entry represents a bacterial domain of unknown function.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF6994)
description: This is a family of uncharacterised bacterial proteins. They are probably remotely related to His-Me finger endonucleases. The conservation of the putative active site residues in this family is not strict, in particular the position of the catalytic histidine. The residues involved in metal coordination are conserved. The presence in the vicinity of two invariant aspartate residues that point toward the putative active site suggests that these proteins may still function as enzymes but probably via a somewhat different catalytic mechanism. They may still retain their catalytic activity by employing these conserved aspartates that in the predicted AF2 models are well positioned to undertake a role in a potential nucleophilic attack.

name: PolB1 Binding Protein 2
description: This is a family of archaeal proteins, previously known as DUF6995, representing homologues of PolB1 Binding Protein 2 (PBP2). PBP2, is a subunit of PolB1 enzyme that is a member of the archaeal B-family of DNA polymerases. PBP2 along with PBP1, associate with distinct surfaces of the larger catalytic subunit and influence the enzymatic properties of the DNA polymerase [[cite:PUB00154412]]. Members of this family adopt a winged helix (HTH) fold.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF6996)
description: This domain is found N-terminal in a group of uncharacterised proteins. It is remotely related to AbiEi winged helix domain and it is predicted to adopt the same structure.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF6997)
description: This domain is found C-terminal in a group of uncharacterised proteins. It usually follows winged helix domain [pfam:PF22515]. This domain is related to PD-(D/E)XK nucleases and it is predicted to adopt the same structure with similar active site architecture.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF6998)
description: This is a family of uncharacterised bacterial proteins. They share significant sequence similarity with PvuII endonucleases and are predicted to adopt similar structure. The predicted structures, however, do not suggest similarity in the active site architecture.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF6999)
description: This is a family of uncharacterised bacterial proteins. They are predicted to adopt alpha-helical structure. These proteins contain several invariant histidines and aspartates that may have a functional role.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7000)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised bacterial proteins. It is predicted to adopt an alpha/beta structure consisting of a cradle-like beta-sheet with alpha-helices pocked on the convex side of it. It contains a highly conserved GYMDFTYF sequence motif that may be of functional importance.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7001)
description: This is a family of uncharacterised proteins found in Archaea. They have sequence similarity to Zincin-like metalloproteases and are predicted to adopt the same structure. Only one of the two zinc binding sites are conserved suggesting that these proteins may possess different function.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7002)
description: This is a family of uncharacterised bacterial proteins. They share sequence similarity with DarT toxin and are likely to adopt the same structure.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7003)
description: This is a family of uncharacterised bacterial proteins. It is predicted to adopt a globular alpha/beta structure with a central antiparallel beta-sheet and helices packed on it.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7004)
description: This family of proteins is found in bacteria and archaea. Proteins in this family are approximately 160 amino acids in length. They are predicted to adopt globular alpha/beta structure. These proteins contain two highly conserved sequence motifs GxFDxWC and KRxKRLG that may be of functional importance.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7005)
description: This is a family of uncharacterised bacterial proteins. These proteins share partial sequence similarity to the collagenase catalytic core with invariant HExxH motif.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7006)
description: Proteins in this family are found in Firmicutes. They are approximately 120 amino acids in length and are predicted to adopt an alpha helical structure. Members of this family contain two highly conserved acid residues aspartate and glutamate.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7007)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised bacterial proteins. It is predicted to adopt a globular structure consisting of segregated alpha-helices and a five-stranded antiparallel beta-sheet. This domain contains two highly conserved sequence motifs TxxHGG and YEED that may be of a functional importance.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7008)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised bacterial proteins. It contains a number of highly conserved positively charged residues that may have functional role.

name: DUF6293 C-terminal winged helix domain
description: This domain is found C-terminal in functionally uncharacterised archaeal proteins. This domain is predicted to adopt winged helix domain structure. It is usually located upstream [pfam:PF19810] and this domain organisation as well as the predicted structure are reminiscent of CRISPR-associated protein, Csa3.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7009)
description: This is a family of uncharacterised proteins found in bacteria. It is predicted to adopt a globular structure consisting of two nearly orthogonal beta-sheets and two helices that connect them. Toward the C terminus these proteins contain a highly conserved enriched with negatively charged residues region having nearly invariant EKDFxC sequence motif.

name: DUF2089 zinc ribbon
description: This entry represents the zinc ribbon found at the N-terminal of DUF2089, which usually occurs as a fusion of ZnR+HTH+SHOCT-like.

name: Active DUF488-N3 subclade
description: This entry represents a subclade of DUF488 domains with degenerate C-terminal core strand. Sometimes it is observed adjacent to the DUF488-s subclade, suggesting it preserves a catalytic activity comparable to other active DUF488 subclades [[cite:PUB00153826]].

name: Inactive DUF488-N3 subclade
description: This entry represents a subclade of DUF488 domains lacking the catalytic residues common to the rhodanese-phosphatase superfamily. The C-terminal core strand is degenerate in this subclade [[cite:PUB00153826]].

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7010)
description: This entry represents a family of uncharacterised bacterial proteins. They are predicted to adopt alpha-helical structure composed of six up-and-down helices. It is likely that these proteins are associated with the membrane.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF4026) C-terminal
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised bacterial proteins. It is usually associated with [pfam:PF13218] and [pfam:PF10077] that flank this domain from N- and C-terminal ends, respectively. This domain is distantly related to SUFU-like domains.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7011)
description: This domain of unknown function is found in a group of proteins predominantly from proteobacteria. It has a LxHDGK/RRL motif and a highly conserved W residue.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7012)
description: This domain of unknown function is found in a group of proteins mainly from alphaproteobacteria. It is normally found N-terminal to [pfam:PF10074]. It is predicted to adopt a configuration formed mainly by beta-strands.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7013)
description: This is a presumed domain found at the N-terminal of phage sequences, which also have a FN3-like domain ([pfam:PF21470]) at the C-terminal.

name: DUF4796 N-terminal
description: This cysteine-rich domain is functionally uncharacterised and is found in eukaryotes. Proteins with this domain are typically between 194 and 289 amino acids in length. AlphaFold structural models reveal a C-terminal beta-strand, usually located after the DUF4796_C domain ([pfam:PF16044]). This beta-strand (not included in this entry's seed alignment) contributes to the beta-sheet structure within this domain.

name: DUF5817, C-terminal domain
description: This entry represents a helix-turn-helix (HTH) domain found in a group of functionally uncharacterized prokaryotic proteins, typically associated with the Domain of Unknown Function (DUF5817) (Pfam: PF19134).

name: C5orf34-like, second domain
description: This entry represents a domain located C-terminal to [pfam:PF15025] in a family of eukaryotic proteins, including the human uncharacterised protein C5orf34, which has been reported to be correlated with an unfavourable prognosis of patients from a variety of human malignancies [[cite:PUB00154384]]. This domain is predicted to show an alpha-beta structure with high structural similarity to a polo box [[cite:PUB00152793]].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7015)
description: This domain of unknown function is found at the C-terminal of a group of bacterial proteins and, according to structure predictions, it may adopt a beta-barrel structure. It is often associated with an Ig-like domain ([pfam:PF08522]).

name: DUF3097, N-terminal domain
description: This entry represents an N-terminal Tudor-like domain found in DUF3097 proteins. This family of proteins with unknown function appears to be restricted to Actinobacteria.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7016)
description: This entry represents a pair of OB fold domains found in a group of uncharacterised proteins from bacteria which have a [pfam:PF22707] domain at the C-terminal.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7017)
description: This entry represents a domain consisting of TPR repeats found at the N-terminal of of group of uncharacterised sequences predominantly from bacteria, which seem to be related to TOTE conflict systems as they are associated with [pfam:PF22708].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7018)
description: This is a domain of unknown function found at the N-terminal of proteins containing DUF3994 at the C-terminal, in most instances. According to structure predictions, this domain consists of alpha helices suggesting they are the membrane spanning region of of these sequences.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7019)
description: This is a family of uncharacterised proteins found mainly in actinomycetes. Their function is unknown. They are predicted to adopt OB fold with significant similarity to Rpa.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7020)
description: This entry represents a family of phage proteins of unknown function. AlphaFold shows confident dimer interaction.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7021)
description: This entry represents a beta barrel domain which is found associated with [pfam:PF10020].

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7022)
description: This uncharacterised protein is found in the T5 bacteriophage. The function of this protein is unknown.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7023)
description: This domain is found in human Protein dispatched homolog 3 (DISP3) and related proteins mainly from vertebrates. DISP3 (PTCHD2), a sterol-sensing domain- containing protein, is highly expressed in neural tissue, promotes cell proliferation and alters expression of genes that are involved in tumourigenesis. The function of this domain is unknown.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7024)
description: This domain has a structure that resembles the galactose-binding domain. This domain is often associated with a [pfam:PF00884] sulfatase like domain. Suggesting that this domain may be part of an enzyme that modifies some kind of carbohydrate.

name: DUF569 associated ubiquitin-like domain
description: This entry represents a small domain with a ubiquitin like fold that is often associated with [pfam:PF04601]. The function of this domain is not known.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7025)
description: This entry represents an SH3 barrel like domain found in a large family of AAA proteins. The function of these proteins is uncertain.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7026)
description: This entry represents a helical domain found in plant proteins. The function of these proteins is unknown.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7027)
description: This is a domain of unknown function found in a group of uncharacterised proteins mainly found in worms. This is likely a transmembrane segment.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7028)
description: This domain is found in a group of uncharacterised proteins mainly from plants. It is predicted to adopt a globular structure that has significant sequence and structural similarity to MBD domains.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7029)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised proteins mainly from fungi. It is predicted to adopt a globular structure that has some similarity to SRA domain ([pfam:PF18491]). The function of this domain is unknown.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7030)
description: This domain of unknown function is found in Lysine-specific demethylase 3B (KDM3B, also known as JmjC domain-containing histone demethylation protein 2B or JHDM2B) and related proteins. KDM3B is a histone demethylase that specifically demethylates lysine at position 9 of histone H3 [[cite:PUB00153916]]. This enzyme plays a central role in histone code. This domain is predicted to adopt an open beta-barrel with an SH3-like topology.

name: Chitin synthase 4-like domain
description: This domain is found in a group of fungal proteins, including Chitin synthase 4 from Gibberella zeae (CHS4), which plays a role in the polymerisation of chitin [[cite:PUB00155063],[cite:PUB00155061]]. This domain is predicted to adopt a globular structure with similarity to Cytochrome b5-like heme/steroid binding domain ([pfam:PF00173]). Despite this global similarity this domain lacks haem coordinating residues and is probably not involved in haem binding.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7032)
description: This domain is found N-terminal in a group of uncharacterised proteins mainly from plants. This domain is predicted to adopt a globular structure that folds into a four helical bundle and has a significant sequence and structural similarity to MLKL executioner domain ([pfam:PF22215]).

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7033)
description: This uncharacterised domain is found in a group of polysaccharide deacetylases and similar proteins from bacteria. It is predicted to adopt an alpha-helical configuration.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7034)
description: This domain is found in a group of uncharacterised proteins from Dictyostelia. It is predicted to adopt Ig-like fold with the fibronectin type III-like topology.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7035)
description: This domain is found in a group of uncharacterised proteins from Dictyostelia. It is predicted to adopt Ig-like fold with the fibronectin type III-like topology.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7036)
description: This entry represents a predicted ferredoxin-like domain found in a family of uncharacterized plant proteins. This group of proteins typically has this domain duplicated.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7037)
description: This entry represents a small domain found in a family of uncharacterized proteins in nematodes. This domain is predicted to fold as a beta-sheet composed of four anti-parallel beta-strands.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7038)
description: This entry represents a domain found in a family of uncharacterized proteins in nematodes. In some proteins, this domain appears internally duplicated.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7039)
description: This entry represents a domain found in a family of uncharacterised proteins in nematodes.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7040)
description: This entry represents a C-terminal domain found in a family of uncharacterised proteins in nematodes.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7041)
description: This is a domain of unknown function predominantly found at the N-terminal of sequences from ticks, spiders and similar sequences from arthropods. According to structure predictions this domain may adopt a alpha-helical bundle fold similar to Ty3 transposon capsid-like proteins.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7042)
description: This domain is found in a group of uncharacterised metazoan proteins. It is predicted to adopt a globular structure with lipocalin fold. It also contains several highly conserved cysteine residues that are likely involved in the formation of intra-domain disulfide bridges.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7043)
description: This domain is found in a group of uncharacterised metazoan proteins. It is predicted to adopt a globular structure with lipocalin fold. It also contains several highly conserved cysteine residues that are likely involved in the formation of intra-domain disulfide bridges.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7044)
description: This domain is found in a group of uncharacterised metazoan proteins. It is predicted to adopt a globular structure with lipocalin fold. It also contains several highly conserved cysteine residues that are likely involved in the formation of intra-domain disulfide bridges.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7045)
description: This domain is found in a group of uncharacterised metazoan proteins. It is predicted to adopt a globular structure with lipocalin fold. It also contains several highly conserved cysteine residues that are likely involved in the formation of intra-domain disulfide bridges.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7046)
description: This domain is found in a group of uncharacterised plant proteins. These proteins are probably distantly related to the plant-specific actin-binding protein SCAB1 and are predicted to contain a fusion domain composed of Ig and PH-like domains in a similar arrangement as in SCAB1 (([pfam:PF16709]) and ([pfam:PF17684])) [[cite:PUB00076164]]. The domain represented by this entry corresponds to an atypical PH-like domain.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7047)
description: This is a domain of unknown function mostly found in arthropods. This domain may adopt a three helical bundle fold. These sequences might be related to reverse transcriptase polymerases.

name: DUF2096 N-terminal four-helical bundle domain
description: This domain, found in various hypothetical archaeal proteins, has no known function. This N-terminal domain is composed of four alpha helices.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7048)
description: This entry represents a domain found in uncharacterised proteins mainly from Trypanosoma sp. According to structural predictions, this domain is likely to adopt a beta-propeller fold.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7049)
description: This domain is found in a group of uncharacterised proteins mainly from plants. This domain is predicted to fold into a globular structure that adopts a ferredoxin-like fold.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7050)
description: This domain is found N-terminal in a group of uncharacterised proteins mainly from plants. It shares a significant sequence similarity with the N-terminal domain of bHLH-MYC and R2R3-MYB transcription factors ([pfam:PF14215]) and it is predicted to adopt similar structure.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7051)
description: This is a domain of unknown function mostly found in organisms within the Trypanosoma genus. This domain adopt a multiple helical bundle fold.

name: NAD-dependent glutamate dehydrogenase, N-terminal domain
description: This domain is found towards the N terminus of yeast NAD-specific glutamate dehydrogenase (GDH2, also known as DHE2) and similar fungal proteins. GDH2 is involved in the degradation of glutamate to ammonia and alpha-ketoglutarate. This domain is predicted to adopt a globular structure composed of four alpha-helices.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7053)
description: This domain is found in a group of uncharacterised proteins mainly from Fungi. It shares significant sequence similarity with domains members of the Bet v1-like superfamily and it is predicted to adopt similar structure.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7054)
description: This domain is found in the uncharacterized protein At4g22758 from Arabidopsis thaliana and related proteins. It shares significant sequence similarity with CRIM domain and it is predicted to adopt a similar structure with ubiquitin-like topology.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7055)
description: This is a presumed domain found in a group of uncharacterised sequences from bacteria. According to structure predictions, this domain is found at the C-terminal and may adopt an all-beta structure consisting of eight anti-parallel beta-sheets.. These proteins also have a glycosyltransferase domain at the N-terminal ([pfam:PF13231]).

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7056)
description: This is a presumed domain found in a group of uncharacterised sequences from bacteria. According to structure predictions, this domain is found towards the C-terminal, after a glycosyltransferase domain ([pfam:PF13231]), and it may adopt an alpha/beta structure. In some instances, this domain is followed by and all-beta domain at the very C-terminal of the sequences ([pfam:PF23157]). The function of this domain is unknown.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7057)
description: This is a presumed domain found at the C-terminal of sequences from Gammaproteobacteria. According to structure predictions it may have an alpha/beta fold.

name: CUL7/CUL9, N-terminal beta-barrel domain
description: This domain is found N-terminal in the homologues of human Cullin-7 (CUL7) and Cullin-9 (CUL9). It adopts a beta-barrel structure with some similarity to chromodomains and is known as a small beta-domain (SBD) [[cite:PUB00156050],[cite:PUB00155195]]. In both CUL7 and CUL9, this domain is usually followed by an ARM-like domain.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7059)
description: This domain is found N-terminal in a group of uncharacterised bacterial proteins. These proteins are probably distantly related to Aeronamide N-methyltransferases AerE. They share two similar domains that are predicted in the same arrangement. This domain is found N-terminal to the methyltransferase domain and has a weak sequence similarity to various HTH domains.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7060)
description: This entry represents a domain found at the C-terminal of a group of proteins from nematodes, members of the BPI/LBP/Plunc family of proteins which share homology with cholesterol ester transfer protein (CETP) and phospholipid transfer protein (PLTP). The exact function of these proteins is unknown, however, according to their structure predictions and homology to CEPT/PLTP, they may play a role in lipid binding.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7061)
description: This entry represents a domain found towards the N-terminal of a group of proteins from nematodes such as Trichuris suis and Trichinella britovi, members of the BPI/LBP/Plunc family of proteins which share homology with cholesterol ester transfer protein (CETP) and phospholipid transfer protein (PLTP). The exact function of these proteins is unknown, however, according to their structure predictions and homology to CEPT/PLTP, they may be involved in lipid binding.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7062)
description: This domain is found in a group of uncharacterised proteins from digenean species.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7063)
description: This is a SH2 domain found mainly in nematodes such as Trichuris trichura, Toxocara canis and Trichinella sp. The function of this domain is unknown.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7064)
description: This entry represents a region of unknown function found in proteins from fungi and bacteria. This region is composed of a pair of two flattened, orthogonally packed, beta-barrels that share significant global similarity to members of the AttH-like superfamily. It is likely that this region possesses enzymatic activity.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7066)
description: This is a beta-beta-alpha zinc finger found in a group of uncharacterised sequences, mainly from fungi.

name: Alpha-glucan water dikinase, DUF7067
description: This domain is found in two tandem copies in the Alpha-glucan water dikinase (GWD1 and GWD2) from Arabidopsis thaliana and related proteins. It is predicted to adopt a globular structure consisting of three helical bundle. GWD1 is involved in the incorporation of phosphate into starch-like alpha-glucan, mostly at the C-6 position of glucose units [[cite:PUB00153995]]. This enzyme acts as regulator of starch mobilization by controlling the phosphate content of starch. The function of the domain represented in this entry is unknown.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7068)
description: This domain is found C-terminal to the NTPase domain [pfam:PF05729] in a group of fungal proteins, including [swissprot:U7Q5X2] from Sporothrix schenckii. It is predicted to adopt an alpha-helical configuration.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7069)
description: This domain of unknown function is found in a fro up of fungal proteins. It is often N-terminal to several copies of ankyrin repeats. It is predicted to adopt an alpha-helical configuration.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7070)
description: This domain is found in a group of uncharacterised proteins mainly from actinopterygians that are distantly related and share overall similar domain organisation to the human NEDD4-binding protein 1 (N4BP1). This domain shares a weak sequence similarity to known UBA domains and it is predicted to fold into a typical three helical bundle.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7071)
description: This domain is found C-terminal in a group of uncharacterised proteins mainly from fungi. It is predicted to adopt a globular structure consisting of two alpha-helical repeats.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7072)
description: This domain is found in a group of uncharacterised proteins mainly from Fungi. It shares a weak sequence similarity to the C-terminal domain of the Escherichia Coli ProQ RNA binding protein ([pfam:PF17516]) and it is predicted to adopt a similar structure with SH3-like topology.
