name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7073)
description: This domain is found in Histone-lysine N-methyltransferase, H3 lysine-4 specific from Plasmodium falciparum ([swissprot:W4J2P1]) and similar sequences from alveolates. In some proteins this domain is found associated with [pfam:PF00628]. It shows a conserved motif LLxxYKxKI/LxDLL.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7074)
description: This domain is found in a group of uncharacterised plant proteins. It is predicted to adopt a globular structure with a Cystatin-like topology consisting of a curved four-stranded beta-sheet and an alpha-helix packed on the concave side of it.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7075)
description: This domain is found in a group of uncharacterised plant proteins. It shares a significant sequence similarity with members of the GDP-fucose protein O-fucosyltransferase family ([pfam:PF10250]) and it is predicted to adopt similar structure.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7076)
description: This domain is found in a group of uncharacterised proteins mainly from fungi. It shares a significant sequence similarity of Ig-like domains found in Trs120 and it is predicted to adopt a structure with a similar topology.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7077)
description: This domain is found in a group of uncharacterised proteins mainly from fungi. It shares a weak sequence similarity with the Ig-like domains found in Trs130, particularly the second Ig-like domain, and it is predicted to adopt a structure with a similar topology.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7078)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised proteins mainly from fungi. This domain is predicted to adopt a globular structure consisting of a four helical bundle and having structural similarity to the alpha-helical domain inserted in the third Ig domain of the Trs130 component of the TRAPPII complex [[cite:PUB00153720]].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7079)
description: This is a presumed domain found in a set of bacterial sequences, whose function is unknown.

name: Highly reducing polyketide synthase sdgA, C-terminal ACP domain
description: This domain is found at the C-terminal of Highly reducing polyketide synthase sdgA from Emericella nidulans and related proteins. SdgA is part of the gene cluster that mediates the biosynthesis of the polyenes aspernidgulenes [[cite:PUB00155054]]. This domain is predicted to adopt an all alpha-helical structure.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7081)
description: This presumed domain is found in a group of plant sequences related to Oberon-like proteins. According to structure predictions this domain may consist of mainly three beta-sheets and two alpha-helices.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7082)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised proteins mainly from Fungi. This domain is predicted to adopt a globular structure consisting of a curved beta-sheet and alpha- helices packed on it. This domain is probably distantly related to the N-terminal domain of STE-like transcription factors ([pfam:PF02200]) based on the similarity of their predicted structures. The predicted structure of this domain has a partial similarity to pseudo Winged helix domains.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7083)
description: This is a presumed domain found at the N-terminal of the uncharacterised protein K02A2.6 from C.elegans and similar worm sequences. This domain may adopt a fold similar to retrotransposons.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7084)
description: This domain is found in a group of uncharacterised proteins mainly from Arthropods. This is a relatively small domain that is predicted to contain mainly alpha-helices.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7085)
description: This domain is found in a group of uncharacterised proteins from flatworms. It is predicted to adopt a PH-like fold with similarity to the PH-like domain found in Shulin and Spt16.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7086)
description: This domain is found in a group of uncharacterised plant proteins. It is predicted to adopt a globular structure consisting of a rubredoxin-like zinc finger capped with an elaborated alpha-helical subdomain. This arrangement is similar to the zinc finger domain found in hypA ([pfam:PF01155]).

name: Integral membrane domain of unknown function (DUF7087)
description: This entry represents a four helical integral membrane domain found in nematode species. The function of this domain is unknown.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7088)
description: This domain is found at the N-terminal of a group of poorly characterised bacterial sequences. The function of this domain is unknown.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7089)
description: This entry represents a family of uncharacterised proteins from halobacteria. Members are predicted to adopt an alpha-beta configuration.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7090)
description: This entry represents a family of proteins from halobacteria. Members of this family, often annotated as ATPases, are predicted to show a central beta-sheet with alpha-helices in both sides.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7091)
description: This family represents a group of proteins from halobacteria. It has a conserved motif VCRRH/YAE and conserved R, Y and W residues. Members are predicted to show an alpha-beta configuration.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7092)
description: This domain represents a small beta barrel domain that is found at the N-terminus of some bacterial peptidase M48 proteins. It has a PH-domain like structure. It likely acts as a chaperone for membrane protein complexes. May interact with [pfam:PF05987] members based on AlphaFold predictions.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7093)
description: This family represents a group of proteins from halobacteria. It shows two conserved motifs WP and several conserved D and R residues. Members are predicted to show beta-sheets at the N- and C-terminal ends.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7094)
description: This domain is found in a group of proteins from halobacteria. It shows several Y and Q conserved residues and is predicted to show an antiparallel beta-sheet and an alpha-helix.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7095)
description: This family represents a group of proteins from halobacteria. They show several highly conserved motifs PVPV, LGL/MDP, AxWA, and PV/IHLEVC. Many members are annotated as nucleotidyltransferases.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7096)
description: This domain is found at the N-terminal end of a group of proteins from eubacteria. It is predicted to show a mainly alpha-configuration. This entry is found associated with [pfam:PF23375] and [pfam:PF23374]

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7097)
description: This protein family includes a group of proteins from halobacteria. It shows several conserved motifs DCPH, RGCL and RPLL/VEEHHLSxY. Members are predicted to show an alpha-beta configuration.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7098)
description: This family represents a group of proteins from halobacteria. It has several conserved motifs WHGP, QLWC and RxYxP. It is predicted to adopt a predominantly beta structure with a short alpha-helix.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7099)
description: This is a beta-propeller domain found in a group on uncharacterised proteins from fungi. The function of this domain is unknown.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7100)
description: This is an alpha-helical domain found at the N-terminal of a group of uncharacterised proteins from fungi. The function of this domain is unknown. Members of this entry also have a beta-propeller at the C-terminal ([pfam:PF23388]).

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7101)
description: This is a domain found in a group on uncharacterised proteins from fungi. The function of this domain is unknown. According to structural predictions, this domain likely adopts an alpha-beta-beta-beta-beta-alpha fold. This domain is usually found associated with an alpha-helical domain at the N-terminal ([pfam:PF23391]) and a beta-propeller at the C-terminal ([pfam:PF23388]).

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7102)
description: This domain has a restriction endonuclease-like fold. The function of these proteins is unknown. Some members of the family are annotated as nucleoporins.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7103)
description: This is a family of unknown function. It is structurally similar to Frag1-like domain, composed of a six-alpha-helix bundle transmembrane region [[cite:PUB00155610]].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7104)
description: This entry includes uncharacterised fungal sequences which consist of repeats that may adopt an alpha-solenoid structure related to ankirin repeats. The overall arrangement of these repeats may have a horseshoe conformation similar to that in leucine-rich repeats.

name: FAZ1, conserved domain
description: This entry represents a conserved repeated domain found twice in FAZ1 from Trypanosoma brucei and similar sequences from trypanosomatids [[cite:PUB00155625]]. This domain is found near the central region and at the very C-terminal of FAZ1. At least 50% of the T. cruzi genome is repetitive sequence, consisting mostly of large gene families of surface proteins, retrotransposons, and subtelomeric repeats [[cite:PUB00155626]].

name: FAZ1, C-terminal
description: The entry represents a repeats-containing region found at the C-terminal of FAZ1 from Trypanosoma brucei brucei and related proteins from typanosomatids. FAZ1 is a component of FAZ filament that is required for correct FAZ assembly and attachment [[cite:PUB00155625]]. These repeats consist of 36x14aa repeats in T.brucei and T.cruzi while in the Leishmania major LmjF34.0690 orthologue there are 70x14aa repeats [[cite:PUB00155625]].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7107)
description: This entry represents a family of uncharacterised domains that show similarities to members of the colipase superfamily/

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7108)
description: This domain is found at the N-terminal end of the uncharacterised protein HVO_0731 from Haloferax volcanii ([swissprot:D4GTA0]) and similar proteins from halobacteria. It has several conserved motifs RLTR/KLxR and LVxHPxEW. It is predicted to adopt an alpha-beta structure. The function of this domain is unknown.

name: DUF7108, C-terminal domain
description: This domain is found at the C-terminal end of the uncharacterised protein HVO_0731 from Haloferax volcanii ([swissprot:D4GTA0]) and similar proteins from halobacteria. It is predicted to adopt an all-alpha structure. The function of this domain is unknown.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7109)
description: This family represents a group of proteins from halobacteria. It has several conserved motifs LAGV/IVDLFG, DxPHI and LxDVxYD/ExExW and five highly conserved R residues. Members are predicted to show a mainly alpha-helical structure with a small beta-sheet.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7110)
description: This family represents a group of proteins from halobacteria. Members are predicted to show an alpha-beta configuration.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7111)
description: This family represents a group of proteins from halobacteria. It has several conserved motifs AxYxET, ERxL/VxF and GYAMLK/RVR. Members are predicted to show a beta-sheet and an alpha-helix.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7112)
description: This family represents a group of proteins from halobacteria. It has several conserved R, D W and Y residues. Members are predicted to show a mainly beta configuration.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7113)
description: This family represents a group of proteins from halobacteria. It has several conserved motifs YVWVCD, RGF and RTQFxR. Members are predicted to show an alpha-beta configuration.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7114)
description: This family represents a group of proteins from halobacteria. It has several conserved motifs GVQLIYEGLR, EPW and GR/K/QxQT/S. Members are predicted to show an all-alpha configuration.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7115)
description: This domain is found at the N-terminal of HVO_2519 from Haloferax volcanii ([swissprot:D4GTV1]) and similar proteins mainly found in halobacteria. It has several conserved motifs RTxxYR, Y/FxHxxxR an RRK. It is predicted to show an alpha-beta configuration.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7116)
description: This family represents a group of proteins from halobacteria. It has several conserved motifs LGY, AERK/EWK/R, RCFV and YxWA. Members are predicted to show an alpha-beta configuration.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7117)
description: This family represents a group of proteins from halobacteria. It has several conserved motifs WSYY, RxYxR and HxK/RR. Members are predicted to show a predominantly alpha configuration.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7118)
description: This family represents a group of proteins from halobacteria. Members are predicted to adopt an all-alpha structure.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7119)
description: This domain is found in a group of uncharacterised proteins mainly from archaea. It is predicted to adopt an all-helical configuration.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7120)
description: This family represents a group of proteins from halobacteria. Members are predicted to adopt an alpha-helical configuration. This family belongs to the ribbon-helix-helix clan.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7121)
description: This family represents a group of proteins mainly from halobacteria. Members are predicted to show an alpha-helical configuration forming an intramolecular coiled-coil structure.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7122)
description: This domain is found in a group of proteins from halobacteria. Members are predicted to show an alpha-beta configuration.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7123)
description: This domain is found in a group of proteins mainly from halobacteria. It is predicted to show an HTH fold.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7124)
description: This domain is found in a group of proteins from halobacteria. It has several W and R conserved residues. This domain is predicted to show an alpha-beta configuration.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7125)
description: This family represents a group of proteins from halobacteria. Members are predicted to show an alpha-beta configuration with similarity to the KaiC domain ([pfam:PF06745]).

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7126)
description: This family represents a group of proteins from halobacteria. Members are predicted to show an alpha-beta configuration with similarity to the Rossmann fold of the TrkA-N domain ([pfam:PF02254]).

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7127)
description: This family represents a group of proteins from halobacteria. Members adopt a beta configuration with high similarity to the CS domain ([pfam:PF04969]).

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7128)
description: This domain is found in a group of small proteins mainly from Halobacteria. It contains highly conserved cysteine and histidine residues arranged in two CxxC and HxxC motifs that likely coordinate zinc. This domain is predicted to adopt a fold similar to the classical C2H2 and variant C2HC zinc fingers containing beta-hairpin and an alpha helix. In addition, it is predicted to contain an extra N-terminal strand that contributes to the formation of a three-stranded antiparallel beta-sheet. This domain also has a number of highly conserved negatively charged residues.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7129)
description: This domain is found in a group of small proteins mainly from Halobacteria. It contains highly conserved cysteine residues arranged in two CxxC motifs that likely coordinate zinc. The first motif could be more broadly defined as YECxxCG. This domain is predicted to adopt zinc ribbon fold.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7130)
description: This domain is found in a group of uncharacterised proteins mainly from Halobacteria. It contains highly conserved cysteine residues arranged in two CxxC motifs that likely coordinate zinc. The first motif could be more broadly defined as a semi-conserved MWRCxxCGEM sequence motif. This domain is predicted to adopt a zinc ribbon fold with similarity to rubredoxin-like domains.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7131)
description: This entry is a domain of unknown function found in some PA-PLA1 family members, which consists of mitochondrial proteins that are probable phospholipases with a specific function to hydrolyze phosphatidic acid. Members of this family are involved in the metabolism of phospholipids, which are critical components of cell membranes. By hydrolyzing phosphatidic acid, these enzymes may play a role in the regulation of mitochondrial membrane composition and dynamics, as well as in signaling pathways related to lipid metabolism.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7132)
description: This entry represents a small family from archaebacteria based on protein PF1546. AlphaFold models show that a dimer of this protein forms a flattened 10 stranded beta barrel structure.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7133)
description: This domain is found in a number of uncharacterised bacterial proteins. It is predicted to form a a six-bladed beta-propeller with significant similarity to glucose/sorbosone dehydrogenases.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7134)
description: This domain is composed of 6 transmembrane alpha helices and is found at the N-terminus of a large family of bacterial signalling proteins. It is structurally related to the N-terminus of the DesK protein. That region is believed to be involved in sensing membrane fluidity.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF1512) C-terminal
description: This family consists of several archaeal proteins of around 370 residues in length. This entry corresponds to the C-terminal domain. The function of this family is unknown. This domain shows structural similarity to peptidyl tRNA hydrolase enzymes.

name: DUF6688 C-terminal domain
description: This family of proteins is functionally uncharacterised. This family of proteins is found in bacteria. Proteins in this family are typically between 360 and 412 amino acids in length. This entry corresponds to the alpha-helical C-terminal domain.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7135)
description: This domain of unknown function is found N-terminal in a group of uncharacterised proteins mainly from plants. This domain is predicted to adopt a beta-barrel with topology typical for PH domains. It has a weak sequence similarity to Dcp1 PH domain.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7136)
description: This domain is found in a group of uncharacterised proteins mainly from Fungi. It is predicted to fold into a beta-sandwich with Ig-like topology.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7137)
description: This domain is found in a group of uncharacterised proteins mainly from Fungi. It is predicted to adopt a beta-sandwich with Ig-like topology and is likely distantly related to the delta subunit of translocon-associated protein (TRAP-delta, [pfam:PF05404]).

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7138)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised proteins mainly from plants. It has sequence similarity to PB1 domain and it is predicted to adopt similar structure with typical ubiquitin-like topology.

name: Cell division protein A, N-terminal domain
description: This entry represents the N-terminal domain of CdpA (Cell division protein A, HVO_0739) from Haloferax volcanii and similar archaeal proteins. CdpA is a ring assembly and anchor protein. It forms part of an anchor complex linked to FtsZ2 and other cell division proteins [[cite:PUB00161026]]. This domain, which is predicted to show four transmembrane helices, possibly together with the linker region of CdpA, are important for CdpA midcell localisation, FtsZ1 ring condensation, and FtsZ2 ring assembly and positioning [[cite:PUB00161026]]. In CdpA and other members of this group, this domain is found associated with [pfam:PF23601]. In some other members these domains are associated with repeats of [pfam:PF07411]. AlphaFold predicts a confident dimeric structure for this domain.

name: Cell division protein A, C-terminal domain
description: This entry represents a likely zinc-binding domain found at the C-terminus of a set of archaebacterial proteins, including CdpA (Cell division protein A, HVO_0739) from Haloferax volcanii, a a ring assembly and anchor protein that forms part of an anchor complex linked to FtsZ2 and other cell division proteins. This domain plays a significant role in cell division but its specific function is currently unknown [[cite:PUB00161026]]. AlphaFold prediction show a structure forming 2-3 beta strands.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7141)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised proteins mainly from Fungi. These proteins are likely involved in chromatin remodelling. The domain represented by this entry is predicted to fold into a globular structure with significant similarity to chromo domain ([pfam:PF00385]).

name: Putative E3 ubiquitin-protein ligase LIN, ARM-like domain
description: This entry represents a domain found in E3 ubiquitin-protein ligase LIN, a putative E3 ubiquitin ligase involved in the rhizobial infection process [[cite:PUB00156036]]. It plays an important role in the early steps of bacterial symbiont thread formation in roots, and in growth, differentiation and maintenance of nodules [[cite:PUB00156036],[cite:PUB00156035]]. This domain may adopt an ARM-repeat fold.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7143)
description: This domain is found in a group of uncharacterised fungal proteins. It is predicted to adopt a globular alpha-helical structure.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7144)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised bacterial proteins. It is predicted to fold into a four-helical up-and-down bundle and it is likely transmembrane.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7145)
description: This entry represents a domain of unknown function found in Trichuris sp., Trichinella sp. and similar sequences from nematodes. This domain is repeated in some sequences from Trichuris spp. (two to four times) and it may adopt a SH2-like fold.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7146)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised bacterial proteins. It has significant sequence similarity to the alpha+beta domain found in DNA primases and it is predicted to adopt similar structure.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7147)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised bacterial proteins. It is predicted to fold into an alpha/beta globular structure with topology similar to NADH-quinone oxidoreductase subunit 16.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7148)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised plant proteins. It is predicted to fold into an alpha/beta structure that is topologically similar to BRSK1/2 KA1 domain ([pfam:PF21122]).

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7149)
description: This domain is found in related bacterial proteins. It is predicted to adopt an alpha/beta globular structure and shares significant sequence and structural similarity to members of PD-(D/E)XK nuclease superfamily, in particular, BpuSI N-terminal nuclease domain ([pfam:PF15516]).

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7151)
description: This entry represents a domain of unknown function found in bacterial proteins. Some of the members of this family might contain an EF-hand calcium binding site. The predicted structure of this domain consists of three beta sheets.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7152)
description: This domain is found in plant proteins that are probably related to NOMO family of proteins. The latter are components of the multi-pass translocon (MPT) complex which mediates insertion of multi-pass membrane proteins into the lipid bilayer of membranes [[cite:PUB00155613]]. The domain represented by this entry is predicted to adopt a globular beta-sandwich structure with a prealbumin-like topology.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7153)
description: This domain is found in Caenorhabditis elegans uncharacterized protein C01C4.2 and related proteins. It is predicted to adopt an alpha+beta barrel with some similarity to the dimeric alpha+beta barrel structures, in particular REDY-like protein Hapk ([pfam:PF11639]).

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7154)
description: This domain is found in the Caenorhabditis elegans uncharacterised protein Clec-72 and related eukaryotic proteins. It is predicted to adopt a globular structure with similarity to Galactose-binding domains.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7155)
description: This protein family includes a group of uncharacterised short sequences from actinobacteria, including the predicted secreted protein [swissprot:K5BB12] from Mycolicibacterium hassiacum [[cite:PUB00155614]].

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7156)
description: This protein family includes a group of uncharacterised short sequences from actinobacteria [[cite:PUB00155614]].

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7157)
description: This domain is found at the C-terminal end of a group of uncharacterised sequences from actinobacteria.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7158)
description: This domain is found at the N-terminal end of a group of uncharacterised sequences from actinobacteria.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7159)
description: This domain is found at the C-terminal end of a group of uncharacterised sequences from actinobacteria. It is normally found associated with [pfam:PF23715].

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7160)
description: This protein family includes a group of uncharacterised short sequences from actinobacteria.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7161)
description: This protein family includes a group of uncharacterised short sequences from actinobacteria. Many members are annotated as UbiD family decarboxylases. They are predicted to adopt an all beta configuration.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7162)
description: This protein family includes a group of uncharacterised short sequences from actinobacteria. Some members are annotated as ESX-1 secretion-associated proteins. They are predicted to adopt a mainly alpha-helical configuration.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7163)
description: This domain is found N-terminal in a group of uncharacterised proteins from Trypanosomes. It has a very weak similarity to the vWA-like domain of the SSL1 subunit of general transcription and DNA repair factor IIH and it is predicted to adopt a structure with similarity to known vWA-like domains.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7164)
description: This domain is found either standalone or in tandem in uncharacterised eukaryotic proteins. It has a weak sequence similarity to Nucleotide-diphospho-sugar transferases, in particular to Glycolipid 2-alpha-mannosyltransferases ([pfam:PF01793]) and is predicted to adopt similar structure.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7165)
description: This entry represents a domain of unknown function found towards the N-terminal of fungal proteins. This domain adopts a beta-propeller like fold and may be found in association with an N-terminal F-box motif.

name: TscA antitoxin
description: This protein domain is found in a variety of staphylococcus phage proteins. It was shown to be the antitoxin TscA of a toxin-antitoxin system [[cite:PUB00159162]], with TscT being the toxin [pfam:PF07342]. It is composed of two alpha helices and a beta hairpin and shows weak structural similarity to archaeal prefoldins. Members of this family form a confident homodimer structure with AlphaFold 3 (A0A0H3JR29 iPTM=0.81).

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7167)
description: This small phage protein forms a predicted strand swapped dimer using AlphaFold. It is composed of three beta strands and two alpha helices.There is also some weaker evidence for a tetramer. The function of these proteins is unknown.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7168)
description: This entry represents a protein domain found in phage proteins that usually contain an N-terminal [pfam:PF10979]. The function of these protein is unknown.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7169)
description: This domain family consists of a group of uncharacterized proteins, typically between 99 to 116 amino acids in length, found in bacteriophages that infect Microbacterium and Arthrobacter bacterial hosts. These proteins are encoded in the genomes of phages belonging to the Caudoviricetes class, primarily within the families Azeevirinae, Dismasvirus, Yangvirus, Manhattanvirus, Liebevirus, Zetavirus, and Armstrongvirus. An AlphaFold prediction shows these proteins are composed of two alpha helices. AlphaFold also predicts that these proteins likely form homodimers.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF7170)
description: The DUF7170 domain family consists of several uncharacterized phage proteins of around 50 amino acids in length. The family is found in a variety of phages that infect bacterial hosts such as Escherichia, Salmonella, Klebsiella, Vibrio, Citrobacter, Shigella, Pseudomonas and Aeromonas. A few longer proteins of around 60-90 amino acids are also included.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF7171)
description: This entry represents a domain of unknown function found in bacterial and phage proteins, particularly in Gordonia phages. The domain is approximately 140 amino acids in length. It contains regions of disorder at the N- and C-termini.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7172)
description: This entry represents a domain found in proteins typically around 200 amino acids in length. It is found in phage that infect Mycobacteria, Gordonia, and Nocardia. The exact function is unknown. The structure of the domain shows an extended beta sandwich fold where one sheet is hinged in the middle to form a kink.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7173)
description: This family contains a set of uncharacterized proteins found predominantly in viruses, particularly bacteriophages. The proteins are typically 130-150 amino acids in length. AlphaFold models of this family show some weak partial structural similarity to the Recombination-associated protein RdgC.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7174)
description: This protein is found in caudoviruses, which are tailed bacteriophages. The protein is typically around 150-180 amino acids in length. Its function is currently unknown. It is found in viruses from the Drexlerviridae family, including Rogunavirinae, Braunvirinae, Tempevirinae, and Kyungwonvirus genera.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7175)
description: This entry represents an uncharacterized protein family found in various phages infecting Gram-negative bacterial hosts, including Salmonella, Shigella, Erwinia, Aeromonas, Vibrio and Klebsiella phages. The family typically contains proteins between 80-120 amino acids in length. The function of this protein family is currently unknown.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7176)
description: This family consists of short bacterial phage proteins, typically around 90 amino acids in length, that contain two transmembrane helices. The family is found in phages that infect Enterobacteria.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7177)
description: The domain is around 80 amino acids in length. It occurs in phage that infect a variety of bacteria including Escherichia, Salmonella, Shigella, Klebsiella, Vibrio, Pantoea, Pectobacterium, Yersinia and Serratia.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7178)
description: This entry describes a family of identified in phage metagenomic datasets. The family contains proteins from a variety of phages that infect actinobacteria, particularly Mycobacterium, Gordonia, and Streptomyces. The exact specificity and function of this metagenomic family is currently unknown. Some members are described as N-glycosylases but the source of that information is uncertain.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7179)
description: This entry represents an uncharacterized protein domain found in phage, predominantly those infecting bacteria in the Enterobacteriaceae family such as Escherichia, Salmonella, Klebsiella and Vibrio. The protein is typically around 80 to 100 amino acids in length. In some phage the protein contains a predicted central coiled-coil region. The function of this protein family is currently unknown.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7180)
description: This entry represents an uncharacterized protein that is found in a variety of phage, predominantly infecting bacteria from the Enterobacteriaceae family such as Escherichia and Salmonella. The protein is typically between 75-120 amino acids in length. These proteins have a highly conserved N-terminus.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7181)
description: This entry represents an uncharacterized protein domain found in bacteriophage proteins, particularly those infecting Salmonella and Dickeya species. The domain is approximately 150 residues in length. The function of this domain is currently unknown.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7182)
description: This entry represents an uncharacterized protein found in various mycobacteriophages. The protein contains a predicted transmembrane helix and is typically around 60 amino acids in length. Its function is unknown.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7183)
description: This entry represents an uncharacterized protein domain found in various mycobacteriophages. The domain averages around 150 amino acids in length. It is found as a single domain in the phage proteins. The function of this domain is currently unknown. One protein in this family [swissprot:G8I4J4] contains an N-terminal associated domain [pfam:PF18909].

name: Anti-DarT factor A
description: This entry represents a family of phage proteins including Anti-DarT factor A from Enterobacteria phage RB69 (AdfA), which plays a role in counteracting the host DarT defense system [[cite:PUB00156038]].

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7185)
description: This entry represents an uncharacterized protein found in various mycobacteriophages. The protein is typically around 80 to 100 amino acids in length. It is found in phages belonging to cluster B, such as the Bclasvirinae and Coopervirus genera. The function of this protein is currently unknown.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7186)
description: This entry represents a small transmembrane protein found in Lactococcus 936-type phages. The function of this protein is unknown. It contains a single transmembrane helix.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7187)
description: This entry represents a family of small proteins of around 60 residues found in Omarvirus and related bacteriophages that infect Streptomyces species. The function of this protein family is currently unknown. Homologous proteins are also found in a small number of Streptomyces genomes. The AlphaFold model of A0A7G7BJ30 shows a pair of alpha helices at the C-terminus of the protein.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7188)
description: This entry represents an uncharacterized protein of around 185-188 amino acids found in phages that infect Cutibacterium and Propionibacterium species. The function of this protein is currently unknown.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7189)
description: This entry represents an uncharacterized protein of approximately 60-70 amino acids that is found in various phages, predominantly phages that infect members of the Enterobacteriaceae family such as Escherichia, Shigella, and Klebsiella.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7190)
description: This entry represents a putative membrane protein found in several mycobacteriophages, especially those belonging to the genus Cheoctovirus. The function is unknown. Most members contain a predicted transmembrane helix near the N-terminus. The family shows some length variation, especially at the C-terminus.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7191)
description: This family of uncharacterized proteins is found in viruses, primarily cyanophages that infect cyanobacteria such as Synechococcus and Prochlorococcus species. The family contains short sequences, generally between 45-50 amino acid residues in length. No functional information is available for members of this family.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7192)
description: This entry represents a bacterial domain of unknown function. The domain is around 270 to 300 amino acids in length. It is found in a variety of bacterial phyla including Actinobacteria, Bacteroidota, Pseudomonadota and Verrucomicrobiota. The domain is also found in some bacterial phages. The function of this domain is unknown. The structure of this domain shows similarity to VWFA domains.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7193)
description: This entry represents a family of viral proteins that are found in various bacteriophages infecting Gram-negative bacteria, such as Pseudomonas, Vibrio, Erwinia, Ralstonia, and Klebsiella. The family members are typically 800-1200 residues in length. Many are annotated as putative virion structural proteins, suggesting they may play a role in phage particle structure or assembly. However, the precise function of this family remains unknown.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7194)
description: This entry represents an uncharacterized protein family found in viruses from the order Caudoviricetes. The family contains proteins between 199 and 219 amino acids in length. The function of this family is currently unknown.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7195)
description: This entry represents a family of uncharacterized bacteriophage proteins, typically around 70-80 amino acids in length. They are found in phages infecting Escherichia, Pseudomonas, Salmonella, Vibrio, and other bacterial hosts.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7196)
description: This entry represents an uncharacterized protein domain found in viruses and bacteria, including Mycobacteriophages, Nocardia, Streptomyces and Rhodococcus species. The domain is typically between 50-99 amino acids in length. In some proteins, the domain is found at the C-terminus. AlphaFold prediction shows a small domain composed of three beta strands in a sheet with a single alpha helix between strands 2 and 3.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7197)
description: This entry represents a domain of unknown function. It is typically between 120 and 250 amino acids in length.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7198)
description: This entry represents a family of putative phage membrane proteins. It is characterized by a single transmembrane helix at the N-terminus that likely serves to anchor these proteins to the membrane. The exact functions of the proteins containing this domain remain unknown.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7199)
description: This family consists of several mycobacteriophage putative membrane proteins of around 99 amino acids in length. These proteins are characterized by an N-terminal transmembrane helix, a small central putative zinc binding domain containing 2 conserved cysteine and 2 histidine residues and disordered C-terminal region rich in basic and acidic residues.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7200)
description: This entry represents an uncharacterized protein found in various phages that infect bacteria including Escherichia, Salmonella, Shigella, Klebsiella, Enterobacter, Citrobacter and Cronobacter. The protein ranges in length from around 66 to 98 amino acids. The protein forms a single compact domain composed of a four stranded beta sheet and two alpha helices. The structure shows some weak structural similarity to the BRICHOS domain. No clear function is known for these proteins.

name: Coiled-coil region of unknown function (DUF7201)
description: This entry represents a family of phage proteins found to be associated with membranes, based on transmembrane region predictions. They are typically around 110 amino acids in length with a C-terminal membrane helix. Many also contain predicted coiled-coil region spanning the rest of the protein. The specific function is unknown. However, it could play a role in membrane fusion.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7202)
description: This entry describes a domain of unknown function (DUF). It is found in phage proteins, generally around 70 amino acids in length. The domain is found in a variety of phages infecting hosts such as Escherichia, Shigella, Yersinia, Erwinia, Providencia, and Pectobacterium. No functional information is known. An AlphaFold model shows this protein adopts a three stranded beta sheet structure.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7203)
description: These proteins are found in various phages infecting bacteria from the Enterobacteriaceae family, such as Escherichia, Salmonella, Shigella, Klebsiella, and Yersinia. They are typically around 100 amino acids in length.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7204)
description: This domain family is found in viruses that infect Streptococcus thermophilus bacteria. All members are from Caudoviricetes viruses. The domain is approximately 50 amino acids in length. The function of this domain is currently unknown. An AlphaFold model shows these proteins adopt a compact domain composed of a three stranded beta sheet with a single alpha helix.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7205)
description: This entry represents a family of phage proteins that adopt a small beta barrel-like domain. The family is found in phages infecting members of the Enterobacteriaceae, such as Escherichia, Salmonella, Klebsiella, Cronobacter, Citrobacter, Erwinia, and Pectobacterium. The exact function of this protein within the phage tail is unknown. The family shows a highly conserved length of around 60-75 amino acids, with a few members having N- or C-terminal extensions.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7206)
description: This entry represents a family of uncharacterised phage proteins including from bacteriophage T6.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7207)
description: This entry represents an uncharacterized protein found in various bacteriophages that infect cyanobacteria and other bacterial hosts. The protein ranges in length from approximately 75 to 136 amino acids.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7208)
description: This entry represents a domain of unknown function found in large phage virion structural proteins. The domain is approximately 290 to 330 amino acids in length. It is found in a variety of phage proteins infecting bacterial hosts such as Pseudomonas, Vibrio, Ralstonia, and Erwinia, among others.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7209)
description: This entry represents a protein that is a component of the virion particle in several bacteriophages infecting hosts such as Bacillus, Staphylococcus, Listeria, Enterococcus and Lactobacillus. The exact function is unknown but it is likely to play a structural role. The protein is typically between 65-80 amino acids in length.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7210)
description: This entry represents a small domain found in a variety of uncharacterised phage proteins.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7211)
description: This entry represents a short highly motif that is found in some phage proteins, usually at the N-terminus. The function of this motif is unknown.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7212)
description: This entry represents a small phage protein that is composed of two alpha helices. According to AlphaFold prediction this protein forms a confident head to tail oriented dimer, forming a four helix bundle. The function of these proteins is unknown.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7213)
description: This entry represents an uncharacterized protein of approximately 70-100 amino acids found in mycobacteriophages. The function of this protein is currently unknown. It is found in phages belonging to the Gracegardnervirinae subfamily, including Cheoctovirus and Terapinvirus genera. This protein forms a confident dimer according to an AlphaFold model of [swissprot:S5Z4M5]. The dimer forms a central four stranded beta sheet with two alpha helices packed orthogonally to the direction of the beta strands on each face of the sheet.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7214)
description: This entry represents a phage protein of unknown function. According to AlphaFold models the domain forms a four stranded beta sheet followed by a single alpha helix. This domain forms a confident dimer according to AlphaFold.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7215)
description: This entry represents a domain of unknown function found in phage proteins, typically 45-60 amino acids in length. It is found in Streptomyces phages of the Caudoviricetes order, primarily in the Arquatrovirinae subfamily. The domain does not contain any conserved motifs or residues that provide hints about its function. A structure prediction shows that it is composed of two non-interacting alpha helices.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7216)
description: This entry represents a family of cyanophage proteins, including Gp130, that are found in a variety of Synechococcus and Prochlorococcus phages. The family members are typically around 100 amino acids in length. Structure predictions do not show a globular fold for this protein. The exact function of this family is unknown.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7217)
description: This entry represents an uncharacterized protein domain found in phage and bacterial proteins.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7218)
description: This entry represents a small conserved sequence region found in a variety of largely mycobacterial phage proteins as well as bacterial proteins. It is often found N-terminal to [pfam:PF07498].

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7219)
description: This entry represents a domain of unknown function. The domain is found in bacteria, primarily in cyanobacteria and their phage. It is typically around 80-90 amino acids in length. AlphaFold prediction suggests this protein is composed of two longer paired alpha helices followed by a shorter third helix.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7220)
description: This short protein is found among some phage. It is possibly distantly related to the small terminase family [pfam:PF05119].

name: DeoxyPurine in DNA protein A
description: This entry represents the DpdA family of proteins, which are involved in the insertion of deazapurine modifications in bacterial and phage DNA. DpdA proteins are paralogues of tRNA-guanine transglycosylases (TGT), but have evolved to act on DNA rather than RNA. They catalyze the incorporation of 7-deazaguanine derivatives such as dADG (7-amido-7- deazaguanine) and dpreQ0 (7-cyano-7-deazaguanine) into DNA, which is thought to function as a protection mechanism against endonucleases. The dpdA gene is typically part of a genomic island, along with dpdB, dpdC and dpdD genes, and is proposed to be part of a restriction/ modification system that protects bacteria from foreign DNA.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7222)
description: This entry represents a family of uncharacterised proteins found in various cyanophages, bacteriophages and bacteria species. The domain is approximately 100-160 amino acids in length. Structure prediction shows this domain is alpha helical.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7223)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised proteins mainly from fungi. It is frequently found associated with ([pfam:PF22974]). This domain is predicted to adopt a globular structure with an elongated beta-sandwich topology.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7224)
description: This entry represents a metalloprotease-like domain found in ABC transporter permease from bacteria, predominantly Streptomyces spp. The function of this domain is unknown.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7225)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised protein YnaC and related bacterial proteins. It is usually associated with ([pfam:PF22522]). This domain is a winged helix (WH) domain decorated at the C terminus with a small three stranded beta-sheet that packs on the WH domain to form a single globular structure.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7226)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised proteins. It is usually found in combination with [[pfam:PF22515]] and [[pfam:PF22518]]. It is predicted to contain a winged helix (WH) domain that is flanked at the C terminus with a small helical subdomain. The latter packs on the WH domain to form a compact globular structure.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7227)
description: This domain of unknown function is found in various phage and bacterial proteins. The domain length ranges from approximately 200 to 260 amino acids.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7228)
description: This family of uncharacterized proteins is found in several Lactococcus phages. All members are short proteins, between 33-59 amino acids in length. The family shows some conserved polar residues at the N-terminus. These proteins appear to be disordered.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7229)
description: This small helical domain is found a small family of phage proteins.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7230)
description: This entry represents a family of uncharacterized proteins found in phage and bacterial species, particularly in the Gammaproteobacteria class. Members of this family are typically short proteins, ranging from 32 to 85 amino acids in length. Many members are predicted to contain disordered regions and AlphaFold predictions show a non-globular structure.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7231)
description: This entry represents a family of unknown function found in phage proteins, typically 120-130 amino acids in length. Some members contain a C-terminal region enriched in basic residues that is predicted to be disordered. The N-terminus of the proteins contain a small globular domain. These proteins are found in the Ackermannviridae family of phages that infect Enterobacteria such as Salmonella, Escherichia, Shigella, and Dickeya.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7232)
description: This entry represents an uncharacterised phage family. A structure prediction suggests that the proteins consist of a three stranded beta meander followed by a C-terminal Alpha helix.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7233)
description: This domain is found in the phages infecting Mycobacterium and Gordonia. The domain is around 70-100 amino acids long.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7234)
description: This family represents a domain of unknown function, which is found in phage proteins ranging in length from 75 to 88 amino acids. The domain is found in phage that infect Salmonella, Shigella, Serratia, and Enterobacter species.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7235)
description: This entry represents an uncharacterized protein found in various phages that infect bacteria. The function of this protein is currently unknown. It is typically around 300-340 amino acids in length. This protein contains a predicted coiled-coil region near its C-terminus.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7236)
description: This entry represents a family of uncharacterised mycobacterium phage proteins.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7237)
description: This entry represents a protein of unknown function found in phage proteins. The domain contains approximately 77 residues and may contain a single transmembrane helix near the N-terminus.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7238)
description: This entry represents a domain of unknown function. It is found in uncharacterized phage proteins in the size range 90 to 120 amino acids. The domain does not appear to be related to any other known Pfam domain. The function of this domain remains to be determined.

name: LtfC-like, beta-sandwich domain
description: This entry, previously known as DUF7264, represents a domain found in the Minor tail protein Gp6, Collar protein p132, Lateral tail fiber protein C (LtfC) and related phage proteins. This domain folds into a beta-sandwich fold with and extended beta-hairpin that projects away from it. The minor tail proteins Gp6 are likely involved in the assembly or function of the tail structure in bacteriophages. The collar protein p132 forms the T5 phage collar structure, which serves as an anchoring point for the side tail fiber protein pb1, suggesting a role in stabilising the tail fibers and ensuring proper attachment to the host cell [[cite:PUB00155631]]. The lateral tail fiber protein C (LtfC) is a component of the DT57C bacteriophage tail tip complex where it forms a dodecameric ring [[cite:PUB00155646]]. LtfC adopts a compact, single-domain structure. The LtfC ring is complemented by another lateral tail fiber protein, LtfA. Each of the LtfA monomers is connected to the LtfC assembly in a unique way by augmenting the edges of LtfC beta-sheets with two short beta-strands and thus completing the LtfC beta-sandwich structure.

name: Minor capsid protein P11, C-terminal conserved region

P11 plays crucial roles in determining the capsid size and binding neighbouring symmetrons together. The P11 proteins zip together most of the capsomers at the boundary of neighbouring tri- or penta- symmetrons via their C-terminal regions. The C-terminal regions of each P11 protein is located underneath the conjunction of a set of three neighbouring capsomers, gluing these capsomers together [[cite:PUB00154526]].
