The dimer shows distinct charge distribution with a linear positively charged surface.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7376)
description: This entry represents a family of uncharacterised phage proteins. Structure prediction suggests these protein may form a homodimer. The dimer contains a large circular channel that is positively charged suggesting a possible DNA-binding function.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7373) C-terminal
description: This domain is found C-terminal in uncharacterised bacterial proteins. It is predicted to adopt a seven-stranded antiparallel beta-sheet with similarity to Mog1p/PsbP-like domains. Some proteins containing this domain have a lipoprotein attachment motif at the N-terminus suggesting they may be associated with the membrane. This domain is usually found in two copies that share little if any sequence similarity to each other.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7377)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised plant proteins. It is predicted to adopt an alpha/beta structure with a central four-stranded antiparallel beta-sheet and alpha helices packed on it. It has weak sequence and structural similarity to NIL domains. It is usually found N-terminal to protein kinase domains.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7378)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised plant proteins. It is predicted to contain transmembrane helices that assemble in a four helical bundle.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7379)
description: This entry represents a domain of unknown function found towards the N-terminal of CHAT domain-containing protein, such as SwissProt:A0A100JVW6, from Streptomyces scabiei. This domain may adopt a A/B hydrolase fold and is often found in association with TCAD7 ([pfam:PF19973]) and CHAT ([pfam:PF12770]) domains.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7380)
description: This domain is found N-terminal in uncharacterised bacterial proteins. It is predicted to adopt a globular structure composed mainly of alpha helices.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7381)
description: This domain is found N-terminal in uncharacterised nematode proteins. It is predicted to adopt a globular alpha/beta structure.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7382)
description: This is a Ig-like domain found in a group of uncharacterised sequences, mainly from archaea.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7383)
description: This entry represents a group of uncharacterised archaeal sequences containing a galactose binding-like domain.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7384)
description: This is a group of uncharacterised sequences from archaea which are related to VapC (virulence-associated protein C) family of proteins. Members of this entry may adopt a PIN-like fold.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7385)
description: This entry represents a small group of archaeal sequences whose function is unknown.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7386)
description: This is a family of archaeal sequences of unknown function.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7387)
description: This entry includes uncharacterised archaeal sequences.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7388)
description: This entry represents uncharacterised archaeal sequences.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7389)
description: This is a domain of unknown function found in a group of archaeal sequences.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7390)
description: This entry represents a family of uncharacterised phage protein. These proteins adopt a compact globular domain. The predicted structure of the domain shows a positively charged surface suggesting a possible nucleic acid binding function.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7391)
description: This entry represents a small family of uncharacterised phage proteins. Many of them are annotated as phage tail assembly chaperones, but there does not appear to be any evidence to support this annotation.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7392)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised proteins from plants. It has sequence and structural similarity to domains members of Dimeric alpha/beta barrel superfamily.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7393)
description: This small uncharacterised phage protein has a 5 stranded beta barrel fold.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7394)
description: This entry represents a protein of unknown function, found primarily in phage proteins of about 60 to 75 amino acids in length. It contains a single predicted transmembrane helix in many members. Most sequences also contain a region of predicted intrinsic disorder at the C-terminus rich in basic and acidic residues. Further experimental study is required to determine the function of these proteins. Some proteins are annotated as holins but the source of this annotation is unknown.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7395)
description: This entry represents a small family of uncharacterised phage proteins, that includes the L1 protein from Lactococcus phage c2 [swissprot:Q38296]. Structure prediction indicates this small protein adopts a compact domain composed of a three stranded sheet with a single alpha helix.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7396)
description: This entry represents an uncharacterized protein found in several bacteriophages that infect bacteria such as Escherichia coli, Enterobacter, Klebsiella and Shigella. The protein is short, around 44-51 amino acids in length. It is predicted to contain a single transmembrane helix. The function of this protein is currently unknown. One representative of this family is the [swissprot:P18922] protein from bacteriophage T4.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7397)
description: This entry represents a small family of uncharacterised phage proteins. These proteins are around 50-60 residues in length.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7398)
description: This entry describes an uncharacterized protein found in several bacteriophages that infect Bacillus species. The protein ranges in length from 158 to 189 amino acids. It is found in the virions of phages from the Bastillevirinae subfamily of the Herelleviridae family. Structure prediction suggests the proteins are composed of a bundle of five alpha helices.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7399)
description: This entry represents a family of phage proteins. The proteins appear to contain two domains. The N-terminal domain contains a small beta sheet wrapped around an alpha helix. The second domain is composed of a pair of alpha helices. The proteins are found in several viruses within the proposed new Crassvirales order of bacteriophages.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7400)
description: This entry represents a domain of unknown function found towards the N-terminal of some PRiA4b ORF-3-like proteins from bacteria, such as SwissProt:A0A1I7K0M5. This domain may adopt a TPR-like fold and is generally associated to PriA4_ORF3 ([pfam:PF07929]) domain.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7401)
description: This entry represents a domain of unknown function found towards the centre of some PRiA4b ORF-3-like proteins from bacteria, such as SwissProt:A0A068QX925. This domain is generally associated to PriA4_ORF3 ([pfam:PF07929]) domain.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7402)
description: This entry represents the domain of unknown function found in bacterial and fungal sequences, including some F5/8 type C domain-containing proteins such as Swissprot:A0A4V0YDU8. This domain may adopt a galactose-binding domain-like fold. This domain is found in several copies, predominantly between two and six times, and it is found in association with PIG-L ([pfam:PF02585]) domain.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7403)
description: This entry represents a domain of unknown function found in some PRiA4b ORF-3-like proteins from bacteria, such as SwissProt:A0A1I7K0M5. This domain may adopt an all-helical fold and is generally found alongside the PriA4_ORF3 ([pfam:PF07929]) domain.

name: ApeC, platyhelminthes
description: This entry represents a divergent ApeC domain found in a group of proteins mainly from flatworms that also contain [pfam:PF16977]. Its specific function is unknown. This domain is predicted to show an alpha-beta configuration.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7405)
description: This entry represents a family or archaeal proteins whose function is unknown. They may adopt a dimeric alpha/beta barrel fold.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7406)
description: This is a small domain found in a group of uncharacterised archaeal sequences. This small domain may have an all-beta fold.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7407)
description: This is a domain of unknown function found in a group of uncharacterised sequences from archaea. This domain may have a beta-sandwich fold.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7408)
description: This is a domain of unknown function found in a group of uncharacterised sequences from archaea. It may adopt an amidotransferase-like fold.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7409)
description: This is a domain of unknown function found in uncharacterised archaeal sequences.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7410)
description: This is a C2H2 zinc finger found in a group of uncharacterised proteins from archaea.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7411)
description: This is a family of unknown function mainly found in archaea but also in some bacterial species. They may have a Rossmann-like alpha/beta/alpha fold.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7412)
description: This entry represents an uncharacterised protein family found in a range of bacteriophage including Phage T2. These proteins include a beta barrel domain. Many members of the family are annotated as IP4 internal head protein, although the source of evidence for this annotation was not found.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7413)
description: This entry represents a small family of uncharacterised phage proteins. Structure prediction suggests these proteins are composed of a three stranded beta sheet packed against a pair of alpha helices.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7414)
description: This entry represents an uncharacterised family of proteins. Structure prediction suggests these proteins form a four stranded beta sheet with a helix packed on one side. Structure prediction also suggests a confident dimer. The structure shows some weak similarity to large ribosomal subunit protein eL38.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7415)
description: This entry represents a family of uncharacterised phage domains. This domain is found in one to two copies per proteins. It seems likely that the proteins with a single copy of the domain form homodimers.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7416)
description: This entry represents a small uncharacterised enterobacterial phage protein family. Structure prediction suggests these proteins might adopt a pair of alpha helices.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7417)
description: This entry represents an uncharacterized protein domain found in various phage and bacterial proteins. The domain is approximately 60-80 amino acids in length. The domain is composed of four alpha helices that form a small bundle. The surface of the domain is negatively charged.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7418)
description: This entry represents a small uncharacterised family of phage proteins. It adopts a novel triangular beta prism structure.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7419)
description: This entry represents a family of uncharacterised mycobacteria phage proteins that adopt a zinc binding domain composed of 5 potential ligand residues. The zinc binding motif is composed of a CXXC and a CXXHH motif.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7420)
description: This entry represents an uncharacterised family of phage integral membrane proteins. The proteins are found in phage of S. aureus and B. subtilis. These proteins contain three potential transmembrane helices. There is a conserved GXXPL motif that is highly conserved between helices 1 and 2.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7421)
description: This entry represents a small family of uncharacterised enterobacterial phage proteins.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7422)
description: This entry represents a small family of phage proteins. The family includes members from Phage T2 and T6. These proteins contain a small three stranded beta domain. Some members have an additional small C-terminal domain composed of a beta-alpha-alpha-beta hairpin domain.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7423)
description: This entry represents a family of uncharacterised mycobacterial phage proteins. The proteins have a domain that contains a four helical bundle.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7424)
description: This entry represents a family of uncharacterised lipoproteins. The family includes a range of both bacteria and phage proteins.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7425)
description: This entry represents a domain of unknown function found in bacteriophage proteins. The domain is around 90-95 amino acids in length. It is found in uncharacterized proteins from phages that infect Enterobacteria such as Salmonella and Shigella species as well as Dickeya. The specific function of this domain remains unknown. Structure prediction suggests that these proteins may form a homotetramer (iPTM=0.88). The domain contains a three twisted stranded beta sheet.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7426)
description: This entry represents an uncharacterised domain found in phage proteins.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7427)
description: This entry represents a family of uncharacterised phage proteins. Family members are largely found in mycobacterial phage.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7428)
description: This entry represents a small family of uncharacterised phage proteins. The structure of this family is predicted to be composed of a four stranded beta sheet and a single alpha helix.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7429)
description: This entry represents a family of small uncharacterised proteins found in mycobacterial phage.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7430)
description: This entry represents a family of uncharacterised phage proteins.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7431)
description: This entry represents the domain of unknown function found towards the C-terminal of some MACPF domain-containing proteins from fungi, such as SwissProt:A0A2P4PCT2. It is found associated with MACPF_1 ([pfam:PF22693]) domain.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7432)
description: This entry represents a family of uncharacterised phage proteins that are composed of two small domains connected by an alpha helix. Structure prediction suggests that these proteins may homodimerise or tetramerise. These proteins are primarily found in Gordonia phage.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7433)
description: This entry represents a small region that is found in a variety of uncharacterised mycobacterial phage proteins. Structure prediction suggests it adopts an alpha helix and beta hairpin structure that likely homodimerises.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7434)
description: This entry represents a small family of uncharacterised mycobacterial phage proteins. Structure prediction suggests that this protein forms a single alpha helix. It is quite hydrophobic with a negatively charged C-terminus. Some proteins are annotated as RDF proteins but there does not appear to be any evidence to support their function as recombination directionality factors.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7435)
description: This entry represents a family of uncharacterized proteins found in Mycobacterium phages. The family members are typically around 67 amino acids in length. Structure prediction suggests these proteins form a small compact domain composed of four beta strands followed by an Alpha helix. The domain possibly shows weak structural similarity to integrase arm-type binding domain.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7436)
description: This domain is found at the C-terminal end of a group of archaeal sequences that contain [pfam:PF01978] at the N-terminal. It is predicted to adopt a Phospholipase D-like fold.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7437)
description: This domain is found at the C-terminal end of a group of archaeal sequences that contain [pfam:PF01978] at the N-terminal. It is predicted to adopt an all-alpha configuration.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7438)
description: This entry represents a family of uncharacterized proteins found in bacteriophages. The function of this protein family is currently unknown. The family appears to be conserved across various phage species that infect Escherichia coli and related bacteria. The family includes members from Phage T2, T4 and T6. Members of this family are typically short proteins of around 60-67 amino acids in length. Bacteriophage T4 contains four proteins that belong to this family. The structure of these proteins is predicted to be composed of two alpha helices that pack together. Structure prediction suggests these proteins may homodimerise (iPTM=0.83).

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7439)
description: This entry represents a family of small putative transmembrane proteins found primarily in Streptomyces phages and some bacteria. The family is characterized by a conserved transmembrane region typically located between residues 20-45 of the alignment. Many members of this family are around 70 amino acids in length. The function of this protein family is currently unknown.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7440)
description: This entry represents a protein family of unknown function found in various bacterial phage proteins. The family typically consists of proteins around 140-160 amino acids in length. It is found in phages that infect bacteria such as Salmonella, Escherichia, Shigella, and Dickeya. The function of this family remains unclear. Some members of this family are annotated as uncharacterized or hypothetical proteins. AlphaFold predictions suggest the proteins in this family contain two distinct domains, with a central domain composed of a three stranded beta sheet and a C-terminal small 3-helix bundle domain.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7441)
description: This entry represents a conserved domain found predominantly in bacteriophage proteins. The domain is characterized by a highly conserved YDRH motif, which likely plays an important role in the domain's function or structure. This family includes proteins from various phages that infect cyanobacteria, particularly Synechococcus and Prochlorococcus species. The proteins contain a central small domain composed of a three stranded beta sheet with an alpha helix inserted between the second and third strands.

name: Phage membrane protein Family of unknown function (DUF7442)
description: This entry represents a family of putative membrane proteins found in various bacteriophages. The proteins in this family typically contain two transmembrane helices. The function of these proteins is currently unknown. They are predominantly found in phages infecting Salmonella, Escherichia, and other enterobacteria. The proteins in this family are generally short, with most members being around 80-81 amino acids in length

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7443)
description: This entry represents an uncharacterized protein family found in bacteriophages. The function of this family is currently unknown. Members of this family are typically around 90-100 amino acids in length. The family includes proteins from various phage species infecting bacteria such as Salmonella, Klebsiella, and Proteus. Some members of this family contain disordered regions, particularly in their C-terminal portions. Conserved basic and acidic residues are present in many family members, which may be functionally important. This entry represents the globular N-terminal domain of these proteins.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7444)
description: This entry represents a conserved family found in various bacteriophages, particularly those infecting Escherichia, Klebsiella, and other Enterobacteriaceae. The function of this domain is currently unknown. This family is commonly found in phages belonging to the Drexlerviridae family, including genera such as Webervirus, Tempevirinae, and Tunavirinae. This entry shows some structurally similar features to [pfam:PF24227].

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7445)
description: This entry represents an uncharacterized protein family found in mycobacteriophages. The function of this protein is currently unknown. The family is approximately 147 amino acids long. These proteins contain two small domains. The most N-terminal one contains a CXXC and HXXC motif that likely bind to zinc.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7446)
description: This entry represents a highly conserved domain found in various bacteriophages, particularly those infecting Salmonella and related bacteria. The domain is also present in some bacterial species, suggesting possible horizontal gene transfer. The function is unknown, but the high degree of conservation implies an important role in phage biology. A conserved motif DVT is present centrally in many family members. The aspartate and threonine form side chain hydrogen bonds that help stabilise the dimeric interaction. Structure prediction suggests these proteins form a confident homodimer (iPTM=0.83).

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7447)
description: This entry represents an uncharacterized family found in various bacteriophage proteins. It is predominantly found in phages infecting diverse bacterial species including Burkholderia, Bacillus, Streptomyces, Listeria, and Caulobacter. The proteins are typically around 100-150 amino acids in length. Many of the proteins containing this domain are annotated as uncharacterized or hypothetical proteins. The proteins form a compact domain composed of a four stranded antiparallel beta sheet.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7448)
description: This entry represents a conserved viral protein domain of unknown function (DUF4241). The domain is approximately 130-160 amino acids in length and is found in various bacteriophages and large DNA viruses. The alignment shows several conserved residues, including a highly conserved DCC motif. The protein contains a beta sandwich domain structural.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7449)
description: This entry represents a small family of uncharacterised proteins found in pseudomonas phage. The protein contains a compact domain composed of two alpha helices followed by four beta strands that form a beta sheet.

name: Repeat of unknown function (DUF7450)
description: This entry represents a group of uncharacterised proteins from bacteria that, according to structure predictions (SwissProt:A0A7C3HQW7 or SwissProt:A0A5C6D6K5), they may contain novel repeats that fold into twisted long beta-hairpins different from typical beta-barrel hairpins and they do not exhibit homology to any beta-barrel.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7451)
description: This entry represents a presumed domain found in a group of uncharacterised sequences from bacteria. According to structure predictions, this domain may adopt and all-beta configuration with beta-strands of different lengths. This domain is usually associated with DUF7450 ([pfam:PF24247]).

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7452)
description: This entry represents a presumed domain found in a group of uncharacterised proteins from bacteria. This domain may adopt an all-beta configuration.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7453)
description: This entry represents a group of uncharacterised sequences from bacteria. According to structure predictions, these proteins may comprise novel repeats consisting of an arrangement of four beta-strands in which the second one is longer and curved. This arrangement is repeated eight times in SwissProt:A0A5B9QB27, which form a closed repeat.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7454)
description: This entry represents a small family of uncharacterised proteins from a set of mycobacterial phage including phage Bxb1 (gene 86). The members of the family range in length from 50 to 90 residues. Structurally, the domain shows some weak similarity to the N-terminal domain of IF5, which adopts an SH3 like barrel fold.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7455)
description: This entry represents a family of uncharacterised actinobacterial zinc binding domains. The proteins contain a characteristic CXHH motif. Only the second of those two histidines acts as the zinc ligand according to structure prediction (ipTM = 0.94).

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7456)
description: This entry represents a family of uncharacterised proteins found in Mycobacterial phage. The family includes gene 48 from phage Bxb1.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7457)
description: This entry represents a small family of uncharacterised phage proteins. This family includes gene 78 from Phage Bxb1.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7458)
description: This entry represents a small family of uncharacterised mycobacterial phage. Some members are annotated as DNA primase. The family includes gene 53 from phage Bxb1.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7459)
description: This entry represents an uncharacterised protein domain found in a mycobacterial phage proteins. These domains form a zinc binding cluster where 8 cysteine and histidine residues bind two zinc ions according to structure prediction (iPTM=0.87).

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7460)
description: This entry represents a small uncharacterised mycobacterial phage domain composed of two alpha helices and three beta strands. The family includes Phage Bxb1 gene 81.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7461)
description: This entry represents a small uncharacterised family of mycobacterial phage proteins. The family includes gene 71 from phage Bxb1 [swissprot:Q9B050]. Structure prediction suggests this protein may form a pair of alpha helices that form a helical hairpin structure.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7462)
description: This entry represents a family of uncharacterised mycobacterial phage proteins. The family includes Phage Bxb1 gene 76. These proteins are short around 40 residues in length.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7463)
description: This entry represents a small family of uncharacterised mycobacterial phage proteins. The family includes gene 82 from mycobacterial phage Bxb1.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7464)
description: This entry represents a small family of uncharacterised phage proteins. The family includes the gene 83 from the mycobacterial phage Bxb1 [swissprot:Q9B038]. This family shows structural similarity to [pfam:PF09926]. These proteins have an SH3 like barrel structure.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7465)
description: This entry represents a small family of uncharacterised phage proteins. The family includes Phage Bxb1 protein 85 [swissprot:Q9B036].

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7466)
description: This entry represents a family of uncharacterised phage proteins. Structurally these are composed of a pair of alpha helices. Structure prediction suggests these proteins may homodimerise (iPTM=0.89). These proteins are annotated as RDF proteins but the source of this annotation is uncertain.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7467)
description: This entry represents a beta sandwich domain found in a variety of bacterial cell surface proteins.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7468)
description: This entry represents a conserved protein family found in cyanophages that infect marine Synechococcus and Prochlorococcus. The function of this protein is unknown. It is typically 70-100 amino acids in length. The protein appears to be specific to cyanophages and is not found in their cyanobacterial hosts.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7469)
description: Members of this family are uncharacterised proteins found in cyanobacteria that grow with a filamentous morphology [[cite:PUB00154605]].

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7470)
description: This family includes a group of short proteins from archaea. Members are predicted to adopt an alpha-helical structure.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7471)
description: This family includes a group of short proteins from archaea.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7472)
description: This family includes a group of short proteins from archaea. Members are predicted to adopt an alpha-helical structure.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7473)
description: This family includes a group of proteins from archaea. Members are predicted to adopt an alpha-helical structure.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7474)
description: This family includes a group of proteins from archaea. Members are predicted to adopt a mainly alpha-helical structure.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7475)
description: This family includes a group of proteins from archaea. Members are predicted to adopt an alpha-helical structure.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7476)
description: This family includes a group of proteins from nematodes.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7477)
description: This entry represents a domain consisting of a novel repeat fold which containing five repeats, each of them comprising three antiparallel beta-strands and a short alpha-helix, according to structure predictions (e.g SwissProt:S8CFV9). This domain is found in Casein kinase 1-like protein HD16 from rice, a protein involved in the regulation of flowering time through gibberellin (GA) signaling and independently of photoperiod [[cite:PUB00155615]].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7478)
description: This entry represents a domain containing a novel repeat fold, according to structure predictions. It may comprise six repeats, each of them consisting of two antiparallel beta-strands and a short alpha-helix.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7479)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised bacterial proteins. It contains four invariant cysteines and it is predicted to adopt a Zn-ribbon fold.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7480)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised bacterial proteins. These proteins contain a highly conserved lipoprotein-type signal peptide sequence at the N terminus and two invariant cysteine residues within this domain suggesting their extracytoplasmic localisation.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7481)
description: This entry represents a group of uncharacterised sequences from bacteria. They may consist on repeats with a novel fold which is organised in three units with twisted beta-strands each.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7482)
description: This entry includes a group of uncharacterised sequences from bacteria and archaea, which, according to structure predictions, they may have a novel repeat fold. They may consist of 5-6 antiparallel beta-strands decorated with short alpha-helices.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7483)
description: This entry includes uncharacterised bacterial sequences that may adopt a novel fold consisting on three repeat units, each of them are type of beta-sandwich with three beta-strands on one side and four or five on the other.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7484)
description: This entry represents an uncharacterised family of phage proteins. These proteins consist of two domains. The first is composed of four alpha helices that are contributed by both the N and C-terminus of the protein. The second domain is a central beta domain. Structure prediction suggests that these proteins might form a large homo-oligomeric ring of 8-10 subunits, but the iPTM scores are marginal.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7485)
description: This entry includes uncharacterised sequences mainly from actinobacteria. According to structure predictions, they may form a beta-propeller-like fold consisting of four repeated units containing three (in one of them) and four (on the other three units) beta-strands. There is an additional unit which is slightly different that resembles a seven stranded beta-sandwich.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7486)
description: This entry represents a group of uncharacterised sequences that, according to structure predictions. they may consist on a novel repeat fold which comprise beta-hairpin-beta units organised in four and five units, forming two domains.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7487)
description: This entry represents a group of uncharacterised sequences from viruses. They may have a novel repeat fold consisting of two domains at the N- and C-terminal with beta-hairpin-beta-alpha configuration that are connected by nine alpha-helices linked by loops.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7488)
description: This entry represents a domain from uncharacterised proteins found mainly in Campylobacterota. Members of this entry contain two highly conserved cysteine residues.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7489)
description: This entry represents a domain from uncharacterised proteins mainly found in Actinomycetes. They are predicted to adopt an OB fold-like beta-barrel.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7490)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised archaeal proteins. Members of this family have a PGF-CTERM motif [pfam:PF18204] at the C-termini.

name: Coiled-coil region of unknown function (DUF7491)
description: This is a coiled-coil region found at the C-terminal of a group of uncharacterised sequences from fungi.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7492)
description: This entry represents a domain of unknown function found in fungal sequences. It may adopt a Ig-like fold similar to that in Auxiliary Activity family 9 (AA9), [pfam:PF03443].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7493)
description: This is a domain of unknown function found in uncharacterised sequences from fungi. Some of these sequences are annotated as sphingosine kinases. This domain may adopt a PH-like fold.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7494)
description: This domain is found in a group of uncharacterised proteins mainly from Epsilonproteobacteria. It is predicted to adopt a globular structure with a beta-sandwich topology.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7495)
description: This domain is found in a group of uncharacterised eukaryotic proteins. It contains six highly conserved cysteines which are predicted to form disulfide bonds. This domain is predicted to adopt structure similar to C-type lectins.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7496)
description: This domain is found in a group of uncharacterised eukaryotic proteins. It is predicted to fold into Ig-like beta-sandwich.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7497)

description: This domain is found in uncharacterised proteins mainly from nematodes. It is predicted to adopt a globular structure consisting of a three-stranded antiparallel beta-sheet and three alpha-helices packed on one side of it.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7637)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised proteins mainly from nematodes. It is predicted to adopt a globular structure consisting of a four-stranded antiparallel beta-sheet and two alpha-helices packed on one side of it.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7638)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised bacterial proteins. It is predicted to adopt an alpha/beta structure consisting of curved beta-sheet and alpha-helices packed on the concave side of it.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7639)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised bacterial proteins. It is predicted to adopt a globular structure composed of a three helical bundle.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7640)
description: This is a presumed domain found in a group of uncharacterised sequences from diatoms. This domain may adopt a beta-solenoid fold and in some members is repeated twice or three times.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7641)
description: This entry includes uncharacterised sequences from Plasmodium sp. and similar sequences from Apicomplexa. This entry may represent transmembrane helices.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7642)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised sequences from plants.

name: Tal, N-terminal tail tube TT1 domain
description: This domain, previously known as DUF7643, is found N-terminal in the tail-associated lysin (Tal, gp59) and related sequences from phages and bacteriophages. gp59 is comprising the tip of the phage tail. The domain represented by this entry is one of the two tail tube domains (TT1 and TT2) that form a quasi-sixfold adapter to the distal tail protein (Dit, gp58) hexamer [[cite:PUB00156034]]. These two domains merge into a continuous eight-stranded beta-sheet on one side.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7644)
description: This entry represents a small family of uncharacterised staphylococcal phage proteins. Structure prediction suggests they form a compact domain composed of a three stranded beta sheet packed against an alpha helix.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7645)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised proteins mainly from plants. It is predicted to fold into a three helical bundle.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7646)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised proteins mainly from plants. It has detectable similarity to winged helix HTH domains and it is predicted to adopt similar structure.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7647)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised proteins mainly from plants. It is predicted to adopt a globular structure consisting of array of helices.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7648)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised proteins mainly from plants. It is predicted to adopt a globular structure consisting of array of helices.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7649)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised bacterial proteins. It is predicted to adopt a non-compact structure consisting of four highly hydrophobic alpha-helices that could potentially dimerise.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7650)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised proteins mainly from plants. It is predicted to adopt mainly helical structure.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7651)
description: This domain is found in the Polycomb group protein EMBRYONIC FLOWER 2 (EMF2) from Arabidopsis thaliana and related proteins. EMF2 is involved in flowering processes by repressing unknown target genes and preventing reproductive development. This domain is predicted to adopt a globular structure that resembles barrel-sandwich hybrid. The beta-sandwich has a topology most similar to C2 domains found in diverse proteins such as CEP120, Dysferlin and Myoferlin.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7652)
description: This is an Ig-like domain found towards the C-terminal of a group of uncharacterised sequences from Strongyloides spp. and similar sequences from nematodes.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7653)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised proteins mainly from plants.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7654)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised bacterial proteins. It is predicted to adopt a globular alpha/beta structure.

name: SNTX, MACPF/CDC-like domain
description: This MACPF/CDC-like domain is found N-terminal in a number of toxins including Stonustoxin (SNTX), Neoverrucotoxin (NeoVTX), Verrucotoxin (VTX), Sp-CTx and related proteins. This domain is a pore-forming domain and is involved in the formation of large ring-shaped pores in rat erythrocyte membranes [[cite:PUB00091171]]. The formation of MACPF/CDC-like pores is probably central to the toxin's hemolytic activity, and cell lysis could explain physiological effects, including edema, increased vascular permeability, and muscle damage.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7656)
description: This domain is found in a group of uncharacterised eukaryotic proteins. It shares detectable similarity to the Thioredoxin-like SNTX domain ([pfam:PF18078]) and it is predicted to adopt similar structure.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7657)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised bacterial proteins. It contains a semi-conserved sequence motif TxYPGxR. It is likely that this domain is a transmembrane domain composed of alpha-helices.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7658)
description: This is a presumed domain found towards the C-terminal of a group of uncharacterised sequences from C. elegans and similar proteins from nematodes.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7659)
description: This family of uncharacterised proteins is found in bacteria and phage. Proteins in this family are typically between 128 and 147 amino acids in length. The proteins contain two subdomains separated by an alpha-helical linker.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7660)
description: This family represents a set of uncharacterised bacterial proteins. Structure prediction shows them to be composed of three alpha helices.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7661)
description: This entry represents a family of small uncharacterised bacterial proteins that adopts a compact domain composed of 5 beta strands and a single alpha helix.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7662)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised bacterial proteins. It is frequently found in combination with [pfam:PF21818] and [pfam:PF20815] which suggests that it may be involved in DNA binding and recognition. It is predicted to adopt a globular structure consisting of a three-stranded antiparallel beta-sheet and alpha-helices packed on one side of it.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7663)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised bacterial proteins. It is frequently found in combination with [pfam:PF21818]. It is predicted to adopt a complex alpha/beta structure composed of a curved beta-sheet that encloses an alpha-helix and a number of helices packed on its exterior.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7664)
description: This entry represents a small accessory domain found at the N-terminus of a small family of archaeal AGOG proteins. These proteins have 8-oxoguanine DNA glycosylase activity.

name: Bacterial E2-like ubiquitin protein BilB
description: This protein family includes Bacterial E2-like ubiquitin protein BilB from Collimonas sp. and similar short uncharacterised bacterial proteins. BilB is a component of the Bil (bacterial ISG15-like) antiviral defense system. BilB probably accepts ubiquitin from the BilA-BilD (E1) complex and catalyses its covalent attachment to target protein (CTF) [[cite:PUB00160357]].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7666)
description: This entry represents an uncharacterised protein domain that is sometimes found associated with [pfam:PF01469]. The family also includes an N-terminal domain found in the Pseudomonas syringae InaZ ice nucleation protein.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7667)
description: This entry represents a small family of uncharacterised bacterial proteins. Structure prediction shows these proteins are alpha helical with a long central alpha helix packed against two shorter N and C-terminal helices. Structure prediction suggests these proteins may form homodimers.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7668)
description: This entry represents a bacterial protein domain of unknown function.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7669)
description: This domain is found in a group of uncharacterised proteins primarily found in Bacteria. It has a detectable similarity to winged helix HTH domain and it is predicted to adopt similar structure. This domain is frequently found in combination with [pfam:PF21818] and [pfam:PF20815].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7670)
description: This entry represents a family of uncharacterised bacterial membrane proteins that contain four transmembrane alpha helices.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7671)
description: This entry represents a family of uncharacterised bacterial proteins. The protein forms a single beta barrel domain which shows some structural similarity to the N-terminal domain of the PriA protein. However, structure prediction does not support this protein having a DNA-binding function like PriA.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7672)
description: This family of uncharacterised proteins is found in bacteria (Bacteroidota and Chloroflexi). Proteins in this family are approximately 80 amino acids in length. The proteins are likely to be integral membrane proteins with two transmembrane alpha helices. Structural modelling suggests that these proteins form a dimeric arrangement with the pairs of alpha helices tilted at close to 45 degrees angle compared to the lipid membrane. Based on the positive inside rule it is likely that the N and C-terminii of the proteins have a cytoplasmic location. Given the geometry of the protein complex it may not span the entire membrane.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7673)
description: This entry represents an uncharacterised family of proteins, which are typically between 100 and 122 amino acids in length. This protein is often found to be plasmid borne and in a few cases is associated with ParBc domains that are critical for plasmid segregation. This suggests that this domain may play a role in chromosome segregation or plasmid partitioning. Structural modelling suggests this domain will form a homodimeric complex.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7674)
description: This family of proteins is found in bacteria. Proteins in this family are typically between 113 and 127 amino acids in length.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7675)
description: This entry represents an uncharacterised family of proteins is found in bacteria and viruses. Proteins in this family are typically between 69 and 93 amino acids in length.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7676)
description: This entry represents a family of bacterial proteins that based on structural similarities are likely to bind to heme or a related derivative molecule. Structural modelling suggests these proteins are likely to form homodimers and that this complex can bind to two heme-like molecules. Each heme binding site is composed of parts of both subunits.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7677)
description: This entry represents a group of uncharacterised proteins found in bacteria. These proteins are predicted to adopt globular structure that folds into a three helical bundle.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7678)
description: This entry represents a conserved domain of unknown function (DUF7678) found in various bacterial species. The domain is approximately 75-100 amino acids in length and contains several highly conserved residues. The function of this domain remains to be determined. Structure prediction suggests this domain is composed of a 6 stranded beta sheet with an Alpha helix packed on one side.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7679)
description: This entry represents a small family of Lactobacillus proteins of unknown function. The predicted structure suggests these proteins contain two subdomains, with an N-terminal partly open beta barrel and C-terminal alpha/beta subdomain.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7680)
description: This entry represents a group of uncharacterised prokaryotic proteins. These proteins share a common semi-conserved EExxWY sequence motif which is predicted as a solvent-exposed in a alpha/beta structure consisting of a four-stranded antiparallel beta-sheet and alpha-helices packed on one side of it.

name: Acb2/Tad1, hairpin domain
description: This domain, previously known as DUF7681, is found in phage proteins including Anti-CBASS protein 2 (Acb2) and Thoeris anti-defense 1 (Tad1). It folds into an alpha-helical hairpin that is found either standalone (in Acb2) or in combination with a four-stranded antiparallel beta-sheet domain (in Tad1) [[cite:PUB00153173],[cite:PUB00156031],[cite:PUB00156032]]. Prokaryotic anti-phage immune systems use TIR and cGAS-like enzymes to produce 1-3-glycocyclic ADP-ribose; and cyclic dinucleotide and trinucleotide signalling molecules, respectively, which limit phage replication. The Thoeris anti-defence proteins Tad1 and Tad2 are both pronged inhibitors and antagonise immunity alongside Anti-CBASS protein 2. These proteins achieve anti-cyclic-oligonucleotide-based anti-phage signalling system (anti-CBASS) activity by sequestering a considerable amount of cyclic nucleotides. Each of these proteins is using distinct binding pockets. The residues conserved in Tad1 and Acb2 are located near these binding sites [[cite:PUB00156032],[cite:PUB00156033]].

name: Zinc-binding Domain of unknown function (DUF7682)
description: This entry represents a small zinc-binding domain found to the N-terminus of proteins that belong to the ParE toxin superfamily. The exact function of this domain is unknown. The zinc ligands are composed of the cys and his in the N-terminal CGH motif and the cys residues in the C-terminal CHXC motif.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7683)
description: This family represents uncharacterised proteins found in bacteria. These proteins are related to members of [pfam:PF03513] which are described as immunity proteins. They are predicted to adopt similar structure composed of a four-stranded antiparallel beta-sheet with alpha-helices packed on one side of it.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7684)
description: This entry represents a group of uncharacterised bacterial proteins found in bacteria. They are predicted to adopt a globular alpha/beta structure that has some similarity to MurD C-terminal domain.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7685)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised bacterial proteins. It contains two pairs of conserved cysteine residues and it is predicted to adopt a fold typical for treble clef zinc fingers. It has a detectable similarity to the N-terminal zinc finger domain of the bacterial AAA+ disaggregase ClpG, which confers extreme heat resistance to bacteria. The latter is is crucial for structural integrity and disaggregase functionality of ClpG.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7686)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised bacterial proteins. It is usually found next to [pfam:PF24734]. It is predicted to adopt alpha/beta structure consisting of a four-stranded beta-sheet curved around an alpha-helix.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7687)
description: This entry represents a domain found in uncharacterised bacterial proteins. It shares detectable similarity to a number of type II restriction endonucleases such as DpnII and Ecl18kI and it is predicted to adopt similar structure. It is likely to possess endonuclease activity given the conservation of putative functional site residues.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7688)
description: This entry represents a small family of uncharacterised protein found in bacteria. They are predicted to adopt alpha+beta structure defined as beta(2)alpha(2)beta(2) structural elements in which the beta-strands form an antiparallel beta-sheet.The function of these proteins is unknown.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7689)
description: This entry represents a group of uncharacterised proteins. They are predicted to adopt a fold typical for cysteine proteinases and topology similar to that of NlpC/P60 family proteins. These proteins are likely enzymes as they have similar active site architecture.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7690)
description: This entry represents a domain found in uncharacterised bacterial proteins. It is found N-terminal to [pfam:PF24736]. This domain is predicted to adopt a globular structure composed of four alpha- helices.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7691)
description: This entry represents a group of uncharacterised bacterial proteins. They share detectable similarity to proteins members of [pfam:PF08974] whose function is unknown. Their predicted structures resemble the structure of DNA mimic protein DMP12 but elaborated with additional alpha helices.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7692)
description: This domain is found in a group of proteins from Halobacteria. It is predicted to adopt a structure that is reminiscent of ribbon-helix-helix fold. Members of this entry are likely to form dimers. They have a stretch of positively charged residues at the N terminus.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7693)
description: This entry represents a group of uncharacterised bacterial proteins. They are predicted to adopt a globular structure consisting of a five-stranded antiparallel beta-sheet and helices packed on one side of it.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7694)
description: This entry represents a domain found in uncharacterised bacterial proteins. They are predicted to adopt a globular structure consisting of an antiparallel beta-sheet and alpha helix packed on it. Most members contain a highly conserved HhW sequence motif where h is hydrophobic residue.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7695)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised bacterial proteins. It contains a pair of conserved cysteines and it is predicted to adopt a fold which is typical for zinc-ribbon domains.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7696)
description: This entry represents a small uncharacterised protein family. Members are composed of an N-terminal beta hairpin followed by three alpha helices.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7697)
description: This entry represents a small family of uncharacterised proteins. Although apparently having a bacterial origin these proteins appear in genomic contexts suggesting they are part of an integrated phage genome. Structurally these proteins are composed of a beta hairpin followed by a pair of alpha helices.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7698)
description: This entry represents a domain from uncharacterised proteins found mainly in Firmicutes. It is predicted to adopt a globular structure consisting of a curved beta-sheet and alpha-helices packed on one side of it. It contains a number of conserved aromatic hydrophobic residues, some of which are predicted to be solvent-exposed.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7699)
description: This domain of unknown function is found in Zinc finger CCCH domain-containing protein 62 from Oryza sativa (C3H62) and similar proteins from plants. Members of this family also show a SAP domain ([pfam:PF02037]). This domain is predicted to adopt a mainly beta configuration.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7700)
description: This domain is usually found in tandem in uncharacterised bacterial proteins. It is predicted to adopt a globular structure consisting of a curved anti-parallel beta-sheet and alpha helices packed on one side of it. It contains highly conserved aspartate and histidine residues that may constitute a metal binding site.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7701)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised proteins mainly from bacteria. It is predicted to adopt an alpha-helical structure with a highly conserved DVHDxWxxW sequence motif which may constitute a ligand binding site. This domain is likely to form a homodimer. Investigation of STRING networks suggests this protein may functionally interact with [pfam:PF24838] a likely octameric membrane complex.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7702)
description: This entry represents a domain found in uncharacterised proteins mainly from fungi. It has a detectable similarity to domains members of Lipid-translocating exporter superfamily and are predicted to adopt similar structure.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7703)
description: This domain is found in a group of uncharacterised proteins mainly from fungi. It is predicted to contain seven transmembrane helices.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7704)
description: This domain is found in a group of uncharacterised eukaryotic proteins. It has a detectable similarity to Tumor protein p53-inducible protein 11 (TP53I11) and it is predicted to adopt similar structure.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7705)
description: This domain is found in a group of uncharacterised plant proteins. It has remote similarity to some glucanases and it is predicted to adopt similar beta-sandwich structure but elaborated with additional strands.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7706)
description: This entry represents an uncharacterised family of bacterial proteins. Structure prediction ([swissprot:B2VAQ8] AF3 iPTM=0.93) suggests that these proteins form dimers. The monomer is composed of three alpha helices. STRING provides some weak evidence that these proteins may be immunity proteins or perhaps part of a plasmid addiction system.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7707)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised fungal proteins. It contains a set of highly conserved cysteine residues that are predicted to form disulfide bonds. It is likely that proteins containing this domain are secreted.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7708)
description: This domain is found N-terminal in uncharacterised fungal proteins. It shares detectable similarity to the N-terminal domain of NACHT proteins and it is predicted to adopt similar structure.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7709)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised proteins. It is predicted to adopt a globular structure consisting of array of helices followed by a beta-hairpin.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7710)
description: This entry represents a small family of uncharacterised bacterial proteins.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7711)
description: This entry represents a small family of uncharacterised Actinomycete proteins. These proteins may form homodimers (AlphaFold3 A6WE73 ipTM = 0.79). The dimerisation is mediated by a C-terminal alpha helical subdomain.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7712)
description: This entry represents a small family of uncharacterised bacterial proteins.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7713)
description: This entry represents a protein domain that forms an intimate self-self dimer. The domain is found at the C-terminus of proteins that often have a [pfam:PF24735] domain.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7714)
description: This entry represents a group of uncharacterised prokaryotic proteins. They are likely to contain two domains that create a compact elongated structure. Toward the C terminus, these proteins have two highly conserved pairs of cysteines which are likely to be involved in metal coordination.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7715)
description: This entry represents a family of uncharacterised actinobacterial proteins that are related to [pfam:PF20115].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7716)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised bacterial proteins either standalone or in combination with other domains. It is predicted to adopt a globular structure consisting of an antiparallel three-stranded beta-sheet and alpha-helices packed on one side of it.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7717)
description: This entry represents a group of uncharacterised proteins mainly from tailed bacteriophages.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7718)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised prokaryotic proteins. It is predicted to adopt alpha/beta structure consisting of a meander beta-sheet and a kinked alpha-helix. It contains several conserved aspartate and histidine residues that are predicted to come close in space and may constitute a metal binding site.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7719)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised proteins mainly from fungi. It is predicted to fold into three transmembrane helices.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7720)
description: This entry represents a small domain found in streptococcal phage proteins. Structurally the domain is composed of a three stranded beta sheet followed by an alpha helix.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7721)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised proteins from fungi. It is predicted to adopt globular structure consisting of array of helices.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7722)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised plant proteins. It is predicted to contain helix-extended loop-helix (HeH) structure and has similarity to domains containing this motif.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7723)
description: This small family of uncharacterised bacterial proteins are often found adjacent to proteins from [pfam:PF13711]. Structure prediction shows that these proteins are very likely to form a complex.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7724)
description: This entry represents a family of bacterial proteins composed of an all beta strand domain composed of 7 beta strands. Structure prediction suggests that these proteins will form a complex with proteins from [pfam:PF24848].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7725)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised plan proteins. It has detectable similarity to winged helix HTH domains and it is predicted to adopt similar structure.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7726)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised fungal proteins. It has detectable similarity to HTH domains and it is predicted to adopt similar structure.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7727)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised fungal proteins. It has detectable similarity to proteins members of the Cytochrome b558 subunit alpha family and it is predicted to adopt similar structure composed of four helices.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7728)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised fungal proteins. It is predicted to fold into a beta-sandwich. It contains highly conserved cysteine residues that are predicted to form a disulfide bond.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7729)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised fungal proteins. It is predicted to adopt a globular structure consisting of array of alpha helices. It contains several conserved cysteine residues that are predicted to form disulfide bonds. It is likely that the proteins containing this domain are secreted.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7730)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised fungal proteins. It contains a highly conserved EXR sequence motif.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7731)
description: This entry represents a domain found in uncharacterised plant proteins. It contains a set of conserved cysteines that are predicted to form disulfide bonds.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7732)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised proteins mainly from fungi. It contains a set of conserved cysteine residues which are predicted to form a disulfide bond.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7733)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised proteins mainly from plants. It is predicted to fold into a structure consisting of six transmembrane helices.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7734)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised proteins. It is predicted to adopt globular structure consisting of a curved beta-sheet and alpha-helices packed on one side of it. It contains a semi-conserved FKGFSS sequence motif.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7735)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised proteins mainly from fungi. It is predicted to form a globular structure consisting of alpha-helices. It contains a set of conserved cysteine residues which are predicted to form disulfide bridges.

name: DUF2110 N-terminal domain
description: This domain, found in various hypothetical archaeal proteins, has no known function. It is found at the N-terminus of the DUF2110 family proteins.

name: DUF2110 C-terminal domain
description: This domain, found in various hypothetical archaeal proteins, has no known function. It is found at the C-terminus of DUF2110 family proteins.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7736)
description: This entry represents a small family of bacterial and phage proteins that are uncharacterised. The domain is composed of three alpha helices, which dimerise to create a larger structure. Some members of the families contain two copies of this domain, most appear to homodimerise.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7737)
description: This domain is found in proteins that contain [pfam:PF13569]. The function of this domain is unknown.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7738)
description: This entry represents a family of uncharacterised bacterial protein domains. The structure of these proteins shows some structural similarity to the PePSy domain.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7739)
description: This entry includes the Shigella phage Sf6 gene 22 protein [swissprot:Q716F3].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7740)
description: This entry represents a family of phage proteins. The core structure of these proteins is a conserved four helix bundle. The function of these proteins is unknown.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7741)
description: This is a presumed domain found in a group of uncharacterised sequences from worms. This domain may consist of eight beta-strands.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7742)
description: This entry represents a likely uncharacterised phage protein. The protein is composed of three alpha helices.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7743)
description: This is a presumed domain of unknown function found in uncharacterised proteins from Dictyosteliales. It may adopt a Ig-like fold.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7744)
description: This entry represents the C-terminal domain of a small set of proteins belonging to the [pfam:PF04465]. Structure prediction suggests that this domain may mediate dimerisation.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7745)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised proteins mainly from plants. It has detectable similarity to plant mobile domains and it is predicted to adopt similar structure.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7746)
description: This presumed domain is found in a group of plant sequences, whose function is unknown. This domain may adopt a three-helical bundle fold similar to that found in viral Gag proteins.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7747)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised protein ZK892.6 from Caenorhabditis elegans and related proteins. It is found either standalone or in combination with other domains. Some proteins contain multiple copies of this domain. It is predicted to adopt a globular structure consisting of an antiparallel six-stranded beta-sheet and alpha-helices packed on both sides of it. This domain contains a highly conserved PxxPP motif.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7748)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised proteins from plants. It is predicted to fold into a beta-sandwich.

name: GlfB-like, C-terminal domain
description: This domain is found at the C-terminal of Ras guanine nucleotide exchange factor glfB from Dictyostelium discoideum and in similar uncharacterised proteins from lower eukaryotes. GflB is a GpaB-activated, rapA-specific guanine nucleotide exchange factor, involved in the regulation of the balance between Ras and Rap signalling at the leading edge of chemotaxing cells [[cite:PUB00159973],[cite:PUB00159975]]. This protein also acts as a key regulator of antin -driven membrane protrusions during processes such as phagocytosis and cytokinesis, possibly by modulating rapA signalling pathways [[cite:PUB00159974]]. This domain is predicted to adopt a globular a/b structure.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7750)
description: This is a domain of unknown function found in plant sequences. It may adopt a three-helical bundle fold.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7751)
description: This domain is found in a group of uncharacterised plant proteins with the AAA domain ([pfam:PF00004]). This domain is predicted to adopt an all alpha configuration.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7752)
description: This domain is found in a group of uncharacterised animal proteins that also contain [pfam:PF05183]. This domain is predicted to adopt a mainly alpha helical structure. Its specific function is unknown.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7753)
description: This is a presumed domain found at the C-terminal of a group of worm proteins. This domain may adopt a hairpin fold.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7754)
description: This is a presumed domain found at the C-terminal of worm proteins. It may be related to BACK domains.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7755)
description: This is a domain of unknown function found in plants. This domain is structurally related to Lipase/lipooxygenase domain (PLAT/LH2 domain).

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7756)

This domain interacts with Ypt35 which recruits VPS13 to endosomal and vacuolar membranes, and with Mcp1 to target VPS13 at mitochondria. Defects in the human protein VPS13A cause chorea-acanthocytosis, an autosomal recessive neurodegenerative disorder [[cite:PUB00100501],[cite:PUB00016718]]. In plants, this domain is found to be the region which interacts with SHR or the SHORT-ROOT transcription factor, a regulator of root-growth and asymmetric cell division that separates ground tissue into endodermis and cortex.
