name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7881) N-terminal domain
description: This entry represents the N-terminal domain of unknown function found in Trypanosoma proteins. According to structure predictions it could adopt a DNA clamp fold.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7883)
description: This entry represents a domain of unknown function (DUF) identified in Trypanosoma. Based on structural predictions, this domain is hypothesised to adopt a winged helix-turn-helix (HTH) fold. Winged helix DNA-binding proteins share a characteristic winged helix-turn-helix DNA-binding motif, in which the \u0022wings\u0022, or loops, are small beta-sheets [[cite:PUB00013195]].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7884)
description: This domain is found in a group of uncharacterised bacterial proteins. It is usually found associated with methyltransferase domains such as [pfam:PF13489] and [pfam:PF13649] and is predicted to adopt an alpha-beta configuration. It has a conserved motif F/YWDG.

name: F-box/LRR-repeat protein 15, leucine rich repeat domain
description: This domain represents a set of tandem leucine rich repeats found in human F-box/LRR-repeat protein 15 (FBXL15) and similar eukaryotic proteins. FBXL15 is the substrate recognition component of a SCF (SKP1-CUL1-F-box protein), an E3 ubiquitin-protein ligase complex which mediates the ubiquitination and subsequent proteasomal degradation of SMURF1, thereby acting as a positive regulator of the BMP signalling pathway. It is required for dorsal/ventral pattern formation and bone mass maintenance [[cite:PUB00147666]].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7886)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised proteins from animals and plants. It is predicted to adopt an unique complex alpha/beta structure.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7887)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised plant proteins. It is predicted to contain two transmembrane helices.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7888)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised fungal proteins. It is predicted to fold into alpha-beta-beta sandwich. It has two pairs of conserved cysteine residues that are predicted to form disulfide bonds.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7889)
description: This presumed domain is found in a group of fungal uncharacterised proteins that also contain [pfam:PF12906] and [pfam:PF23113]. It has highly conserved E and L residues.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7890)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised plant proteins. It is predicted to contain two short alpha-helices. At the N-terminus, it contains a number of highly conserved positively charged residues.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7891)
description: This domain is found in a group of uncharacterised fungal sequences that also contain [pfam:PF00069]. It has a conserved I/LWG motif.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7892)
description: This predicted domain is found in a group of uncharacterised fungal proteins that also contain an F-box domain. This domain is predicted to adopt a winged helix fold.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7893)
description: This predicted winged helix domain is found in a group of uncharacterised fungal proteins. It is often found associated with [pfam:PF00145].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7894)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised plant proteins. It is predicted to fold into a alpha/beta structure with a central mixed beta-sheet and alpha-helices packed on both sides. The predicted structure has a topological similarity to PACT family domains members of [pfam:PF09754].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7895)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised plant proteins. It contains four pairs of highly conserved cysteine residues that may be involved in metal coordination. It also contains a highly conserved CxxCxGxG sequence motif.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7896)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised proteins from fungi. It contains two pairs of conserved cysteine and histidine residues that may be involved in metal coordination.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7897)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised proteins predominantly from bacteria. It is predicted to adopt a complex alpha/beta structure. These proteins share similarity with the Clan MA zinc-dependent metallopeptidases.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7898)
description: This entry describes the N-terminal domain of unknown function of DNA polymerase theta subunit (PolQ) majoritarily from fungal and and yeast proteins. Structural predictions suggest that this family adopts Helix-Helix-Helix (HHH) motifs. Proteins containing HHH motifs are typically associated with DNA-binding functions. These structural elements are often found in enzymes involved in DNA metabolism, such as DNA polymerases and helicases [[cite:PUB00101275],[cite:PUB00021052]].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7899)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised plant proteins. It is predicted to adopt an eight-bladed beta-propeller.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7900)
description: This domain is found at the C-terminal end of a group of uncharacterised plant proteins. It is often found associated to [pfam:PF06839]. It has a conserved motif GWQK.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7901)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised bacterial proteins. It is predicted to adopt a beta-sandwich structure with significant topological similarity to known galactose-binding domains, in particular to lectin-like domain of the Cwp84, a surface layer associated protein of Clostridium difficile. It is likely that this domain is involved carbohydrate binding.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7902)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised bacterial proteins. It is predicted to adopt a three-helical bundle with some topological similarity to spectrin.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7903)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised plant proteins. It has detectable similarity to members of the CYTH-like phosphatase superfamily and it is predicted to adopt similar structure.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7904)
description: This gelsolin-like domain is found in a group of uncharacterised fungal proteins. Its function is unknown.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7905)
description: This domain is found in the Uncharacterized protein C582.04c from Schizosaccharomyces pombe and related proteins. It has detectable similarity to domains members of the CYTH-like phosphatase superfamily and it is predicted to adopt similar structure.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7906)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised plant proteins. It is predicted to adopt a globular alpha/beta structure.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7907)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised fungal proteins. It is predicted to adopt beta-Trefoil fold. It is probably distantly related to domains members of [pfam:PF22799].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7908)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised fungal proteins. It is predicted to adopt beta-Trefoil fold.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7909)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised fungal proteins. It is predicted to adopt beta-Trefoil fold.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7910)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised plant proteins. It is predicted to adopt beta-Trefoil fold. It is closely related to members of Fascin [pfam:PF06268].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7911)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised nematode proteins. It is predicted to fold into a five-bladed beta-propeller.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7912)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised plant proteins. It is predicted to adopt an SH3-like fold.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7913)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised plant proteins. It is predicted to fold into an array of four alpha-helices.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7914)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised proteins mainly from Trypanosomes. It is predicted to fold into a seven-bladed beta-propeller.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7915)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised plant proteins. It is predicted to fold into an alpha/beta structure consisting of a central mixed beta-sheet and alpha-helices packed on both sides. It is usually found upstream DUF7913 ([pfam:PF25500]).

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7916)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised bacterial proteins. It is predicted to adopt a TIM-barrel structure. It shares detectable similarity with Mycobacterium tuberculosis Indole-3-glycerol phosphate synthase (TrpC).

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7917)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised bacterial proteins. It is predicted to adopt a three alpha-helical bundle. It is usually found in combination with [pfam:PF23916].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7918)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised fungal proteins. It is predicted to fold into a beta-sandwich structure.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7919)
description: This entry represents a family of uncharacterised bacterial proteins. This domain likely contains a zinc binding site.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7920)
description: This entry represents a domain of unknown function found mostly in Trypanosoma. According to structure predictions it could adopt an ATP-grasp fold which is characterised by two alpha-beta subdomains that grasp the ATP molecules between them [[cite:PUB00020972],[cite:PUB00015342]].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7921)
description: This entry represent the domain of unknown function found in Drosophila. According to structure predictions, it may adopt fybronectin type I module (FN1) fold.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7922)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised bacterial proteins. It is found sometimes in combination with (DUF6128) [pfam:PF19623]. This domains is predicted to adopt a beta-sandwich with an Ig-like topology.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7923)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised fungal proteins. It has detectable similarity to known PIN domains, in particular to NYN domain, and it is predicted to adopt a similar structure.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7924)
description: This entry represents a domain found in uncharacterised fungal proteins. It has a remote similarity to members of the PD-(D/E)XK nuclease superfamily and it is likely to adopt similar structure with a conserved active site architecture.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7925)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised proteins predominantly from cyanobacteria. It is predicted to fold into a beta-sandwich. Some members are likely to contain an isopeptide bond.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7926)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised bacterial proteins mainly from Actinomycetes. It is predicted to fold into a beta-sandwich with topological similarity to domains members of the adhesin superfamily. Most members contain conserved lysine aspartate and asparagine residues that are likely to form an isopeptide bond. This domain is frequently found in combination with DUF5979.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7927)
description: This domain of unknown function is found in multiple copies in a number of bacterial proteins. It is closely related to domains represented by DUF11 ([pfam:PF01345]). Similarly to DUF11, this domain contains a conserved N-terminal lysine and a C-terminal asparagine with central aspartate/glutamate residues suggesting that it may contain an isopeptide bond.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7928)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised proteins mainly from fungi. It is predicted to fold into an alpha/beta structure with topological similarity to AraD-like domains.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7929)
description: This domain is found in a very small group of proteins mainly from Phyllobacteriaceae. It is predicted to fold into a beta-sandwich with topological similarity to domains members of the adhesin superfamily. Members contain conserved lysine, aspartate and asparagine residues that are likely to form an isopeptide bond.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7930)
description: This entry represents a C-terminal OB-fold domain found in nematode proteins that generally contain 3 OB-like domains.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7931)
description: This entry represents a domain of unknown function mostly found in bacteria. According to structure predictions it might adopt a phospholipase D/nuclease fold. Whilst the typical phospholipase D motif HxK(x)4D(x)6GSxN is not strictly conserved the overall fold suggests a potential distant evolutionary relationship to the PLD superfamily. The PLD nucleases can have endonuclease or exonuclease activity. These enzymes use the imidazole group of histidine as a nucleophile in their catalytic mechanism [[cite:PUB00152066],[cite:PUB00160607],[cite:PUB00024729]].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7932)
description: This entry describes a domain of unknown function located at the N-terminal of proteins mostly found in fungi. According to structure predictions it might adopt an immunoglobulin, fibronectin type III fold. It is formed of two antiparallel beta-sheets stacked against each other, forming a beta-sandwich [[cite:PUB00158558]].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7933)
description: This domain of unknown function is found in multiple copies in a number of bacterial proteins. It is closely related to domains represented by DUF11 ([pfam:PF01345]). Some members, similarly to DUF11, contains a conserved N-terminal lysine and a C-terminal asparagine with central aspartate/glutamate residues suggesting that they may contain an isopeptide bond.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7934)
description: This entry represents a family of uncharacterised proteins found in Bacillota species. From genomic context it is likely to be a phage derived protein. It contains a helical domain composed of segments from the N-terminus and C-terminus connected by a coiled coil region.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7935)
description: This entry represents an uncharacterised protein family. Structure prediction suggests that these proteins form a membrane bound octameric complex. The N-terminus of the protein contains an transmembrane alpha helix and the rest of the protein adopts a four helical bundle domain. This family is often found associated with gliding motility proteins in STRING networks.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7936)
description: This entry represents a small family of uncharacterised phage proteins. Structure prediction shows a compact domain composed of a three stranded beta sheet followed by two alpha helices packed on one side of the sheet.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7937)
description: This entry represents a family of uncharacterised membrane proteins found in Actinomycetes. These proteins contain 12 putative transmembrane helices.

name: Phage family of unknown function (DUF7938)
description: This entry found in a small number of phage is uncharacterised. There is some evidence form AlphaFold 3 prediction that these proteins may form homodimers.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7939)
description: This entry is a small alpha-helical domain found at the C-terminus of proteins a family of uncharacterised bacterial proteins that have a set of beta sandwich domains towards the N-terminus including [pfam:PF13584].

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7940)
description: This family contains a set of uncharacterised bacterial and phage proteins that are annotated as putative holins.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7941)
description: This entry represents an uncharacterised family of phage proteins from Uroviricota. These proteins are about 300 amino acids in length. They may represent phage structural proteins.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7942)
description: This family of uncharacterised bacterial proteins is found mainly in Actinomycetes. Members of this family are predicted to contain three transmembrane helices. A member of this family, SCO4225, is a putative integral membrane protein found in Streptomyces coelicolor, [swissprot:Q9FCE5]. The gene encoding SCO4225 is part of a cluster of genes (phoU to sco4225) that are involved in phosphate regulation and metabolism. This gene cluster is regulated by the two-component system PhoR-PhoP, which responds to phosphate availability in the environment [[cite:PUB00159567]]. The expression of SCO4225 is directly regulated by MacR, a response regulator that binds to a specific sequence in the promoter region of SCO4225. This regulation links SCO4225 to other genes in the MacR regulon, many of which are also membrane proteins [[cite:PUB00159414]].

name: Family of unknown function (DUF5983) N-terminal domain
description: This family of proteins are likely to be phage derived. This domain likely forms a homodimeric structure composed of three beta strands provided by each monomer, with one strand swapped with the other monomer.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7943)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised bacterial proteins. It is predicted to fold into an alpha- helical bundle. This domain is found in the hypothetical protein ESA_00282 from Cronobacter sakazakii that plays a significant role in biofilm formation and bacterial adhesion. This protein contributes to the adhesion of C. sakazakii to biotic surfaces, such as intestinal epithelial cells and play a role in the pathogenesis [[cite:PUB00159769]].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7944)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised bacterial proteins mainly from Moraxellales. It is predicted to fold into an array of alpha-helices. It contains two invariant cysteine residues which are predicted to form a disulfide bond.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7945)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised bacterial proteins predominantly from Actinomycetes. It is predicted to fold into array of alpha-helices.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7946)
description: This entry represents a domain of unknown function found at the N-terminus of a set of bacterial and phage proteins. It is often associated with a C-terminal small beta barrel domain.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7947)
description: This entry represents a domain of unknown function found at the C-terminus of a set of bacterial and phage proteins. It forms small five stranded beta barrel domain.

name: N-terminal domain of DUF1619
description: This is domain is found N-terminal in tectonic proteins (TCTN1/2/3) It contains a number of conserved cysteine residues predicted to form disulfide bonds. Although function of this domain is currently unknown, studies on TCTN2 suggest that it is indispensable for its functions [[cite:PUB00097826],[cite:PUB00097827]]. TCTN1, TCTN2, and TCTN3 are members of the tectonic protein family that play crucial roles in ciliogenesis and ciliary function. While they share some common functions, each protein also has specific roles in the process of cilia formation and maintenance. These proteins interact with several other ciliopathy proteins, forming a complex known as the Tectonic ciliopathy complex. This complex is required for hedgehog signalling transduction and regulation of ciliary membrane composition [[cite:PUB00069722],[cite:PUB00160606]].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7948)
description: This entry represents a potential adhesive domain found at the N-terminus of a variety of bacterial cell surface proteins. The structure shows a large beta sandwich fold.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7949)
description: This entry describes a domain of unknown function in putative EGF-like domain-containing proteins found in eukaryotes, mainly ameobas. According to structure predictions it adopts an EGF-like fold which contain six conserved cysteine residues. The EGF-like fold has two-stranded beta-sheets followed by a loop to a short C-termini. It usually occurs in tandem repeats [[cite:PUB00001555]]. The domain described by this entry has the 6 conserved cysteine residues. It also acquires a similar structure to the EGF-like fold and it is 40 amino acids long.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7950)
description: This entry represents a domain of unknown function in a group of uncharacterised proteins mainly from plants and prokaryotes. According to structure predictions it adopts a sensor-like fold, consisting of 7 beta-strands arranged in a beta-barrel like fold, surrounded by a small alpha-helix.

name: Repeat of unknown function (DUF7951)
description: This entry describes a repeat of unknown function found at the C-terminal of uncharacterised proteins mainly from animals. It displays a TPR fold.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7952)
description: This entry represents a domain of unknown function found in putative SANT domain-containing proteins and uncharacterised proteins found in plants. This domain is predicted to adopt an EF-hand-like fold. The EF-hand fold is a helix-loop-helix motif that can bind calcium atoms. The EF-hand fold is usually tandemly repeated, and the number of repeats ranges from two to eight [[cite:PUB00023098]].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7953)
description: The domain described by this entry is located towards the N-terminal in putative transmembrane and uncharacterised proteins found in plants. It is predicted to adopt a C2 fold. C2 domains are membrane-binding modules that share a common overall fold: a single compact greek-key motif organised as an eight-stranded anti-parallel beta-sandwich consisting of a pair of four-stranded beta-sheets [[cite:PUB00160608]].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7954)
description: This domain is found at the N-terminus of a range of spirochete proteins. Based on structural similarity to LolA these proteins are likely to be involved in lipid transport.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7955)
description: This entry represents a C-terminal domain found in a family of spirochete proteins that are likely involved in lipid transport.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7956)
description: This entry corresponds to a mycobacterial domain of unknown function that shows structural similarity to [pfam:PF04603].

name: DUF6242 beta propeller domain
description: This entry represents the C-terminal beta propeller domain of this family.

name: DUF6311 C-terminal domain
description: This entry represents a C-terminal domain found in a presumed integral membrane domain is functionally uncharacterised.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7957)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised protein from Halogeometricum borinquense (Hbor_03000) and related prokaryotic proteins. This protein is found next to a toxic gene Hbor_02990 and is likely a immunity protein which is able to prevent self-intoxication [[cite:PUB00160456]]. This domain is predicted to fold into three four-stranded beta-sheets that pack in a similar way as blades in beta-propellers.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7958)
description: This entry represents uncharacterised protein from Halogeometricum borinquense (Hbor_38910) and related archaeal proteins. This protein is found next to a toxic gene Hbor_38900 and is likely a immunity protein which is able to prevent self-intoxication [[cite:PUB00160456]]. This protein is predicted to adopt a complex alpha/beta structure with an unique topology.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7959)
description: This entry represents a ferredoxin-like fold domain found at the C-terminus of a range of proteins that contain LolA-like domains suggesting these proteins may act as lipoprotein chaperones. The function of this domain is uncertain.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7960)
description: This entry represents an uncharacterised family found in Methanobacteriota. Structure prediction suggests that this protein binds to a zinc ion. This family includes gene HVO_1405 from Haloferax volcanii.

name: DUF7961 N-terminal domain
description: This domain has a restriction endonuclease-like structure, suggesting this protein may function as an endonuclease.

name: DUF7961 C-terminal domain
description: This domain is found to the C-terminus of a restriction endonuclease-like domain [pfam:PF25902]. Many members of this family contain two copies of this domain. The structure of the domain forms a small partial beta barrel.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8564)
description: This entry represents an uncharacterised halobacterial protein family. This family is surprisingly composed of half a TIM-barrel fold, related to the [pfam:PF01261] domain found in xylose isomerase.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7962)
description: This entry describes a domain of unknown function predominantly found in bacteria and fungi. It is often associated with pfam:PF13471 which is located at the N-terminal. This domain forms an all alpha-helical bundle and shows structural similarity to the C-terminal domain of glutathione S-transferase (GST).

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7963)
description: This entry represents the domain of unknown function found in putative BED-type domain containing proteins and in uncharacterised plant proteins. This domain is predicted to adopt a beta-beta-alpha zinc finger fold.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7964)
description: This entry represents a family of uncharacterised proteins from halobacteria. These proteins contains a conserved LPXXXP motif towards the N-terminus.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7965)
description: This entry represents a small family of uncharacterised halobacterial integral membrane proteins. These proteins have four transmembrane helices with the N and C-terminus likely being cytoplasmic.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7966)
description: This entry represents a small family of uncharacterised halobacterial proteins. Structure prediction shows that these proteins form a non-compact fold composed of four alpha helices. There is weak evidence from structure prediction that this protein may form a domain swapped homodimer

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7967)
description: This entry represents a family of uncharacterised halobacterial proteins. The domain adopts a compact domain structure composed of a twisted 5 stranded sheet with a C-terminal alpha helix.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7968)
description: This entry represents a family of uncharacterised halobacterial proteins. The protein assumes a compact domain structure with an N-terminal helix that is packed onto the concave face of a twisted four stranded beta sheet.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7969)
description: This entry represents a family of uncharacterised halobacterial proteins that adopt a small beta sandwich domain structure with a glycine rich C-terminal tail.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7970)
description: This entry represents a family of uncharacterised proteins found in halobacteria. Proteins in this family are predicted to adopt a series of four alpha helices that do not form a compact domain. There is weak evidence for a homodimer from structure prediction.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7971)
description: This entry represents a family of uncharacterised proteins found in halobacteria. The proteins are composed of four alpha helices.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7972)
description: This entry represents a family of uncharacterised proteins found in halobacteria. These proteins are about 350-400 amino acids in length. These proteins form a large all alpha helical fold. These proteins may be integral membrane proteins.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7973)
description: This entry represents a family of uncharacterised integral membrane proteins found in halobacteria.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7974)
description: This entry represents a family of uncharacterised proteins found in halobacteria. These proteins have an immunoglobulin-like domain.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7975)
description: This entry represents a family of uncharacterised proteins found in halobacteria.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7976)
description: This entry represents a family of uncharacterised proteins found in halobacteria. Structure prediction suggests this protein forms a loose arrangement of three alpha helices.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7977)
description: This entry represents a family of uncharacterised integral membrane proteins found in halobacteria. These proteins contain a pair of likely transmembrane helices at the C-terminal end.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7978)
description: This entry represents a family of uncharacterised integral proteins found in halobacteria.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7979)
description: This entry represents a family of uncharacterised proteins found in halobacteria. Some members of this protein have an N-terminal lipoprotein attachment motif.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7980)
description: This entry represents a family of largely cyanobacterial proteins of unknown function. Predictions of structure suggest a non-globular alpha helical fold.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7981)
description: This entry represents a family of uncharacterised integral membrane proteins found in halobacteria. These small proteins are composed of two transmembrane alpha helices.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7982)
description: This entry represents a family of uncharacterised proteins found in halobacteria.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7983)
description: This entry represents a family of uncharacterised halobacterial proteins.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7984)
description: This entry represents a family of uncharacterised proteins found in halobacteria. These proteins are about 160 amino acids in length and have an alpha helical domain fold. Shows structural similarity to the YutG/PgpA superfamily, which includes Phosphatidylglycerophosphatase. Thus this family may represent a similar enzyme.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7985)
description: This entry represents a family of uncharacterised proteins found in halobacteria.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7986)
description: This entry represents an uncharacterised family of bacterial proteins. The predicted structure shows a 5 stranded beta barrel elaborated with many alpha helical elements.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7987)
description: This entry represents a family of uncharacterised integral membrane proteins found in halobacteria. Proteins in this family contain two conserved transmembrane helices.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7988)
description: This entry represents a family of uncharacterised proteins found in halobacteria.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7989)
description: This entry represents uncharacterised proteins from Halobacteria. They small in size (~80 aa) and are predicted to be largely disordered.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7990)
description: This family represents a set of bacterial and archaeal proteins that are uncharacterised. Many proteins in the family have a CC-Star motif (Cys-Cys-COOH).

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7991)
description: This entry represents a family of uncharacterised integral membrane proteins found in halobacteria. These proteins have three transmembrane alpha helices.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7992)
description: This entry represents a family of uncharacterised proteins found in halobacteria.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7993)
description: This entry represents a family of uncharacterised proteins found in halobacteria.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7994)
description: This entry represents a family of uncharacterised integral membrane proteins found in halobacteria. These proteins have four predicted transmembrane helices.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7995)
description: This entry represents a family of uncharacterised proteins found in halobacteria. These proteins are about 160 amino acids in length. The proteins contain small beta sheet which has two adjacent strands contributed by the N and C-terminus of the protein.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7996)
description: This entry represents a family of uncharacterised integral membrane proteins found in halobacteria. These proteins contain two predicted transmembrane helices.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7997)
description: This entry represents the N-terminal beta sandwich domain found in a family of likely halobacterial carbohydrate phosphorylase enzymes.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF7998)
description: This entry represents a family of uncharacterised proteins found in halobacteria.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF7999)
description: This entry represents a family of uncharacterised proteins found in halobacteria. These proteins are small and adopt a five stranded beta barrel fold.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF8000)
description: This entry represents a family of uncharacterised integral membrane proteins found in halobacteria. These proteins contain two predicted transmembrane helices.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF8001)
description: This entry represents a family of uncharacterised proteins found in halobacteria. These proteins are about 80 amino acids in length and adopt a compact fold composed of a 5 stranded beta sheet with two alpha helices packed on one side. The sheet has a simple 1-2-3-4-5 topology of strands.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF8002)
description: This entry represents a family of uncharacterised proteins found in halobacteria. Proteins in this family form a compact structure with two long beta strands and an alpha helix. These proteins are predicted to form homooligomeric complexes. These proteins likely form large oligomeric ring complexes (E4NL25 14mer ipTM=0.84 pTM=0.85). The function of this complex are not known.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8003)
description: This is a domain rich in cysteines often found several times in a group of uncharacterised eukaryotic proteins. Many members of this family are annotated as tyrosine-protein kinases.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8004)

description: This domain is found at the N-terminal end of Scytalone dehydratase-like protein Arp1 from Metarhizium brunneum and similar fungal proteins. Arp1 is part of the Pks2 gene cluster that encode for proteins that mediate the formation of infectious structures (appressoria), enabling these fungi to kill insects faster [[cite:PUB00095155]]. name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8017)

name: VP3-like

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8050)
description: Members of this integral membrane protein family are found exclusively in halophilic archaea. In at least three species (Haloarcula marismortui, Haloquadratum walsbyi, and Haloferax volcanii), members are found in the gene neighbourhood of archaeosortase A, suggesting a role in protein sorting. Structure prediction show these proteins have four likely transmembrane helices, with a four stranded beta meander inserted between helices one and two. The structure of this domain shows significant structural similarity to claudin proteins. This suggests that these proteins may be accessory components of an as yet unidentified membrane complex.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8097)
description: This entry represents a family of small transmembrane proteins found exclusively in extremely halophilic archaea (Halobacteria). Members of this family typically contain two transmembrane helices with a conserved cytoplasmic region. Most proteins in this family are approximately 115-130 amino acids in length. The family is widely distributed across different genera within Halobacteriales, including Halococcus, Haloferax, Natrialba, Natronobacterium, and Haladaptatus. The specific function of these proteins remains unknown, but their conservation suggests they may play an important role in the adaptation to high-salt environments.

The proteins in this family are predominantly found in halophilic archaea, specifically within the Halobacteria class. The family includes proteins from various genera such as Haloarculaceae, Natrialbaceae, and Haloferacaceae. Proteins in this family typically range from 320 to 400 amino acids in length.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF8099)

The proteins containing this domain are predominantly found in the class Halobacteria, which is part of the Methanobacteriota phylum. This domain is typically found in proteins ranging from 57 to 88 amino acids in length.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8100)

Proteins in this family are predominantly found in the order Halobacteriales, including genera such as Halobacterium, Haladaptatus, and Halonotius. The proteins in this family typically range from 145 to 227 amino acids in length. These proteins are predicted to be integral membrane proteins, as they contain multiple transmembrane helices.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8101)
description: This entry represents a domain from a family of uncharacterised proteins found predominantly in the Halobacteria class of Archaea. The proteins containing this domain are primarily distributed among members of the Haloarculaceae and Haloferacaceae families. The domain is typically found in proteins ranging from 85 to 117 amino acids in length. The domain adopts a four helical bundle structure.

name: Domain of unknown function
description: This entry represents a domain from a family of uncharacterised proteins found in the class Halobacteria. The proteins containing this domain are predominantly found in archaea, specifically within the order Halobacteriales. The domain is typically found in proteins ranging from 150 to 220 amino acids in length.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8103)
description: This entry represents a domain from a family of uncharacterised proteins in the Halobacteria class of Archaea. Proteins containing this domain are found predominantly in the order Halobacteriales, with representatives in families such as Haloferacaceae and Halobacteriaceae. The domain is typically found in proteins ranging from 73 to 103 amino acids in length.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF8104)
description: This entry represents a domain from a family of uncharacterised proteins in archaea. The proteins in this family are predominantly found in the class Halobacteria, which includes organisms such as Haloferacaceae and Halobacteriales. The proteins in this family typically range from 124 to 143 amino acids in length. Many proteins in this family contain predicted coiled-coil regions.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF8105)
description: This entry represents a domain from a family of uncharacterised proteins in halobacteria. The proteins in this family are predominantly found in archaea, specifically within the Halobacteria class. The taxonomic distribution includes genera such as Halorubrum, Haloquadratum, and Haloarcula, among others. The proteins in this family are typically around 116 to 118 amino acids in length. Some proteins in this family are associated with plasmids, suggesting potential roles in horizontal gene transfer or adaptation. The subcellular localization of these proteins is not well-defined, but they may contain zinc finger-like motifs, indicating potential roles in nucleic acid binding or protein-protein interactions.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8106)
description: This entry represents a domain from a family of uncharacterised domain in the Halobacteria class of Archaea. The proteins in this family are predominantly found in various families within the Halobacteriales order, including Natrialbaceae, Haloferacaceae, and Haloarculaceae. The domain is typically found in proteins ranging from 58 to 130 amino acids in length. A reviewed protein containing this domain is found in Haloferax volcanii ([swissprot:D4GSN3]). This domain contains two CXXC motifs suggesting it is likely to be zinc binding.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8107)

The proteins containing this domain are predominantly found in the class Halobacteria, which are known for their extreme halophilic nature. The domain is typically found in proteins ranging from 59 to 80 amino acids in length. Proteins containing this domain are predicted to be integral membrane proteins, as suggested by the presence of multiple transmembrane helices.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF8108)
description: This entry represents a family of uncharacterised proteins in archaea. The proteins containing this domain are predominantly found in the class Halobacteria, which are known for their adaptation to high-salt environments. The proteins in this family are typically around 100 to 300 amino acids in length. Many of these proteins are predicted to be integral membrane proteins, as suggested by the presence of multiple transmembrane helices. The family contains a C-terminal zinc ribbon domain.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF8109)
description: This entry represents a domain from a family of uncharacterised proteins predominantly found in halophilic archaea. The proteins in this family are primarily distributed among the Halobacteria class, including genera such as Natronomonas and Haloarcula. Additionally, some members are found in viruses infecting these archaea. The proteins are relatively short, with lengths ranging from approximately 113 to 131 amino acids.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8110)
description: This entry represents a domain from a family of uncharacterised proteins in archaea. The proteins in this family are predominantly found in halophilic archaea, particularly within the Halobacteria class. The proteins are generally short, with lengths ranging from 89 to 123 amino acids. The reviewed protein from Halogeometricum borinquense (UniProtKB:E4NSC8) is included in this family.

name: Putative primase C-terminal domain
description: This entry represents the C-terminal alpha-helical domain from a family of putative primase protein in halophilic archaea. The proteins in this family are predominantly found in the class Halobacteria, which includes several families such as Haloferacaceae, Halobacteriaceae, and Natrialbaceae. The proteins containing this domain are typically around 500 amino acids in length, as observed in several sequences from the SEED alignment. This domain is associated with proteins that are often encoded on plasmids in various halophilic archaea.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8112)

The proteins containing this domain are primarily distributed among various genera such as Halorubrum, Halalkalicoccus, and Natronococcus. The domain is typically found in proteins ranging from 90 to 250 amino acids in length. These domains contain to CXXC motifs suggesting they are zinc binding domains.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8113)

These proteins are typically found in extreme halophilic environments. The proteins in this family generally range from 88 to 138 amino acids in length. AlphaFold3 predicts this protein can form a homodimer [swissprot:U1Q8T4] (ipTM=0.81 pTM=0.81) which is composed of a four stranded beta sheet with a pair of helices packed on one side and two stacked pairs of helices on the other.

Many of these proteins exhibit regions of disorder, particularly towards the C-terminal end, which are rich in acidic residues. According to the TED database proteins in this family are composed of three small domains.

description: This entry represents a domain from a family of uncharacterised proteins predominantly found in the class Clostridia. The proteins containing this domain are typically between 60 and 130 amino acids in length. The domain is highly conserved across various species within the Bacillota and Thermodesulfobacteriota phyla. Structure prediction suggests this protein is composed of two alpha helices and forms a head to tail dimer conformation. The sequences contain a set of histidines in helix one that according to AlphaFold 3 confidently binds to a zinc ion.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF8181)
description: This entry represents a domain from a family of uncharacterised proteins in the archaeal phylum Thermoproteota. The proteins are predominantly found in the order Sulfolobales, which includes genera such as Acidianus, Metallosphaera, and Sulfolobus. The domain is approximately 110 amino acids in length. The reviewed protein SSO0428 from Saccharolobus solfataricus is a representative member of this family. Proteins in this family are predicted to form a single long alpha helix. Structure prediction suggests that this protein does not form a homomeric coiled-coil complex. Based on genomic context this protein may be an accessory subunit of the V-type ATP synthase complex.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8182)
description: This entry represents a domain from a family of uncharacterised proteins predominantly found in the bacterial phylum Thermodesulfobacteriota. The proteins containing this domain are mainly distributed among the orders Desulfovibrionales and Desulfobacterales. The domain is approximately 85 amino acids in length. Proteins containing this domain are predicted to be involved in various cellular processes, but their exact function remains unknown. The domain is sometimes associated with the [pfam:PF11823] domain, which is a putative Se/S carrier protein-like domain. This domain shows structure similarity to the N-terminal domain of Enolase.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8183)
description: This entry represents a protein domain found in a family of uncharacterised archaebacterial proteins. This domain shows strong structural similarity to the SycN protein from Y. pestis that forms a heterodimeric complex with YscB and acts as a secretion chaperone to YopN. This family of proteins contains a C-terminal HTH domain.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF8184)
description: This entry represents a family of uncharacterised proteins from the Bacteroidota phylum, particularly within the Chitinophagales order. Proteins in this family are found in various bacterial species, including Chitinophaga and Flavobacterium. The proteins typically range from approximately 200 to 380 amino acids in length. This family corresponds to a duplication of a PH-domain-like fold.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8185)
description: This domain is found at the C-terminal end of a group of uncharacterised bacterial proteins. It is predicted to show an alpha-beta configuration. It has highly conserved W and R residues as well as GW and GF motifs.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8186) N-terminal domain
description: This entry represents the N-terminal domain found in a family of uncharacterised proteins from archaea. The proteins are predominantly found in the Halobacteria class, which includes members of the Haloferacaceae, Haloarculaceae, and Natrialbaceae families. The proteins in this family are typically around 550-580 amino acids in length.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8186) central domain
description: This entry represents the central domain found in a family of uncharacterised proteins from archaea. The proteins are predominantly found in the Halobacteria class, which includes members of the Haloferacaceae, Haloarculaceae, and Natrialbaceae families. The proteins in this family are typically around 550-580 amino acids in length.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8186) C-terminal domain
description: This entry represents the C-terminal Ig-like domain found in a family of uncharacterised proteins from archaea. The proteins are predominantly found in the Halobacteria class, which includes members of the Haloferacaceae, Haloarculaceae, and Natrialbaceae families. The proteins in this family are typically around 550-580 amino acids in length.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8187)
description: This entry represents a domain found in uncharacterised proteins from beta-proteobacteria. It is predicted to fold into a beta-barrel-like structure. This domain is frequently found associated with [pfam:PF07589] (PEP-CTERM).

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8188)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised proteins mainly from gram-negative bacteria. It is usually preceded by a hydrophobic alpha-helix predicted as transmembrane. This domain is predicted to adopt an OB-fold and has a significant structural similarity to bacterial enterotoxins and related domains members of this superfamily.

name: PLL-like beta propeller
description: This domain, previously known as DUF8189, is found in the L-fucose-binding lectins PHL and PLLs(1-5) from various Photorhabdus species and their homologues. This domain forms a seven-bladed beta-propeller [[cite:PUB00100843],[cite:PUB00109482],[cite:PUB00161611]]. Each blade makes a W-motif composed of four antiparallel beta-strands (beta1-beta4) connected by beta-turns and loops. The C and N terminus are located on the same side of the torus and create a cap of the inner cavity of the torus. With exception of PLL3, which is a monomer, all other domains assemble into oligomeric structures, either homo-dimeric or homo-tetrameric, connected with an inter-subunit disulfide bridge [[cite:PUB00100843],[cite:PUB00109482],[cite:PUB00161611]]. Besides L-fucose or fucosylated saccharides, some of these domains bind to unusual O-methylated disaccharide 3,6-O-Me2-d-Glc-beta1-4(2,3-O-Me2)-l-Rha-alpha (MGMR) [[cite:PUB00161611]].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8190)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised fungal proteins. It is predicted to fold into an alpha/beta structure with unique topology.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8191)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised fungal proteins. It is predicted to fold into an unique alpha/beta structure consisting of a mixed five-stranded beta-sheet in which the last beta-strand is antiparallel to the rest, and an alpha-helix which packs nearly orthogonal to the beta-sheet.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8192)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised proteins mainly form gram-negative bacteria. It is predicted to fold into an unique alpha/beta structure composed of a central mixed beta-sheet and alpha-helices packed on it. Homologues contains several highly conserved positively charged residues.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8193)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised bacterial proteins. It is predicted to fold into an alpha/beta structure with unique topology.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8194)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised bacterial proteins. It is predicted to adopt Ig-like fold. It is usually found C-terminal to [pfam:PF26613].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8195)
description: This domain is found C-terminal in uncharacterised bacterial proteins. It is predicted to adopt Ig-like fold. It is usually found in combination with [pfam:PF26613] and [pfam:PF26614].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8196)
description: This entry represents a bacterial family that belongs to the PD-(D/E)XK nuclease superfamily. Proteins in this family generally contain a long N-terminal alpha helix that likely forms a trimeric coiled-coil structure according to AlphaFold prediction. The proteins are predominantly present in the Thermoprotei class of archaea and the Pseudomonadati class of bacteria.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF8197)
description: This entry represents a group of uncharacterised proteins mainly from bacteria. These proteins are small in size and are predicted to adopt a single alpha-helix. One member, PA3496 from Pseudomonas aeruginosa, was shown to be upregulated in the presence of inulin or inulin-derived fructooligosaccharide.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8198)
description: This entry represents uncharacterised proteins found in gamma- and beta-proteobacteria. They are predicted to adopt an alpha-helical structure with a complex topology.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF8199)
description: This entry represents uncharacterised proteins, widespread in gram-negative bacteria. Members contain three well-conserved motifs, HYC, CC (which may appear twice), and PP.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF8200)
description: This entry represents a family of uncharacterised proteins found mainly in Alphaproteobacteria. These are predicted to fold into a alpha/beta structure, composed of a five-stranded antiparallel beta-sheet that curves around a single helix, which partly resemble TATA-box binding protein individual repeats. These proteins contain two pairs of conserved cysteine residues that are predicted to form disulfide bonds suggesting that they may be secreted.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8201)
description: This entry represents uncharacterised bacterial proteins. These proteins are highly hydrophobic and contain a conserved DxxxY sequence motif. Some proteins have a sequence similarity to members of the Glycosyl transferase GT-C superfamily and are predicted to fold into similar structures, suggesting they may be glycosyltransferases.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8202)
description: This entry represents a domain found in uncharacterised bacterial proteins. This domain is found in one or multiple copies and in combination with [pfam:PF01345], [pfam:PF13585] and others. It has a significant structural similarity to known ZU5 and Gain domains suggesting it may be involved in adhesion.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8203)
description: This entry represents a domain found in a family of uncharacterised halobacterial species. The predicted structure shows structural similarity to ribonuclease HII suggesting it may act as a nuclease enzyme.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8204)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised plant proteins. It is predicted to fold into an open barrel-like structure. It contains two pair of conserved cysteine residues which are predicted to form disulfide bonds. It may be involve in oligomerisation given the number of conserved exposed hydrophobic residues.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8205)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised fungal proteins. It is probably distantly related to CcmS and [pfam:PF26617] and it is predicted to adopt topologically similar structure. It is found frequently in combination with zf-MYND [pfam:PF01753] and in multiple copies.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8206)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised eukaryotic proteins. It contains a number of highly conserved cysteine and histidine residues that may be involved in metal coordination. Some proteins contain two copies of this domain. It probably adopt a novel fold judging by its predicted structure.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8207)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised metazoan protein. It is predicted to adopt an alpha/beta structure composed of curved beta-sheet and alpha-helices packed on it.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8208)
description: This entry represents the N-terminal domain in large, membrane-embedded proteins of mobile elements such as the Bacillus subtilis natto plasmid pLS20. It is predicted to contain five transmembrane alpha-helices.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF8209)
description: This entry represents uncharacterised proteins found in gamma- and beta-proteobacteria. A member of this family, STM2901, is a putative cytoplasmic protein from many but not all forms of SPI-1 (Salmonella Pathogenicity Island 1).

name: Family of unknown function (DUF8210)
description: This entry represents uncharacterised cyanobacterial proteins that are probably related to Psb35 protein and are restricted to species that have photosystem II.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8211)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised fungal proteins. It is predicted to fold into unusual alpha/beta structure composed of a four-stranded antiparallel beta-sheet capped with alpha-helices.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8212)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised proteins mainly from fungi. It is found frequently C-terminal to Het [pfam:PF06985] and it is predicted to fold into a beta-barrel structure similar to Het-6 beta-barrel domain.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8213)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised proteins mainly from filamentous fungi. It contains ten highly conserved cysteine residues which are predicted to form disulfide bonds.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8214)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised proteins mainly from Agaricomycetes. It is probably distantly related to chaperone protein CcmS, [pfam:PF26617] and [pfam:PF26632] and it is predicted to adopt topologically similar structure. It is found frequently in combination with zf-MYND [pfam:PF01753].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8215)
description: This entry represents a domain from a family of uncharacterised proteins in the class Halobacteria. The proteins containing this domain are predominantly found in various genera within the Halobacteriales order. The domain is typically found in proteins ranging from 129 to 225 amino acids in length. These proteins are predicted to be integral membrane proteins, as suggested by the presence of two transmembrane helices.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF8216)
description: This entry represents a domain from a family of uncharacterised proteins in archaea, specifically within the Halobacteria class. The proteins in this family are typically around 116 amino acids in length. They are predicted to be integral membrane proteins, as suggested by the presence of four predicted transmembrane helices.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8217)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised proteins from Alphaproteobacteria. It is predicted to adopt a beta- sandwich with unique topology. It contains four highly conserved cysteine residues that are predicted to form disulfide bonds.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8218)
description: This entry represents a conserved region located at the N terminus of uncharacterised fungal proteins. It contains a number of highly conserved arginine residues.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8219)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised proteins. It has detectable similarity to members of Immunity protein 19 family [pfam:PF15563] and it is predicted to adopt similar structure.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8220)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised bacterial proteins. It is predicted to fold into an unique alpha/beta structure composed on a four-stranded mixed beta-sheet (order 2143) and alpha-helices that pack on one face of the sheet, spanning edge to edge.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8221)
description: This entry represents a long alpha helical region found in dynactin-like proteins from eukaryotes. This region may mediate oligomerisation forming a coiled-coil.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8222)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised proteins mainly from Eurotiomycetes. They are predicted to fold in a very distinct six-stranded beta-barrel structure which is topologically very similar to phage Gp54 protein structure.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8223)
description: This entry represents a domain found in uncharacterised plant proteins. It is predicted to fold into unique alpha/beta structure consisting of a meander curved beta-sheet and alpha-helices packed on one face of the sheet and sandwiched with another four-stranded small beta-sheet.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1631) C-terminal tudor domain
description: This entry represents the C-terminal domain found in DUF1631 family proteins. This domain structurally resembles a tudor domain. The members of this family are sequences derived from a group of hypothetical proteins expressed by certain bacterial species.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1631) 2nd domain
description: This entry represents the second domain found in DUF1631 family proteins. The members of this family are sequences derived from a group of hypothetical proteins expressed by certain bacterial species.

name: Protein of unknown function (DUF1631) third domain
description: This entry represents the third domain found in DUF1631 family proteins. The members of this family are sequences derived from a group of hypothetical proteins expressed by certain bacterial species.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8224)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised proteins. It is predicted to fold into a globular structure consisting mainly of alpha-helices. It contains one histidine and two cysteine residues which are highly conserved and may be essential for function.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8225)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised proteins. It is predicted to adopt an unique complex alpha/ beta structure. IT contains a number of conserved negatively charged residues that may be essential for function.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8226)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised proteins mainly from Bacteroidota. It is predicted to fold into alpha/beta structure with unique topology. This domain is flanked by coiled coil regions.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8227)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised plant proteins. It is predicted to fold into two meander beta-sheets that sandwich each other.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8228)
description: This entry represents a family of domains found in Halobacteria at the C-terminus of a set of ABC transporter proteins. This suggests this may be a substrate binding domain.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8229)
description: This entry represents an uncharacterised beta-sandwich domain found in a small family of uncharacterised halobacterial proteins. STRING shows that this protein is often found associated with a [pfam:PF10936] domain and an SpeE enzyme.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8230) N-terminal domain
description: This entry represents the N-terminal domain of an uncharacterised putative enzyme. It shows structural similarity to the N-terminal domain of enolase.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8230) C-terminal domain
description: This entry represents the C-terminal domain of an uncharacterised putative enzyme. It shows structural similarity to the C-terminal domain of enolase and has a TIM barrel fold.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8575)
description: This entry represents a functionally uncharacterised domain that shows structural similarity to [pfam:PF14032] which is the sensor domain of the PknH protein kinase protein.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF8231)
description: This entry represents a family of uncharacterised proteins from archaebacteria. These proteins contain and N and C-terminal transmembrane alpha helix. These alpha helices interact with each other. The central portion of the protein is likely to form a series of extracellular domains.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8232)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised proteins mainly from dinoflagellates. It is predicted to fold into an alpha-helical structure. It contains several invariant residues including aspartate and cysteine that may be essential for function.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8233)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised proteins from Methanobacteriati. It is predicted to fold into unusual alpha/beta structure. AlphaFold predicts that it may form a swapped dimer.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8234)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterized proteins. It is predicted to fold into an alpha-helical structure which is usually found inserted into endonuclease domain (CL0530). It contains a highly conserved Gx(2)Rx(2)SxPDRxTN sequence motif which is predicted to face the endonuclease domain active site and is likely involved in substrate recognition/binding.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8235)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised proteins from betaproteobacteria. It is predicted to adopt alpha-helical structure. In some proteins it is found repeated.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8236)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised proteins. It is predicted to fold into a small open beta-barrel with an alpha-hairpin packed on one side.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF272), C-terminal
description: This domain is majoritarily found in Caenorhabditis proteins and has no known function. It has a ubiquitin fold. The GO annotation for the protein indicates that it has a function in nematode larval development.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8237)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised bacterial proteins. It is predicted to fold into a globular structure with significant similarity to C-type lectin. Compared to known C-type lectin domains this domain contains a large insertion comprising a six-stranded beta-meander. Some proteins contain two copies of this domain.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8238)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised proteins mainly from aquatic invertebrates. It is predicted to fold into a very distinct curved beta-sheet and alpha-helices packed on the concave side of it.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8239)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised proteins from Gram-negative bacteria. It is predicted to fold into a beta-sandwich which has some similarity to known carbohydrate binding domains. It is frequently found in combination with [pfam:PF07589] PEP-CTERM sorting motif suggesting that it may be associated with the membrane.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8240)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised proteins from halobacteria. It is predicted to fold into a beta-barrel structure which has a similarity to Heme iron utilization protein domains. The heme binding site is not conserved. Although, structurally it is more similar to HemS/ChuS-like domains, this domain has probably undergone a large deletion.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8241)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised plant proteins. It contains three repeats with topology similar to the C-terminal domain of defensin. Each of these repeats has two predicted disulfide bonds that are conserved and occupying the same spatial position as the disulfide bonds in defensin. This domain is frequently found in combination with [pfam:PF23106] and [pfam:PF13920].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8242)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised fungal proteins. It is predicted to fold into an unique alpha/beta structure composed of a small central four-stranded antiparallel beta-sheet surrounded by alpha-helices.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8243)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised proteins. It contains two pairs of highly conserved cysteine residues that may coordinate a metal ion. This domain is predicted to fold into a structure that is probably distantly related to domains with beta-tent fold (CL0080). The zinc ribbon in this domain is grafted into alpha/beta core.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF8244)
description: This entry describes a set of proteins of unknown function, mainly from Dictyostelium discoideum. These uncharacterised proteins display a CUB-like fold, a structural motif of approximately 110 residues found almost exclusively in extracellular and plasma membrane-associated proteins [[cite:PUB00035659]].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8245)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised proteins from gram-negative bacteria. It contains highly conserved histidine and three cysteine residues arranged in HCCC pattern. These residues are predicted to be located in proximity and likely to coordinate a metal ion. This domain is usually found preceding HNH nuclease domain.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8246)
description: This domain is found in the uncharacterised protein At4g37920 from Arabidopsis thaliana and similar proteins. This domain is predicted to adopt an all-alpha configuration. Its specific function is unknown.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8247)
description: This domain is found in the uncharacterised protein ZK1098.2 from Caenorhabditis elegans and similar sequences. It is predicted to adopt an alpha/beta configuration.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8248)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised proteins from Gammaproteobacteria. It is predicted to adopt a structure which has similarity to SPM domain. The Ca2+ binding sites are not conserved suggesting that this domain doesn't bind Ca2+ ions. This domain is frequently found in combination with [pfam:PF13645] representing a group of putative L,D-transpeptidase domains.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8249)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised eukaryotic proteins. It is predicted to fold into unique alpha/beta structure. It has two highly conserved histidines and a serine that may have functional importance.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8250)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised proteins predominantly from bacteria. It contains two pairs of conserved cysteine residues that may be involved in metal ion coordination. This domain is predicted to adopt a fold typical for zinc beta-ribbon domains.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8251)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised bacterial proteins. It is predicted to fold in a beta-sandwich with unique topology.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8252)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised proteins. It contains several highly conserved cysteine residues that are predicted to form disulfide bonds. Some proteins contain multiple tandem copies of this domain.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8253)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised proteins mainly from Microbacteriaceae. It contains repetitive QC sequence motif frequently found in the context of NQCN motif. This domain is predicted to fold into an unique beta-sandwich formed of these consecutive motifs.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8254)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised eukaryotic proteins. It share similarity with known CHORD domains and it is predicted to adopt similar structure. In some proteins it is found in combination with AAA+ domains [pfam:PF00004]. It contains several cysteine and histidine residues which are highly conserved and likely involved in metal coordination.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8255)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised bacterial proteins. It contains four pairs of highly conserved cysteine residues that may be involved in metal coordination. It is predicted to contain two zinc beta ribbon domains with one domain inserted into the other.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8256)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised bacterial proteins. It is predicted to fold into an unique structure composed of two meander beta-sheets that pack close.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8257)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised fungal proteins. It contains two pairs of highly conserved cysteine residues that are likely involved in metal coordination. This domain is predicted to fold into a structure which closely resembles domains members of the Zn(2)-Cys(6) binuclear cluster superfamily. Despite its conserved residues occupy equivalent spacial positions as the metal coordinating residues in Zn(2)-Cys(6) domains, this domain contains only four cysteines of six suggesting it can only coordinate one zinc atom.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8258)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised insect proteins. It contains several highly conserved cysteine residues that are predicted to form disulfide bonds. Many proteins contain multiple copies of this domain.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8259)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised proteins mainly from Planctomycetia. It contains four pairs of highly conserved cysteine residues that are probably involved in zinc coordination. This domain is predicted to contain two zinc ribbon domains inserted one into the other.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8260)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised bacterial proteins. It contains a two pair of highly conserved cysteine residues that may be involved in metal coordination. It is predicted to fold into a structure typical for zinc beta ribbon domains. Some proteins contain multiple copies of this domain.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8261)
description: This domain is found exclusively in uncharacterised proteins from Legionellales species. It contains several highly conserved cysteine residues which are predicted to form disulfide bonds. It is composed of two repeats predicted to consist of a small three-stranded antiparallel beta-sheet and an alpha-helix packed on it.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8262)
description: This entry represents the N-terminal helical domain found in a family of secreted halobacterial proteins.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8263)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised fungal proteins. It is predicted to fold into a small three stranded beta-sheet and alpha helices. It contains a highly conserved SD[ED]E sequence motif.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8264)
description: This entry represents the C-terminal helical domain found in a family of secreted halobacterial proteins. This domain is found C-terminal to [pfam:PF26790].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8265)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised proteins mainly from alphaproteobacteria. It is predicted to fold into an alpha/beta structure composed of a four-stranded beta-sheet and alpha-helix. It contains to highly conserved cysteine residues that are predicted to form disulfide bond bridging the alpha-helix and the beta-sheet. Besides the conserved cysteine residues, this domain contains a conserved NLxDP sequence motif which may have a functional role.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8266)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised proteins from Halobacteria. It is predicted to fold into an alpha/beta structure composed of a small four stranded antiparallel beta-sheet and alpha-helices packed on one side of it. It contains two conserved sequence motifs IPLH and RxRFW which may have functional importance. This domain is frequently found in combination with domains members of AAA superfamily.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8267)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised fungal proteins. It is predicted to adopt an alpha/beta structure consisting of an antiparallel beta-sheet and alpha-helices packed on one side of it.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8268)
description: This entry represents a domain from a family of uncharacterised proteins in the Archaea. The domain is predominantly found in members of the Methanobacteriota phylum, specifically within the Halobacteria class. Proteins containing this domain are typically integral membrane proteins with two transmembrane helices. The domain is approximately 60-70 amino acids in length. This domain is sometimes associated with [pfam:PF09997].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8269)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised bacterial proteins. It is predicted to fold into a beta-sandwich structure consisting of two pairs of swapped beta-hairpins. This domain is found in combination with TauE ([pfam:PF01925]) suggesting it may be associated with the membrane.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8270)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised proteins. It contains two pairs of conserved cysteine residues which are predicted to form disulfide bonds.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8553)
description: This entry represents a domain found at the C-terminus of a family of uncharacterised fungal proteins. These proteins are long and largely composed of disordered regions. This domain is predicted to adopt an alpha/beta structure.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8271)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised proteins mainly from Trypanosomatidae species. It is predicted to fold into a beta-barrel structure that is reminiscent to the beta-barrel observed in VirK family proteins [pfam:PF06903]. These two barrels, however, relate not only by circular permutation but also by strand flip with a change of directionality.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF8272)
description: This entry represents a family of small phage proteins of unknown function.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8273)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised proteins mainly from insects. It is predicted to adopt an alpha/beta structure composed of a curved six-stranded antiparallel beta-sheet packed with alpha-helices.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8274)
description: This entry represents a domain found in uncharacterised proteins exclusively from Vitrellaceae. It is predicted to adopt an unique alpha/beta structure featuring antiparallel beta-sheet and an alpha-helix nearly orthogonal to the former.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8275)
description: This entry represents a domain of unknown function found mostly in fungal proteins. This domain contains a coiled coil hairpin domain similar to that of [[pfam:PF24481]].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8276)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised prokaryotic proteins. It is predicted to adopt mainly alpha-helical structure with unique topology. It is found in combination with [pfam:PF00271] and [pfam:PF00176].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8277)
description: This entry represents a domain found in a variety of mycobacteriophage. Structure prediction suggests that these proteins form a confident homodimer. The domain is composed of a four stranded beta sheet with two helices packed on one side. The homo-oligomer interaction is mediated by the C-terminal beta strand. The function of this protein is not known.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8278)
