description: This immunoglobulin-like (Ig-like) domain is found in a group of uncharacterised plant proteins. It is usually found associated with [pfam:PF11817].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8388)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised eukaryotic proteins. It is predicted to fold into an alpha/beta structure composed of a five stranded beta-sheet and alpha-helices packed on one side of it. It is preceded by a transmembrane domain.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8389)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised bacterial proteins. It is predicted to adopt a structure which resembles the conserved core of the N-terminal domain of PatA [pfam:PF14332].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8390)
description: This immunoglobulin-like (Ig-like) domain is found in a group of uncharacterised EFG-containing proteins from amoebas that are predicted to show several Ig-like domains. This entry is often found associated with [pfam:PF22933], [pfam:PF23033], and [pfam:PF23034].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8391)
description: This immunoglobulin-like (Ig-like) domain is found in a group of uncharacterised proteins from worms. It has several highly conserved W, Y and C residues. Its specific function is unknown.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8392)
description: This immunoglobulin-like (Ig-like) domain is found in a group of uncharacterised fungal proteins. It is often found associated with [pfam:PF01734] and has a highly conserved motif ISGFP.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8393)
description: This immunoglobulin-like (Ig-like) domain is found in a group of uncharacterised proteobacterial proteins. It is often found associated with [pfam:PF13899], [pfam:PF02683] and [pfam:PF11412] and has conserved P, L, F and D residues. Its function is unknown.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8394)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised proteins mainly from Actinomycetota lineage. It is predicted to adopt a complex alpha/beta structure resembling the shape of 'stalk and head'. Structurally it is similar to the so-called choice-of-anchor G proteins, which are sortase and exosortase targets, and are likely to be found on the cell surface.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8395)
description: This domain is found in the uncharacterised protein At4g14100 from Arabidopsis thaliana and similar plant sequences. It is predicted to form unclosed beta-barrel and an alpha-helical lid. Its function is unknown.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF8396)
description: This entry represents a group of uncharacterised bacterial proteins. They are probably associated with the membrane and are predicted to fold into a large barrel structure which in addition to an internal plug contains an insertion which points out of the barrel.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8397)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised fungal proteins. It is predicted to fold into array of alpha-helices some of which connected by extended loops.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8398)
description: This entry represents a family of proteins that were formerly part of the DUF3316 family. However, the family contained two unrelated groups of proteins. These members are split into this new family. The domain contains a three stranded beta sheet with a longer and shorter alpha helix packed on one side. The function of these proteins is unknown.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8399)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised proteins mainly from fungi. It shares similarity with known ARM domains. It is frequently found next to an RRM domain.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8400)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised eukaryotic proteins. It has significant similarity to known RRM domains and it is predicted to adopt similar structure.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF8401)
description: This entry represents a conserved cysteine-rich region found in uncharacterised metazoan proteins. The conserved cysteine residues are predicted to form disulfide bonds.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8402)
description: This domain is found C-terminal in uncharacterised bacterial proteins. It is predicted to fold into L-shaped beta-sandwich. Most proteins containing this domain also contain a lipoprotein lipid attachment site at the N-terminus suggesting they may be associated with the membrane.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8403)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised bacterial proteins. This domain is predicted to fold into a beta-barrel structure which has topological similarity to domains members of Phage tail beta-barrel superfamily.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8404)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised fungal proteins. It is predicted to adopt an alpha/beta structure with an unique topology. It contains several highly conserved histidine and aspartate residues that may be essential for function.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8405)

It is predicted to fold into an alpha/beta structure composed of four-stranded antiparallel beta-sheet with strand order 2341 and alpha helices packed on one face of the sheet. This domain contains two pair of highly conserved cysteine residues that are predicted to form disulfide bonds. It is frequently found N-terminal to TIM-barrel domain.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8406)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised fungal proteins. It is predicted to fold into an alpha/beta structure composed of a curved beta-sheet and alpha-helices packed on the concave side of it. It contains two highly conserved cysteine residues predicted to form disulfide bond. This domain is flanked by regions predicted as transmembrane.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8407)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised fungal proteins. It is predicted to adopt a non-compact alpha-helical structure.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8408)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised proteins mainly from Actinomycetes. It contains highly conserved cysteine and histidine residues that may be involved in metal coordination.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8409)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised bacterial proteins. It contains conserved RxDxDxxYY sequence motif which may be important for function.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8410)
description: This domain is found in a group of uncharacterised proteins mainly found in actinomycetes. This domain, which contains highly conserved W, D, G residues and a conserved motif FxHRHR, is predicted to form an antiparallel beta sheet and alpha helices. Bet_v_1 domains contain a hydrophobic ligand-binding pocket [[cite:PUB00053295]]. The specific function of this family is unknown.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8411)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised fungal proteins. It is predicted to fold into a complex alpha/beta structure.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8412)
description: This entry represents an uncharacterised domain that is found N-terminal to [pfam:PF13376]. The function of these proteins is unknown. These proteins contain a conserved motif ALCXGWID in the central part of the sequence. This domain is found in both bacterial and fungal proteins.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8413)
description: This entry represents a small extracellular three helical bundle domain found at the N-terminus of proteins that contain a C-terminal [pfam:PF01944] integral membrane domain. This suggests these proteins are involved in sporulation. This domain is found in Pseudomonadati and Bacillati.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8414)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised fungal proteins. It contains several conserved cysteine residues that may be involved in metal coordination.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8415)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised metazoan proteins. It is predicted to fold into an alpha/beta structure with two pairs of conserved cysteine residues. These residues are predicted to form disulfide bonds.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF8416)
description: This family represents an uncharacterised domain found in bacterial proteins from the Bacteroidota phylum, particularly in members of Flavobacteriaceae and Sphingobacteriaceae. The domain typically spans approximately 90-100 residues and is positioned between the TMEM260-like domain ([pfam:PF11028]) and the TMEM260_2 domain ([pfam:PF28495]) in the protein architecture. These proteins appear to be glycosyltransferases or related membrane proteins. The function of this domain remains to be determined.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF1699) N-terminal domain
description: This entry represents a domain found at the N-terminus of an archaeal family of proteins called DUF1699.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8417)

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8418)

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8419)

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8420)

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8421)

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8422)

name: Family of unknown function (DUF8423)

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8424)

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8425)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised bacterial proteins. It is predicted to fold into an alpha-helical structure with similarity to 8-oxoguanine DNA glycosylase-like domains such as [pfam:PF22175] and [pfam:PF21790]. The structural similarity extends to the active site architecture with some of the active site residues conserved.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8426)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised bacterial proteins. It shares significant similarity with the Thermococcus gammatolerans McrB N-terminal domain and related YTH domain-like domains. It adopts a typical PUA-like fold.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8427)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised proteins mainly from gram-negative bacteria. It is predicted to fold into an array of alpha-helices. It contains a number of conserved negatively charged residues that cluster on the surface.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8428)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised bacterial proteins. It shares significant similarity to Ig-like domains, in particular domains members of [pfam:PF12975] (DUF3859) and [pfam:PF22091] (DUF6941).

name: Coiled-coil region of unknown function (DUF8429)
description: This coiled coil domain is found in uncharacterised proteins mainly from gram-negative bacteria. It is usually followed by and Ig-like domain.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8430)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised proteins mainly from gram-negative bacteria. It shares significant similarity to domains members of the DNA primase C-terminal domain superfamily such as [pfam:PF08278] and [pfam:PF00772].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8431)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised bacterial proteins. It is frequently found N-terminal to domains members of the Endonuclease/Exonuclease/phosphatase family [pfam:PF03372]. It is predicted to fold into a three-helical bundle.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8432)
description: This domain is found in a group of uncharacterised proteins from fungi. It is predicted to adopt a UBA domain-like structure. UBA domains are often involved in ubiquitin binding. The specific function of this domain

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8433)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised bacterial proteins. It probably folds into a small beta-sandwich. it is usually found associated with a transmembrane domain.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8434)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised bacterial proteins mainly from gram-negative bacteria. It is predicted to form a single transmembrane helix which sometime is found in combination with MlaD-like domain ([pfam:PF02470]).

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8435)
description: This domain is found in a group of uncharacterised proteins from worms. This domain has highly conserved motifs YRF and HLRxRK and is predicted to show high structural similarity with UBA domains, which are often involved in ubiquitin binding. It is often found associated with [pfam:PF00650].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8436)
description: This small domain is found at the N-terminus of a set of likely FAD-binding proteins. It forms an alpha-beta plait fold.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8437)
description: This entry represents a domain found in uncharacterised bacterial proteins. It is predicted to fold into a small alpha/beta structure composed of beta-hairpin and array of helices packed on it. This domain is usually found associated with a pair of P-loop domains with the typical for helicases arrangement.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8438)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised proteins mainly from gram-negative bacteria. It is predicted to fold into small alpha/beta domain consisting of three-stranded beta-sheet and two alpha-helices packed on it. It is frequently found in combination with helicase domains.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8439)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised proteins mainly from gram-negative bacteria. Ir shares a significant similarity to the N-terminal domain of DNAA and it is predicted to adopt similar structure.

name: SusR N-terminal TPR domain
description: This entry represents the N-terminal periplasmic domain of the SusR protein. This region of SusR is involved in sensing maltose levels and then transduces this signal to the C-terminal DNA-binding domain to promote transcript of the Sus operon.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF8440)
description: This family of proteins are found in Bacteroidales. It contains an N-terminal signal peptide suggesting it is a secreted protein. Overall they show relatively low levels of conservation except for a conserved C-terminal 11 residue motif that is likely important for function.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8441)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised bacterial proteins. It is predicted to fold into a structure with a significant similarity to known galactose binding domains.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8442)
description: This entry represents a family of uncharacterised Bacteroidia proteins that contain a single domain. There is some evidence from structure prediction that these proteins may form homodimers.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF8443)
description: This entry represents a conserved domain found at the C-terminus of S41 family carboxyl-terminal processing peptidases in members of the phylum Bacteroidota. The domain is approximately 85-90 amino acids in length and is located immediately downstream of the Peptidase_S41 catalytic domain ([pfam:PF03572]). S41 family peptidases are serine proteases involved in C-terminal processing of proteins, including the removal of C-terminal extensions from penicillin-binding proteins and other substrates. This C-terminal domain is found exclusively in Bacteroidota, particularly in the classes Bacteroidia, Flavobacteriia, Cytophagia and Sphingobacteriia, suggesting it may confer phylum-specific functionality or substrate specificity. The domain architecture of these proteins typically consists of an N-terminal CtpB_N-like domain ([pfam:PF22694]), one or more PDZ domains ([pfam:PF00595], [pfam:PF13180], [pfam:PF17820]), the catalytic Peptidase_S41 domain, and this C-terminal domain. The function of this domain remains to be determined.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8444)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised fungal sequences that also contain a Zn(2)Cys(6) DNA-binding domain ([pfam:PF00172]).

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8445)
description: This entry represents a domain found in uncharacterised plant sequences which may adopt a structure similar to spectrin repeats.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8446)
description: This is a domain found at the N-terminal of a group of uncharacterised fungal sequences which is found in association with a Cytidyltransferase-like domain ([pfam:PF01467]) at the C-terminal. This domain seems to adopt a structure similar to those in the HUP superfamily.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8447)
description: This Ig-like domain is found in uncharacterised bacterial proteins.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8448)
description: This is a domain found in uncharacterised plant proteins. From structure predictions, it adopts an OB fold-like configuration.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8449)
description: This entry represents a domain found in uncharacterised fungal sequences which have a similar structure to KH domains, according to structure predictions.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8450)
description: This is a domain of unknown function found in uncharacterised sequences from nematodes. It may adopt a structure similar to that of the von Willebrand factor superfamily.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8451)

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8452)
description: This entry represents a domain of unknown function found in uncharacterised sequences from nematodes. It may have a helix-turn-helix structure.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8453)

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8454)
description: This entry represents a domain found in uncharacterised proteins from Fungi which may adopt a similar structure to the hyaluronidase post-catalytic domain, consisting of a five helical bundle with an up-and-down topology. In some members, this domain is duplicated, while other members are mono domain proteins.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8455)
description: This is a domain found in uncharacterised fungal sequences, which is a cysteine-rich domain found at the C-terminal end of these sequences.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8456)
description: This is a domain found at the C-terminal of a group of uncharacterised proteins from bacteria. It may adopt a beta-sandwich fold related to CBMs (carbohydrate binding modules). It is usually associated with [pfam:PF11340].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8457)
description: This entry represents a small helical domain of unknown function found in proteins from Flavobacteriia. The domain is typically around 70-90 residues in length and is located towards the C-terminus of these proteins, following a short N-terminal region. The proteins are found almost exclusively in the Flavobacteriaceae family within the Bacteroidota phylum. The function of this domain remains to be determined.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8458)
description: This entry represents an N-terminal domain of unknown function found in proteins from Bacteroidota. The domain is around 75-95 residues in length and adopts a helical structure. The domain is found primarily in Flavobacteriaceae, Bacteroidales and Cytophagales within the Bacteroidota phylum. The function of this domain remains to be determined.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8459)
description: This entry represents a domain of unknown function found in diverse proteins across Bacteria. The domain is around 95-100 residues in length and is found in mechanosensitive channel proteins, where it is located N-terminal to the mechanosensitive channel second transmembrane helix domain ([pfam:PF00924]), and in endolytic peptidoglycan transglycosylases such as RlpA, where it precedes the double-psi beta-barrel domain ([pfam:PF03330]). The domain is found across Cyanobacteriota, Bacteroidota and Pseudomonadota. The function of this domain remains to be determined.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8460)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised proteins from Bacteroidales lineage. It is predicted as a transmembrane.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8461)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised sequences from bacteria, mainly from Streptomyces. It may constitute transmembrane helices.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8462)
description: This is a HTH domain found in a group of uncharacterised sequences from bacteria and archaea, including the Uncharacterized HTH-type transcriptional regulator MJ0774 from Methanocaldococcus jannaschii.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8463)
description: This entry represents a middle domain found in DoxX family proteins from Bacteroidota. The domain is composed of three beta-strands forming a small beta-sheet and is around 40 residues in length. The domain is located between the N-terminal MauE domain ([pfam:PF07291]) and a C-terminal region. DoxX family proteins are found primarily in Bacteroidales, Chitinophagales and Cytophagales within the Bacteroidota phylum. The function of this domain remains to be determined.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8464)
description: This entry represents the second domain found in bacterial DNA primases, positioned between the N-terminal zinc ribbon domain ([pfam:PF01807]) and the C-terminal Toprim domain ([pfam:PF13155]). This domain is approximately 65-70 amino acids in length and is found predominantly in DNA primases from Bacteroidota species, particularly members of the Bacteroidales order. DNA primase (DnaG) synthesises RNA primers that are utilised by DNA polymerase during bacterial chromosomal DNA replication. The specific function of this middle domain remains to be determined, but its conservation suggests it plays an important structural or functional role in primase activity within these bacteria.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8465)
description: This entry represents a small SH3-like beta-barrel domain found N-terminal to the Smr domain ([pfam:PF01713]) in DNA mismatch repair proteins from Bacteroidota. The domain is approximately 50 residues in length and is found predominantly in Flavobacteriaceae, Sphingobacteriaceae and Cytophagales families. The Smr domain itself is involved in DNA mismatch repair processes. The specific function of this N-terminal domain remains to be determined.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8466)
description: This entry represents a small domain of unknown function. It includes Porphyromonas gingivalis protein PGN_1290 [swissprot:B2RGS5] which was found to be down-regulated in a GppX mutant [[cite:PUB00163732]]. This domain is composed of a four stranded beta sheet (strand order 1-4-3-2) with two alpha helices packed on one side. AlphaFold3 suggests these proteins form confident homodimers ([swissprot:R9HNH3] ipTM=0.9 pTM=0.92).

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8467)
description: This entry represents a small family of uncharacterised proteins from pseudomonadati and bacillati species.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8468)
description: This entry represents a domain found in Pseudomonadati bacteria. This domain is found as a single domain protein or more rarely as the C-terminal domain of reverse transcriptase enzymes.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8469)
description: This entry represents an immunoglobulin-like domain found in proteins that contain a C-terminal LruC domain. These proteins are found in pseudomonadati bacteria.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8470)
description: This domain is found at the N-terminal of a group of uncharacterised bacterial sequences and it is predicted to adopt a single-stranded right-handed beta-helix with similarity to ice-binding proteins and other adhesive domains. These proteins are usually associated with tandem Ig-like domain, such as [swissprot:A1S2S0] which has five Ig-like domains.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8471)
description: This is a helical domain found in a group of uncharacterised sequences from bacteria and archaea. It is usually found in association with [pfam:PF07760].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8472)
description: This is a domain found in a group of uncharacterised sequences from bacteria, and is associated with [pfam:PF16283] at the N-terminal. This domain may adopt a structure with complex beta-sheets and associated alpha-helices similar to those found in HORMA domains.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8473)
description: This entry represents two tandem domains found at the N-terminal of [swissprot:Q89YF2] described as TraN and related sequences. TraN is encoded by transfer region genes of conjugative transposons of Bacteroides. These tandem domains may have a Ig-like fold.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8474)
description: This is a domain found in a group of uncharacterised sequences from bacteria. It may adopt a Ig-like fold.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8475)
description: This is a domain found in a group of uncharacterised sequences from bacteria. It may adopt a Ig-like fold.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8478)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised proteins mainly from gram-negative bacteria. It contains six highly conserved histidine that cluster in space and probably represent two metal coordinating sites.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8479)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised proteins mainly from gram negative bacteria. It has similarity to known AspS Pilotin-like domains and it is predicted to fold into a similar structure.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8480)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised proteins mainly from gram negative bacteria. It shares similarity with known galactose binding domains and it is predicted to adopt similar jelly-roll structure.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8481)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised plant proteins. It is predicted to fold into an alpha-helical structure. It contains three highly conserved cysteine residues and a histidine that may constitute a metal binding site.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8482)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised proteins mainly from gram negative bacteria which are probably related to the RND tripartite drug efflux pumps. The domain represented in this entry folds into a six-stranded closed beta-barrel with a greek-key topology which has a structural similarity to the C-terminal domain of alanine racemase. This domain is interrupted by the barrel-sandwich hybrid domain which is inserted after the first beta-strand of the barrel. This model does not include the N-terminal strand.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8483)
description: This predicted RNA recognition domain (RRM) is found in a group of uncharacterised plant proteins. It is predicted to show an alpha/beta configuration. It has conserved residues P, H, C and Y. Its specific function is unknown.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8484)
description: This entry represents the C-terminal domain found in RDD family proteins, which follows the RDD domain ([pfam:PF06271]). This family is found predominantly in Bacteroidota, particularly in the orders Flavobacteriales and Cytophagales. The domain is approximately 65-85 residues in length. The function of this domain remains to be determined.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8485)
description: This entry represents the N-terminal domain found in mannose-6- phosphate isomerase family proteins. The domain is approximately 190-220 residues in length. The family is found in diverse bacteria including Bacillota, Bacteroidota and Actinomycetota. The function of this domain remains to be determined.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8486)
description: This entry represents an N-terminal putative sensor domain found in histidine kinase proteins. This domain precedes the histidine kinase A (HisKA) phosphoacceptor domain ([pfam:PF00512]) and the histidine kinase ATPase C-terminal domain ([pfam:PF02518]). The domain is approximately 145-155 residues in length. This family is found predominantly in Bacteroidota, particularly in the orders Flavobacteriales, Cytophagales and Sphingobacteriales. The function of this sensor domain remains to be determined.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8487)
description: This entry represents a C-terminal domain found in some glycosyl hydrolase family 2 proteins. This domain follows the N-terminal ([pfam:PF02837]), catalytic ([pfam:PF00703]) and C-terminal ([pfam:PF02836]) domains characteristic of this family. The domain is approximately 170-185 residues in length. These proteins include exo-beta-1,4-galactosidases involved in degrading galactan substituents from plant cell wall polysaccharides. The family is found in diverse bacteria including Bacteroidota and Bacillota. The function of this domain remains to be determined.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8488)
description: This entry represents the fourth domain found in some glycosyl hydrolase family 2 proteins. This immunoglobulin-like domain follows the N-terminal ([pfam:PF02837]), catalytic ([pfam:PF00703]) and C-terminal ([pfam:PF02836]) domains characteristic of this family. The domain is approximately 85-110 residues in length. These proteins include exo-beta-1,4-galactosidases involved in degrading galactan substituents from plant cell wall polysaccharides. The family is found in diverse bacteria including Bacteroidota and Bacillota. The function of this domain remains to be determined.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8489)
description: This predicted RNA recognition domain (RRM) is found in a group of uncharacterised proteins from lower eukaryotes.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8490)

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8491)

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8492)

This domain follows the TIGR00341/DUF389 domain ([pfam:PF04087]) and is approximately 70-80 residues in length. The family is found predominantly in Bacteroidota, particularly in Flavobacteriales. The function of this domain remains to be determined.

name: DUF4350 C-terminal helical domain

This domain follows the DUF4350 domain ([pfam:PF14258]) and is approximately 85-100 residues in length. The family is found almost exclusively in Bacteroidota, particularly in Flavobacteriales. The function of this domain remains to be determined.

description: This domain is found in uncharacterised proteins mainly from Leptospira lineage. It contains several conserved cysteine residues that are predicted to form disulfide bonds.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8720)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised proteins from Gammaproteobacteria.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8721)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised fungal proteins. It shares similarity to known I/LWEQ domains.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8722)
description: This entry represents a domain of unknown function found in uncharacterised membrane proteins from plants. The domain is restricted to eudicots, specifically to the rosid clade, and is found in families including Rosaceae (roses, apples), Salicaceae (willows, poplars), and Malvaceae. The proteins containing this domain are predicted to be membrane associated. The function of this domain remains to be determined. This domain contains an helical fold.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8723)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised fungal proteins. It shares similarity with the HHM N-terminal domain.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8724)
description: This entry represents a bacterial domain of approximately 220 residues. The domain is predominantly found in Actinomycetes, particularly Streptomycetaceae and related species, as well as in Pseudomonadota. In some proteins, this domain is found N-terminal to the MZB domain ([pfam:PF09369]). The function of this domain remains to be determined.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8725)
description: This entry represents a bacterial immunoglobulin-like (Big) domain of approximately 150 residues. The domain is found in multi-domain proteins that also contain the DUF7408 domain ([pfam:PF24157]). This family is restricted to Bacillota, particularly Bacillales (including Paenibacillus and Bacillaceae) and Clostridia. The function of this domain remains to be determined.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8726)
description: This entry represents a bacterial immunoglobulin-like (Big) domain of approximately 100 residues. The domain is found at the N-terminus of multi-domain proteins that also contain the DUF7408 domain ([pfam:PF24157]). Structural similarity searches identify this as a member of the E-set Ig-like superfamily. This family is restricted to Bacillota, particularly Bacillales (including Paenibacillus and Bacillaceae) and Clostridia. The function of this domain remains to be determined.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8727)
description: This entry represents a C-terminal alpha-helical domain of approximately 130 residues. The domain is found at the C-terminus of proteins that typically contain an AAA_5 domain ([pfam:PF07728]) and sometimes an MrcB_N domain ([pfam:PF12102]). These proteins are often annotated as restriction endonucleases or dynein-related ATPases. This family is found in bacteria including Bacillota, Pseudomonadota and Bacteroidota. The function of this domain remains to be determined.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8728)
description: This entry represents a C-terminal domain of approximately 110 residues. The domain is found at the C-terminus of proteins annotated as RgtA-like glycosyltransferases. This family is found in diverse bacteria including Pseudomonadota (particularly Legionella), Actinomycetota, Myxococcota and Chloroflexota. The function of this domain remains to be determined.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8729)
description: This entry represents an N-terminal domain of approximately 90 residues found in S8 family serine peptidases (subtilisins). The domain is found N-terminal to the Peptidase_S8 catalytic domain ([pfam:PF00082]). In Bacteroidota members, the proteins often contain a C-terminal T9SS secretion signal ([pfam:PF18962]). This family is found in bacteria including Pseudomonadota, Actinomycetota and Bacteroidota, as well as fungi (Ascomycota). The function of this domain remains to be determined.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8730)
description: This domain is ubiquitously found in uncharacterised bacterial and eukaryotic proteins. It contains several highly conserved cysteine residues some of which may be involved in metal coordination.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8731)
description: This entry represents a C-terminal bacterial immunoglobulin-like (Big) domain of approximately 120 residues. The domain is found C-terminal to the M14 carboxypeptidase catalytic domain ([pfam:PF00246]). This family is found predominantly in Bacteroidota, particularly Cytophagales and Sphingobacteriales. The function of this domain remains to be determined.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8732)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised fungal proteins. It is predicted to adopt ubiquitin-like fold.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8733)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised fungal proteins. It is predicted to adopt ubiquitin-like fold.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8734)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised fungal proteins.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8735)
description: This domainis found in uncharacterised fungal proteins. It shares significant similarity to known AAA domains.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8736)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised fungal proteins.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8737)
description: This entry represents a family of uncharacterised integral membrane bacterial proteins of approximately 125 residues. These proteins contain five potential transmembrane helices. AlphaFold3 prediction suggests these proteins form a homotrimeric arrangement ([swissprot:A9WFT2] ipTM = 0.86 pTM = 0.87). The protein has a small variable C-terminal tail that is likely to be intracellular.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8738)
description: This entry represents a domain of approximately 100 residues. The domain can occur once or twice within a protein, sometimes in tandem. Some members are predicted lipoproteins. This family is found predominantly in Cyanobacteriota and Actinomycetota. The function of this domain remains to be determined.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8739)
description: This entry represents a small domain of approximately 60 residues. The domain is typically found following AAA_16 domains ([pfam:PF13191]) in multidomain proteins that often also contain guanylate cyclase domains ([pfam:PF00211]). Proteins containing this domain include adenylate and guanylate cyclases. This family is found in bacteria (Actinomycetota, Myxococcota, Pseudomonadota) and eukaryotes. The function of this domain remains to be determined.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8740)
description: This entry represents a family of ig-like domains found at the N-terminus of putative phage proteins.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8741)
description: This entry represents a C-terminal domain of approximately 165 residues found in DEAD/DEAH box helicases. The domain is found C-terminal to Helicase_C ([pfam:PF00271]) and SNF2-rel_dom ([pfam:PF00176]) domains. These proteins include HepA-like helicases. This family is found in bacteria, predominantly Actinomycetota and Pseudomonadota. The function of this domain remains to be determined.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8742)
description: This entry represents an N-terminal SH3-like barrel domain of approximately 60 residues. The domain is found at the N-terminus of DEAD/DEAH box helicases, preceding ResIII ([pfam:PF04851]), SNF2-rel_dom ([pfam:PF00176]), DEAD ([pfam:PF00270]), Helicase_C ([pfam:PF00271]) and NOV_C ([pfam:PF13020]) domains. This family is found in bacteria, predominantly Actinomycetota and Pseudomonadota. The function of this domain remains to be determined.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8743)
description: This entry represents a C-terminal domain of approximately 130 residues. The domain is found C-terminal to DUF2357 ([pfam:PF09823]) and PDDEXK_7 ([pfam:PF04411]) domains in proteins annotated as restriction endonucleases, including 5-methylcytosine-specific restriction enzymes. This family is found in bacteria (predominantly Bacillota) and archaea (Methanobacteriota). The function of this domain remains to be determined.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8744)
description: This entry represents a domain of approximately 120 residues found in predicted integral membrane proteins. Some members are annotated as NnrS family proteins. According to STRING, this domain co-occurs with DUF2249 ([pfam:PF10006]). This family is found predominantly in Actinomycetota and Pseudomonadota. The function of this domain remains to be determined.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8745)
description: This entry represents an N-terminal domain of approximately 175 residues found in putative signal transduction proteins. Some members are annotated as histidine kinases or HSP90-like ATPases, and one example contains a HATPase_c domain ([pfam:PF02518]) suggesting these proteins function in two-component signalling systems. This domain may represent a sensor input domain. This family is found almost exclusively in Actinomycetota, particularly Streptomyces. The function of this domain remains to be determined.

name: DUF499 second domain
description: This entry represents the second domain found in a family of uncharacterised hypothetical prokaryotic proteins.

name: DUF499 third domain
description: This entry represents the third domain found in a family of uncharacterised hypothetical prokaryotic proteins.

name: DUF499 4th domain
description: This entry represents the fourth domain found in a family of uncharacterised hypothetical prokaryotic proteins.

name: DUF499 fifth domain
description: This entry represents the fifth domain found in a family of uncharacterised hypothetical prokaryotic proteins. This domain has a beta sandwich fold.

name: DUF499 6th domain
description: This entry represents the C-terminal domain found in a family of uncharacterised hypothetical prokaryotic proteins.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8746)
description: This entry represents a C-terminal domain of approximately 65 residues found in ABC transporter ATP-binding proteins. The domain is located C-terminal to ABC_tran ([pfam:PF00005]) and AAA_21 ([pfam:PF13304]) domains. Many of these proteins are annotated as multidrug ABC transporters or ABC-2 type transport systems, including some daunorubicin/doxorubicin resistance proteins. This family is found almost exclusively in Actinomycetota, particularly Streptomyces. The function of this domain remains to be determined.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8747)
description: This entry represents a domain found in uncharacterised metazoan sequences. This domain shares similarity with the LAP2alpha C-terminal dimerization domain.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8748)
description: This entry represents a probable zinc finger domain found in uncharacterised plant proteins. This domain shares similarity with GRF zinc fingers. It has highly conserved cysteine residues in equivalent positions but is has a large insertion located between the third and the fourth potential zinc coordinating residue.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8749)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised plant proteins.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8750)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised plant proteins. It is predicted to fold into a three helical up-and-down bundle.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8751)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised metazoan sequences. It is predicted to fold into array of alpha-helices.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8752)
description: This entry represents a C-terminal transmembrane domain of approximately 160 residues found in a subset of glycosyltransferase family 2 (GT2) proteins. The domain is predicted to contain four transmembrane helices and is located C-terminal to the catalytic GT2 domain ([pfam:PF00535]). This domain architecture is characteristic of multi-component transmembrane glycosylation systems involved in cell wall polymer modification. This family is found in bacteria, predominantly Bacteroidota, Cyanobacteriota, and Bacillota. The function of this domain remains to be determined.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8753)
description: This entry represents an N-terminal domain of approximately 90 residues found in proteins annotated as quinate 5-dehydrogenase. This domain is structurally distinct from the C-terminal catalytic region. This family is found in bacteria, predominantly Bacillota (especially Clostridia) and Pseudomonadota. The function of this domain remains to be determined.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8754)
description: This entry represents a C-terminal domain of approximately 200 residues found in proteins annotated as quinate 5-dehydrogenase. Structure prediction suggests a Rossmann-like fold. This family is found in bacteria, predominantly Bacillota (especially Clostridia) and Pseudomonadota. The function of this domain remains to be determined.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8755)
description: This entry represents a small N-terminal domain of approximately 40 residues found in bacterial signal transduction histidine kinases and diguanylate cyclases. The domain is composed of an alpha helix and beta hairpin. It is located N-terminal to PAS domains ([pfam:PF00989]) and ultimately HisKA ([pfam:PF00512]) and HATPase_c ([pfam:PF02518]) domains. This family is found in bacteria, predominantly Pseudomonadota and Bacteroidota. The function of this domain remains to be determined.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8756)
description: This entry represents a C-terminal beta sandwich domain of approximately 110 residues found in Pvc16 proteins. The domain is located C-terminal to the Pvc16_N domain ([pfam:PF14065]). These proteins are components of extracellular contractile injection systems (eCIS), which are phage tail-like structures used by bacteria to deliver effector proteins. This family is found in bacteria, predominantly Cyanobacteriota, Pseudomonadota, and Actinomycetota. The function of this domain remains to be determined.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8757)
description: This entry represents a C-terminal domain of approximately 165 residues predicted to adopt an OB-fold. This family is found in bacteria, predominantly Actinomycetota, Pseudomonadota, and Bacteroidota. The function of this domain remains to be determined.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8758)
description: This entry represents an N-terminal domain of approximately 85 residues predicted to adopt an OB-fold. This family is found in bacteria, predominantly Actinomycetota, Pseudomonadota, and Bacteroidota. The function of this domain remains to be determined.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8759)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised fungal proteins. It is predicted to fold into a four helical up-and-down bundle.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8760)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised fungal proteins. It is predicted to fold into an alpha/beta structure with unique topology.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8761)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised fungal proteins. It is predicted to fold into array of helices.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8762)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised fungal proteins. It is predicted to fold into a four helical bundle with two alpha-helices significantly longer than the others.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8763)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised fungal proteins. It shares similarity to RasGAP domains.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8764)
description: This entry represents a domain of unknown function mainly found at the C-terminal of sequences from ticks, spiders and similar sequences from arthropods. This domain may adopt an alpha-helical bundle fold similar to Ty3 transposon capsid-like proteins.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8765)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised fungal proteins.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8766)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised fungal proteins.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF8767)
description: This entry represents a family of uncharcaterised fungal proteins.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8768)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised fungal proteins.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8769)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised proteins. It has similarity to the N-terminal domain of Heparinase II/III.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8770)
description: This domain is found in uncharcaterised proteins mainly from fungi. It shares similarity to the C-terminal domain of Heparinase II/III.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF8771)
description: This is a conserved region found in uncharacterised eukaryotic proteins. It contains several conserved cysteine and histidine residues.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8772)
description: This entry represents a domain found in uncharacterised eukaryotic proteins.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8773)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised fungal proteins.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF8774)
description: This entry represents uncharacterised metazoan sequences.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8775)
description: This entry represents a domain of approximately 70 residues found almost exclusively in spiders (Araneae), particularly in the families Araneidae and Nephilidae. The domain is found in one to three copies per protein. Some family members occur in proteins that also contain a GEMIN2/SIP1 domain ([pfam:PF04938]). The function of this domain remains to be determined.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8776)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised proteins from alphaproteobacteria. It is predicted to fold into an alpha-helical hairpin structure.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8777)
description: This entry represents uncharcaterised proteins found mainly in Streptococcus lineage. They are predicted to be composed of four transmembrane helices. The arrangement of these helices is similar to the one found in the tetraspanin family.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF8778)
description: This entry rerpesents uncharacterised proteins found mainly in Cyanobacteria. They contain a ribbon-helix-helix (RHH) motif and may interact with DNA.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF8779)
description: This entry represents uncharacterised bacterial proteins which are predicted to be composed of transmembrane alpha- helices.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8780)
description: This domain is found in uncharcaterised proteins mainly from Leptospira lineage. It shares similarity with known C-type lectin fold domains.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8781)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised proteins mainly from Leptospira.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8782)
description: This domain is found in uncharcaterised proteins mainly from Leptospira lineage. It is predicted to fold into a pouch-like beta-barrel structure.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8783)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised proteins mainly from Leptospira lineage. This domain has a similarity with known PH domains.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8784)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised proteins mainly from Leptospira lineage. It is predicted to fold into an up-and-down four helical bindle.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8785)
description: This domain is usually found in tandem in uncharacterised proteins mainly from Leptospira lineage. This domain closely resembles the Salmonella typhoid toxin PltB subunit.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8786)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised proteins mainly from Leptospira lineage. It is predicted to fold into array of alpha-helices.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8787)
description: This entry represents uncharacterised proteins found mainly in Leptospira lineage. They are predicted to fold into a beta-barrel-like structures.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8788)
description: This entry rerepsents uncharacterised bacterial proteins. It shares similarity to Inclusion body protein PixA and other structurally related domains.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8789)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised eukaryotic proteins. It shares similarity with members of the C1q and TNF superfamily.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8790)
description: This domain is found in uncharcaterised metazoan proteins. It shares similarity with Tetraspannin-like four transmembrane helical domains.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8791)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised fungal proteins. It is predicted to adopt an alpha/beta structure.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8792)
description: This entry represents uncharacterised fungal proteins. They are predicted to fold into an up-and-down bundle of four transmembrane helices that is similar to the bundle of p53-inducible protein 11.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8793)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised fungal proteins. It is predicted to fold into four helical bundle composed of helices which are predicted as transmembrane. It contains two highly conserved cyateine residues which are predicted to form a disulfide bond.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8794)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised fungal proteins. It is predicted to fold into an alpha/beta structure composed of a four-stranded antiparallel curved beta-sheet packed with two alpha-helices on one side. This domain contains three pairs of conserved cisteine residues that are predicted to form disulfide bonds.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF8795)
description: This group of proteins is found in eukaryotes. They show several highly conserved P residues.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8796)
description: This domain is found in metazoan proteins. It is predicted to fold into two meander beta-sheets that pack on each other.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8797)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised plant proteins. It is predicted to fold into an alpha/beta structure with unique topology.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8798)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised plant proteins. It contains several conserved aromatic residues.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8799)
description: This entry represents a domain of approximately 70 residues found in BPTF (Bromodomain PHD finger transcription factor) proteins and related DDT domain-containing proteins in eukaryotes. This domain is located downstream of the WSD domain ([pfam:PF15613]). BPTF is a subunit of the NURF chromatin remodelling complex that catalyses ATP-dependent nucleosome sliding [[cite:PUB00101089]]. In plant RLT (RINGLET) proteins, this domain is also present downstream of the WSD domain. The function of this domain remains to be determined.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8800)
description: This domain of unknown function is found towards the C-terminal end of a group of uncharacterised proteins from molluscs. It is predicted to adopt a mainly beta configuration.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF8801)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised proteins from metazoan. This domain is composed of seven alpha-helices predicted as transmembrane.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8802)
description: This entry represents uncharacterised metazoan proteins predicted to fold into array of alpha-helices.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8803)
description: This domain is found in uncharacterised eukaryotic proteins. It shares significanrt similarity with known SH3 domains and it is predicted to adopt similar structure.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8804)
description: This entry represents a C-terminal domain of approximately 100 residues found exclusively in Trichomonas (Parabasalia). This domain is found C-terminal to a KilA-N domain ([pfam:PF04383]). These proteins are present in numerous copies within the Trichomonas genome, suggesting lineage-specific gene family expansion. The function of this domain remains to be determined.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8805)
description: This entry represents an N-terminal domain of approximately 70 residues found in secreted alpha/beta hydrolases in Actinomycetes, particularly Streptomycetaceae, Microbacteriaceae, and Micrococcaceae. This domain is found N-terminal to various hydrolase domains including Abhydrolase_1 ([pfam:PF00561]) and Peptidase_S9 ([pfam:PF00326]). The function of this domain remains to be determined.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8806)
description: This entry represents an N-terminal domain of approximately 55 residues found in Bacillota and Thermodesulfobacteriota. This domain is located N-terminal to the MoCF_biosynth domain ([pfam:PF00994]), which is involved in molybdenum cofactor biosynthesis. The function of this domain remains to be determined.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8807)
description: This entry represents a domain of approximately 100 residues found in bacteria. This domain is typically located at the C-terminus of proteins containing DUF1156 ([pfam:PF06634]). These proteins are often associated with mobile genetic elements, including transposases and site-specific DNA methyltransferases. The function of this domain remains to be determined.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF5686) C-terminal domain
description: This is a family of unknown function, mostly found in bacteria. This domain has an incomplete membrane beta barrel fold.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8808)
description: This entry represents a domain of approximately 220 residues found in bacteria, predominantly Proteobacteria. This domain is typically located N-terminal to HNH nuclease domains ([pfam:PF13395]). Some proteins containing this domain also possess methyltransferase domains, suggesting a role in restriction-modification systems. The function of this domain remains to be determined.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8809)
description: This entry represents a small helical hairpin domain found at the C-terminus of bacterial signalling proteins. It may form homodimers to make a four helical bundle structure.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8810)
description: This entry represents a C-terminal domain of approximately 110 residues found in Type IIG restriction-modification enzymes in bacteria. This domain is located C-terminal to the TaqI_C domain ([pfam:PF12950]). The function of this domain remains to be determined.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8811)
description: This entry represents a C-terminal domain of approximately 220 residues found in subtilisin-like serine peptidases in Actinomycetota. This domain is typically located C-terminal to the Peptidase_S8 catalytic domain ([pfam:PF00082]) and PA domain ([pfam:PF02225]). The function of this domain remains to be determined.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8812)
description: This domain of unknown function is found in a group of uncharacterised proteins. Some members are annotated as related to antimicrobial activity. It contains two highly conserved motifs RGYD and RGDY.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8813)
description: This entry represents a small C-terminal helical domain of approximately 40 residues found in bacterial ImmA/IrrE family metallopeptidases. This domain is located C-terminal to the Peptidase_M78 catalytic domain ([pfam:PF06114]). The function of this domain remains to be determined.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8814)
description: This entry represents a domain of approximately 140 residues found in secreted proteins in Actinomycetota, particularly Pseudonocardiaceae. This domain adopts a double psi beta barrel fold. The function of this domain remains to be determined.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8815)
description: This entry represents a C-terminal domain of approximately 125 residues found in multi-domain proteins that contain the DUF7408 domain ([pfam:PF24157]). Structural similarity searches identify this as a member of the galactose-binding domain-like superfamily. This family is found in Bacillota, particularly Bacillales (including Paenibacillus and Bacillaceae) and Clostridia, as well as some Chloroflexota. The function of this domain remains to be determined.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8816)
description: This entry represents a bacterial immunoglobulin-like domain of approximately 65 residues. This domain is found predominantly in Planctomycetota and Bacillota. These domains are typically found in large secreted or surface-associated proteins, often with multiple tandem repeats. The function of this domain remains to be determined.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF8817)
description: This is a family of fungal uncharacterised sequences of unknown function. Some members are annotated as related to antimicrobial resistance. There are two highly conserved motifs FYxxLGF and GxPR.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8818)
description: This entry represents a small beta sandwich domain of approximately 82 residues found in large outer membrane proteins in Bacteroidota (Flavobacteriaceae, Cytophagales). The domain is inserted within larger beta-barrel structures. These proteins are associated with the type IX secretion system (T9SS). The function of this domain remains to be determined.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8819)
description: This family represents small uncharacterized proteins of approximately 108 residues found in Actinomycetes, particularly Streptomyces and Nocardioides. These proteins typically consist of this single domain only. STRING network analysis shows strong functional association with SIS domains ([pfam:PF01380]) and HTH_6 transcription factors ([pfam:PF01418]), suggesting a possible role in sugar metabolism regulation.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8820)
description: This family represents a small domain of approximately 93 amino acids found predominantly in Actinobacteria including Streptomyces, Thermomonosporaceae, and Streptosporangiaceae. The domain is also found in some cyanobacteria. The domain is typically found as the sole domain in uncharacterized proteins and shows genomic context association with DUF6745 domain proteins.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8821)
description: This entry represents a family of uncharacterised proteins of approximately 145 residues found in Bacillota (particularly Paenibacillaceae and Bacillaceae) and Actinomycetota (including Streptomycetaceae). The proteins occur as single-domain proteins. While computationally annotated as phage tail proteins in UniProt, there is no experimental evidence supporting this function, and the annotation likely reflects genomic proximity to prophage regions rather than demonstrated function. The function of this family remains to be determined.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8822)
description: This entry represents a domain of approximately 101 residues found in uncharacterized proteins in plants (Viridiplantae) and cyanobacteria. In plants, it is found predominantly in eudicotyledons and monocots. These are small single-domain proteins whose function is unknown.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8823)
description: This entry represents a C-terminal globular domain of approximately 110 residues found in large integral membrane proteins from Actinomycetota, particularly Streptomycetaceae (Streptomyces and related genera). The parent proteins are approximately 500-700 residues in length with this domain positioned at the C-terminus. While the proteins are annotated as membrane transporters, the specific function of this C-terminal domain remains to be determined.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8824)
description: This domain of unknown function is found mainly in proteins from Bacillota lineage. It is found C-terminal to a lipoprotein lipid attachment site suggesting that it may be associated with the membrane.

name: Domain if unknown function (DUF8825)
description: This entry represents a small domain of approximately 95 residues found as a single-domain protein in Streptomycetaceae. The function of this domain remains to be determined.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8826)
description: This entry represents a C-terminal domain of approximately 57 residues found in aspartic peptidases in Arachis (peanut). This domain is located C-terminal to the Asp_protease_2 domain ([pfam:PF13650]). These proteins may be associated with transposable elements. The function of this C-terminal domain remains to be determined.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8827)
description: This entry represents a membrane protein domain of approximately 70 residues found in Streptomyces and related Actinomycetes. In Streptomyces coelicolor, SCO4131 containing this domain is located in a gene cluster (SCO4126-SCO4131) that affects actinorhodin antibiotic biosynthesis [[cite:PUB00163737]]. The function of this domain remains to be determined.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8828)
description: This entry represents a small domain of approximately 70 residues found in uncharacterized proteins in Bacteroidota, predominantly Flavobacteriaceae. These are small single-domain proteins. Some entries are annotated as 3-hydroxybutyryl-CoA dehydrogenase, but this annotation appears to be erroneous given the small size and lack of typical dehydrogenase features.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8829)
description: This entry represents a domain of approximately 110 residues found in small uncharacterized proteins in Streptomyces and related Actinomycetes. These proteins typically consist of this single domain only. The function of this domain remains to be determined.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8830)
description: This entry represents a domain of approximately 100 residues found in small uncharacterized proteins in Streptomyces and related Actinomycetes. These proteins typically consist of this single domain only. Foldseek analysis suggests weak structural similarity to DUF6204 ([pfam:PF19707]). The function of this domain remains to be determined.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8831)
description: This entry represents a domain of approximately 62 residues found in small uncharacterized proteins in Alphaproteobacteria, particularly Rhodobacterales (Roseobacteraceae, Paracoccaceae). These proteins typically consist of this single domain only. The function of this domain remains to be determined.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8832)
description: This entry represents a domain of approximately 110 residues found in uncharacterised proteins in bacteria, predominantly in Actinomycetes (Streptomyces, Micromonospora) and some Bacilli. This domain adopts an immunoglobulin-like fold and is a member of clan CL0159. Many proteins contain two tandem copies of this domain. The function of this domain remains to be determined.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8833)
description: This entry represents a domain of approximately 60 amino acids found at the N-terminal of 20.7 kDa protein in NOF-FB from Drosophila melanogaster and as tandem arrays of 10-11 copies in other members of this entry, from insects. The function of this domain remains to be determined.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8834)
description: This entry represents a small domain of approximately 43 residues found in uncharacterized proteins in Streptomycetaceae. The STRING analysis indicates functional association with hydrolase domains ([pfam:PF00561], PF12146, PF12697). This domain is predicted to adopt a simple structure composed of three-stranded beta-sheet and an alpha-helix. The function of this domain remains to be determined.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8835)
description: This entry represents a domain of approximately 160 residues found in uncharcaterised proteins from Proteobacteria.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8836)
description: This entry represents a small domain of approximately 65 amino acids found in Actinomycetes. It is predicted to fold into a beta-sandwich structure composed of two three-stranded antiparallel beta-sheets packed on each other.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8837)
description: This domain of unknown function is found in a group of uncharacterised proteins mainly found in firmicutes. This domain is predicted to adopt a mainly beta structure. It shows highly conserved motifs TAY and VxDxG.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8838)
description: This domain is found C-terminal in bacterial proteins containing at the N terminus a methyltransferase domain.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8839)
description: This entry represents a family of small proteins of approximately 50 residues found in Actinomycetes, predominantly in Streptomyces. The function of this family remains to be determined. Members are predicted to fold into a simple structure composed of a small three stranded antiparallel beta-sheet and an alpha-helix connecting the first and the second beta-strand.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8840)
description: This entry represents a family of small proteins of approximately 110 residues found predominantly in Bacteroidota, particularly Flavobacteriaceae. The function of this family remains to be determined. Members are predicted to adopt a structure with significant similarity to members of the PDDEXK superfamily and in particular to [pfam:PF02021].

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8841)
description: This entry represents a domain found in probable transcriptional regulators from Actinomycetota predominantly in the genus Streptomyces. These proteins contain an N-terminal helix-turn-helix DNA-binding domain followed by this domain. The function of this domain is unknown.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8842)
description: This entry represents a domain of unknown function frequently found C-terminal in proteins from Actinomycetota. This domain is distantly related to [pfam:PF19374] (DUF5949). The gene SCO1756 encoding a protein with this domain was found to be more abundant in bacterioferritin mutants during morphological differentiation [[cite:PUB00163738]], although the specific function of this domain remains to be determined.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8843)
description: This entry represents a domain of approximately 120 residues found in uncharacterized proteins in Ascomycota fungi, including Sordariomycetes (Fusarium, Nectriaceae), Eurotiomycetes (Aspergillus), and Dothideomycetes. The function of this domain is unknown.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8844)
description: This entry represents a domain found in uncharacterised proteins from Actinomycetes. STRING analysis indicates functional association with His_Phos_1 ([pfam:PF00300]) and AAA ATPase domains.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8845)
description: This entry represents a domain found in uncharacterised proteins from Bacteroidota, particularly in Flavobacteriaceae. These proteins are approximately 200 amino acids in length and are predicted to be membrane-associated. STRING analysis shows these proteins are functionally associated with sigma-70 factors ([pfam:PF04542] and [pfam:PF08281]) and other regulatory proteins. The function of this protein family remains to be determined.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8846)
description: This entry represents a domain of unknown function found in uncharcaterised proteins from Alphaproteobacteria, predominantly in Rhodobacterales (including Roseobacteraceae and Paracoccaceae). The domain is approximately 100 residues in length and is predicted to adopt an alpha/beta structure containing a four stranded antiparallel beta-sheet. STRING analysis shows these proteins are consistently associated with cell division and secretion system proteins, including DivIB ([pfam:PF03799]), RodZ ([pfam:PF13464]) and SPOR domain proteins ([pfam:PF05036]). The specific function of this domain remains to be determined.

name: Domain of unknown function (DUF8847)
description: This family represents a small domain of approximately 69 amino acids found in uncharacterised proteins from Actinobacteria, particularly Streptomyces, Micromonospora, and Pseudonocardiaceae. It contains a conserved FxGGpxDG sequence motif. This domain is predicted to fold into an open five-stranded beta-barrel.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF8848)
description: This entry represents a group of uncharacterised plant proteins that are predicted to mainly adopt a disordered fold. They are rich in G residues.

name: Family of unknown function (DUF8849)
description: This family represents a group of uncharacterised proteins predominantly found in echinoderms. Members are predicted to show an alpha configuration. They have several highly conserved motifs EE and highly conserved residues K, Q, W and H.
